### ⚡ Bolt: Parallelize LLM categorization in transaction ingestion

#### 💡 What:
Optimized the `TransactionDatabase.insert_transactions` method by parallelizing LLM-based categorization calls using `asyncio.gather`.

#### 🎯 Why:
Transaction ingestion was previously bottlenecked by sequential calls to the local Ollama LLM for each unique unknown payee. For a file with many new payees, this resulted in linear growth in ingestion time.

#### 📊 Impact:
- **Reduced Ingestion Latency**: Changes the performance complexity from O(N) to O(1) relative to the number of unique payees (limited only by the LLM server's concurrency capacity).
- **Improved Robustness**: Individual LLM call failures no longer abort the entire ingestion process.

#### 🔬 Measurement:
Verified via `make test-backend` (all 22 tests passing). The optimization can be observed by ingesting a transaction file with multiple new payees; the total time for LLM categorization will now be close to the duration of a single slowest call rather than the sum of all calls.

author: thgterto
body:
**💡 What:** 
Optimized the `computeIMR` function to calculate the values required for moving range using a single-pass `for` loop and a pre-allocated array (`mrData = new Array(len)`) instead of using `.push()`, redundant `SPC.mean` calls, and the spread operator `[0, ...ranges]`. Added explicit edge case handling for `len === 0`.

**🎯 Why:**
The original implementation had an `O(N)` reallocation overhead during `.push()`, iterated over arrays multiple times to calculate mathematical bounds, and utilized the spread syntax which triggers `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` vulnerabilities in V8 when iterating over huge statistical distributions.

**📊 Impact:** 
The optimization delivers approximately a **~5x speedup** on datasets of 1 million points (from ~125ms to ~25ms). It dramatically improves memory efficiency by minimizing Garbage Collector thrashing and eliminating internal array resizing.

**🔬 Measurement:**
Tested via ad-hoc benchmark script to guarantee mathematical correctness (comparing bounds of both systems directly up to 1e-10 precision). Executed all end-to-end frontend Playwright checks using `verify.py` locally on port 8080 successfully.

## Summary

Extends the QtWebEngine argument builder in `qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py` so that it recognizes and propagates `--disable-features=...` flags with the same fidelity it currently applies to `--enable-features=...` flags. Previously, `--disable-features=SomeFeature` flags supplied via `--qt-flag` on the command line or via the `qt.args` configuration option were silently dropped, leaving the corresponding Chromium feature enabled.

## Changes

### Source (`qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py` — 31 net additions)
- Added two module-level constants `ENABLE_FEATURES_PREFIX = '--enable-features='` and `DISABLE_FEATURES_PREFIX = '--disable-features='` (lines 32–33), creating a single source of truth for both prefix literals.
- Replaced all four prior hardcoded `'--enable-features='` literals with references to `ENABLE_FEATURES_PREFIX` (lines 61, 65, 79, 184).
- Generalized the extract/filter pipeline at the top of `qt_args()` (lines 60–67) so it now collects enable- and disable-prefixed flags into separate lists and strips both families from `argv` before forwarding into `_qtwebengine_args()`.
- Added a new module-private generator `_qtwebengine_disabled_features()` (lines 131–141) that strips the `--disable-features=` prefix and yields each comma-separated token. Per AAP requirement, it performs **pure pass-through** with no internal disabled-feature injection, no version checks, and no config lookups.
- Extended `_qtwebengine_args()` signature by **appending** a new `disable_feature_flags: Sequence[str]` parameter (lines 144–148) — preserving the existing `namespace` and `feature_flags` parameters unchanged in name, order, and absence of defaults.
- Added a parallel `--disable-features=` emission block (lines 186–188) that yields exactly one combined flag when the disabled list is non-empty.

### Tests (`tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py` — 103 net additions)
Three new parametrized test methods added to the existing `TestQtArgs` class:
- `test_disable_features_flag` (6 parametrizations: 3 feature permutations × `via_commandline ∈ {True, False}`) — verifies the flag survives unmodified from both CLI and config sources and never leaks into `--enable-features=`.
- `test_enable_and_disable_features_combined` (2 parametrizations) — verifies enable/disable flags coexist as separate argv entries with no cross-contamination, and that `OverlayScrollbar` is injected only on the enable side.
- `test_feature_flag_prefix_constants` — locks in the exact literal values of both module-level prefix constants.

### Documentation (`doc/changelog.asciidoc` — 4 net additions)
Added a bullet under `v2.0.0 (unreleased)` → Fixed describing the new behavior.

## Validation
- All 91/91 tests in `tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py` pass (baseline 82, added 9 parametrizations) — 0.84s wall time.
- Critical regression sentinels still pass: `test_overlay_features_flag` (6 cases), `test_referer` (10 cases), `test_overlay_scrollbar` (5 cases).
- `flake8` reports zero violations on both modified Python files.
- `python -m py_compile` clean on both files.
- Module imports cleanly (`from qutebrowser.config import qtargs`, `import qutebrowser.app`).
- All function signatures verified: `qt_args(namespace)` and `_qtwebengine_enabled_features(feature_flags)` unchanged; `_qtwebengine_args(namespace, feature_flags, disable_feature_flags)` appended one parameter.

## AAP Compliance
All §0.7.3 Pre-Submission Checklist items satisfied. Working tree clean. 4 commits pushed to `origin/blitzy-647be6af-da65-4e68-80c8-14720b78229b`.

The project is **83.3% complete**, with the remaining ~2 hours covering human code review, final maintainer acceptance, and optional integration smoke-testing across the Qt 5.12–5.15 matrix.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## Summary

#9943 reports a 20-minute keeper turn (1,204,542 ms on taskmaster
2026-04-24) whose post-turn compaction step appears to no-op while
the turn keeps running.  The duration was visible only in a single
info log line.  This PR raises the long-turn signal to Prometheus.

This is **option #4** from the issue's resolution list — observability
+ operator-actionable WARN — and is the bucket-counter foundation a
later fix (#9933 oas_timeout_budget cap tightening / #10121 livelock
gate) can hang an alert on.

## Why a counter, not just a histogram

`masc_llm_inference_duration_seconds` is already a histogram labelled
by `model`.  That measures per-LLM-call latency.  The #9943 symptom
is per-turn (post-tool-loop) latency on a specific **keeper**.
A bucketed counter labelled by `keeper × bucket` gives:

- direct \`rate(...{bucket="over_1200s"}[5m])\` alerting,
- bounded cardinality (5 bucket strings × keeper count),
- one row in the export for every JSONL ledger row, so dashboards and
  on-disk records stay aligned.

## Bucket vocabulary

\`\`\`
under_60s    | 60-300s   | 300-600s  | 600-1200s | over_1200s
routine      | acceptable| slow      | long      | over OAS budget cap
\`\`\`

Boundaries are inclusive on the lower edge: 60_000 ms → \`60-300s\`,
600_000 ms → \`600-1200s\`, 1_200_000 ms → \`over_1200s\`.  That last
bucket is the #9943 sample.

## WARN threshold

\`record_turn_latency_bucket\` emits a \`Log.Keeper.warn\` line when
\`latency_ms >= long_turn_warn_threshold_ms\` (default 600_000 ms = 10 min).
The threshold reads \`MASC_KEEPER_LONG_TURN_WARN_MS\` on each call so
operators can dial it without restarting the process — module-init
capture would have made the env var dead.

## Files

- \`lib/prometheus.ml/mli\`: \`metric_keeper_turn_latency_bucket\` +
  registration with bounded label vocabulary.
- \`lib/keeper/keeper_unified_metrics.ml/mli\`:
  \`turn_latency_bucket\`, \`long_turn_warn_threshold_ms\`,
  \`record_turn_latency_bucket\`; wired into
  \`append_metrics_snapshot\` (single emit site, JSONL-row-rate).
- \`test/test_keeper_long_turn_9943.ml\`: 6 tests pinning bucket
  vocabulary, boundary points, per-keeper isolation, threshold default,
  env-override behaviour.

## Test plan

- [x] \`dune build --root . lib/\` clean (mli/ml aligned)
- [x] \`dune exec test/test_keeper_long_turn_9943.exe\` — 6/6 pass
- [ ] Roll forward locally on a long keeper run; confirm
      \`/metrics\` exposes \`masc_keeper_turn_latency_bucket_total\` with
      keeper labels and that taskmaster appears in \`over_1200s\` after
      a budget-exhaustion turn.

## Refs

Refs #9933 (oas_timeout_budget cap tightening, the next layer of
defence on top of this counter), #9982 (trust pause residual UI bug
that left "long turn" invisible), #10121 (same-turn livelock counter
which this complements).

## Do-not-merge

\`do-not-merge\` label set so the auto-merge pipeline does not flip
this Draft to Ready.  Operator validation on a real long-running
keeper required before this can land.

author: danielgerlag
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive workflow testing and debugging UX to prevent costly mistakes (mass emails sent, LLM tokens burned) when developing workflows.

## What's included

### Shadow Mode & Test Runner
- **Shadow execution mode**  side-effecting actions (tool calls, emails, agent invocations, workflow launches) are intercepted and recorded instead of executed. Read-only tools still run normally.
- **Test cases in YAML**  define tests directly in the workflow definition with trigger inputs, mocked step outputs (`shadow_outputs`), expected tool call assertions (partial argument matching), and rich expectations (status, output, step reachability, action counts).
- **Test runner UI**  run tests from the workflow designer's Tests panel with real-time progress badges, clickable result cards, and a detailed results dialog (Steps / Output / Actions tabs).

### Agent Interactions in Tests
- **Auto-respond**  when agents call `ask_user` or request tool approvals during tests, they're automatically answered (first choice / auto-approve) so tests don't block.
- **Interaction capture**  auto-responded `ask_user` questions and tool approvals are recorded as intercepted actions, visible in the Actions tab alongside tool calls.

### Test UX
- **Progress streaming**  `TestCaseStarted` / `TestCaseCompleted` / `TestRunCompleted` events stream via SSE for live progress badges.
- **Cancel support**  stop button with per-run `AtomicBool` token (soft cancel between test cases).
- **Result summary** on test cards  step count, action count, duration, click-for-details hint.

### Bug Fixes
- **Fix shadow_mode not applied to test agents**  `BotConfig.to_agent_spec()` hardcoded `shadow_mode: false`. Fixed by (A) passing workspace_path through `launch_test` so agents use the `AgentSpec` path, and (B) adding `shadow_mode` field to `BotConfig` as a safety net.
- **Fix duplicate workflow triggers**  same incoming message no longer spawns multiple workflow instances.
- **Fix stuck thinking badge**  long agent sessions no longer leave the thinking indicator stuck.
- **Fix stop button**  cancel endpoint now returns JSON instead of bare StatusCode (Tauri's `async_post_empty` requires parseable JSON).
- **Multi-turn conversation refactor**  cleaner handling of multi-turn agent interactions.

### Documentation
- **concepts/workflows.md**  new Testing & Shadow Mode section.
- **guides/workflows.md**  full Testing Your Workflows guide (writing tests, mocking, assertions, running, stopping, what gets intercepted, tips).
- **DESIGN_NOTES.md**  documents shadow mode as a deliberate addition.

## Testing
- All existing tests pass: hive-workflow (33), hive-workflow-service (20), hive-chat (64), hive-agents, hive-tools
- Frontend builds cleanly (`npx vite build`)
- Pre-existing broken test files (`multi_agent_collaboration.rs`, `chat_agent_integration.rs`) are NOT touched by this PR

#### 5d5abab4e3bf53b240499b1964734620fb53101a 
[Site Isolation] https/wpt/resource-timing/crossorigin-servertiming.html fails
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=313280
rdar://175553453

Reviewed by Ryosuke Niwa.

A cross-origin iframe's initial navigation should appear as a
PerformanceResourceTiming entry in the parent document's performance timeline.

Resource timing does not work in site isolation because
ResourceTiming::addResourceTiming() relies on document.parentDocument and
frame->ownerElement(), which are null in the Site Isolation case.

To address this problem, we send the ResourceTiming data to the parent WCP
via IPC in SubresourceLoader::reportResourceTiming().

Then the parent adds the information to the document's Performance
object through the new ResourceTimingInformation::addResourceTimingToDocument().

body:
## Problem

Several backend routes had broken or mismatched implementations: the upload route inserted videos with status `'processing'` instead of `'pending'` and ran the indexing pipeline synchronously after `res.json()` in a way that could swallow the response on DB errors; the search and library routes returned camelCase JSON keys instead of the snake_case schema the frontend expects; and `GET /api/index-status/:videoId` was entirely missing — only the aggregate `GET /api/index-status` existed.

## Solution

Fixed `routes/upload.js` to insert with `status='pending'`, respond immediately with the correct schema, then run the full indexing pipeline (status update → frame extraction → embedding generation → mark ready) inside a self-invoking async IIFE so errors in the background job can never prevent the HTTP response from being sent. Fixed `routes/search.js` to map internal camelCase scene fields to the snake_case response schema (`anime_title`, `clip_name`, `video_id`, `start_timestamp`, `end_timestamp`). Fixed `routes/library.js` to return `video_id`, `clip_name`, `frame_count`, `created_at`, `updated_at` for both the list and single-video endpoints. Added `GET /api/index-status/:videoId` to `routes/index_status.js` with a 404 on unknown IDs and a `frames_processed` / `total_frames` / `message` payload for frontend polling.

### Changes
- **Modified** `routes/search.js`
- **Modified** `routes/upload.js`
- **Modified** `routes/index_status.js`
- **Modified** `routes/library.js`

author: joao-o-santos
body:
# Add XDG Base Directory support (backward compatible)

First off, let me thank you for building this plugin and open sourcing it. I'm still just trying out the plugin, but I'm already seeing the benefits!

## PR Rationale

I like to keep my \$HOME directory as clean as possible, and have configured XDG_ env vars to help keep it that way. It is just a personal nit pick, but I wanted to get plannotator to respect XDG spec.

## What this PR does

This PR adds support for the [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/latest/) while keeping `~/.plannotator` as the default for full backward compatibility.

### Before this PR

All plannotator data lived in a single `~/.plannotator/` directory:
- Config (`config.json`)
- Data (`plans/`, `history/`, `hooks/`)
- Cache/transient files (`drafts/`, `sessions/`, `pastes/`, debug logs,
  schemas)

### After this PR

Path resolution now follows this priority (highest wins):
1. `PLANNOTATOR_*_DIR` env var (explicit override)
2. `XDG_*_HOME` env var (spec compliance)
3. `~/.plannotator` (original default — unchanged)

| Category | Contents | Env override | XDG fallback | Default |
|----------|----------|--------------|--------------|---------| Config |
|`config.json` | `PLANNOTATOR_CONFIG_DIR` | `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` |
|`~/.plannotator` | Data | `plans/`, `history/`, `hooks/` |
|`PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` | `XDG_DATA_HOME` | `~/.plannotator` | Cache |
|`drafts/`, `sessions/`, `pastes/`, logs, schemas | `PLANNOTATOR_CACHE_DIR` |
|`XDG_CACHE_HOME` | `~/.plannotator` |

### Migration strategy

- **Reads**: new resolved path first, then fallback to `~/.plannotator/`
- **Writes**: always go to the resolved path
- **No forced migration**: old data is never moved or deleted
- **Indefinite legacy support**: existing users see zero change unless they set
XDG vars

### Files changed

- `packages/shared/paths.ts` — new path resolution module
- `packages/shared/config.ts`, `storage.ts`, `draft.ts`, `improvement-hooks.ts`
— use new paths
- `packages/server/sessions.ts`, `browser.ts`, `codex-review.ts`, `tour/tour-review.ts` — use new paths
- `apps/vscode-extension/src/extension.ts` — match server's IPC path
- `apps/paste-service/targets/bun.ts` — paste store uses cache dir
- `packages/ui/components/Settings.tsx`, `utils/planSave.ts`,
`utils/quickLabels.ts` — UI strings updated
- `scripts/install.sh`, `install.ps1`, `install.cmd` — dynamic config path resolution
- `packages/shared/improvement-hooks.test.ts`, `tests/manual/local/test-sessions.sh` — tests updated
- Documentation (AGENTS.md, marketing docs, env var reference)
- `XDG_DESIGN.md` — design decision record

## Testing

- Compiled and tested locally on Arch Linux
- `plannotator --help` ✓
- `plannotator annotate md_file.md` ✓
- Hook mode (plan review) creates data in resolved path ✓
- `~/.plannotator` is **not** created when XDG vars are set ✓
- Install scripts seem to dynamically resolve config path ✓

## About this PR

The key design constraint was: **no breaking changes**. Users who don't set `XDG_*_HOME` should see absolutely zero difference in behavior. XDG support is
purely opt-in.

I am not a Node.js/TypeScript developer by trade, nor an AI tooling specialist. I reviewed the generated changes, tested them on my machine, and validated that the behavior is correct. The implementation was done with the help of an AI coding assistant (namely, OpenCode with the plannotator plugin). I reviewed the decisions, and overall approach. Still, this is not my wheel house.

**Please review carefully**, and do let me know what I need to fix.

Thank you for reading and considering the PR. Please keep up the good work!

﻿## Summary

Phase 1 — Foundations of Epic #951 (Studio → Pitch). Backend-only. Lays the data layer + agent archetype + prompt library that later phases (generator, REST surface, UI, exporters) build on. No UI in this PR.

## Sub-issues closed

Refs #951
Closes #952  (Zod slide/deck schemas)
Closes #953  (8 starter brand kits + idempotent seed)
Closes #955  (Brand Kit extension: font_heading, font_body, footer_text)
Closes #956  (PitchRepository — decks/slides/assets, transactional, FK-cascaded)
Closes #960  (`pitch-writer` agent archetype + `pitch-prompts.ts`)

Phase 2+ tracked separately under the remaining sub-issues of Epic #951.

## What''s in this PR

- `src/pitch/pitch-schema.ts` — `BrandKitSchema`, `DeckSchema`, `SlideAssetSchema`, plus a discriminated union over the 14 slide templates.
- `src/pitch/pitch-repository.ts` — `PitchRepository` with `migrate`, atomic `insertDeck` (validates every slide before opening the transaction), CRUD for decks/slides/assets, transactional `reorderSlides`, defensive `DeckSchema.parse` on every read, allowlisted UPDATE columns.
- `src/pitch/starter-brand-kits.ts` — 8 starter kits + `seedStarterBrandKits` (idempotent, preserves user edits).
- `src/pitch/pitch-prompts.ts` — `buildDraftSystemPrompt` + `buildRegenerateSystemPrompt` with prompt-injection guard and "never invent image URLs" rule.
- `src/video/brand-kit.ts` — schema extended with `font_heading`, `font_body`, `footer_text` via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`. Existing rows untouched; legacy callers keep working.
- `config/agents.json` — new `pitch-writer` archetype.
- `src/server.ts` — wires the starter-kit seed in after `brandKitRepo.migrate()`.
- Test fixtures in `src/api/director.test.ts` and `src/mcp/tools/brand-kit-tools.test.ts` updated to the new BrandKit shape.

## Quality gate

- `pnpm lint`           PASS
- `pnpm typecheck`      PASS
- `pnpm test`           PASS (6601/6601 tests; trailing tinypool worker-exit noise unrelated)
- `cd ui ; npx next build`  PASS

## Coverage on new files

| File | Stmts | Branch | Funcs | Lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| src/pitch/pitch-schema.ts        | 100   | 100   | 100   | 100   |
| src/pitch/pitch-repository.ts    | 98.42 | 93.84 | 95.45 | 98.42 |
| src/pitch/starter-brand-kits.ts  | 100   | 100   | 100   | 100   |
| src/pitch/pitch-prompts.ts       | 99.10 | 86.36 | 100   | 99.10 |
| src/video/brand-kit.ts           | 96.77 | 90.00 | 100   | 96.77 |

All four new `src/pitch/*` modules clear the 80% gate on every metric.

## Security review (OWASP)

- **Injection (A03):** All UPDATE statements use a closed allowlist of column names; all queries use parameterized binds. No string interpolation into SQL.
- **Insecure deserialization (A08):** Every read from SQLite is re-parsed through Zod (`DeckSchema.parse`, `SlideSchema.parse`, `SlideAssetSchema.parse`) so corruption fails loudly.
- **SSRF / path traversal (A01/A10):** This phase introduces no filesystem or network I/O driven by user input — assets are only persisted as repository records here; the file-system pipeline is Phase 2+.
- **Prompt injection:** `buildDraftSystemPrompt` and `buildRegenerateSystemPrompt` carry an explicit guard sentence telling the model to treat the user script as data, not instructions.
- **Auth surface:** No new HTTP endpoints in this PR; existing `/api/admin` auth boundaries unchanged. (`src/api/admin.ts` deliberately untouched per Phase 1 scope.)

## Out of scope

- No new HTTP/REST surface for decks (Phase 2 — generator/router).
- No `reveal.js`, `pptxgenjs`, or `decktape` install (deferred to the export phase).
- No UI work.

author: movm
body:
## Why

The monitor module had three classes of silent failure that made it impossible to tell from logs whether a refresh actually worked:

1. **Critical writes logged-and-swallowed.** \`upsertArticles\` and \`saveSnapshotAggregates\` caught DB errors, logged them, and returned normally — so \`refreshMonitor()\` would continue, the HTTP handler would respond \`{ success: true }\`, and the user would think the refresh worked while nothing got persisted. (This is exactly how today's prod incident hid for so long: every refresh was 'succeeding' while every \`INSERT\` was failing on the missing \`emotion_scores\` column.)
2. **13 fire-and-forget warm tasks each had their own \`.catch(log.warn)\`.** A Mistral outage or a single broken briefing path produced 13 independent WARN lines scattered through the log; nothing aggregated them, so unless someone tailed the right grep, partial degradation was invisible.
3. **Three empty \`catch {}\` blocks** around Redis reads/writes in \`getLatestSnapshot\` and \`getStimmung\` masked actual Redis errors as 'cache miss', making Redis-side problems indistinguishable from a normal cold cache.

## What

Single-file change in \`apps/api/services/monitor/MonitorService.ts\` (+71/-34):

- **Critical writes re-throw.** \`upsertArticles\` and \`saveSnapshotAggregates\` now \`throw error\` after logging. \`refreshMonitor()\` propagates, and the route returns 500 — which is correct for 'refresh that didn't persist'.
- **Background warm uses \`Promise.allSettled\` with a single structured summary.** Tasks are now collected as \`{ name, run }\` descriptors. Result: one log line per refresh — \`INFO 13/13 succeeded\` or \`ERROR 4/13 failed — briefing:de: …; entity-summary:scholz/de: …\`. Future warmers join the same aggregator automatically; no more 'forgot to add a .catch' regressions.
- **Empty Redis catches replaced with \`log.warn\`** that includes the actual error message via \`toError\`. The fall-through behaviour is preserved (Redis hiccups still don't fail the request) but they're observable now.
- All error stringification routed through \`toError()\` for consistency with the rest of the API.

## Test plan

- [x] Typecheck passes (\`tsc --noEmit --project apps/api/tsconfig.json\` → 0 errors).
- [ ] Trigger a successful refresh on test → expect single \`INFO Background warm: N/N succeeded\` line per refresh.
- [ ] Simulate a downstream failure (e.g. revoke Mistral key in test) → expect single \`ERROR Background warm: K/N failed — <task>: <reason>; …\` line.
- [ ] Force a DB write failure (e.g. lock the table) → expect refresh to return 500 instead of \`{ success: true }\`.
- [ ] Stop Redis → expect \`/monitor/latest\` to still serve via DB rebuild, with WARN log lines naming the read/write that failed.

## Out of scope

- Adding a scheduler (separate concern; flagged in earlier conversation).
- Switching warm to blocking (would 3× the user's perceived refresh latency; the right tradeoff is non-blocking but observable).
- Cleanup of unbounded \`monitor_articles\` growth (separate cron PR).

author: miapritchina
body:
## Summary

### Tree → popup interaction (new)
- Tapping a tree card no longer pushes a new tree modal. It opens a **character popup** layered on top: hanzi-writer stroke animation (tap to replay), pinyin, full definition list, etymology, and a star to save the character. The tree stays mounted underneath; ESC, backdrop tap, or the close button dismiss the popup.
- Popup also lists every word in your saved set that contains this character as chips — tap a chip to jump to that word's tree.

### Cards
- **Word-root card is back.** No more vertically stacked column; the word renders as a single horizontal text glyph (font size scales by character count).
- **Bigger.** Card dimensions 220×280 (was 168×210). Glyph slot 150×150 (was 110). Fallback hanzi 132px (was 92).
- **Tighter spacing.** dx = CARD_W + 10, dy = CARD_H + 24 — cards are nearly touching.
- **Etymology now grows the card.** The foreignObject `height` attribute is updated by the d3-zoom handler — at high zoom (k > 1.7) each card jumps from 280→380px and the etymology text reveals inside.

### Fonts (all bumped)
- Card pinyin 12→16, card gloss 11.5→14, card etymology 10→12.5
- Home grid hanzi 38→46, search-results hanzi 26→32

### Saved set
- Supports characters as well as words now. Char-only saves get a minimal card on the home **Saved** shelf that opens straight into the popup.

### Data
- Seed bumped 2000 → 8000 by `movieWordRank`. Words outside the previous cutoff (e.g. `胡萝卜` "carrot" at rank 6986) now resolve.
- `data.json`: 1.27 MB raw / 313 KB gzip → 3.08 MB raw / **778 KB gzip** (under the 800 KB target). Held in budget by capping definitions at 4 (was 6) and capping each char's `appearsIn` list at 40 entries.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open `你好`. Confirm the word-root card displays at the top with `你好` in one horizontal row (no vertical column).
- [ ] Confirm character glyphs in the tree are noticeably larger than v9.
- [ ] Tap a child card (e.g. `亻`). Confirm a **popup** opens with stroke animation, pinyin, full definition list, etymology, star, and "in your saved words" list. Tree stays visible underneath; popup dismisses on ESC, backdrop tap, or X.
- [ ] Tap the popup star. Confirm it toggles; close popup; confirm the character appears in the home **Saved** shelf with a minimal card.
- [ ] Search `胡萝卜` — confirm it resolves now (it didn't in v9). Open it; tree renders.
- [ ] Pinch / scroll-zoom past 1.7×. Confirm each card grows downward and the etymology paragraph reveals inside.
- [ ] iPhone-width: card sizing and popup layout work; popup fits within viewport with safe-area insets respected.
- [ ] `chinese v10` shows in the bottom-right after deploy.

## Risks

- Cards growing on zoom overlap the connecting links — at high zoom the card's solid background hides them. At default zoom links are fully visible.
- Popup uses `HanziWriter.create` directly; on the small chance the CDN data fetch fails, falls back to a static glyph.
- 778 KB gzip is close to the 800 KB target; further seed expansion will need data splitting.

author: lijunzh
body:
## Summary

Foundation for the **#996** multi-agent UX series. **Pure plumbing** — no slash commands, no LLM tools, no UI changes. Layers 1+ consume this surface.

Modeled on Codex's `tokio::sync::watch::Receiver<AgentStatus>` pattern (`codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs`).

## Why this PR is small on purpose

This is the first of a phased series tracked in #996. Reviewing pure infrastructure separately from UX makes both easier to audit:

| PR | Layer | Surface |
|---|---|---|
| **this PR** | 0 | `AgentStatus` enum + watch channel + per-task cancel + snapshot |
| #1042 (next) | 1 | `/agents` and `/cancel <id>` slash commands |
| #1043 | 2 | `ListBackgroundTasks` / `CancelAgent` / `AgentStatus` LLM tools |
| #1044 | 3 | Status-bar pill (`◇ N agents`) |
| #1045 | 4 | Live per-iter heartbeat |

#1042 alone closes the original #996 P0 bug.

## What's in this PR

### Surface added to `BgAgentRegistry`

| Item | Purpose | Future consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `AgentStatus` enum | `Pending \| Running { iter } \| Cancelled \| Completed { summary } \| Errored { error }` | All status surfaces |
| `BgTaskSnapshot` | Display-ready metadata bag (id, name, prompt, age, status) | `/agents`, `ListBackgroundTasks` |
| `cancel(task_id) -> bool` | Fire one task's cancel token | `/cancel <id>`, `CancelAgent` tool |
| `snapshot() -> Vec<BgTaskSnapshot>` | Sync read of pending state, sorted by ascending `task_id` | `/agents`, status pill, `ListBackgroundTasks` |
| `watch::channel<AgentStatus>` per task | Live status push, no polling | All status surfaces |

### Wiring

- `BgAgentReservation` gains `status_tx` + `status_rx` (paired with the existing oneshot `tx`/`rx` pattern).
- `BgAgentEntry` stores `status_rx` + `started_at`.
- `run_bg_agent` drives transitions: `Pending → Running { iter: 0 }` on entry; `Completed` / `Errored` / `Cancelled` before `tx.send`. **Cancellation is disambiguated by checking the cancel token *after* the inner call**, since cancellation typically surfaces as an error from inside the loop.
- `attach()` takes `status_rx` as a new param (8 args trips `clippy::too_many_arguments` — added a targeted allow with rationale).

### Two follow-ups baked into the design

- **`Running { iter: 0 }`** is a Layer-0 placeholder. Layer 4 populates `iter` from inside the inference loop. Field shape is stable across PRs so Layer 4 won't churn callers.
- **`snapshot()` returns currently-pending only.** The Claude-Code "completed lingers 30s" UX is a *display* concern — implemented at the slash-command layer in #1042.

## Tests

7 new bg_agent tests, 10 pre-existing all green = **17 total in `bg_agent`**:

- `cancel_known_task_fires_token`
- `cancel_unknown_task_returns_false`
- `cancel_is_idempotent_while_pending`
- `snapshot_lists_pending_tasks_in_id_order`
- `snapshot_reflects_status_writes` (`status_tx` → `snapshot` round-trip, no async yield required because `watch::Receiver::borrow` is sync)
- `snapshot_age_is_monotonic`
- `snapshot_empty_registry_is_empty_vec`
- `snapshot_drops_drained_tasks`

## CI

- ✅ `cargo build --workspace`
- ✅ `cargo test -p koda-core` (1063 passing, 0 failed)
- ✅ `cargo clippy -p koda-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- ✅ `cargo fmt --all`

## Refs

- Bug: #996
- Related discussion: #1024
- Builds on: #1022 (cancellation cascade), #1030 (BufferingSink)

author: avifenesh
body:
## Summary

Adds `EngineBackend::seed_waitpoint_hmac_secret` (issue #280) so cairn-fabric can drop its raw-`HSET` boot path and unblock Postgres adoption.

- **Trait** (`ff-core`): `seed_waitpoint_hmac_secret(args) -> Result<SeedOutcome, _>` with default returning `EngineError::Unavailable { op: \"seed_waitpoint_hmac_secret\" }`. New contracts `SeedWaitpointHmacSecretArgs { kid, secret_hex }` and `SeedOutcome::{ Seeded { kid }, AlreadySeeded { kid, same_secret } }` — `#[non_exhaustive]` with paired `new()` per the project memory rule.
- **Valkey impl**: per-execution-partition HGET probe + HSET install against the existing `waitpoint_hmac_secrets:{p:N}` layout, reusing `admin_rotate_fanout_concurrency`. Idempotent: repairs torn `secret:<kid>` writes, returns `AlreadySeeded { same_secret: true }` on exact replay. A mismatched stored `current_kid` surfaces `Validation(InvalidInput)` — operators rotate, not re-seed.
- **Postgres impl**: single INSERT into `ff_waitpoint_hmac` when no kid is active. Replay against the same kid returns `AlreadySeeded` with `same_secret` comparing stored bytes. A different active kid surfaces `Validation(InvalidInput)`.
- **Validation**: `secret_hex` must be 64 ASCII-hex chars (256-bit secret); `kid` non-empty. Surfaced as `Validation(InvalidInput)`.

## Parity matrix

`docs/POSTGRES_PARITY_MATRIX.md`:

```
| Admin seed (seed_waitpoint_hmac_secret, issue #280) | impl | impl | ... |
```

## Tests

- `crates/ff-server/tests/parity_stage_a_backfill.rs::default_seed_waitpoint_hmac_secret_is_unavailable` — trait default falls through to `Unavailable { op }` with the correct label.
- `crates/ff-backend-postgres/tests/suspend_signal.rs` (gated on `FF_PG_TEST_URL`):
  - `seed_happy_path_installs_new_kid`
  - `seed_replay_same_kid_and_secret_reports_already_seeded_matching`
  - `seed_replay_same_kid_different_secret_reports_mismatch`
  - `seed_different_active_kid_is_validation_error`
  - `seed_rejects_invalid_secret_hex_length`
- Existing `waitpoint_hmac_rotation_fcall` integration tests still pass (no regression in the rotation FCALL path).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --workspace`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ff-core -p ff-script -p ff-engine -p ff-scheduler -p ff-sdk -p ff-server -p ff-test -p ff-backend-valkey -p ff-backend-postgres --features ff-sdk/direct-valkey-claim -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p ff-backend-valkey -p ff-backend-postgres --lib`
- [x] `cargo test -p ff-server --test parity_stage_a_backfill default_seed_waitpoint_hmac_secret`
- [x] `cargo test -p ff-test --test waitpoint_hmac_rotation_fcall` (against live Valkey)

## Out of scope (per issue #280)

- Single-user authentication system with password-based login and JWT session management

### Database & Schema
- MySQL/TiDB database integration using Drizzle ORM
- Comprehensive schema for influencers, posts, and generation jobs
- Support for multiple platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Twitter) and content formats (reel, photo, carousel, tweet)

### Influencer Management

### Content Pipeline

- **Script Generation**: Platform-specific script writing with tone/style adherence

- **Asset Generation**:

### API Routes
- RESTful endpoints for influencer CRUD operations
- Post generation and download workflows
- Reference image and weekly plan generation triggers

### UI Components
- Dashboard with influencer and post overview

- Post detail pages with platform-specific previews (Instagram, TikTok, Twitter)
- Influencer form for creation and editing
- Action buttons for generation workflows with loading states

### Integration with BytePlus Seed
- LLM integration (Seed 2 for planning/scripting)
- Image generation (Seedream 5.0)

- Optimistic UI updates with toast notifications
- Dynamic content generation with proper error handling and validation
- Platform-specific constraints (aspect ratios, character limits, video duration ranges)

author: andymai
body:
## Summary
- Adds two register-level setters to the `aw88298` crate that the firmware will need once the I²S TX streaming PR lands.
- **No firmware changes.** `init()` still leaves the chip in the same boot state (muted, -24 dB, boost off); these methods just expose the levers TX will need.

## API additions
- `set_volume_db(db: i8)` — 0.5 dB / LSB encoding via HAGCCFG4 upper byte; saturates outside `[VOLUME_MIN_DB, VOLUME_MAX_DB] = [-127, 0]`. Lower byte preserved at the fixed `0x64` AGC preset.
- `set_boost_enabled(bool)` — toggles BSTCTRL2 between esp-adf's `0x0673` (off) and `0x6673` (on). The 10.25 V smart-boost converter stays off by default per the existing comment about the 1 W speaker on the 8 V VBAT rail.
- New public consts: `VOLUME_MIN_DB`, `VOLUME_MAX_DB`.

## Implementation notes
- **Decomposed `HAGCCFG4_DEFAULT`**: split the opaque `0x3064` constant into `HAGCCFG4_AGC_PRESET = 0x64` + `HAGCCFG4_DEFAULT_VOLUME_BYTE = 0x30`, then re-composed via `<<`/`|`. Makes the volume↔AGC coupling explicit and lets `set_volume_db` reuse the AGC preset without a dance. The existing `init_issues_canonical_sequence` test pins the resulting wire bytes to the same `0x30, 0x64` as before.
- **`db_to_volume_byte` is a free `const fn`**: clamping + sign-flip + ×2 lives outside the impl so it's host-testable in isolation and can run at compile time when the input is a const literal.
- **Saturation, not error**: `set_volume_db(50)` clamps to 0 dB rather than returning `Err`. Keeps the API monomorphic on the bus error type and matches the `set_muted` style.

## Tests
- `init_issues_canonical_sequence` (existing) — pins the init wire bytes; unchanged
- `set_volume_db_writes_hagccfg4_with_default_agc` — `-12 dB` → `0x18, 0x64`
- `set_volume_db_default_matches_init_constant` — `-24 dB` → `0x30, 0x64` (matches init default)
- `set_volume_db_clamps_out_of_range` — `+50` → `0 dB`; `-127` → `0xFE, 0x64`
- `set_boost_enabled_toggles_bstctrl2` — `true` → `0x66, 0x73`; `false` → `0x06, 0x73`

9 passing now (was 5).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] Host clippy: `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude stackchan-firmware --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] Firmware clippy: `cd crates/stackchan-firmware && cargo +esp clippy --release -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p aw88298` — 9 pass
- [x] Doc tests pass
- [ ] **Hardware validation**: deferred to the TX-streaming PR. These setters are write-only register pokes that the existing init test format already covers; their actual audible effect can only be checked once TX clocks are flowing.

PR 2D-prep of the audio stack. The next PR (2D proper) will start the I²S TX DMA and call `set_volume_db` + `set_boost_enabled` + `set_muted(false)` in the firmware audio task.

author: nathanhowell
body:
## Summary

- Fixes a 7–22% blob-size regression vs. the C++ reference on smooth float ramps at byte-plane sizes < 8192 bytes (i.e., images up to ~64×64 pixels for f32, smaller for f64).
- Root cause is in `src/fpl/mod.rs:get_best_level`. When the snippet-sampling target produces no snippets (small planes), Rust fell through to `get_best_level_full`, which tested every delta level on the full plane via the entropy estimator. The C++ reference's `getBestLevel2` instead reaches its empty-snippets branch with `comp = 0` for every level and locks in level 0 via its `l == 0` short-circuit.
- For data already flattened by the row+column (predictor 2) cross delta — the typical case for smooth gradients — the byte planes are mostly zeros, and any further delta level *adds* variation rather than removing it. The full-plane entropy estimator misled the level search into picking a non-zero level on these planes.
- Fix: when count == 0 (no snippets), return level 0 directly, matching C++ behavior.

## Empirical impact (lossless f32/f64 vs C++ reference)

Patterns: ramp / constant / random / sinusoidal / step. Sizes: 32×32, 64×64, 128×128, 256×64, 33×31.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| f32 | rust=220725 cpp=225233 (-2.00%, 5W/8L/17T) | rust=219828 cpp=225233 (-2.40%, 6W/5L/19T) |
| f64 | rust=384084 cpp=392285 (-2.09%, 7W/5L/18T) | rust=387161 cpp=392285 (-1.31%, 4W/2L/24T) |

All ramp regressions go from 7–22% larger to TIE or slightly smaller. f64 net shrinks slightly because some random-data *wins* (where Rust's non-zero level happened to beat C++'s level 0) become ties; the wider distribution is clearly more aligned with the reference.

## Investigation provenance

This came out of the empirical comparison in #18 (cpp-byte-identity). The byte-identity test found that f32/f64 lossless blobs differed in size from C++ even though both correctly emit version 6. Hypothesis-testing the entropy-based skip heuristics in `compress_buffer` found those did *not* fire on the test set — total bytes were identical with them removed. Reading the C++ `getBestLevel2` next to ours surfaced the real divergence in the empty-snippets fall-through path.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test` (default features) — all 18 binaries pass
- [x] `cargo test --features cpp-validation` — all 13 binaries pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] Empirical size comparison vs C++ reference across 30 patterns × shapes per dtype (table above)

body:
Restructures the repo from a single-page React app into a DDD-based monorepo split into `backend/` (FastAPI) and `frontend/` (React 19 + Vite).

## Backend — `backend/` (FastAPI + DDD)

Six bounded contexts, each with `domain/ → application/ → infrastructure/ → presentation/` layers:

| Domain | API Prefix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | `/api/v1/auth` | JWT, roles: ADMIN / OWNER / RENTER |
| `owner` | `/api/v1/owners` | Vehicle owners + admin verification |
| `vehicle` | `/api/v1/vehicles` | PENDING → APPROVED / REJECTED / SUSPENDED + document uploads; listing is public |
| `renter` | `/api/v1/renters` | Drivers with CNH + admin verification |
| `rental` | `/api/v1/rentals` | Daily rentals: PENDING → ACTIVE → COMPLETED / CANCELLED; `total_amount` computed on create |
| `finance` | `/api/v1/finance` | Per-vehicle cost ledger (MAINTENANCE / IPVA / FINE / …) + `FinancialSummary` (revenue vs costs) — ADMIN only |

**Shared kernel:** `BaseEntity`, `BaseRepository[T]` (ABC), `CPF` / `Email` / `Money` value objects, async SQLAlchemy engine + `get_db` dependency.

**Infra:** async SQLAlchemy 2.0 + `asyncpg`, Alembic configured with async `env.py` importing all models for autogenerate.

**Security:** patched two vulnerable dependencies:
- `python-jose` `3.3.0` → `3.4.0` (ECDSA algorithm confusion)
- `python-multipart` `0.0.9` → `0.0.22` (arbitrary file write + DoS)

## Frontend — `frontend/`

- Existing React components and landing page moved under `frontend/src/`
- Page scaffolds added: `admin/Dashboard`, `admin/VehicleCosts`, `owner/RegisterVehicle`, `marketplace/VehicleListing`, `renter/Register`
- `src/services/api.ts` — Axios client with JWT ****** redirects to `/login` on 401
- `src/types/index.ts` — TypeScript interfaces mirroring all 6 backend domains
- `vite.config.ts` alias updated to `src/`; `tsconfig.json` paths updated to `"@/*": ["src/*"]`

## Other

- `.gitignore` extended with Python patterns (`__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.env`)
- Root `README.md` replaced with architecture overview and quickstart

body:
## What this PR does

 - Enhance GenericModelConfig fallback to probe nested sub-configs (text_config, llm_config, language_config) commonly found in multimodal models                                                                    
  - Add MoE-aware parameter estimation for unregistered Mixture-of-Experts models                                                                                                                                     
  - Move `estimateMoEParams()` from `deepseek_vl.go` to interface.go as a shared utility   
## Why we need it
 When an unregistered multimodal model (e.g., composite vision-language-audio models) falls back to GenericModelConfig, critical fields like hidden_size, max_position_embeddings, and transformers_version are      
  missed because they are nested under keys like llm_config, text_config, or language_config. This causes:                                                                                                            
  - GetContextLength() → 0                                                                                                                                                                                            
  - GetParameterCount() → 0 (or massively underestimated for MoE models)                                                                                                                                              
  - GetTransformerVersion() → ""                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - HasVision() → false  

## What changes in this PR

 `pkg/hfutil/modelconfig/interface.go`                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - Add MaxSequenceLength, MoE fields (NRoutedExperts, NSharedExperts, MoeIntermediateSize), and hasVisionConfig to GenericModelConfig                                                                                
  - Add probeNestedConfig() helper that extracts fields from nested sub-configs and detects vision_config presence                                                                                                    
  - Override GetContextLength() to fall back to MaxSequenceLength                                                                                                                                                     
  - Override HasVision() to return detected vision config presence                                                                                                                                                    
  - Override GetParameterCount() to use MoE-aware estimation when experts are detected                                                                                                                                
  - Move estimateMoEParams() here from deepseek_vl.go (general-purpose, not DeepSeek-specific)                                                                                                                        
  - Call probeNestedConfig() unconditionally in loadGenericModelConfig() (safe — only fills zero-valued fields)                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  `pkg/hfutil/modelconfig/deepseek_vl.go`                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - Remove estimateMoEParams() (moved to interface.go, same package — no behavior change)                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  `pkg/hfutil/modelconfig/interface_test.go`                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  - TestGenericMultimodalFallback — nested llm_config + vision_config with MoE fields                                                                                                                                 
  - TestGenericMultimodalFallback_TextConfig — text_config variant                                                                                                                                                    
  - TestGenericMultimodalFallback_LanguageConfig — language_config variant                                                                                                                                            
  - TestGenericMoEFallback — flat MoE config with num_local_experts field name variant                                                                                                                                
  - TestGenericContextLengthMaxSequenceLength — max_sequence_length fallback           

Fixes #

## Summary

Consolidates the v0.8.0-alpha.1 primitives sprint for core/go. RFC-cited new primitives unblock banned-import purges across the workspace.

## Headline changes

- `sync.Pool` — 3 workspace hits, deferred until consumer count exceeds 10

author: graphcs
body:
## Summary

Generated letters are markdown stored on the document row, but there's no way to export them as a PDF for filing or sharing — the user has to copy/paste into Word and reformat. Edits also have no history, so a bad save permanently overwrites a good draft. This PR adds PDF export, per-edit version snapshots with restore, validates document writes, and gives the dashboard a coherent view of generation/OCR status while content is in flight.

## Changes

- New `GET /api/documents/[id]/pdf` renders letter documents as PDF via `lib/pdf/` (React-PDF Document + a markdown-to-PDF converter built on `unified` / `remark-parse`). Honors `?mode=inline` vs `attachment` content-disposition.
- New `POST /api/documents/[id]/versions/[versionId]/restore`. Every `PUT /api/documents/[id]` also creates a `document_versions` row, so any write can be rolled back. Document writes are validated by `documentUpdateSchema`.
- Document comments POST is validated by `commentSchema` (1–5000 chars; rejects whitespace-only).
- `doc-viewer` gains a `deriveStatus()` that surfaces `generation_status` states (animated loader for `generating`, retry CTA for `failed`) so the UI doesn't render a half-empty doc as "ready".
- `documents-list` integrates an upload sheet, `StatusDot` reads `generation_status` / `ocr_status`, and uploads are gated to the case's current stage.
- New `.letter-prose` CSS class set in `globals.css` (Times-aware spacing, `pre-wrap` whitespace, list/blockquote/code styles) for letter rendering on the dashboard and PDF preview.
- Add `@react-pdf/renderer` dependency.
- Add `commentSchema` to `lib/validations.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] Open a generated letter on the dashboard — `/api/documents/[id]/pdf` returns a valid PDF (open inline; download as attachment)
- [x] Edit a document, save → a new `document_versions` row exists with the prior content; hit `POST /restore` for an old version → document content reverts and a new version row is added (so restore is itself a versioned change)
- [x] Submit `PUT /api/documents/[id]` with neither `content` nor `status` → 400 ("Nothing to update")
- [x] Submit a comment of `"   "` (whitespace) → 400; submit valid comment → posted
- [x] On the dashboard while a doc is `generating`, the doc-viewer shows the spinner; when it transitions to `failed`, retry CTA renders
- [x] Upload a document for a stage other than the current stage → blocked / hidden by the upload gate

author: brandonkindred
body:
Closes #347.

## Problem

`POST /api/persona-testing/job/{id}/resume` (added in #310) re-dispatches `run_workflow` from the very beginning. For a `failed` run that died in Phase 3 (SE-team build), this re-runs spec generation (LLM call) and product analysis (~4h poll loop) even though `spec_content`, `analysis_job_id`, and `repo_path` are already on the `user_agent_founder_runs` row.

## Change

`run_workflow` now reads the run row at entry and skips phases whose checkpoint columns are populated:

| `spec_content` | `analysis_job_id` | `repo_path` | `se_job_id` | What happens on resume |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ∅ | ∅ | ∅ | ∅ | All three phases run (regression baseline) |
| ✓ | ∅ | ∅ | ∅ | Skip Phase 1; submit + poll Phase 2; submit + poll Phase 3 |
| ✓ | ✓ | ∅ | ∅ | Skip Phase 1; **poll only** Phase 2 against existing analysis job; submit + poll Phase 3 |
| ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ∅ | Skip Phases 1 & 2; submit + poll Phase 3 |
| ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Skip Phases 1 & 2; **poll only** Phase 3 against existing SE job |

Achieved by:

- Adding an `existing_job_id` kwarg to `_run_product_analysis` and `_run_se_team` (`backend/agents/user_agent_founder/orchestrator.py`). When supplied, each function bypasses its submit block and enters the poll loop with the existing job id.
- Wrapping `run_workflow`'s phase calls in `if run.<checkpoint>: skip` guards using the existing `FounderRunStore.get_run` API.

No schema, API, or UI changes — `POST /job/{id}/resume` already triggers re-dispatch; the orchestrator just gets smarter about what to skip.

## Tests

New `backend/agents/user_agent_founder/tests/test_orchestrator_resume.py` (6 cases) using a stubbed `httpx.Client` and an in-memory `FakeFounderStore` to assert which network calls fire on each resume scenario.

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest agents/user_agent_founder/tests/
============================== 60 passed in 3.68s ==============================
```

Lint clean on the two modified files.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest agents/user_agent_founder/tests/test_orchestrator_resume.py` — 6 passed
- [x] `pytest agents/user_agent_founder/tests/` — 60 passed (no regressions)
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on modified files
- [ ] Manual smoke (Postgres up, no Temporal):
  1. Start a Testing Personas run; let it pass Phase 1 + Phase 2; kill the API mid-Phase-3 polling.
  2. Restart the API; click Resume on the row.
  3. Confirm logs show `Resuming run … past Phase 2 (analysis already complete)` and the next request is a `GET /api/software-engineering/run-team/{se_job_id}` against the same SE job, not a `POST /run-team`.

## Out of scope

- Pause (closed in #319 as `not_planned`).
- Mid-phase resume tokens — only phase boundaries are short-circuited.
- Backfilling resume short-circuit to blogging / investment / other teams.

author: bytkim
body:
# Summary
- `CreateSandboxRequest.resourceLimits.gpu` is documented in the schema and honored by the Docker runtime (#775), but the Kubernetes runtime silently dropped it. `_build_main_container` in `services/k8s/provider_common.py` passed the raw `resource_limits` dict straight into `V1ResourceRequirements.limits` and `.requests`, so a `gpu` key flowed through unchanged. Kubernetes treats `gpu` as an unknown extended resource — the NVIDIA device plugin never sees the request, and pods schedule with no GPU. Both `AgentSandboxProvider` and `BatchSandboxProvider` route through this single chokepoint, so both K8s providers were affected.
- Adds `_translate_resource_limits_for_k8s` in `provider_common.py` that reuses the existing `parse_gpu_request` from `services/helpers.py`, translates the portable `gpu` key to the canonical `nvidia.com/gpu` extended-resource name, and pops the raw `gpu` key so it cannot leak onto the pod as an unknown resource. Hardcoding `nvidia.com/gpu` mirrors the NVIDIA-only scope of #775 (Docker `DeviceRequest capabilities=[["gpu"]]`); other vendor keys (`amd.com/gpu`, `gpu.intel.com/i915`) can be a follow-up.
- Rejects the `"all"` sentinel with `HTTP 400` rather than silently dropping it. Docker accepts `"all"` (unbounded `DeviceRequest`), but Kubernetes extended resources require an integer count, and silent fallback would mask the misconfiguration. Mirrors #775's "failures remain visible rather than silent" principle.
- Closes #781.

**Scope note:** The Kubernetes Windows profile path (`apply_windows_profile_overrides`) already strips the entire resources block via `pop("resources", None)`, so GPU on Windows is still implicitly suppressed on the outer pod — no separate change is needed there.

**Failure mode:** On clusters without the NVIDIA device plugin, the pod will surface a clear scheduling failure (Pod stays in `Pending` with `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu`), so GPU request failures remain visible rather than silent.

# Testing
- [ ] Not run (explain why)
- [x] Unit tests
- [ ] Integration tests (see note below)
- [ ] e2e / manual verification

Focused checks from `server/AGENTS.md`:

```
uv run ruff check

author: 392fyc
body:
## Summary

Add support for a new optional env var `CLAUDE_HANDOFF_AUTO_LAUNCH_FLAGS` that gets injected between `claude` and the `--` sentinel in all three Step 5 auto-launch commands (Windows wt, tmux new-window, tmux new-session).

When the env var is unset, expansion is empty (`${CLAUDE_HANDOFF_AUTO_LAUNCH_FLAGS:-}`) and behavior is identical to before — fully backward compatible.

## Why

Auto-launched handoff sessions currently inherit nothing beyond the SHORT_PROMPT bootstrap message. Users running with persistent flags like Anthropic Channels (`--channels server:foo --dangerously-load-development-channels`) had to manually re-launch each handoff session to keep the flags in effect.

This change lets users set the env var once in `~/.claude/settings.json` env block and have all handoff-spawned sessions inherit the flags transparently.

Use case that motivated this: a personal Telegram channel server that needs `--channels server:mercury-telegram --dangerously-load-development-channels` on every session including auto-spawned ones. The mechanism is **generic** — not coupled to any specific channel, transport, or feature.

## Diff

3 launch lines + 1 documentation paragraph in `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`. 14 insertions, 3 deletions.

```diff
-wt -w 0 nt --title "Handoff" -d "<cwd>" -- claude -- "$SHORT_PROMPT"
+wt -w 0 nt --title "Handoff" -d "<cwd>" -- claude ${CLAUDE_HANDOFF_AUTO_LAUNCH_FLAGS:-} -- "$SHORT_PROMPT"

-tmux new-window -n handoff "claude -- '$SHORT_PROMPT'"
+tmux new-window -n handoff "claude ${CLAUDE_HANDOFF_AUTO_LAUNCH_FLAGS:-} -- '$SHORT_PROMPT'"

-tmux new-session -d -s handoff "claude -- '$SHORT_PROMPT'"
+tmux new-session -d -s handoff "claude ${CLAUDE_HANDOFF_AUTO_LAUNCH_FLAGS:-} -- '$SHORT_PROMPT'"
```

Plus a documentation paragraph above the launch commands explaining the env var and its substitution semantics.

## Backward compat

`${CLAUDE_HANDOFF_AUTO_LAUNCH_FLAGS:-}` evaluates to empty string when env var is unset (POSIX `:-` default). Existing users see no behavior change.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual: skill source diff reviewed — only adds env var injection between `claude` and `--`
- [x] Manual: documentation paragraph clearly explains the substitution mechanism
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm `${VAR:-}` substitution behaves identically across Windows wt (MSYS2 bash) + tmux on macOS/Linux
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm no regression for users who do not set the env var

## Notes

- No new dependencies
- No frontmatter / version bump (skill has no version field)
- Bash form only — Python wrapper / other shells unaffected (those paths don't shell-out)

body:
🥕 *(spoilers below — close this if you want to discover it organically!)*

## The cheat
Enter `↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A` on the keyboard anywhere in the game to toggle **Golden Rabbit Mode**:
- Gold tint applied to the rabbit body / head / limbs (eyes + nose stay normal)
- 1.5× score multiplier on every carrot pickup
- Subtle ★ indicator on the main menu when active
- 3.5s on-screen toast with fade-out when toggled, and a menu-click chime

## Architecture
- `Core.EasterEggs`: static, PlayerPrefs-backed flag store + score-bonus helper + change event.
- `Core.KonamiCodeDetector`: DontDestroyOnLoad singleton auto-spawned via `RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod` so the cheat is discoverable in any scene. New Input System. Timing-tolerant (4 s gap resets), ignores non-sequence keys.
- `ScoreManager.AddScore`: multiplies gained points by `EasterEggs.ScoreBonusMultiplier` (1f when off → zero overhead).
- `RabbitController.ApplyEasterEggVisuals`: clones the shared Rabbit_Mat once, tints it, and assigns it to every renderer that used the original. Tracked + destroyed in OnDestroy so there's no material leak.
- `MainMenuUI`: live indicator synced via `OnGoldenRabbitChanged`.

## Robustness
- Setter no-ops on identical writes; saves immediately so the choice survives hard exits.
- All cross-system reads are lazy / event-driven — no hard wiring.
- Toast uses unscaled time so it survives `Time.timeScale = 0` pause.

Budget: full PRO implementation, no shortcuts.

## Summary

- Multi-file model: \`tabs[]\` + \`activeTabId\` replaces the single-document state. Each tab has its own \`path\`, \`content\`, \`savedContent\`, \`cursorPosition\`, \`scrollPosition\`, and \`editorMode\`. Opening a path that's already open switches to its tab instead of duplicating it.
- New \`TabBar\` component above the editor: filename + dirty/close indicator (● vs ×), drag-and-drop reorder, middle-click close, horizontal overflow scroll, active-tab highlight.
- Per-tab cursor + scroll restoration: \`SourceEditor\` exposes get/set for both. Switching tabs captures the outgoing tab's position and restores the incoming one's after Monaco picks up the new content.
- Shortcuts:
  - \`Cmd/Ctrl+W\` closes the active tab (with the dirty prompt); last close drops back to the welcome screen. With no tabs, \`Cmd/Ctrl+W\` closes the window.
  - \`Ctrl+Tab\` / \`Ctrl+Shift+Tab\` cycle next/previous tabs (\`Cmd+Tab\` is reserved by macOS for app switching, so we follow VS Code and use \`Ctrl\` on all platforms).
- Window-close + multi-dirty: main intercepts close based on the renderer-mirrored \`dirtyCount\`. On \"Save All\" main asks the renderer to save every dirty tab via a request/response IPC; close only proceeds when all writes succeed. Drops the old main-side cached content / \`saveCachedFile\` path now that the renderer drives every save.

This PR implements a series of disciplined micro-adjustments to improve consistency, accessibility, and API correctness across the core foundation components. 

Key changes include:
1. **Consolidated Form Utilities**: Relocated input type definitions and validation logic to a central utility for better organization.
2. **Enhanced Property Reflection**: Enabled `reflect: true` for standard native attributes across all form components. This ensures that the DOM state matches the property state, which is critical for CSS targetability and accessibility tools.
3. **API Tightening**: Added missing standard properties like `name` to `sp-fieldset` and normalized the `label` property implementation in checkbox and radio components.
4. **Type Safety Improvements**: Adjusted optional property types to properly handle `undefined`, ensuring robust type declaration generation under strict TypeScript settings.
5. **Standardized Labeling**: Improved attribute reflection for labeling primitives.

These changes strengthen the component layer while strictly adhering to the project's architectural boundaries and rendering strategy.

author: henrik-me
body:
## Summary

Fixes the "infinite retry" symptom on localhost when developers run `docker compose up --force-recreate` on the mssql stack.

## Root cause

Caddy auto-generates a self-signed local CA on first start and stores it under `/data/caddy/pki/`. Without a persistent volume mount, every container recreate wipes this directory and Caddy generates a brand-new CA. The browser still trusts the **old** CA (now gone), so all subsequent requests fail with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`.

Top-level navigations show the cert warning so users can re-trust. But **Service Worker `fetch()` calls cannot prompt for cert acceptance** — they fail silently. Our SW (`public/sw.js:78-86`) catches the throw and returns a synthetic 503, which the SPA cannot distinguish from a real server cold-start failure. The user sees an "infinite retry" banner with no clue that it's actually a TLS issue.

## Fix

Add `caddy-data:/data` and `caddy-config:/config` named volumes to the caddy service in `docker-compose.mssql.yml`.

## Verification

```
$ sha256sum /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt   # before recreate
a86acf41...
$ docker compose -f docker-compose.mssql.yml up -d --force-recreate caddy
$ sha256sum /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt   # after recreate
a86acf41...   # identical
```

Lint clean. 542/542 tests pass (no test changes; fix is purely compose config).

## Related

Companion to CS53-14 (still pending): make the SW's catch path return a distinguishable error so this class of issue is self-diagnosing rather than masquerading as a server cold-start retry loop.

body:
# Logic-Lens v0.4.2 — Cost-Conscious Default + Release Notes i18n

## TL;DR

A small housekeeping patch. Two user-facing changes:

1. **`scripts/run-trigger-evals.sh` now defaults to `claude-sonnet-4-6`** instead of `claude-opus-4-7`. Sonnet 4.6 handles the run_loop description-optimization workflow at roughly 5× lower cost; upgrade to opus only if you observe the proposals failing to improve test scores.
2. **`.github/RELEASE-NOTES-v0.4.x.md` rewritten in English** (v0.4.0 and v0.4.1 included). GitHub Release bodies and titles updated too. Makes the project more accessible to an international audience.

No code, SKILL.md, guide, or evaluation logic changes.

## 🎯 Changes

### Default model for trigger optimization

`scripts/run-trigger-evals.sh`:

```bash
# Before (v0.4.1):
MODEL="${MODEL:-claude-opus-4-7}"

# After (v0.4.2):
MODEL="${MODEL:-claude-sonnet-4-6}"
```

Reasoning: `run_loop.py` uses one model for two distinct jobs — bulk per-query evaluation (cheap, many calls) and the extended-thinking description-proposal step (fewer calls, more demanding). Since it's a single `--model` flag, the practical default should minimize cost. Sonnet 4.6 has produced usable proposals in our POC runs; opus remains available via `MODEL=claude-opus-4-7 bash scripts/run-trigger-evals.sh` for cases where proposal quality matters more than spend.

`scripts/README.md` updated with the new default + override guidance.

### Release notes internationalization

- `.github/RELEASE-NOTES-v0.4.0.md` — rewritten end-to-end in English while preserving all section structure, tables, and the English/Chinese header-map example (the one place Chinese is **meaningful content**, not just prose style).

- GitHub Release titles and bodies updated via `gh release edit` to match.
- `CHANGELOG.md` remains bilingual (internal-facing); only the release-facing notes moved to English.

None.

### Motivation
- Remove heuristic recovery, manual boosts, and recovery locks so stability is mathematically enforced only by L2 projection onto the constrained simplex. 
- Ensure the canonical invariant `C + R + S = 1` with `C,R,S ≥ 0.05` is enforced on every update path. 
- Expose raw vs governed outputs and build a research-grade console to visualize simplex state, projection activity, ADV entropy, and run SSS-50 stress tests. 

### Description
- Kernel: removed `is_recovering` and recovery-gating logic and removed manual +0.02 boost paths in `transduce`; `check_stability` no longer halts execution and relies on projection only. 
- Projection enforcement: `project_to_simplex` is now invoked unconditionally after transduction, after governor (ADV) update, before persistence/settlement, and again before return; the projection returns whether it changed state and `receipt["safety_projection_triggered"]` is updated accordingly. 
- Invariant guard & traces: added a pre-return guard that re-applies projection if `abs(sum(state) - 1.0) > 1e-6` or `min(state.values()) < 0.05`, and added debug traces `print("RAW STATE:", raw_state)` and `print("PROJECTED STATE:", self.state)`. 
- API & UI: preserved the `/praxis/run` decomposition fields (`raw_response`, `governed_response`, `state`, `receipt`) and set `app/static/SIA_Dashboard_v2.html` as the default frontend; added `SIA_Dashboard_v2.html` implementing response decomposition, simplex triangle canvas (animated history), stability/CBF badges, ADV entropy waveform, prompt threat estimator, and an SSS-50 test panel/table. 
- Tests: updated `tests/test_kernel.py` cleanup to remove references to the removed `is_recovering` field.

body:
## Summary
Five corrections in `README.md` that drifted between 0.1.2 and 0.3.1:

- **Architecture diagram** — described MLX as prebuilt and fetched from GitHub. That's no longer accurate for either path: hex consumers get MLX statically linked into `libemily` inside the precompiled NIF tarball, and contributor source builds clone MLX via a Mix git dep and cmake-build it locally.
- **Installation example** pinned `~> 0.1.0`; bumped to `~> 0.3`.
- **Default `$EMILY_CACHE`** was shown as `~/Library/Caches/emily`; macOS now uses `DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR` (Linux falls back to XDG).
- **Hex-consumer build section** claimed checksums are baked into `@nif_checksums` in `mix.exs`; they aren't — the consumer fetches a `.sha256` sidecar alongside each tarball at compile time, and the cached tarball is re-verified against the freshly-fetched sidecar on every compile.
- **JIT-variant section** referenced `:no_jit`; the actual default variant atom is `:aot`.

## Test plan
- [x] `mix precommit` (compile, credo, 454 tests) green
- [x] `grep -nE "~> 0\.1|Library/Caches/emily|nif_checksums|:no_jit" README.md` returns nothing

author: octo-patch
body:
Fixes #338

## Problem

Images extracted from PDFs by `pdf_extractor_poc.py` were saved to
`assets/images/` correctly, but never referenced in the generated
markdown files. The `_generate_reference_file` method in `pdf_scraper.py`
checked for `page["images"]` (a legacy format expecting raw `data` bytes),
while the extractor stores images as `page["extracted_images"]` with
`filename` and `path` keys — images already written to disk.

## Solution

Added a new block in `_generate_reference_file` that handles the
`extracted_images` format: it writes `![filename](../assets/images/filename)`
markdown references for each image. The legacy `images` format (with raw
binary data) is preserved as a fallback via `elif` for backward compatibility.

## Testing

- Added `test_extracted_images_references_in_markdown` to `TestImageHandling`
  which verifies the new format produces correct `![...]()` references
- All 6 existing `TestImageHandling` tests continue to pass

author: tmatens
body:
## Summary

PR #143 fixed the registry alias and added a `vex-author` override for Docker Scout, but Scout **still flagged all three pip CVEs** on the post-merge `scout-scan.yml` dispatch ([run 24921123739](https://github.com/tmatens/compose-lint/actions/runs/24921123739/job/72982651768) on commit `5abd036`). Scout logged `Loaded 1 VEX document` — the document loaded but no statement matched. This PR addresses the two suspect axes simultaneously so the next dispatch is conclusive.

## Changes

- **Multi-identifier products.** Every VEX statement now ships two `products[]` entries: the existing `pkg:oci/compose-lint?repository_url=index.docker.io/composelint/compose-lint` form (Trivy and Grype accept this) plus a bare `pkg:docker/composelint/compose-lint` form, which is the shape [Docker Scout's own "Create exceptions" docs page](https://docs.docker.com/scout/how-tos/create-exceptions-vex/) uses.
- **Permissive `vex-author: .*`** on every `docker/scout-action` step (`scout-scan.yml` × 2, `publish.yml` × 1). PR #143's first override (`<.*@gmail\.com>`, mirroring Scout's bracket-anchored default `<.*@docker.com>`) was silently dropped — Scout appears to use full-string regex match rather than substring, so the bracket-anchored shape did not match the full author string `Todd Matens <tmatens@gmail.com>`. `.*` accepts any author; safe because the document in CI comes from `actions/checkout` and is also cosign-attested to the image manifest at release time.
- VEX `version` bumped 2 → 3, `timestamp` refreshed.
- ADR-012 revised to record the empirical evidence from #143 and the multi-identifier rationale. Status changed to "Accepted (revised after PR #143's first attempt did not suppress on Scout)".
- CHANGELOG updated under `[Unreleased]`.

## Why two PURL types

The PURL spec registers both `pkg:oci/` and `pkg:docker/` types for the same artifact class, and scanners disagree on which they normalise to. Trivy/Grype docs use the `pkg:oci/` form; Scout's exception docs use the `pkg:docker/` form. OpenVEX's spec explicitly invites multi-identifier products for exactly this case: "list as many software identifiers as possible to help VEX processors when matching the product." Twelve extra lines of JSON buys us both scanners matching without picking a winner in a disagreement that has no winner.

## Verification

- **Trivy 0.70.0** with the new multi-identifier doc against `composelint/compose-lint:latest`: zero pip CVEs (`pip-25.1.1.dist-info/METADATA: 0`). Unchanged from PR #143.
- **Scout** verification deferred to the post-merge `scout-scan.yml` dispatch on `main`. The outcome we're watching for is `Loaded 1 VEX document` → CVE-2025-8869, CVE-2026-1703, CVE-2026-3219 all absent from the per-severity output, and alerts #82/#83/#84 transitioning to closed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/`, `pytest` — all pass locally (310 tests).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR.
- [ ] After merge, dispatch `Docker Scout (scheduled)` from the Actions tab. Target signal: per-severity output lists 0 vulnerabilities from pip.
- [ ] `docker-scout-scheduled` SARIF upload reports `results_count: 0` for the resulting commit.
- [ ] Alerts #82/#83/#84 auto-close (if not, dismiss as "won't fix - VEX'd" linking ADR-012).
- [ ] If Scout **still** flags the CVEs: the next escalation is digest qualification (add a third `products[]` entry `pkg:oci/compose-lint@sha256:<index-digest>?repository_url=...`), with a substitution step in `publish.yml`. Not doing it in this PR because it adds release-pipeline complexity only justified if the static multi-identifier form is proven insufficient.

Reopens the work tracked by #139 (closed by #143) since the suppression is still not effective on Scout.

author: eterna2
body:
## Summary

Closes #79

This PR implements the full Data Vault expansion requested in Issue #79:

### VaultCodec — Encryption & Compression Pipeline
- Composable codec applied before data enters the cache
- Compression (optional): `ZlibCompressor`, `GzipCompressor` (stdlib); `LZ4Compressor` (`kest[lz4]`), `ZstdCompressor` (`kest[zstd]`)
- Encryption (optional): `AES256GCMEncryptor` (AES-256-GCM, random nonce per call), `FernetEncryptor`
- Pipeline order: pickle → compress → encrypt; fully reversible on unseal
- `HandleVault(codec=VaultCodec(...)))` — no-op when codec is not set

### Pluggable Cache Backends (5 implementations)
| Backend | Extra | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SQLiteCache` | stdlib | ACID, in-memory or persistent, thread-safe |
| `LMDBCache` | `kest[lmdb]` | Memory-mapped B+tree, fastest embedded reads |
| `CachetoolsCache` | `kest[cachetools]` | Pure-Python LRU/TTL cache |
| `RedisCache` | `kest[redis]` | RESP-protocol; also KeyDB-compatible |
| `ValkeyCache` | `kest[valkey]` | Valkey open-source RESP fork |

### Vault Service Transports (all stdlib)
- `VaultHTTPServer` — REST/JSON (HTTP); endpoints: POST /handles, POST /handles/{id}/unseal, DELETE /handles/{id}, GET /handles/{id}/safe_view
- `VaultRPCServer` — XML-RPC; faults mapped to typed vault errors
- `VaultSocketServer` — JSON-RPC 2.0 over TCP or Unix socket; 4-byte length-framing
- `VaultClient` — unified factory: `.http()`, `.rpc()`, `.socket()`

### Testing
- 344 unit tests passing (9 skipped: optional deps not installed in CI)
- SQLite thread-safety fixed (shared connection + `threading.Lock` replacing per-thread `threading.local`)
- Redis/Valkey tests use `fakeredis` (no live server required)

### Documentation
- README: new §5a–5d covering codec, backends, transports, and `@kest_verified` integration
- CHANGELOG: complete 0.4.0 entry for all new vault features

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The deployment healthcheck fails because the `ForceHttps` middleware 301-redirects all plain HTTP requests to HTTPS, including Railway's internal healthcheck requests to `/up`. Railway sends healthchecks over plain HTTP without an `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` header, so `$request->secure()` returns false and every healthcheck attempt gets a 301 instead of the expected 200.

## Solution

Added an early return in `ForceHttps::handle()` that bypasses the HTTPS redirect when the request path is `up`. This allows Railway's internal healthcheck to reach the `/up` route handler and receive a 200 response, while all other requests continue to be redirected to HTTPS as before.

### Changes
- **Modified** `app/Http/Middleware/ForceHttps.php`

- **Deployment**: [#fca1ff](https://railway.com/project/8e492dbb-faa1-4257-97fd-7a70e166e79b/environment/dd1e8037-6c0a-46a5-a79d-953a9e23ebf2/deployment/fca1ff44-7bf3-41ee-a1a6-c22a5bbde225)
