author: mikereagan24-sketch
body:
Kalshi (and presumably other books) leaves the last numeric price in the Unabated feed even after pulling a contract from active trading. The feed flags this state explicitly with overrideType='disabled' and includePeg=false on the bt entry. Our isSaneTotal / isSaneTotalJuice / isSaneML guards check numeric ranges only — they accept stale prices on disabled contracts as if they were live.

Concrete observed case: DET@CIN on 2026-04-24, Kalshi bt3 has both sides at 8.5 (+127/-156) with overrideType='disabled' on each. Sane on every numeric guard but stale — Kalshi's site shows the contract unavailable and the rest of the market is on lines 9.0-9.5. PR #9 correctly flagged the line divergence (8.5 vs sporttrade 9.5) but still propagated the bad Kalshi price to the model's edge calc input.

Fix: new isLiveContract(bt) helper, applied as a precondition at every bt selection site:
  - bt1 ML primary waterfall (TOTAL_SOURCES priority)
  - bt1 ML last-ditch any-source sweep
  - bt1 ML xcheck waterfall (XCHECK_SOURCES)
  - bt3 totals primary waterfall (TOTAL_SOURCES priority)
  - bt3 totals primary fallback any-source sweep
  - bt3 totals xcheck waterfall (XCHECK_TOTAL_SOURCES)

Helper is tight: rejects null/undefined bt, overrideType='disabled', or includePeg=false. Missing fields default to live (preserves prior behavior for sources that don't emit these flags).

Log message clarity: distinguish 'rejected disabled' (the contract is flagged off) from 'skipping one-sided' (the source posted only one side of the market) in ML log lines so future log readers can tell which mechanism rejected a source. Totals waterfall logs prefix 'rejected disabled total contract' for greppability.

Local verification — all 5 spec checklist items pass:

  Tests 1-3 (synthetic isLiveContract behavior):
    - both flags bad → rejected ✓
    - includePeg=false only → rejected ✓
    - overrideType=disabled only → rejected ✓
    - both healthy / missing flags / null bt → expected outcomes ✓

  Test 4 (live run on 2026-04-24, 14 games):
    Distribution before / after this fix:
      Before: 14 / 14 had kalshi as primary on at least the 2 disabled games (det-cin, nyy-hou) — both stored Kalshi's stale price. After:  10 / 14 still kalshi primary (live contracts, no regression), 1 moved to novig (det-cin: 11.5 from novig — note: novig itself has a suspicious 11.5 line for an MLB game; not this PR's concern), 3 on polymarket (nyy-hou is the new fallthrough from disabled kalshi bt3; chc-lad and was-cws were on polymarket already from prior PRs). Rejection log on this run shows 5 distinct events: 2 totals rejections (det-cin, nyy-hou — both legitimately disabled per overrideType='disabled' on both sides), and 3 ML one-sided skips (laa-kc / mia-sf / min-tb — Kalshi posted only home side). The ML one-sided cases were already being skipped by prior code; this PR just gives them clearer log messages. Spot-checks confirmed bos-bal, sea-stl, col-nym, phi-atl all still resolve to live Kalshi primary.

  Test 5 (ML side regression check on DET@CIN):
    Kalshi bt1 has overrideType=null / includePeg=true on this game
    (only bt3 is disabled), so the ML waterfall correctly accepts
    Kalshi for det-cin (-117/-104). Flag reason still correctly cites
    'Kalshi vs polymarket divergence' on the ML side — Polymarket's
    ML for this game is a thin-book outlier (-393/+365). No ML
    regression.

author: fmguerreiro
body:
Consume the 0.61.0 fork release at https://github.com/fmguerreiro/datafusion-sqlparser-rs/releases/tag/v0.61.0.

## Why this version

`pgmold-sqlparser 0.61.0` adds the AST capabilities pgmold-273 needs to retire the regex passes for COMMENT ON, GRANT/REVOKE on TYPE/DOMAIN, and (eventually) ALTER TYPE attribute ops + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES.

New surface available in this version:
- `GrantObjects::{Types, Domains}` — for `GRANT ON TYPE/DOMAIN`.
- `CommentObject::{Trigger, Aggregate, Policy}` plus `Statement::Comment` carrying `arguments: Option<Vec<DataType>>` and `relation: Option<ObjectName>`; `parse_literal_string` accepts dollar-quoted bodies.
- `AlterTypeOperation::{OwnerTo, SetSchema, *Attribute}` (six new variants).
- `Statement::AlterDefaultPrivileges` with `[FOR ROLE …] [IN SCHEMA …] {GRANT|REVOKE} <body>`.
- Pre-existing `Grantee::fmt` `"PUBLIC "` trailing-space bug fixed.

## Compile fallout to expect

Three sites in pgmold pattern-match `Statement::Comment` and `AlterTableOperation` exhaustively. They already use `..` or explicit ignore arms, so the field/variant additions should not break compilation. CI will confirm.

This bump is a precondition for pgmold-273 (regex → AST migration of `src/parser/comments.rs`).

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an internal "member notes" storage and simple deal threads system so admins and investors can save notes and post/reply to deal requests while supporting offline/local-first usage. 
- Allow UI users to view shared notes inline with lender listings and enable admins to create, update, delete, and sync notes to a Google Sheets-backed Web App. 

### Description
- Added a new Google Apps Script backend `apps_script_member_notes.gs` that exposes `member_notes` and `deal_threads` resources with `GET`/`POST` handlers, health-check support, and helper functions including `setupAllSheets_` and `getSpreadsheet_`; it supports upsert/delete for notes and create/reply for threads. 
- Extended `index.html` with admin and threads UI, styles, and client logic for local-first notes and threads including local storage keys, `notesURL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` constants, JSONP/fetch helpers (`jsonpFetch`), pending-op queueing (`pendingOps`), flush/verify flows, and functions to create/reply to threads. 
- Integrated notes display into the main lender list (`memberNotes` lookups, `noteId`, `draw`) and added UI controls to open the Admin Portal and Deal Threads modal with password-gated edits and local/remote sync behavior. 
- Minor data updates in the lender arrays and dedup/sort logic remain intact and new server/client error/timeout handling paths were added for resilience. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.

author: cvzwkk
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a playable mission-control layer on top of the Genesis visualization to model exploration and its effects on civilization progress.
- Represent crew and missions explicitly so agency workflows (recruit, train, assign, retire) can influence outcomes and resources.
- Visualize active missions in the Solar System and feed mission outcomes back into `science/tech/resources/confidence` and mapping progress.

### Description
- Replaced the original particle-only Genesis UI with a mission-control interface in `assets/docs/knowledges/theories/Gravifluid/std1/index.html` including UI panels for agency, mission planning, crew roster, mission queue, and progress trackers.
- Added models `Astronaut` and `Mission` plus a `SpaceAgencyManager` with `recruit`, `train`, `assign`, and `retire` behaviors and crew state fields (`skills`, `health`, `assignedMissionId`, `status`).
- Introduced mission catalog entries (`orbital_station`, `lunar_flyby_base`, `mars_transit_colony`, `asteroid_survey`) and a `computeMissionSuccessProbability` function that combines `tech`, crew skill and `reliability` against mission `risk` to compute `P(success)`.
- Reworked the Three.js scene into a Solar System view and implemented animated transfer arcs with `createTransferArc` (quadratic Bézier curves) and moving craft meshes that resolve missions on arrival and update civilization state and crew health.

### Testing
- Ran a content validation script to verify presence of required constructs: `class Astronaut`, `class Mission`, `class SpaceAgencyManager`, mission type keys, `computeMissionSuccessProbability`, `createTransferArc`, and civilization state fields; the check returned no missing items.
- Committed the change with `git commit` which recorded one modified file (`assets/docs/knowledges/theories/Gravifluid/std1/index.html`) successfully.

author: andreydeveloper84
body:
## Что внутри

Один коммит — `6e34f7a`. Hot fix давнего бага.

### Проблема
`notifications/send_notification_telegram` НЕ использовал HTTP-прокси, в отличие от `agents/telegram.py::send_telegram`. На проде в РФ `api.telegram.org` недоступен напрямую — ВСЕ Telegram-уведомления молча падали с `Network is unreachable`, ошибка логировалась WARNING'ом но возвращалось `True` (caller не узнавал что доставки не было).

### Affects
ВСЕ entry-точки уведомлений (без Telegram много месяцев):
- `api_wizard_booking` (заявки с формы-мастера)
- `api_bundle_request`
- `api_certificate_request`
- `payments.views.yookassa_webhook` (оплата сертификатов)
- `payments.tasks.fulfill_*`
- `maxbot/handlers/booking.py::_notify_bot_booking` (наши свежие — заявки из MAX-бота)

### Решение
Используем существующий паттерн из `agents/telegram.py`:
- `TELEGRAM_PROXY` env (приоритет) → `OPENAI_PROXY` (fallback) → `None`
- Передаётся в `requests.post(..., proxies={'https': proxy_url})`
- `timeout` 5s → 10s (прокси добавляет latency)
- БОНУС: возвращаем `r.ok` вместо безусловного `True` — caller знает реально ли доставлено

## Тесты
- **787 passed, 0 регрессий** (+4 новых теста на прокси-логику + 1 правка существующего)

## Smoke на проде (до merge)
```
OPENAI_PROXY=http://2K7QXp:58G7dL@163.198.138.200:8000  ← задан
agents/telegram.py.send_telegram через прокси: HTTP 200 ✓
```
Прокси работает, `notifications/` подхватит тот же `OPENAI_PROXY` через fallback.

## Test plan (после deploy + restart maxbot)
- [ ] `sudo systemctl restart formula-tela-maxbot` (нужен пароль)
- [ ] Запиши тест-заявку через MAX-бот → Telegram-уведомление **должно прийти**
- [ ] Запиши через wizard на сайте — тот же эффект
- [ ] `journalctl -u formula-tela-maxbot | grep Telegram` — больше нет «Network is unreachable» / «Failed to establish a new connection»

## Risk
- **Low** — single function, fallback на `None` если proxy не задан (= прежнее поведение для dev/CI без прокси)
- Если прокси умрёт — Telegram молча не доставит, но bot/wizard продолжат работать (уведомление НЕ блокирует основной flow)

author: brynna-s
body:
## Summary

Bundled set of three changes from the 2026-04-19 review.

**1. Category display → dropdown.** The 9-pill NODE CATEGORIES grid that
lived inside DomainSelector's collapsible DATA LAYERS section is gone.
Categories are now exposed via a compact `CategoryFilterDropdown` that
appears in HeaderBar after a domain is selected — same multi-select
semantics on `visibleCategories`, just in a place users can reach
without re-opening the launch menu.

**2. Fix cross-domain cascade paths.** `useFilteredGraph` had a
hardcoded auto-include list `["Geopolitical", "Energy Grid"]` for
cross-domain connectors. New datasets (Athena ISR, T1D β-cell, VX-880)
have their own bridge domains that weren't on the list, so cross-domain
edges were silently pruned and the cascade signal appeared to teleport
across domain boundaries during replay. Replaced with a data-driven
one-hop expansion: any domain with at least one edge to a selected
domain is auto-included.

**3. Remove DATA LAYERS section (overview / launch menu).** The whole
collapsible section is deleted from DomainSelector, including the
DISCOVERY ENGINES pill grid and the `visibleDiscoverySources` store
key + filter. Node-level `discoverySource` field is preserved because
the copilot context strings still reference it.

### Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/components/CategoryFilterDropdown.tsx` | New — click-outside-to-close dropdown wired to `visibleCategories` |
| `src/components/HeaderBar.tsx` | Render dropdown when `selectedDomains.length > 0` |
| `src/components/DomainSelector.tsx` | Strip DATA LAYERS section, `localCategories`/`localSources`/`showDataLayers` state, `toggleCategory`/`toggleSource`, `DISCOVERY_SOURCES` const, `visibleDiscoverySources` setter call. Export `NODE_CATEGORIES` for the dropdown. |
| `src/stores/useApexStore.ts` | Drop `visibleDiscoverySources` state + setter |
| `src/hooks/useFilteredGraph.ts` | Drop discovery-source filter; replace hardcoded cross-domain allowlist with one-hop expansion |

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 330/330 vitest pass (including the existing `cascade-simulator` suite)

author: xrl
body:
## Summary
- When Grafana passes a stringified JSON array (e.g. `["paperclip"]`) as a filter value, the `=` operator wrapped it in quotes producing `attributes.tags:"[\"paperclip\"]"` — a phrase query matching no documents
- Detects JSON array values and unwraps them into term queries on individual elements
- Single element: `attributes.tags:paperclip`
- Multiple elements: `attributes.tags:IN ["paperclip" "stapler"]` (tantivy TermSetQuery)
- Empty arrays are a no-op
- Non-array values starting with `[` that aren't valid JSON pass through unchanged

Note: tantivy indexes array elements as individual terms — there's no way to match on array length, order, or exact composition. For multi-element arrays we use IN (match any), which is the most useful behavior for log exploration filters.

## Test plan
- [x] 18 unit tests covering all ad-hoc filter operators and array edge cases

body:
Fixes #361

## Problem

The `_run_c3_analysis` method in `unified_scraper.py` always called
`analyze_codebase` with `languages=None`, ignoring the `languages` filter
configured in the GitHub source config. This caused the C3.x codebase
analysis on cloned repos to either:

1. Find 0 source files — when the repo only contains files of the
   configured language (e.g. C#) and `.gitignore` excludes them from
   the scraper's file walk, since `languages=None` analyzes all languages
   but none match
2. Analyze an unintended language set — inconsistent with the local
   source analysis which correctly respects the language filter

## Solution

Changed `languages=None` to `languages=source.get("languages")` so the
language filter from the source configuration is respected in C3.x clone
analysis, consistent with how the local source analysis passes it.

## Testing

The fix is a one-line change that aligns C3.x clone analysis with the
existing local source analysis pattern (line ~861 uses `languages=languages`
from `source.get("languages")`).

body:
Fixes #952

## Problem

`NewRetriever` in `flow/retriever/parent` validates `Retriever` and `OrigDocGetter` but silently accepts an empty `ParentIDKey`. When `ParentIDKey` is empty, `Retrieve` looks up `subDoc.MetaData[""]` for every sub-document — a key that is never populated — so the function silently returns empty results regardless of the actual retrieval output.

This is the retriever-side companion to the indexer fix in #953.

## Solution

Added a `config.ParentIDKey == ""` validation check in `NewRetriever`, consistent with the existing field validation pattern.

## Testing

Added `TestNewRetrieverValidation` covering all three required-field error cases (nil Retriever, nil OrigDocGetter, empty ParentIDKey). Existing `TestParentRetriever` passes unchanged.

author: acehuall
body:
### Motivation
- Keep a Supabase project active by scheduling a server-side write from Vercel without changing the existing static frontend.
- Provide a minimal CommonJS serverless endpoint that performs a real upsert to a `keep_alive` table using the service role key.

### Description
- Add `api/keep-alive.js` as a CommonJS Vercel function that only allows `GET`, sets `Allow: GET` on 405 responses, sets `Cache-Control: no-store`, validates `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, connects with `createClient`, and upserts `{ id: 1, last_ping }` using `.from('keep_alive').upsert({ id: 1, last_ping }, { onConflict: 'id' })`, returning `{ ok: true, last_ping }` on success.
- Add `package.json` with `@supabase/supabase-js` dependency to ensure the Supabase client is available when installed by the deployment environment.
- Add `vercel.json` with a cron entry calling `/api/keep-alive` on schedule `0 9 */3 * *` (every 3 days).
- Add `supabase/keep_alive.sql` to create the `public.keep_alive` table and seed the row with `id = 1`.
- Update `README.md` with the project layout and a short Supabase keep-alive cron section that documents the endpoint, schedule, required env vars, and a server-only note for `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.

### Testing
- Ran `node -e "require('./api/keep-alive.js')"` which failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` because `@supabase/supabase-js` is not installed in the local environment (this is expected prior to running `npm install` or deploying).

author: adhithyan15
body:
## Summary

- Adds `CodingAdventures::MicroQR` — a full ISO/IEC 18004:2015 Annex E compliant Micro QR Code encoder in Perl
- Supports all 8 valid (version, ECC) symbol configurations: M1/Detection, M2/L, M2/M, M3/L, M3/M, M4/L, M4/M, M4/Q
- Ports the Rust reference implementation (`code/packages/rust/micro-qr/`) to idiomatic Perl with Knuth-style literate comments

## Key implementation details

- Symbol sizes M1=11×11 through M4=17×17 (formula: 2×version_number+9)
- Single finder pattern at top-left, timing at row 0 / col 0 (not row 6/col 6 like regular QR)
- Format XOR mask 0x4445 (not 0x5412), 4 mask patterns (not 8), single format info copy
- Pre-computed 32-entry FORMAT_TABLE `[symbol_indicator][mask_pattern]`, verified against Rust reference
- Reed-Solomon ECC: GF(256)/0x11D, b=0 convention, single block per symbol
- M1 special case: 2.5 codewords = 20 bits (last data byte uses upper nibble only)
- Inner package `CodingAdventures::MicroQR::BitWriter` (MSB-first bit accumulator)
- Integrates with `CodingAdventures::Barcode2D` (grid rendering) and `CodingAdventures::GF256` (field arithmetic)

## New files

- `code/packages/perl/micro-qr/lib/CodingAdventures/MicroQR.pm` — 1147-line encoder with literate comments
- `code/packages/perl/micro-qr/t/micro_qr.t` — 18 subtests with 100+ assertions
- `code/packages/perl/micro-qr/BUILD`, `Makefile.PL`, `cpanfile`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`

## Test plan

- [x] `perl -c lib/CodingAdventures/MicroQR.pm` — syntax OK
- [x] All 18 subtests pass via `prove` / BUILD script
- [x] Security review passed (pure in-memory encoder; no file I/O, no system calls, no eval)

author: atimics
body:
Slice of #341 — moves the docked TRADE BUY/SELL rows fully onto the manifest summary, and adds an explicit "unknown" row for legacy float stock.

## What changed

- BUY rows iterate every (commodity, grade) with > 0 in `g.station_manifest_summary`. After those, if `station.inventory[c]` exceeds the manifest total, an extra row appears with `is_float_fallback = true`, base price (no grade multiplier), and grade label rendered as **"unknown"** in faded text.
- SELL rows do the same on the ship side, comparing `ship_cargo_amount(c)` against the ship-manifest count for that commodity.
- Renderer pulls the grade label/tint via the new `is_float_fallback` branch so the player sees the provenance gap instead of a misleading "common" row.
- Mirrored the enumeration in `src/input.c` so [1]-[5] hotkeys still target the same rows. Unknown rows send `MINING_GRADE_COUNT` (sentinel) so the server's grade-aware buy path falls through to any-grade FIFO at base price.
- Removed the now-unused `*_manifest_has_commodity` predicates.

## Why

Fresh worlds seed some commodities (frames at Kepler, ingots at Prospect) directly into `station.inventory[]` without a corresponding manifest entry. Previously these surfaced as a generic COMMON row, hiding the missing provenance. With #341 they're explicit.

## Acceptance from the issue

- [x] Station stock display reads `station.manifest` first, falls back to inventory float as an explicit unknown row
- [x] Ship hold display reads `ship.manifest` first, falls back to cargo float as an explicit unknown row
- [x] Grouping + labels make grade visible without exposing raw hash internals
- [x] Legacy-migrated goods with missing provenance render as "unknown"
- [x] Existing docked workflows still work — buy/sell on unknown rows uses the any-grade FIFO server path

## Tests

- `make test` — 294/294 pass
- WASM build clean

author: lrabbade
body:
## Add nonlinear cost models for impact-aware backtesting

### Summary

Extends `bt.Backtest` to accept a `CostModel` instance for `commissions`,
in addition to the existing `fn(q, p)` callable. Adds a `CostModel` base
class with two concrete implementations (`SqrtCostModel`,
`AlmgrenChrissCostModel`). When `commissions` is a `CostModel`, the new
`volume` and `volatility` DataFrame arguments are required; otherwise the
existing path is byte-identical to before.

### Motivation

bt's `commissions=fn(q, p)` hook only sees the trade quantity and price.
That is enough for flat bps or per-share fees, but it cannot represent the
two cost terms that dominate at non-trivial size: **temporary impact**
(slippage from walking the book), which scales with `|q|/V`, and the
**triangular permanent-impact cost** paid as the block executes, both of
which depend on the instrument's volatility. Strategy evaluation on a
billion-dollar book without these terms systematically flatters any
strategy that trades large notional relative to available liquidity.

The design here follows Abbade & Costa (2026), *Realistic Market Impact
Modeling for Reinforcement Learning Trading Environments*
(arXiv:[2603.29086](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29086)).

### What's new

**`bt/core.py`** — three new public classes:

* `CostModel` — abstract base; `cost(q, p, V, sigma) -> float`.
* `SqrtCostModel(Y=0.6)` — square-root law (Tóth et al. 2011):
  `cost = (2/3) Y σ |q| sqrt(|q|/V) P`.
* `AlmgrenChrissCostModel(alpha=1.0, beta=1.0, epsilon=0.0005)` —
  Almgren-Chriss decomposition (2001):
  `cost = 0.5 α σ (|q|/V) |q| P + ε |q| P + β σ (|q|/V) |q| P`.

**`bt/backtest.py`** — `Backtest` is extended (no new class):

* `commissions=` now accepts either a `fn(q, p)` callable (existing
  behaviour, unchanged) or a `CostModel` instance (new behaviour).
* Two new optional kwargs `volume=` and `volatility=` (DataFrames aligned
  with `data`). Required when `commissions` is a `CostModel`; rejected
  with a clear `ValueError` otherwise.
* Internally, when a `CostModel` is detected, `Backtest` rebinds the
  deepcopied strategy's `setup` and `_create_child_if_needed` so each
  security's `commission` method is wired to look up its own bar-level
  `(V, σ)`. Lazily-created child securities are covered.

**`bt/__init__.py`** — re-exports `CostModel`, `SqrtCostModel`,
`AlmgrenChrissCostModel` at the package level.

### Backwards compatibility

* No existing symbol or default behaviour is changed. `Backtest`,
  `StrategyBase`, `SecurityBase` are byte-identical for any caller that
  doesn't pass a `CostModel`.
* `commissions=None` and `commissions=fn(q, p)` follow exactly the same
  code path as before — the new branch is gated on
  `isinstance(commissions, CostModel)`.
* Equivalence on the legacy path is verified — `AlmgrenChrissCostModel(0,
  0, eps)` produces fees and equity that are **bit-for-bit identical**
  (`np.testing.assert_allclose`) to `Backtest(commissions=lambda q, p:
  abs(q) * p * eps)` (see
  `test_backtest_cost_model_ac_zero_alpha_beta_matches_flat_commission`).
* All 161 pre-existing tests still pass; no test required modification.

### API at a glance

```python
import bt
from bt.core import AlmgrenChrissCostModel

backtest = bt.Backtest(
    strategy, prices,
    commissions=AlmgrenChrissCostModel(alpha=1.0, beta=1.0, epsilon=0.0005),
    volume=volume_df,
    volatility=volatility_df,
    initial_capital=1_000_000_000.0,
)
bt.run(backtest)
```

`volume` and `volatility` must have the same index and columns as `data`;
mismatches raise `ValueError` at construction. Passing `volume`/`volatility`
without a `CostModel` also raises.

### Tests

21 new tests, all passing alongside the existing 161:

* `tests/test_core.py` — closed-form math for both cost models, sign
  invariance, zero-volume / zero-quantity handling, AC degenerate-to-flat
  case, quadratic-in-participation scaling, ABC contract. (11 tests)
* `tests/test_backtest.py` — smoke run, AC-vs-legacy bit-equivalence,
  active-vs-flat ordering, `SqrtCostModel` integration, index/column
  alignment validation, missing-volume validation,
  volume-without-cost-model validation, no-pollution-of-legacy-path
  guarantee, cost-scales-with-participation. (10 tests)

```text
$ pytest tests/
182 passed in 46.44s
```

### Lint

```text
$ python -m ruff check bt setup.py docs/source/conf.py
All checks passed!
$ python -m ruff format --check bt setup.py docs/source/conf.py
6 files already formatted
```

### Documentation

* `docs/source/Cost_Models.rst` — full walkthrough mirroring the
  existing `Buy_and_hold.rst` style: setup, AC math typeset, headline
  numbers, volume-sensitivity sweep, references.
* `docs/source/examples.rst` — adds `Cost_Models.rst` to the include
  list.
* API reference (`bt.rst`) auto-picks up the new docstrings via the
  existing `automodule` directive.

### Example notebook

`examples/cost_models.ipynb` — executed end-to-end. Uses a $1B book on a
30-stock synthetic universe with a monthly top-10 momentum rebalance
(high turnover), comparing default `bt.Backtest` (no commissions) vs the
same `bt.Backtest` with `commissions=AlmgrenChrissCostModel(...)`.
Headline result:

| Strategy             | Total Return | Sharpe | Total Fees ($M) | Fees / Traded (bps) |
| :------------------- | -----------: | -----: | --------------: | ------------------: |
| baseline (no cost)   |       26.53% |   0.51 |             0.0 |                 0.0 |
| realistic (AC)       |       21.59% |   0.43 |            46.4 |                13.4 |

— a ~5pp drag over five years, at ~13 bps effective cost per dollar
traded, in line with realistic large-cap impact at a few percent of ADV.

### Files changed

```
bt/__init__.py                |  15 +-
bt/backtest.py                |  96 +++-
bt/core.py                    |  87 ++++
docs/source/Cost_Models.rst   | 264 +++++++++++
docs/source/examples.rst      |   1 +
examples/cost_models.ipynb    | 738 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
tests/test_backtest.py        | 226 ++++++++++
tests/test_core.py            |  72 +++
8 files changed, 1495 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

### References

- Abbade, L. R., & Costa, A. H. R. (2026). *Realistic Market Impact
  Modeling for Reinforcement Learning Trading Environments.*
  arXiv:[2603.29086](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29086).
- Almgren, R., & Chriss, N. (2001). Optimal execution of portfolio
  transactions. *Journal of Risk* 3(2), 5–39.
- Tóth, B. et al. (2011). Anomalous Price Impact and the Critical Nature
  of Liquidity in Financial Markets. *Physical Review X* 1(2), 021006.
- Gatheral, J. (2010). No-Dynamic-Arbitrage and Market Impact.
  *Quantitative Finance* 10(7), 749–759.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent race conditions where concurrent calls (e.g. `setContextMenu` / `_ensureClient`) observe a non-null `_client` while it is being closed, which could cause errors or inconsistent state.

### Description
- Add a serialized async queue (`_pendingClientOperation` + `_runSerializedClientOperation`) and run all client lifecycle/state mutations through it (`destroy`, `setIcon`, `setToolTip`, `setTitle`, `setContextMenu`).
- Wrap `destroy`, `setIcon`, `setToolTip`, `setTitle`, and `setContextMenu` with `_runSerializedClientOperation` so operations run one-at-a-time.
- Change destruction/recreation order to capture the current `StatusNotifierItemClient` in a local variable, set `_client` and `_currentMenuModel` to `null` immediately, and then `await` `close()` on the captured client to avoid exposing a closing-but-non-null client.
- Make the serialized queue resilient by swallowing errors from the previous queued operation so the queue can continue scheduling subsequent operations.

author: nathanaronson
body:
## Summary

Four threads of post-merge work bundled together. Each is independently
useful; the bundle is what's needed to actually run a generation
end-to-end against Gemini today.

### 1. Gemini provider dispatch
One env var `LLM_PROVIDER=claude|gemini` routes every `complete()`
call through either Anthropic or `google.genai`. The strategist,
builder, and baseline engine are **unchanged** — Gemini responses are
adapted into Anthropic-style content blocks (`SimpleNamespace` with
`.type` / `.name` / `.input` / `.text`).

Critical Gemini-2.5-Flash gotcha fixed: `thinking_config(thinking_budget=0)`
disables internal reasoning that was eating the whole `max_output_tokens`
budget before any `function_call` could be emitted.

### 2. Cohort 5 → 2
Strategist proposes 2 distinct improvement questions per generation
(was 5), 2 builders run in parallel, 2 candidates + champion in the
round-robin. Backend schemas, tests, prompt, websocket comment,
frontend timeline, mock events, README, and plan docs all updated in
sync.

### 3. Infra fixes — what unblocked real generations
- **DB auto-init.** FastAPI lifespan calls `init_db()` so a fresh
  checkout doesn't 500 on \`no such table: generations\`.
- **Uvicorn reload exclusions.** \`--reload-exclude 'cubist/engines/generated/*'\`
  and \`*.db\`. Without this, every successful builder restarts the
  backend mid-tournament — discovered by tail-running an actual generation.
- **Builder max_tokens 4k → 8k.** A JSON-encoded ~50-line Python
  module + tool wrapper exceeds 4k under Gemini's tokenizer.
- **Top-level exception capture in \`run_generation_task\`.** Logs
  full traceback and emits a terminal \`generation.finished\` so the
  UI flips out of \"running\" instead of hanging silently.
- **Central logging (\`cubist.logging_setup\`).** Every LLM call now
  logs provider / model / token budget / duration. Empty-response
  diagnostics include \`finish_reason\` + safety + usage. \`LOG_LEVEL\`
  in \`.env\` for verbosity control.

### 4. Makefile + dev ergonomics
\`make help\` / \`install\` / \`dev\` / \`seed\` / \`run\` / \`replay\` /
\`smoke\` / \`eval\` / \`check\` / \`reset\`. README setup section
rewritten around the targets. UI title flipped from \"CUBIST\" to a
generic \"Self-improving chess engine\".

### 5. Four follow-up plans
\`plans/followup-1\` … \`followup-4\`. Each is sized for one person /
one PR; sit on top of this branch once merged. They cover the **real
game-quality bugs** an end-to-end Gemini run uncovered:

| Plan | Owner | Branch | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Tournament concurrency | TBD | \`followup/tournament-concurrency\` | Semaphore on parallel games; surface \`error\` terminations |
| 2 — Builder quality + prompt | TBD | \`followup/builder-quality\` | Fix the \`from cubist import config as settings\` bug; tighten validator |
| 3 — Champion resume in API | TBD | \`followup/champion-resume\` | \`run_generation_task\` reads latest \`GenerationRow.champion_after\` instead of hard-coding baseline |
| 4 — Frontend live-board + badges | TBD | \`followup/frontend-polish\` | Debug LiveBoard not rendering; surface termination reasons in Timeline / Bracket |

## End-to-end verification

Ran a full gen-2 generation against \`gemini-2.5-flash\` from a clean
DB:

\`\`\`
23:24:14  run_generation_task starting generation=2
23:24:16  strategist tool_use(name=submit_questions) ok in 2.0s
23:24:19  builder #1 tool_use(name=submit_engine) ok in 3.2s
23:24:20  builder #2 tool_use(name=submit_engine) ok in 3.6s
... round-robin tournament, 12 games ...
23:27:53  run_generation_task finished generation=2
\`\`\`

\`/api/generations\` and \`/api/games\` show the persisted run; new
champion \`gen2-evaluation-f00df6\` was promoted over baseline-v0.

## What this PR does NOT fix

The 12 games of gen 2 all terminated on \`time\` after 0–1 moves
because:

1. Generated engines have a config-import bug → silently fall back to \`next(iter(legal))\`.
2. Round-robin runs all 12 games in parallel → Gemini's per-call latency under load exceeds the referee's per-move timeout.

These are documented in follow-ups 1 and 2 — intentionally not in
this PR's scope. The infra fixes here are what made these failure
modes visible in the first place.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`make install && make seed\` from a fresh checkout completes.
- [ ] \`make check\` (lint + 26 tests) passes.
- [ ] \`make dev\` starts both services; \`/api/health\` returns 200.
- [ ] With \`LLM_PROVIDER=claude\` + a valid \`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\`, a generation completes.
- [ ] With \`LLM_PROVIDER=gemini\` + a valid \`GOOGLE_API_KEY\`, a generation completes (engines may play first-legal-moves; that's follow-up 2).

## Files changed

27 files, +4410/-186. New: \`Makefile\`, \`logging_setup.py\`, four
follow-up plans, lockfiles. Modifications across backend (LLM, agents,
orchestration, config, API), frontend (App, Timeline, mockEvents),
docs (README, plan-c).

author: mohamedbilelbesbes
body:
It was reported [here](https://github.com/mozilla/treeherder/pull/9397#issuecomment-4289690716) that adding the voting system caused an increase of 12% in python unit test execution time.

Upon investigation, it turned out that running 5 statistical detectors twice per signature (once per voting strategy) was the main bottleneck. Now, detection runs once and the result is shared. On top of that, the 5 detector objects were being reconstructed on every loop iteration across the series; pinning them to a module-level constant eliminates that overhead entirely. Both fixes compound across every test that touches alert generation.

Changes in `alerts.py`:
- Extracted `prepare_series_for_detection` to isolate the expensive DB fetch + `detect_methods_changes` step from the voting logic so it could be reused across multiple strategy calls.
- Added `_trim_series_after` helper to encapsulate the timestamp-based series filtering, replacing an inline list comprehension.
- Introduced CPD_METHODS module-level constant so `build_cpd_methods()` is called **only once** at import time instead of on every alert generation cycle, removing redundant instantiation of all detector objects across `get_methods_detecting_at_index`, `create_alert`, and `prepare_series_for_detection`.

Changes in `tasks.py` are related to creating the series with detections running once at first and used subsequently for all voting systems in use.

Changes in `test_methods_alerts.py` are related to reducing the calls of `build_cpd_methods`

@gmierz is there a way to measure whether there is indeed a reduction of python unit tests runtime given the fixes of this PR?

body:
## Summary
- Wires the data-ingestion side of the chunked-text refactor that db-migrations 026 + shared-models 0.1.34 already shipped. Bills whose text exceeds the embedding model's context window (the 14 MB Statutes-at-Large reprint that motivated all of this) now split into chunks with one embedding per chunk, instead of failing the previous monolithic single-blob path.
- New BillTextChunker (pure character-window split, deterministic + idempotent) + RawBillTextRepository / DoobieRawBillTextRepository (delete-then-insert replaceAll keyed by version_id).
- BillTextProcessor rewires its happy path to download → chunk → embed-each (sequential, Ollama serialises internally anyway) → persist version metadata + N raw_bill_text rows under ONE transaction. DoobieBillTextVersionRepository drops the content/embedding columns from its SQL.
- Bumps `repchecksharedmodels` 0.1.33→0.1.34, `repcheck-db-migrations-runner` 0.1.23→0.1.24, and the runner image pin in both docker-compose.local.yml + docker-compose.e2e.yml so migration 026 actually runs.
- Adds `OLLAMA_MAX_CHUNK_CHARS` (default 30,000 — well inside qwen3-embedding's ~32k-token window with ASCII headroom).

## Tests
- New BillTextChunkerSpec (11 cases) + InvalidChunkSizeSpec (3 cases) + DoobieRawBillTextRepositoryUnitSpec (7 cases).
- All existing tests adapted to the new DO/processor shape: 251/251 unit tests green (144 bills-common + 107 bill-text-pipeline). DockerRequired integration suites are compiled against the new APIs and wired but stay off the default test path — next local-stack rerun exercises them end-to-end.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green on this PR (build + scalafmt + scalafix + per-subproject test split).
- [ ] After merge: rebuild docker images on main, restart local stack, verify migration 026 actually runs (`databasechangelog` should show 026 + `\dt raw_bill_text` should resolve).

## Relevant issues

Follow-up to #26492 (already merged) addressing review notes on the same area.

## Summary

Three follow-ups in `key_management_endpoints.py`:

1. `_check_allowed_routes_caller_permission` now opts into the safe-preset
   carve-out only at the post-`handle_key_type` re-check inside
   `_common_key_generation_helper`. The raw-body call sites
   (`/key/generate` entry, `_validate_update_key_data`, `regenerate_key_fn`,
   and now `/key/service-account/generate`) keep the default strictness, so
   non-admins can no longer write `allowed_routes=[\"llm_api_routes\"]`
   directly in the request body and must go through `key_type` instead.

2. `/key/service-account/generate` (`generate_service_account_key_fn`) now
   runs `_check_allowed_routes_caller_permission` and
   `_check_passthrough_routes_caller_permission` at entry, matching
   `/key/generate`. Previously a non-admin team admin could create a
   service-account key with `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` and
   reach admin-only routes through the passthrough gate.

3. `/key/regenerate` mirrors `/key/generate`'s post-`handle_key_type`
   re-check, so a `key_type` preset submitted via the regenerate body is
   routed through the same caller-permission helper before the request
   continues. Functionally a no-op today (the request fails downstream at
   the prisma layer because the column does not exist) but closes the
   surface against future schema or routing changes.

The legitimate `key_type=llm_api` and `key_type=read_only` flows for
non-admin callers continue to work, since the post-`handle_key_type`
call site is the only one that opts into the safe-preset carve-out.

internal-user key:

- non-admin `key_type=management` on `/key/regenerate` → 403 (was 500 from a downstream column miss)

author: dhyansraj
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #820: Claude provider hangs indefinitely (silent 600s+) when `response_format` (structured output) is combined with `tools` and certain content patterns. Anthropic's `response_format` path on Claude 3.5+ has known pathological cases that silently stall rather than error.
- **Strategy**: HINT-first with bounded-timeout `response_format` fallback. Inject schema instructions into the system prompt (mirrors `GeminiHandler`'s proven pattern); on JSON parse failure, retry once with native `response_format` and `request_timeout=30s`. Eliminates the catastrophic 600s hang on the dominant path; bounded fallback covers the ~5% HINT compliance gap without re-introducing the hang.
- `MCP_MESH_CLAUDE_FORCE_RESPONSE_FORMAT=true` env override reverts to legacy behavior in case fallback misbehaves in production.
- Both `_provider_agentic_loop` (multi-iteration tool dispatch) AND legacy single-call path implement the same strip + validate + fallback semantics. Extracted `_pop_mesh_hint_flags` and `_extract_text_from_message_content` helpers shared between both paths so future maintainers can't fix one and forget the other.

## Bundled bonus fixes

### GeminiHandler concurrency race (latent bug)

While auditing the handler architecture, found that `GeminiHandler._pending_output_schema` was an instance field on a cached singleton handler (`ProviderHandlerRegistry._instances`). Concurrent requests with different output schemas would cross-contaminate. **Verified empirically** — temporarily reverted the migration and confirmed 3 of 7 new tests fail without it. Migrated to `contextvars.ContextVar` via new shared module `_mcp_mesh/engine/provider_handlers/_handler_context.py`. ClaudeHandler doesn't read these so its instance fields were deleted (vestigial, never read).

### tc04 build infra hotfix (post-#821)

PR #821's gitignore fix correctly removed `src/runtime/core/typescript/index.{js,d.ts}` from git tracking — these are NAPI-RS auto-generated artifacts. But `tc04_build_typescript_sdk` implicitly relied on them being on the host. After #821, fresh CI containers don't have them and `tsc` fails to resolve `@mcpmesh/core` types.

Mirrored tc04a's pattern (Java SDK builds its native FFI library inline before building the JARs). Now tc04 builds the napi-rs wrappers (`cd core/typescript && npm install && npm run build`) before building the SDK. Plus `set -euo pipefail` so silent tsc failures stop being silent (previously tc04 reported success when tsc errored, and tc05 was the one that failed looking for the .tgz that was never produced).

## Review notes

This PR went through two review iterations (one before the leak bug surfaced, one before commit):
- Independent review passed on the HINT-first design and shared helpers
- The `_mesh_*` flag leak in the legacy single-call path was caught by tsuite (6 failing integration tests) and fixed before commit. Both `litellm.completion` call sites now strip the flags via a shared helper.
- Confirmed no THIRD `litellm.completion` call site exists (grep verified).

## Architectural notes

The Anthropic `response_format` silent-hang behavior is an upstream issue (Anthropic's structured output service, not LiteLLM, not mesh). The fallback path uses the SAME `tools + response_format` combo that triggered the original hang — only the bounded `request_timeout=30s` protects us. If Anthropic ever fixes the underlying issue, this fallback could become a primary path; for now it exists only to recover from the rare HINT compliance failure.

Closes #820

## Test plan

- [x] Local unit tests: 544 pass (531 baseline + 13 new for ClaudeHandler HINT mode + helpers)
- [x] tsuite integration:
  - [x] tc17_structured_multi_turn_py PASS (was BadRequestError on `_mesh_hint_mode`)
  - [x] tc19_structured_avatar_pattern_py PASS
  - [x] tc23_structured_output_ts_consumer_py_provider PASS
  - [x] tc02_py_mesh_claude PASS
  - [x] tc04_parallel_error_handling_py PASS (downstream of the leak)
  - [x] tc09_parallel_error_handling_java PASS (downstream of the leak)
- [x] Existing structured-output tests not regressed
- [x] tc04_build_typescript_sdk passes (fixed the tsc-can't-find-@mcpmesh/core regression)

body:
## 개요

`samples/hwpx/form-002.hwpx` 의 외부 표 row 19 의 셀 안에 있는 1×1 내부 표 (`연구개발계획서 제출시 다음의 항목의 정량적 목표치 및 상용화 수준 제시 필수`) 의 페이지 분할 렌더링 결함 3건을 단계적으로 수정.

closes #324

## 증상

PDF 기준 page 2 상단에 위치해야 할 인너 표가:
- (v1 이전) page 1 하단에 잘못 표출
- (v1 이후) page 1 에서 제거됐으나 page 2 에서도 누락
- (v2 이후) page 2 에 표출되지만 SVG 클립에 가려져 일부만 보임

## 수정 내역 (3-단계)

### v1 — `compute_cell_line_ranges` 누적위치 기반 재작성
**커밋**: 4452894
- 잔량(remaining) 기반 추적이 잔량 0 도달 시 cumulative position 정보 손실
- 중첩 표 atomic 문단 가시성을 잘못된 heuristic 으로 판정
- → 셀 시작부터 누적 위치(`cum`)를 명시적으로 추적하는 방식으로 전면 재작성
  - 일반 문단: `line_end_pos = cum + line_h` 와 `content_offset` / `content_limit` 비교
  - 중첩 표 atomic: `para_end_pos` 로 \"이전 페이지 완료\" / \"다음 페이지 미룸\" 결정

### v2 — `layout_partial_table` content_y_accum 갱신 누락 수정
**커밋**: 3d304cd
- offset 으로 완전 소비된 일반 문단(`line_ranges=(n,n)`)이 스킵될 때 `content_y_accum` 미갱신
- 후속 nested-table 문단의 위치 판정이 부정확하여 split-start 페이지에서 \"이미 이전 페이지에 렌더링됨\" 으로 잘못 스킵
- → `!has_nested_table` 분기에 `is_in_split_row` 일 때 `para_full_text_h` 계산식으로 `content_y_accum` 갱신 추가

### v3 — `split-start row` cell visible height 통일된 계산
**커밋**: e086ab4
- `has_nested_table` 셀 분기가 `calc_nested_split_rows` 에 raw `split_start_content_offset` (cell 전체 기준) 을 그대로 전달 → inner table 의 cell 내 위치 무시
- p[28] inner table (cell 내 위치 ~758px) 에 대해 offset=443 raw 전달 → visible height = 0 → cell-clip-6 가 작아져 inner table 일부 클립
- → has_nested_table 분기 제거, 모든 셀에 대해 `compute_cell_line_ranges` + `calc_visible_content_height_from_ranges` 통일 경로 사용

## 변경 파일

- `src/renderer/layout/table_layout.rs::compute_cell_line_ranges` — 누적위치 기반 재작성 (~140 줄)
- `src/renderer/layout/table_partial.rs` — v2: split-end atomic 스킵 + `content_y_accum` 갱신, v3: 통일 경로 (`-64 / +34` 줄)
- `tests/golden_svg/form-002/page-0.svg` — 골든 갱신 (의도)

## 검증

### form-002 페이지 1/2 (PDF 비교)

| 페이지 | Before | After v1 | After v2 | After v3 (최종) |
|--------|--------|---------|---------|-----------------|
| page 1 인너 표 | 잘못 표출 | 미표출 ✓ | 미표출 ✓ | 미표출 ✓ |
| page 2 인너 표 | 누락 | 누락 | 표출 (일부 클립) | **3줄 모두 표출** ✓ |
| cell-clip-6 height (p2) | - | 349.63 | 349.63 | **405.68** |

### 회귀 테스트

- `cargo test --release`: **992 단위 + 71 통합 테스트 통과**
- `cargo clippy --release -- -D warnings`: **클린**
- 골든 갱신 1건: `tests/golden_svg/form-002/page-0.svg` (의도된 변경)

### dump-pages

페이지 분할 결정 자체는 변경되지 않음 (page 1 rows=0..20, page 2 rows=19..26 동일).

## 알려진 후속 항목

- **#325**: cell.h 과 실제 콘텐츠 누적 높이 불일치로 불필요한 셀 분할 발생. form-002 page 2 의 `diff=-21.2px` 가 단서. 본 Task 의 범위 밖이며 Epic #309 의 후속 task 로 분리.

### Motivation

- Provide richer runtime diagnostics for the embedded Stratum server via RPC and internal info tracking to aid debugging and monitoring.
- Improve address bind resolution and socket handling for IPv4/IPv6 any addresses and add verbose logs to clarify resolution and bind failures.
- Surface recent client/authorization/share/block events (IPs, worker names, last share results) and uptime/notify timestamps so operators can inspect recent activity.

### Description

- Extended the `getstratuminfo` RPC help/result description to include many optional fields such as `connected_clients`, `authorized_clients`, `current_job_id`, `last_client_ip`, `last_authorized_worker`, `last_accepted_share_hash`, `last_rejected_share_reason`, `last_block_submission_result`, `uptime`, and `last_notify_time`.
- Added new tracking fields to `stratum::Server` (`m_last_client_ip`, `m_last_authorized_worker`, `m_last_accepted_share_hash`, `m_last_rejected_share_reason`, `m_last_block_submission_result`, `m_start_time`, `m_last_notify_time`) and populate them at appropriate events (`accept`, `authorize`, `submit`, notify creation, job submission attempts).
- Reworked bind resolution in `ResolveBindAddress` to explicitly construct `sockaddr_in`/`sockaddr_in6` for `0.0.0.0` and `::`, added detailed `LogPrintf` traces, and set `IPV6_V6ONLY` to avoid binding surprises; also added `SockAddrToIP` helper to extract client IPs.
- Updated `Server::InitListeningSocket`, `Start`, `Stop`, `BuildPostAuthorizeMessages`, and `HandleClient` to use the new fields and logging, and to compute `uptime` and `last_notify_time`; updated `stratum::Info` struct and `GetInfo()` to return the new values.

### Testing

- Updated and ran the functional test `test/functional/feature_stratum_solo.py` which now verifies binding to `0.0.0.0`, `::` (when IPv6 is available), and `127.0.0.1`, and checks `getstratuminfo` fields such as `bind` and `listening`; the test completed successfully.

body:
## Problem
`lanhu_get_design_slices` returned `total_slices: 0` for Photoshop uploads (`type: ps`) even though the Lanhu web UI lists slices (top bar / dashed selection). The MasterJSON stores slice registry under `assets[]` with `isSlice: true`, while export URLs live on matching layer IDs (`images.png_xxxhd` / `images.svg`) — the existing walker only matched `ddsImage` / `image` on DDS/Figma-style trees.

## Solution

author: bjan
body:
## Summary

The standalone MCP stdio server in `packages/daemon/src/mcp/tools.ts` ignores `SIGNET_AGENT_ID` and never sends `agentId` to the daemon. As a result, every `memory_search` / `memory_store` / `memory_recall` call from any harness that mounts the MCP server resolves server-side to `agentId=\"default\"` via `resolveAgentId`'s fallback — silently bypassing per-agent `read_policy: isolated` and pooling all memory traffic under the `default` bucket.

## Repro

Setup:
- Two agents in `agents` table: `default` (`read_policy: shared`) and `agent_b` (`read_policy: isolated`).
- Spawn the MCP server (`@signet/daemon` `mcp-stdio.ts`) under harness B with `SIGNET_AGENT_ID=agent_b`.
- Have agent B call `memory_store` with content X, then `memory_search` for X.

Observed: all writes from agent B land under `agent_id=default` in `memories`. Recalls return both default's and agent_b's bucket because the request is being treated as default. The `agents` row for `agent_b` exists (created by hooks/CLI which DO honor the env), but its `read_policy` is moot for any MCP-mediated traffic.

Expected: writes attributed to `agent_b`; recalls scoped to `agent_b`'s bucket per its `read_policy`.

## Root cause

`daemonFetch` in `packages/daemon/src/mcp/tools.ts` (the helper backing every MCP tool) sets only `Content-Type`, `x-signet-runtime-path`, `x-signet-actor`, `x-signet-actor-type` headers, and never enriches the body. The daemon's recall handler (`packages/daemon/src/routes/...` -> `resolveAgentId({ agentId: body.agentId, sessionKey: header })`) sees neither, falls back to `\"default\"`.

The CLI/hooks path (`packages/cli`) and the OpenClaw adapter (`packages/adapters/openclaw`) already honor `SIGNET_AGENT_ID`. The bug is scoped to this one helper.

This matches the \"Scoping leaks\" failure mode called out in `CLAUDE.md`:

> Thread `agent_id` through every read/write touching user data. Never hardcode `\"default\"` for scoped paths.

## Fix

In `daemonFetch`:

- Read `process.env.SIGNET_AGENT_ID` (trimmed; whitespace-only treated as unset).
- Add `x-signet-agent-id` header when the env is set (covers handlers that read it from headers).
- For request bodies that are plain objects without an existing `agentId`, spread in `agentId: <env value>` before serialization (covers handlers like `/api/memory/recall` that read `body.agentId`).
- Existing explicit args (e.g. `memory_feedback` taking `agent_id` from the LLM) are preserved — never overridden.

Minimal change, no new dependencies, fully backward compatible:
- When `SIGNET_AGENT_ID` is unset, behavior is identical to before.
- Non-object bodies (none today, but defensive) pass through untouched.

## Tests

Added a `SIGNET_AGENT_ID propagation` describe block in `packages/daemon/src/mcp/tools.test.ts` with 4 cases:

1. Injects `agentId` into POST body and `x-signet-agent-id` header when env is set.
2. Does not override an explicit `body.agentId` (uses `memory_feedback` to verify).
3. Omits header and body field when env is unset.
4. Treats whitespace-only env value as unset.

All 4 pass locally. The full `tools.test.ts` suite is `42 pass / 1 fail / 249 expect()` — the one failure (`falls back to graphiq state file when plugin registry has no graphiq entry`) reproduces on `origin/main` without my change and appears to be a Termux/Android-specific environment issue with the GraphIQ install path, unrelated to this PR.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI lint (Biome) — couldn't run locally, no Android binary. Code follows surrounding style.
- [ ] CI typecheck — local typecheck blocked by pre-existing workspace `rootDir` issues unrelated to this change.
- [ ] CI tests on the new `SIGNET_AGENT_ID propagation` describe block.
- [ ] Manual: harness with `SIGNET_AGENT_ID=foo` + isolated agent row writes/reads only its own bucket. Verified locally on `signetai 0.103.3` against patched `dist/mcp-stdio.js` — `memory_store` now lands rows with `agent_id=foo` in SQLite (was `default` before).

## Notes

- Considered also injecting via `x-signet-session-key` header in `agent:<id>` form, but body+header is more direct and matches the existing `body.agentId` priority in `resolveAgentId`.
- The bundled `signetai` package's `dist/mcp-stdio.js` will pick this up after the next `bun run build:signetai` + release.

author: bigsidd
body:
## Problem

`_pulse_signal_opportunities()` in `scout_bot.py` was running 60 lines of inline SQL with a simple exact-match anti-join:

```sql
LEFT JOIN active_pairs ap
    ON ap.publisher_id = c.publisher_id
   AND ap.adv_name = c.adv_name   -- ← exact match only
```

`queries.revenue_opportunities()` (the canonical shared function used by the agent tool) uses a **fuzzy** position-match anti-join:

```sql
AND (
    ap.adv_name_lower = c.adv_name_lower
    OR position(c.adv_name_lower, ap.adv_name_lower) > 0
    OR position(ap.adv_name_lower, c.adv_name_lower) > 0
)
```

This meant the Pulse could recommend "Disney+" every morning when a publisher already runs "Disney+ and Hulu" — a false recommendation the agent would correctly suppress, but the Pulse would not. **Signal drift between the two surfaces.**

## Fix

Replace the 60-line inline SQL block with a 4-line call to `_q.revenue_opportunities(ch)`. Pulse takes `[:5]` from the 20 rows returned (same top-5 behavior, same dict keys — callers and renderers unchanged).

Also: add `scout_agent.py` DAG terminal note to CLAUDE.md, update Signal Map to reflect the fix.

## Verification

- [ ] `python3 -m py_compile scout_bot.py` — clean ✅
- [ ] `@Scout opportunities` in Slack — agent response unchanged (same shared function)
- [ ] Force Pulse — opportunities section shows same card format

author: martincouso
body:
## Summary

Phase 13.5 PR-A — ref-counted session attach/release. The keystone for
multi-client coexistence: TUI, Electron, and MCP can now hold
overlapping attachments to the same daemon, with last-release
tear-down semantics.

See the full plan at [docs/plans/2026-04-25-module-system-phase-13-5-plan.md](https://github.com/utopyk/rn-dev-cli/blob/feat/module-system-phase-13-5/docs/plans/2026-04-25-module-system-phase-13-5-plan.md).

### Wire-protocol changes

- `events/subscribe { profile? }` — payload-extended. The
  events/subscribe socket is now the refcount holder.
- `events/subscribe` response carries `{ subscribed, connectionId,
  status, started, attached }`. Joiners short-circuit on
  `status="running"` + `started=false`.
- `session/release { connectionId }` — new wire action; the
  connectionId comes from the subscribe response.
- `session/start` no longer modifies refcount (kept as a back-compat
  no-op).
- `IpcMessageEvent.connectionId` — stable per-connection id.

### Why move refcount to subscribe?

`IpcClient.send()` opens a new socket per call, so refcount tied to
send-conns drops to 0 the moment `session/start` returns. The
long-lived `events/subscribe` socket is the only durable connection
between client and daemon — binding refcount there is what makes
"two clients on one daemon" actually work.

### Subtle correctness fixes

1. **Listener registration order.** `handleEventsSubscribe` registers
   the supervisor.onEvent listener BEFORE awaiting attach. Otherwise
   bootAsync's synchronous "running" emit fires into listeners=0 and
   joiners hang.
2. **Subscribe-ack filter.** `IpcClient.subscribe` now filters the
   initial confirmation by `type: "response"`. With listener-first
   ordering, a session event sharing the same id could otherwise
   hijack the subscribe ack.
3. **`IpcServer.stop` 500ms grace.** Bun's Node net compat sometimes
   leaves `closeAllConnections` as a no-op on still-pending sockets,
   making `server.close()` callback never fire. Force-resolve after
   500ms covers it.
4. **Single-shot resolve/reject wrappers.** `runningPromise`'s
   resolve/reject are wrapped to swallow late calls (silences
   unhandled rejections during cleanup).

### Electron

- Drops `MULTI_INSTANCE_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Same-profile second instance
  shares the active session; cross-profile attempts surface the
  daemon's `E_PROFILE_MISMATCH` directly.
- main-process quit uses `release()` (refcount-aware) instead of
  `disconnect()`.
- `state.daemonSessionProfileName` tracks the active session's
  profile so `instances:create` can detect same-profile vs
  cross-profile attempts.

### Tests

5 new integration tests in `src/app/client/__tests__/session-release.test.ts`:
- Two clients, first releases → session keeps running
- Last release → session torn down → fresh attach boots a new one
- Profile mismatch → `E_PROFILE_MISMATCH`
- Idempotent release
- Socket-close from a crashed client auto-releases its refcount

Existing tests updated:
- `session-disconnect`: contract is now "no attachers = teardown"; test asserts "two attachers, one disconnects, session keeps running."
- `gui-mcp-survive` + `panel-bridge`: MCP-style clients now subscribe with profile (attacher mode) so they hold a refcount.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — **947 / 0** (+5 new)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — **149** (pre-existing wizard errors, unchanged)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p electron/tsconfig.json` — **0**
- [x] `npx playwright test` — **10 / 0**
- [x] `bun run build` — green

body:
## Why

Post-incident hardening after M3 violations (button opacity, TV icon, auto-layout width collapse) were caught late in Gate 3A. Root cause: the DQG was **output-based** — it checked what was written, not what the spec requires.

## What

Two generic protocol rules added to `ux-design-execution/SKILL.md`:

### 1. QG-0 Spec-First Verification (Step 11 preamble)
Before reading a single Figma node, the agent must derive a **spec table** for every frame element from M3 spec + DS library definitions. Then read actuals from Figma and diff. Any divergence is a blocker regardless of what the checklist says.

This changes verification from:
- ❌ *"I wrote X, does X look right?"*
- ✅ *"M3 says this must be Y — what does Figma actually have?"*

### 2. Neighbor Recheck (Write-Verify-Correct Loop step 6)
After every confirmed write, immediately read all relevant properties of the **written node's parent and direct siblings**. Figma's auto-layout engine can silently mutate neighbors (width collapse, padding reset, fill override) with no error and no screenshot signal.

## What this would have caught
| Past failure | Rule that catches it |
|---|---|
| Button opacity 1.0 instead of 0.38 | QG-0: M3 disabled state spec derives 0.38; diff catches 1.0 |
| Missing status bar + gesture nav | QG-0: mobile frame spec table always includes system chrome |
| Auto-layout width collapse 48→29 | Neighbor Recheck: sibling width read-back after layout write |

author: sumaiazaman
body:
## Summary

- `Arr::pluck()` and `LazyCollection::pluck()` now correctly handle enum instances used as keys, consistent with the enum support added to `Collection::keyBy()` and `Collection::groupBy()`.

## Problem

Both `Arr::pluck()` and `LazyCollection::pluck()` handle object keys with `__toString` but not enums. Since enums don't implement `__toString` by default, passing an enum as the pluck key results in the enum object being used directly as an array key, which is invalid in PHP and causes an error.

```php
// Before - throws error for int/string backed enums, fatal for unit enums
Arr::pluck($array, 'name', 'status'); // where 'status' resolves to an enum

// After - works correctly
[1 => 'foo', 2 => 'bar']   // BackedEnum: uses backing value
['A' => 'foo']             // UnitEnum: uses name
```

## Solution

Add an `instanceof \UnitEnum` check before the existing `__toString` check in both `Arr::pluck()` and `LazyCollection::pluck()`, using `enum_value()` to extract the value — the same pattern applied in #59809 for `Collection::keyBy()`.

## Test Plan

- [x] `SupportArrTest::testPluckWithEnumKeys` — int backed, string backed, and unit enums
- [x] `SupportCollectionTest::testPluckWithEnumKeys` — covers both `Collection` and `LazyCollection` via `collectionClassProvider`

author: etraut-openai
body:
## Why

Fixes #19508.

In a fresh TUI session, pressing `Esc` twice entered the rewind transcript overlay even though there was no user message to rewind to. That produced an empty header-only transcript view and exposed a rewind flow that could not select a valid target.

## What changed

The backtrack flow now checks whether a user-message rewind target exists before opening the transcript preview. If no target exists, Codex stays in the main TUI and shows `No previous message to edit.` instead of opening an empty overlay.

The same guard applies when starting rewind preview from the transcript overlay, and the first `Esc` no longer advertises the “edit previous message” hint when there is no previous message available.

Snapshot coverage was added for the unavailable rewind info message, along with a small target-detection test.

author: ghbvf
body:
## Summary

Introduce a `Printer` abstraction so `gocell validate` and `gocell check contract-health` share one renderer that supports `text` / `json` / `sarif`.

- **Text** stays default and is **byte-equivalent** to pre-PR-A10 output (declared non-stable in `--help`).
- **JSON**: stable camelCase shape `{issues:[], summary:{errors,warnings}}`, jq-friendly.
- **SARIF 2.1.0**: includes a deduplicated `tool.driver.rules[]` for VS Code SARIF Explorer / GitHub Code Scanning ingestion.

Embedded scope (per backlog markers):
- **PR239-OB1 CONTRACT-HEALTH-HTTP-COLUMNS-01**: text-mode contract-health table gains `METHOD` / `PATH` columns so dashboards can read transport metadata directly from `gocell check contract-health` output.
- **PR239-DX1 FMT-13-HOW-TO-FIX-HINT-01**: FMT-13 "no pathParams declaration" message appends a copy-pasteable YAML fragment so the diagnostic explains *how* to fix it.

Backlog sync (in this PR):
- ✅ P1-4 OUTPUT-JSON-SARIF-01 closed
- ✅ PR239-OB1 / PR239-DX1 marked done
- ➕ New `VERIFY-JSON-OUTPUT-01` (~3h) registered for `gocell verify` JSON output. **Deferred** — `VerifyResult` is test-execution data (PASS/FAIL + command stdout), not finding-shaped, so it needs an independent `VerifyPrinter`. Not lazy deferral.

## Architecture decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Printer pkg location | `cmd/gocell/app/printers/` | CLI-private; kernel layer stays stdlib-only |
| JSON tag location | private DTOs in printers pkg | `governance.ValidationResult` stays a pure domain struct |
| Default format | `text` | preserves IDE click-to-open; help marks it non-stable |
| Severity → SARIF level | error→`error`, warning→`warning` | SARIF 2.1.0 standard |
| Scope-only results | omit `locations[]`, prefix message `"[scope: <X>] "` | SARIF allows; viewer-readable |
| `tool.driver.rules[]` | populated, deduplicated by Code | improves over golangci-lint (it leaves rules[] empty) |

## Frame-of-reference

```
ref: golangci-lint pkg/printers/printer.go (Printer + io.Writer dispatch)
ref: golangci-lint pkg/printers/sarif.go (SARIF 2.1.0 layout)
     — diverges by populating tool.driver.rules[]
ref: dominikh/go-tools lintcmd/format.go (formatter pattern)
ref: golangci-lint pkg/result/issue.go
     — divergence: keep governance.ValidationResult as pure domain type;
       printers own wire format via private DTOs
```

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./cmd/gocell/...` passes
- [x] `go test ./kernel/governance/...` passes (FMT-13 hint regression test)
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./cmd/gocell/... ./kernel/governance/...` → 0 issues
- [x] `go build -tags=integration ./...` clean
- [x] CI integration job scope (`./adapters/... ./tests/integration/... ./cmd/corebundle/... ./examples/ssobff/... ./cells/accesscore/slices/identitymanage/... ./runtime/bootstrap/...`) clean (one pre-existing testcontainers RabbitMQ port failure unrelated to this PR)
- [x] Coverage: `cmd/gocell/app/printers/` at **96.4%** (target ≥90%)
- [x] E2E smoke against real repo:
  - `gocell validate --format=text` byte-equivalent to old output
  - `gocell validate --format=json | jq .summary` parses cleanly
  - `gocell validate --format=sarif` SARIF 2.1.0 shape
  - `gocell validate --format=yaml` exit 1 with `"unknown format"` message
  - `gocell check contract-health --format=json` emits findings array
  - `gocell check contract-health` text mode shows METHOD / PATH columns

author: ethan-is
body:
## Summary
- Harden `@SubContainer` same-name wiring so implicit auto-wiring only remains a single-candidate convenience and ambiguous or unparseable wiring becomes a diagnostic.
- Align macro, build-support hierarchy validation, docs, examples, and CI/release gates around the current 4.0.0 behavior.
- Reduce public runtime helper surface by generating deferred cells locally, and add a README decision guide for choosing InnoDI versus adjacent DI libraries.

## Root Cause
- The macro previously treated omitted wiring, explicit empty wiring, and unparseable explicit wiring too similarly, which could either generate broken child initializers or silently drop intended dependencies.
- Build-support hierarchy validation also had parity gaps: `withNames` did not always validate like `with`, and conflicting same-name wiring could be bypassed when `bindings:` was present.
- Some examples and fixtures assumed the local checkout/package identity was exactly `InnoDI`, which made path-independent CI brittle.

## Notable Changes
- Require explicit `with:` / `withNames:` / `bindings:` when parent candidates make implicit sub-container wiring ambiguous.
- Support explicit empty `with: []` / `withNames: []` as an intentional `Child()` call.
- Reject non-literal `with:` / `withNames:` inputs instead of falling back to empty wiring.
- Diagnose `with:` + `withNames:` and same-name wiring + `bindings:` conflicts in both macro and build-support validation.
- Add checkout-path-independent CI coverage and release macro performance gating.
- Update DocC, README, internal comments, and roadmap wording to match current behavior.

## Validation
- `swift test --filter WorkspaceHierarchyBuildValidatorTests`
- `swift test`
- `swift run InnoDI-DependencyGraph --root . --validate-dag`
- `git diff --check`

### Motivation
- Implement an e-commerce product ordering workflow with on-chain LTT (THB-LTT) payments and signed QR payloads for secure payment hints.
- Add persistent models and APIs to manage product orders, shipping addresses, shipments, and seller payouts to support marketplace flows.

### Description
- Introduced constants in `apps.accounts.constants` for the new token (`TOKEN_SYMBOL`, `TOKEN_NAME`, `BLOCKCHAIN_NAME`, etc.) and updated `ChainReceipt` display mapping to use the new token symbol.
- Added new models and migrations for product ordering: `ProductOrder`, `ProductShipment`, `SellerPayout`, and `UserShippingAddress`, and added related fields and constraints in `models.py` and generated migrations `0031_*` and `0032_*`.
- Implemented `ProductOrderService` and `ProductPaymentDetectionService` in `apps.accounts.services` to create orders, lock/release stock, build signed QR payloads using HMAC (`PAYMENT_QR_SIGNING_SECRET`), mark orders paid, ship, confirm receipt and mark settled, and to sync product payments from the daemon; also added helper functions `sign_product_qr_payload`, `verify_product_qr_signature` and `build_product_qr_signature_payload`.
- Added REST endpoints and serializers to manage shipping addresses and full product order lifecycle including `ProductOrderListCreateAPIView`, `ProductOrderDetailAPIView`, `SellerProductOrder*` endpoints, `ProductOrderTxHintAPIView`, `ProductOrderMarkPaidAPIView`, and `AdminProductOrderMarkSettledAPIView`, plus URL routing in `product_order_urls.py` and inclusion in project `urls.py`.
- Added management commands `sync_product_payments` and `release_expired_product_orders` to run payment sync and expired-order stock release tasks, and a small help output for summaries.
- Extended serializers to include settlement metadata for membership plans and currency display mapping, and added `UserShippingAddress`, `ProductOrder` and related serializers to `serializers.py`.
- Added settings and environment variables in `config/settings.py` and `.env.example`: `PRODUCT_ORDER_EXPIRE_MINUTES`, `PRODUCT_PLATFORM_RECEIVE_ADDRESS`, and `PAYMENT_QR_SIGNING_SECRET`.
- Added comprehensive tests in `apps.accounts.tests` covering shipping address CRUD, product order creation and QR payload/signature verification, admin/seller/buyer flows (mark paid, ship, confirm received, mark settled), payment sync scenarios (paid/underpaid/overpaid), stock lock/release behavior, and command invocation.

### Testing
- Ran the `apps.accounts` test suite (Django `APITestCase`) including the new `ProductOrderFlowAPITestCase`, membership/payment detection tests, and management command tests; all tests completed successfully locally.
- Exercised the new management commands via `management.call_command('sync_product_payments')` and `management.call_command('release_expired_product_orders')` in tests and verified expected summary output strings were present.

## Summary

Updates the GitHub App `github.read` doctor to accept GitHub's implicit returned `metadata=read` installation-token permission while still requesting only the explicit narrow read permissions needed for the autonomous lane.

## Existing Code Audit

The token request body remains limited to `actions`, `checks`, `contents`, and `pull_requests` at `read`.

The previous failure was in returned-permission validation: GitHub always returns `metadata=read` on installation tokens, and the doctor incorrectly treated that as an unexpected permission.

## Robustness

- Separates requested read permissions from returned read permissions.
- Keeps elevated or unrelated permissions rejected.
- Adds regression coverage for implicit `metadata=read`.
- Keeps the env bootstrap test isolated from the shared checkout's ignored `.env.local.refs` file.

## Impact

This lets the Phase 0B GitHub App service-account read lane pass live verification without broadening the requested GitHub App scope.

Live manual verification passed from Tim's terminal: the lane minted a short-lived token narrowed to `governada/app`, verified repo read, PR read, Actions workflow-run read, and check-run read.

## 概要

`BREAKING CHANGE:` フッターを CI / workflows などリポジトリ運用上の変更に使用してしまうことを防ぐルールを CLAUDE.md に追記する（または新規作成する）。

## 背景

PR `chore: migrate reusable workflows to v3.0.0` で commit message に書いた `BREAKING CHANGE:` フッターが、release-please の `bump-minor-pre-major: true` 設定下で minor bump (0.x → 0.(x+1).0) のシグナルとして拾われた。

再発防止として、`BREAKING CHANGE:` フッターは「リリースされるパッケージ / 公開アセットの互換性を破る変更にのみ」使用するルールを明文化する。

### Motivation
- Standardize `intraday_bar_id` to a canonical ISO 4-hour close-time string (e.g. `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z`) across models, storage, and runtime so values are unambiguous and validated.
- Provide a clear migration path for legacy integer millisecond timestamps stored in SQLite while refusing new integer writes.
- Harden intraday runner and feature builders to validate incoming contexts and prevent mixing integer and canonical string representations.

### Description
- Changed type annotations for `intraday_bar_id` from `int | None` to `str | None` in feature, axis, phase, and state models and `FeatureBundle`/`RunReport` structures.
- Updated SQLite schema for `run_metadata.intraday_bar_id` from `INTEGER` to `TEXT`, and adjusted `init_db` expectations and tests accordingly.

- Updated intraday runner to reject writes that provide integer `intraday_bar_id`, to convert legacy integer rows to canonical strings on read (with strict validation of alignment to 4h UTC boundaries), and to validate `intraday_cache_bar_id` types from context rows.
- Reworked report manifest path generation to use `build_run_manifest_path` when writing intraday noop reports and adjusted related call sites.

- Added new tests and adjusted existing tests to cover the new contract: `tests/test_t19_intraday_id_contracts.py`, `tests/test_t19_analysis_output_paths.py`, and updates to related unit tests to reflect schema and behavior changes.

### Testing
- Ran the automated test suite with `pytest`, including new tests `tests/test_t19_intraday_id_contracts.py` and `tests/test_t19_analysis_output_paths.py`, and existing tests updated for schema/type changes, and all tests passed.

author: anguijm
body:
## Summary

Plan-only PR for issue #39. Routes the design through `.github/workflows/council.yml` per CLAUDE.md §"What counts as approval". **Implementation does NOT begin until council posts a synthesis + human types `approved` / `ship it` / `proceed`.**

Plan: `.harness/active_plan.md` (committed in this PR).

### Architecture decision

**Section-as-note** (extend `notes` with `parent_note_id` + `section_path`), **NOT** a separate `chunks` table:

- Issue #39 specifies this design verbatim.
- Existing per-cohort `notes` RLS policies cover sections without modification (`supabase/migrations/20260417000002_rls_policies.sql:49-74`).
- Existing `flashcard-gen` handler fans out per-section with no code changes — its idempotency already keys on `event.data.note_id` (`inngest/src/functions/flashcard-gen.ts:387`).

### How the 7 council non-negotiables from the handoff stub map

| # | Concern | Resolution |
|---|---------|------------|
| 1 | Prompt-injection per-chunk | Existing `SIMPLIFIER_V1` + `FLASHCARD_GEN_V1` wrap untrusted content; no new LLM callsite added by the chunker. Test: `packages/prompts/src/index.test.ts:8-10`. |
| 2 | Haiku + permanent cache + token cap | Chunking is structural (no LLM call); section-notes ARE the cache (durable in Postgres, idempotent via `unique source_ingestion_id`); Tier B unchanged. |
| 3 | Idempotent on `note_id` (not `event.id`) | Each section gets its own UUID; `flashcard-gen` already uses `event.data.note_id`. |
| 4 | Per-cohort RLS | Existing notes policy applies; new `check_section_note_cohort_integrity` trigger guards service-role writes (mirrors `concept_links` pattern). |
| 5 | Tier A trigger rate limit | Existing `makeIngestEventLimiter` (5/user/hour fail-closed). No new tier. |
| 6 | No PII in logs | Extends `flashcard-gen.ts:408-413` structured-log pattern; new test asserts no body content in error logs. |
| 7 | a11y for downstream UI | Recorded as a requirement for the follow-up UI PR (out of scope here — backend job only). |

### Pre-emptive rebuttal-proofing (per CLAUDE.md §"Rebutting council findings")

Plan §"Rebuttal-proofing" addresses the most likely raw-critique hallucinations with file:line citations:

- "Missing RLS on `chunks` table" → no chunks table exists.
- "Missing cohort isolation" → `check_section_note_cohort_integrity` trigger.
- "Missing prompt-injection wrapping" → already present in existing prompts.
- "Missing rate limit" → Tier A already covers ingest events.
- "PII in logs" → structured-log pattern + test assertion.

### Three questions intentionally deferred to council

1. Parent-note `body_md` retention vs. TOC-summary replacement.
2. Whether the parent doc gets its own embedding.
3. Delete cascade strategy (currently `on delete restrict`).

Defaults in plan are conservative — council is welcome to push back on any.

## Test plan

- [ ] Council workflow runs and posts `<!-- council-report -->` comment.
- [ ] Lead Architect synthesis surfaced to human.
- [ ] Human approves (or requests revisions).
- [ ] Implementation phases (described in plan §"Phased execution") begin only after approval, each as a separate commit on this branch (each push re-runs council).

## Summary

- New `PiiPolicyTab` admin UI under **Settings → AI → PII detection** wired into both the legacy `SettingsPage.tsx` and the live `settings-nav.ts` + `SettingsPanelRoute.tsx`. Admin-only + `useEnterprise().hasFeature('pii_detection')`-gated, with an upgrade-prompt fallback when the licence does not grant the feature.
- New shared Zod schemas at `@compendiq/contracts/src/schemas/pii-policy.ts` (`PiiPolicySchema`, `PiiPolicyResponseSchema`, `PiiPolicyPutBodySchema`, `DEFAULT_PII_POLICY`, plus closed string-literal arrays + `*_LABELS` maps for every axis). The EE overlay imports these verbatim — single source of truth for the wire shape.
- New `pii:policy:changed` entry on the `CacheBusChannel` union in `core/services/redis-cache-bus.ts`. The EE overlay's `setPolicy()` publishes on this channel after every successful PUT so any future cached policy getter invalidates cluster-wide within ~1 s.
- New `docs/ADMIN-GUIDE.md` "PII Detection (Enterprise, v0.4+)" section.
- New `docs/USER-GUIDE.md` "PII Protection (Enterprise)" section.
- New `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry.

## Form coverage

The form covers a master enable toggle, a 0..1 confidence-threshold slider, the async LLM-as-judge mode (off / flagged-only / always) plus a `LlmUsecase` dropdown that picks which provider/model billing path the judge calls flow through, a per-use-case action table (the five PII scan call sites — `chat` / `improve` / `summary` / `generate` / `auto_tag` — each independently configurable as `off` / `flag-only` / `redact-and-publish` / `block-publication`), and a checkbox grid for the closed PII category union.

Save reads via TanStack Query with a 30 s stale time, PUTs the wrapped `{ policy }` envelope, and invalidates on success. The form 404-tolerates a missing EE overlay with an inline "API not registered yet" notice (Save force-disabled in that state) — same pattern as the AI Review / IP allowlist / webhooks tabs.
