author: pizzimenti
body:
## Summary

Three UI-shaping features for v0.4.0, plus a perf fix for mic-button click latency.

- **Symbolic toolbar icons + icon-only theme button.** Voice Models, theme, and mute actions switch to `*-symbolic` glyphs so they pick up the palette in both Breeze Light and Dark. Theme button drops its dynamic text label and uses `Kirigami.DisplayHint.IconOnly`; Auto/Light/Dark sub-actions unchanged.
- **Conversation log verbose vs simple modes.** New eye-icon toggle in the Conversation pane header switches between simple (final user/assistant turns only) and verbose (also shows pipeline status: Transcribing, Thinking, Generating voice, Speaking). Verbose entries render as plain italic purple `#9b6bcc` text inline — no bubble. Persisted via QSettings (`log_verbose_mode`). Filter is applied at capture; toggling on records only forward. Implementation adds `role="status"` to `ConversationModel` plus a `StateNameRole` for the raw `AppState.value`.
- **Cap window width and drop large two-column layout.** `maximumWidth = Kirigami.Units.gridUnit * 49` and `Qt.WindowMaximizeButtonHint` removed from window flags. The large dashboard layout (`largeMode`, `dashboardColumns`, `largeMicPaneComponent`, `largeDashboardRow`, `largeMicPriorityMode`) is removed entirely. Two responsive views remain: medium and compact. `MainWindow.qml` shrank from 882 → 778 lines.
- **Pre-warm `sounddevice` + verbose UI logging.** `MicrophoneRecorder.start()` lazy-imported `sounddevice` on first call, loading PortAudio on the main Qt thread between mic-button click and next paint (100-500 ms). The import is now pre-warmed in `app.main()`. `VOICEAGENT_VERBOSE_UI=1` env var bumps the file log to DEBUG; new `ui-timing label=<name> ms=<float>` entries trace the click chain (window slot → recorder.start → sounddevice import → stream open).

## What works

- All 93 tests pass (90 baseline + 3 new for the `status` role).
- `./voiceagent-compiletest.sh` ends with `compile ok`.
- The compiletest stub gained the matching `logVerboseMode` property and `setLogVerboseMode` slot so it stays in sync with the real `MainWindow` surface.
- `AGENTS.md` softening: review-guideline line on responsive layouts now reflects two layouts (was three); the two "no statuses in bubbles" lines acknowledge verbose log mode while keeping bubbles reserved for final user/assistant content.
- Version bumped 0.3.3 → 0.4.0 in `pyproject.toml`, `PKGBUILD`, `packaging/PKGBUILD.aur`, `src/voiceagent/__init__.py`.

## What doesn't yet (deferred, not blockers)

- Direct `MainWindow`-level integration tests for `logVerboseMode` and the `_apply_state` push path are not added. The repo has no `MainWindow` unit-test surface today (it's the deferred FOLLOWUPS item "Add MainWindow-level integration tests"). The model-side change (status role + `StateNameRole`) is covered in `tests/test_conversation_model.py`.
- Visual confirmation of the `#9b6bcc` purple against Breeze Light and Dark backgrounds is a manual check (see Test plan). If contrast is insufficient on Dark, swap to `#b794d6`.
- The `sounddevice` pre-warm only addresses the import cost. The remaining cost (`sd.RawInputStream` open + start) still runs on the main thread. If the PortAudio open is the dominant cost on this hardware, the diagnostic logs will show it via `ui-timing label=audio.stream_open_and_start` and a follow-up can move that to a worker thread.

## Test plan

- [ ] Launch `python -m voiceagent` on the desktop session — toolbar icons read cleanly in Breeze Light AND Dark; theme button has no text label
- [ ] Window cannot be widened beyond `gridUnit * 49`; maximize button is absent or disabled
- [ ] Medium and compact responsive layouts render correctly across the supported width range
- [ ] Verbose toggle in the Conversation pane header toggles `view-visible-symbolic` ↔ `view-hidden-symbolic` icon
- [ ] With verbose ON: push-to-talk → record → STT → LLM → TTS round trip shows "Transcribing…", "Thinking…", "Generating voice…", "Speaking…" inline as italic purple text between user and assistant bubbles
- [ ] With verbose OFF: same round trip yields a clean transcript (only user + assistant bubbles, plus any system rows for model/voice loading)
- [ ] Verbose toggle persists across an app relaunch
- [ ] Sticky-to-bottom scroll behavior intact when status entries are appended
- [ ] System/error messages (model loading, TTS loading, errors) remain visible regardless of verbose toggle state
- [ ] Mic-button click → first visible response feels snappier than v0.3.3 (the pre-warm fix)
- [ ] Optional: launch with `VOICEAGENT_VERBOSE_UI=1`; tail `~/.local/share/voiceagent/voiceagent.log` and confirm `ui-timing label=...` DEBUG entries appear during a mic-button click

## Summary

User flagged that prior docs referenced legacy keys. Per Supabase official Next.js quickstart and the 2025-07 [jwt-signing-keys announcement](https://supabase.com/blog/jwt-signing-keys), the legacy JWT keys are replaced by opaque keys:

| Old (legacy JWT) | New (canonical) | Format |
|---|---|---|
| \`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY\` | **\`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY\`** | \`sb_publishable_<22>_<8>\` |
| \`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\` | **\`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY\`** | \`sb_secret_<22>_<8>\` |

## Changes

- \`docs/external-setup-guide.md §2.3\` — replaces "Service role key" section with "API keys (new format)" describing both new keys + migration note + canonical doc links
- \`docs/external-setup-guide.md §6\` — Vercel env table updated
- \`docs/decisions/0003-persistence-strategy.md\` — addendum recording the rename
- \`lib/db/supabase-env.ts\` (new) — accessors prefer new names, fall back to legacy with single \`console.warn\`. Smooth transition for projects mid-migration.
- \`tests/supabase-env.test.ts\` (new, 7 cases) — preference, fallback, single-warn, missing keys, composed reader.

## CI

\`\`\`
$ npm run ci
Test Files  23 passed (23)
Tests  174 passed (174)
Red-team CI gate PASSED.
✓ Compiled successfully
exit=0
\`\`\`

## User-facing action

After merging, rename in \`.env.local\` AND fetch fresh values from Supabase dashboard (opaque keys cannot be derived from legacy JWTs):

\`\`\`bash
# Old
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=eyJh...
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=eyJh...

# New
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_xxx
SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY=sb_secret_xxx
\`\`\`

The accessor in \`lib/db/supabase-env.ts\` reads the new names first; if it sees the legacy names it warns once but keeps working, so this PR doesn't break anyone mid-transition.

author: ronnyabuto
body:
## What

**Supply chain hardening:** `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-python` pinned to commit SHAs rather than mutable version tags. Mutable tags were the attack vector in the March 2025 tj-actions incident.

**CI matrix:** Python 3.13 added to match pyproject.toml classifiers — claiming 3.13 support without testing it was misleading.

**New `security` job (CI + publish):**
- `pip-audit` — checks all installed packages against the PyPA advisory database; fails the build on any known CVE
- `bandit` — SAST scan of `src/` at medium/high severity (`-ll`), test files excluded to suppress false positives

**Publish workflow — version consistency gate:** New `version-check` job asserts the GitHub release tag matches `pyproject.toml` before any build or PyPI upload runs. A tag mismatch exits immediately with a clear error, preventing "v0.2.0" tags that ship `0.1.9` packages.

All existing publish jobs now depend on `version-check` and run the security scan first.

author: wnt
body:
A drained collector loop holds no water, so neither the freeze drain
nor the overheat drain (which both circulate fluid through the loop)
can fire. Sending operators a "Freeze drain may activate at 4°C"
notification in that state is misleading — the system is already in
the post-drain protected state.

Guards both checkFreezeWarning and checkOverheatWarning on the
flags.collectors_drained field already published in the controller's
state snapshot. Adds a Collectors / DRAINED · FILLED tile to the
Status view's Critical Components grid so the protected state is
visible at a glance.

author: ohenak
body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 1 of the Luopan compass app — a fully functional compass screen with magnetometer-based heading using Madgwick 9-DOF sensor fusion, a 5-step calibration wizard, real-time interference detection, and a 5-dimension confidence model.

- **Sensor fusion**: Madgwick filter (quaternion-based, gimbal-lock-safe) fusing uncalibrated magnetometer + accelerometer + optional gyroscope; no-gyroscope fallback path with advisory
- **Calibration wizard**: 5-step flow (pre-check → guidance → 3D collection → ellipsoid fit → result); GOOD/FAIR/POOR quality classification; two-tap confirmation for POOR; rollback slot for safe re-calibration
- **Interference detection**: EMA-based geomagnetic baseline; field-magnitude and inclination deviation triggers at 15%/25% thresholds; MODERATE/WARNING states; tap-to-dismiss banner (resets on CLEAR)
- **Confidence model**: 5-dimension min-aggregation (interference, tilt, noise variance, calibration age, calibration quality); STUCK→SENSOR_ERROR, STABILIZING→STABILIZING overrides
- **Edge cases**: no-magnetometer error screen, sensor-stuck detection (2 s gap), power-saving advisory (sub-15 Hz rate), heading frozen on STUCK
- **Persistence**: SQLCipher-encrypted Room database; current + rollback calibration slots; `DatabaseKeyManager` for passphrase
- **Localization**: English, Simplified Chinese (`zh`), Traditional Chinese (`zh-rTW`), Japanese (`ja`)
- **Screen-on**: `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` + `WakeLockManager` belt-and-suspenders

## What was reviewed

Full PDLC pipeline ran against `REQ-luopan-p1-core-compass.md`:
- REQ cross-review (se-review ✅, te-review ✅)
- FSPEC cross-review (se-review ✅, te-review ✅)
- TSPEC cross-review (pm-review ✅, te-review ✅)
- PLAN cross-review (pm-review ✅, te-review ✅)
- PROPERTIES cross-review (pm-review ✅, se-review ✅)
- Implementation batches 0–6 executed by tech-lead
- PROPERTIES test suite (19 JVM property tests, all passing)
- Final codebase review — 4 iterations; pm-review ✅ Approved, te-review ✅ Approved

## Known limitations (Phase 2 scope)

- Ellipsoid fit is sphere-only (hard-iron offset); full soft-iron correction deferred
- `CalibrationRepository.save()` is non-atomic (two Room upserts); write-then-rename atomic swap deferred
- `PROP-FUSION-06` test uses synthetic JSON sequence, not real hardware capture
- `PROP-SENSOR-04` zero-magnitude immediate STUCK not implemented in `SensorStateMonitor`
- All Espresso/instrumented tests are stubs (Phase 2 gate)
- Confidence badge text hardcoded English (Low finding, Phase 2)

## Build notes

Requires Java 17 (`JAVA_HOME` must point to JDK 17 — not 25/26). Set in Android Studio via **File → Project Structure → SDK Location → Gradle JDK**.

```
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/Cellar/openjdk@17/17.0.19/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home
./gradlew assembleDebug
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Build debug APK: `./gradlew assembleDebug`
- [ ] Run JVM unit tests: `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest`
- [ ] Launch on device/emulator — emulator shows no-magnetometer screen (expected; no hardware mag)
- [ ] On physical device: verify compass rose rotates with device, heading displays to 0.1°
- [ ] Rotate aggressively → "Stabilizing…" badge → settles to heading
- [ ] Cover mag sensor with metal → interference banner appears; tap to dismiss
- [ ] Complete calibration wizard → quality badge shown; confidence improves
- [ ] Background app → verify no battery drain (sensors release via Flow `awaitClose`)

## Summary

End-of-session wrap. Closes the 2026-04-23/25 arc that took this repo from "extracted but never run" to "live data shipping to Firestore."

The doc updates are the council-review payload (138 lines across 5 files). The data commits land the actual pipeline output state from the parked-19 unpark run; council strips `data/**` via `DIFF_EXCLUDES` and won't see them.

## Why

User directive at session close: *"wrap it up, update all stale docs, prep files for handoff, update readme, do anything else you can think of to preserve appropriate context for the next session, run it all thru council. then we'll reset."*

Prior session-close commits this week (`1d28464`, `0c781fe`, `84aab64`, `526b7d1`, `dc60a3c`, `b6baf39`) all went direct-to-main under the doc/state-capture lane. This one routes through council per the explicit "run it all thru council" ask — and per the precedent in the urban-explorer 2026-04-20 learnings entry that knowledge-content edits deserve council review even when the diff is markdown-only.

## What changed

### Doc updates

- **`README.md`** (+13/−2): "Status" updated from "operational" → "operational and producing live Firestore data" with concrete numbers (16/19 parked metros ingested, 4 verified). New "Open work" section enumerates issues #5–#9, #11, #12 with one-line scopes.

The "Session 2026-04-23/24 summary" now extends to 2026-04-25 covering the validation arc + the three porting-miss bug-fix commits + the production ingest result. "Open follow-up issues" adds #11 + #12, notes #10 closed. "When you come back to this repo" rewritten as a numbered cold-start checklist with `.harness/learnings.md` elevated to step 2. Test-count corrected 31 → 41.
- **`src/pipeline/README.md`** (+18/−8): Test count 31 → 41. New "Entry-point smoke" subsection documenting the porting-miss bug class (3 instances: `90b8c2a`, `f627d83`, `1f173b7`) and pointing at issue #12.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** (+10/−1): New "Admin override" subsection codifies the pattern used twice this session (PR #3, PR #4) — when it's appropriate, what's required, how it differs from `[skip council]`. Also enriches the `src/pipeline/` description with `phase_c_threshold.py` + the `build_cache.ts` (strict Zod) vs `enrich_ingest.ts` (no Zod, `enrichment-*` filter) contrast.

### Data commits (council won't see these)

- All 19 parked metros now have fresh-as-of-2026-04-25 scrape outputs: `data/wikipedia/{city}.md` + `data/reddit/{city}.md` (17/19 for Reddit; algiers + cincinnati had no quality-gated subreddit posts, expected).

- 3 failures at `data/research-output/failed/` (geneva + lisbon + the prior honolulu).

## Out of scope (intentional)

- **Honolulu recovery** — one-step `mv` + single-city re-ingest, documented in handoff "Now" tier; user can do it whenever convenient.
- **Issue #11** (scraper refinement: Atlas Obscura, Infatuation, retire SBL) — separate scoped follow-up; would catch the "scrapers run but URL pattern is wrong" residual.
- **Issue #12** (CI smoke-test on entry-point scripts) — separate scoped follow-up; would catch the next porting-miss bug at port time. Three instances this session is enough data points to file but not enough urgency to land in this PR.
- **Issues #5–#9** — pre-existing follow-ups from earlier rounds.

## 概要

`BREAKING CHANGE:` フッターを CI / workflows などリポジトリ運用上の変更に使用してしまうことを防ぐルールを CLAUDE.md に追記する（または新規作成する）。

## 背景

PR `chore: migrate reusable workflows to v3.0.0` で commit message に書いた `BREAKING CHANGE:` フッターが、release-please の `bump-minor-pre-major: true` 設定下で minor bump (0.x → 0.(x+1).0) のシグナルとして拾われた。

- 実害発生: nozomiishii/git-harvest で 0.1.20 → 0.2.0 と誤判定 (release PR #88、close 済み)。修正後は 0.1.21 (#110)。

再発防止として、`BREAKING CHANGE:` フッターは「リリースされるパッケージ / 公開アセットの互換性を破る変更にのみ」使用するルールを明文化する。

- 元事故 PR: nozomiishii/git-harvest#106

author: jbouse
body:
## Summary

Adds three new admin-only MQTT client ban management commands backed by the EMQX v5 HTTP API.

## New Commands

- **`mqtt.ban <clientid> [days] [reason]`** — Bans a client by ID for a configurable duration (default: 7 days, via `EMQX_BAN_DEFAULT_DAYS`). Requires confirmation.
- **`mqtt.unban <clientid>`** — Removes an active ban for a client ID. Requires confirmation.
- **`mqtt.ban.list [page] [limit]`** — Lists all active bans with paginated Discord embed output.

## Changes

### New Files
- `scripts/lib/mqtt-emqx-api.js` — EMQX v5 HTTP API client (`banClient`, `unbanClient`, `listBans`, `getDefaultBanDays`)
- `test/mqtt-emqx-api.test.js` — 16 unit tests for the API client
- `test/mqtt-ban-format.test.js` — 13 unit tests for ban embed builders

### Modified Files
- `scripts/mqtt.js` — ban handler functions and command registrations
- `scripts/lib/mqtt-discord-format.js` — `buildBanEmbed`, `buildUnbanEmbed`, `buildBanListEmbed`, `parseBanUntilUnix`, `formatBanUntil`
- `.env.example` — added `EMQX_API_URL`, `EMQX_API_KEY`, `EMQX_API_SECRET`, `EMQX_BAN_DEFAULT_DAYS`

## Details

- All commands are admin-only (`MQTT_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS`) with full audit trail via `wrapHandler`
- `mqtt.ban` and `mqtt.unban` require `confirm: "always"`; `mqtt.ban.list` does not
- `target_clientid` added to `buildAuditMetadata` for ban/unban audit records
- Ban list renders one embed field per entry with Discord native `<t:UNIX:f>` timestamps (reader's local timezone), 📅 / ♾️ emoji indicators, and optional ban reason on a second line
- Safely handles all EMQX `until` formats returned by the API: Unix integer, ISO string, `"infinity"`, and `null`
- Pagination displayed in embed footer only when results span multiple pages; hard cap at 25 fields (Discord embed limit)
- 69 tests all passing

author: danny-avila
body:
## Summary

Skills were activating on every agent run that had the capability + RBAC enabled, regardless of whether the user (ephemeral) or author (persisted) had explicitly opted in. The root cause was `scopeSkillIds(undefined)` falling through to "full accessible catalog" whenever `agent.skills` was unset — the default state for any agent created before skills existed and for every ephemeral agent.

This PR enforces strict opt-in:

- **Ephemeral agent** → per-conversation skills badge toggle (`req.body.ephemeralAgent.skills`). Toggle ON = full accessible catalog; OFF = no skills.
- **Persisted agent** → new `skills_enabled` master switch on the agent document, surfaced as a toggle in the Agent Builder skills section.
  - `skills_enabled: true` + empty/undefined allowlist → full accessible catalog
  - `skills_enabled: true` + non-empty `skills[]` → narrow to those ids
  - `skills_enabled: false` / undefined → no skills available (even if allowlist is set)

## Migration / Breaking Change

> **Not a concern in practice.** The skills feature has not shipped to any user — this PR targets `feat/agent-skills`, which is still in development. No production agents exist with a configured `skills[]` array, so no migration is required. Going forward, every agent author opts in explicitly via the new toggle.

## Implementation

- New `resolveAgentScopedSkillIds` helper in `@librechat/api` centralises the activation predicate. Wired into the primary-agent init path, the handoff/discovery accessor, the subagent loop, and both OpenAI controllers (`openai.js`, `responses.js`) so the four call sites share one source of truth. The lower-level `scopeSkillIds` is now marked `@internal`; runtime callers should prefer the resolver so the activation predicate is enforced uniformly.
- Schema: `skills_enabled?: boolean` added to `agent.ts` (Mongoose), `Agent` / `AgentCreateParams` / `AgentUpdateParams` (data-provider types), Zod create/update validators, and the form default.
- Agent Builder UI: master toggle above the existing allowlist; help text explains what each state does. Allowlist UI dims + disables when the toggle is off (selections preserved). The label is associated to the toggle via `htmlFor` for keyboard/click affordance. Toggle handler emits explicit `false` (not `undefined`) so save doesn't get stripped by `removeNullishValues`.
- Frontend `$` popover (`SkillsCommand.tsx`) mirrors the same activation logic so the UI never offers skills the backend would refuse to activate.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: 134 backend (`packages/api/src/agents/__tests__/skills.test.ts`) covering the new persisted-agent activation matrix.
- [x] Frontend tests: 19 in `SkillsCommand.spec.tsx`, including the new "skills_enabled:true + empty allowlist = full catalog" path and the "skills_enabled:false hides everything" regression.
- [x] Controller specs (`openai.spec.js`, `responses.unit.spec.js`) updated to mock `resolveAgentScopedSkillIds` so the agent init path runs to completion under jest.
- [x] Manual end-to-end against a live server with diagnostic logging:
  - Ephemeral, badge OFF → `scoped=0` (skill tool not registered)
  - Ephemeral, badge ON → `scoped=N` (full ACL catalog)
  - Persisted, toggle OFF → `scoped=0`
  - Persisted, toggle ON, no allowlist → `scoped=N` (full catalog)
  - Persisted, toggle ON, allowlist set → `scoped=M` (intersection)
  - Persisted, toggle ON → save → toggle OFF → save: version bumps both saves, no spurious "no changes" toast.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean across `packages/api`.

body:
## Summary

`bm-code-management` を「コード管理ライフサイクル」を扱う skill として再構成し、`references/` で領域別に分割（skill-creator の **Pattern 2: domain-specific organization**）。

- `skills/bm-code-management/SKILL.md`（80 行）: 概要 + navigation + 共通項
  - 共通項: Pre-flight / パッケージマネージャー検出 / `bm sync --dry` ガードレール / 認証
- `skills/bm-code-management/references/ts-config.md`: `defineAction` / `defineConfig` 編集ワークフロー、型エラー復旧、削除の論理削除挙動（docs 未記載の暗黙知）
- `skills/bm-code-management/references/js-action.md`: JS アクションのコード本体作成ワークフロー（型定義の Read、`bm sync --dry` での差分確認）

## docs と重複する記述を排除

ユーザー方針「docs を参照したら分かることは skill に書かない」に従い、各 reference から docs に記述がある内容を削除:

- 組み込み関数（`executeAction` / `createActionJob` / `wait`）の引数仕様 → docs 参照に委譲
- JS アクションの利用不可機能（JSON 値・SQL パラメータ等） → docs 参照に委譲
- エラーハンドリングの推奨パターン（`return` / `throw` / `ResultError`） → docs 参照に委譲
- JS アクションの宣言コード例（`class: \"javascript\"`, `readFile`） → docs 参照に委譲

## CI/CD は skill 化しない判断

CI/CD（GitHub Actions / OIDC / 環境別反映）は当初 reference として含めていましたが、ユーザー判断で削除。docs 直接参照に委ねます。

- 公式ドキュメント: <https://docs.basemachina.com/preview/code_management/ci_cd/>
- 2 ブランチ: <https://docs.basemachina.com/preview/code_management/examples/two_branch/>
- 3 ブランチ: <https://docs.basemachina.com/preview/code_management/examples/three_branch/>

## skill 側に残した「docs にない / エージェント特有」の知見

- ワークフロー（Read → 編集 → tsc → `bm sync --dry` → 引き渡し）の手順
- `node_modules/@basemachina/action/dist/*.d.ts` を Read してから書く実務（docs だけだと最新シグネチャを取りこぼしうる）

body: ## Summary Initial scaffold for `sushi` — a mobile-first PWA for restaurant staff to view schedules and swap shifts without training. **Architecture** - Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 (via `@tailwindcss/vite`). - Single `useReducer` in `src/state/shiftsReducer.ts` is the **only** place shift state mutates. Every action is a guarded transition from the spec's table; guard failures return state unchanged (silent no-op). `assignedUserId` is mutated in **exactly one** case (`APPROVE`), which — combined with the synchronous nature of `useReducer` — guarantees a shift can never be assigned to two users. - Two contexts: `ShiftsContext` (state + dispatch) and `SessionContext` (acting-as user, staff/manager toggle, active tab). No Redux, no Firebase, no backend — mock data only per spec. - Pure selectors in `src/state/selectors.ts` derive `nextShiftForUser`, `boardForUser`, `pendingApprovalQueue`, `weeklyHoursFor`, `wouldExceedOvertime`, `hasOverlapForUser`. Views never filter inline. **UI** - Mobile frame: `max-w-md mx-auto h-screen relative shadow-2xl` per spec. - Top bar has "Acting as" user picker (testing aid) + Staff/Manager toggle. - Staff mode: 3-tab bottom nav — My Schedule / The Board / Time Off. - Manager mode: replaces the tabs with the Approval Queue (overtime badge is non-blocking, Approve stays enabled). - Inter font bundled locally via `@fontsource/inter`. **Seed data** Four users (2 servers, 2 bartenders) and 15 shifts across the next ~2 weeks. Includes one already-`Offered` shift and one already-`PendingApproval` shift so every screen shows something on first load. Sam Okafor is pre-loaded near 40 hrs to exercise the overtime warning. **Run** ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human Yellow risk — single-user MVP with mock state, no persistence, no backend. - [ ] **State machine correctness** — walk the full lifecycle end to end: Maya clicks "Need coverage" on an Active shift → Alex (a Server) sees it on The Board → Alex claims → switch to Manager → Approve. Shift's `assignedUserId` should now be Alex, status back to Active, visible only on Alex's My Schedule. - [ ] **Role filter on The Board** — as a Bartender, confirm Maya's (Server) offered shift is hidden; as a Server, confirm Jules's (Bartender) offered shift is hidden. - [ ] **Conflict filter** — offer a shift that overlaps one of Alex's existing shifts; confirm Alex does not see it on The Board. - [ ] **Overtime warning (non-blocking)** — make a swap that pushes Sam Okafor over 40 hrs for the week; confirm the red "Overtime" badge appears in the manager queue but Approve is still enabled. - [ ] **Deny returns to Offered** — Deny a pending approval; confirm the shift reappears on The Board for eligible users (original assignee still owns it). - [ ] **Withdraw from board** — Maya clicks "Withdraw" on an offered shift; status returns to Active. - [ ] **Pending visibility** — while a shift is `PendingApproval`, it must still appear on the *offering* user's My Schedule with "Waiting on manager approval" (not reassigned until Approve). - [ ] Visual polish on a real phone: tap targets, scrolling inside the frame, safe-area insets on iOS. ### Notes - `tsc -b` and `vite build` both pass locally. - No tests in this MVP pass — the reducer is structured so guard logic can be unit-tested straightforwardly in a follow-up. - No PWA service worker yet; `vite-plugin-pwa` can be added later without touching state. - No router — single `useState` drives the active tab, matching the "no hidden menus" spirit of the spec. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/fe20f39f6c5d45f1b8e68601a2f1970e Requested by: @anthnylee33 ---

author: kudotaka0421
body:
## Summary

fanc-lab カリキュラム #11 (pprof) のフロント側。\`/lab/pprof\` で「重い処理 1 回 / 100 回」ボタンを押して \`/api/lab/pprof/heavy?n=N\` を発火、押した直後に別ターミナルで \`go tool pprof http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10\` を叩くと flame graph に \`crypto/sha256.block\` が支配的に出るのを観察するための UI。

これで Lab カリキュラム 11 項目すべての UI が埋まったので、未使用になった \`LabPlaceholder.vue\` も削除した。

### UI 構成（凝らない方針通り素朴に）

- **負荷生成セクション**: 2 ボタン (1 回 / 100 回) + 結果表示 (iterations / elapsed / digest 16 文字)
  - n=100 で 3 秒前後ブロックする想定なので axios timeout を 60s に伸ばしてる
- **pprof UI 直リンク**: \`/debug/pprof/\`, \`/debug/pprof/heap\`, \`/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1\` の 3 本
  - target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener\" を付けて新タブ
- **コマンド例**: \`go tool pprof -http=:9090 ...\` (Flame Graph), heap, CLI モード (\`top10\` / \`list Heavy\`) の 3 パターンを \`<pre><code>\` で貼る
- **本番運用ガード注記**: env opt-in / internal LB / auth の方針を画面下に明記して、面接で説明できる材料を UI 自体に持たせる

### 設計判断（PR 解説として残す）

- **GET endpoint を素直に GET する**
  - POST にする理由 (副作用) が無い + UI のリンクとしても使える方が便利
  - レビュアーから「副作用あるなら POST では？」と聞かれても、heavy は読み取り処理 (CPU を食うだけで状態を変えない) なので GET で正しい

- **n=100 で 3 秒前後固まる UI**
  - lab なので「重い処理を実感する」のが目的、ローディング表現は最低限 (running フラグだけ) で充分
  - 本番アプリならこういう同期 long-running は避けて job queue + status polling にするが、それは別 lab (#2 SQS) でやってる

- **pprof UI は新タブで開く**
  - SSE/breaker UI と違って自前で結果を表示する必要がない、go tool pprof のブラウザ UI が圧倒的に便利
  - ブラウザ拡張で flame graph が出る方が体験が良い

### 関連

- バックエンド PR: kudotaka0421/fanc-api#84
- ナレッジ: \`~/.claude/docs/interview/system-design/pprof-essentials.md\`
- カリキュラム: \`~/.claude/docs/interview/system-design/fanc-lab/curriculum.md\` #11

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run build\` が通る (vue-tsc 含む)
- [ ] \`make up-lab\` で backend を起動して \`/lab/pprof\` にアクセス、「重い処理 1 回」が ~30ms で完了
- [ ] 「100 回」を押して 3 秒前後ブロックしてから結果表示
- [ ] その実行中に \`go tool pprof -http=:9090 http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10\` を叩いて flame graph に sha256 が出る
- [ ] pprof UI のリンク 3 本 (\`/debug/pprof/\`, \`/heap\`, \`/goroutine?debug=1\`) が新タブで開く
- [ ] LabIndex から /lab/pprof のリンクが正しく開く

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
## Summary

Phase 8 of the project deployment plan — Dataplane sync visibility in the shell. Surfaces the daemon's existing Dataplane bind state as a pill in the shell UI so the cloud-mode misconfiguration loop becomes a clickable affordance instead of a silent stderr log line.

**Stacked on #23** (Phase 3d). Reuses the daemon HTTP client and discovery flow from #22/#23 — no new endpoints, no new IPC paths.

### The problem this solves

Existing state in this repo:

> *Dataplane connection deferred (2026-04-18) — code wired, runtime offline; needs API key in launchd plist to flip to bound.*

The daemon already computes the bind state in `getDataplaneState()` (server.ts) and emits it as `[Lore MCP] Dataplane ping: bound|offline|error`. But that's a stderr log line. The user's UI gives no indication whether their workspace is actually syncing to the team tenant. **Phase 8 makes the loop visible.**

### What lands

**Rust side (`apps/lore-shell/src-tauri/src/daemon.rs`):**
- `HealthBody` adds optional `dataplane` / `deploymentMode` / `telemetryOptOut` fields. All `#[serde(default)]` — older daemons (<2.1) that omit them still parse.
- `HealthReport` surfaces them to the frontend via `Option<...>`.
- 2 new tests: parses with full Phase 8 body; tolerates missing fields against pre-2.1 daemons.

**TS side (`apps/lore-shell/src/loreClient.ts`):**
- `HealthReport` interface mirrors the new Rust fields.
- `DataplaneState` type union: `unknown` | `offline` | `opted-out` | `bound` | `error`.
- `describeDataplaneState()` — tooltip text per state. The `offline` branch phrases differently for cloud-mode (misconfiguration: "Add `DATAPLANE_API_KEY` to your launchd plist") vs. local-mode (expected: "intentionally not configured").

**UI (`apps/lore-shell/src/App.tsx`):**
- New `<DataplanePill>` renders next to the daemon pill from Phase 3d.

| State        | Pill colour                     | Why                                              |
|--------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `bound`      | green                           | tenant reachable, syncing                        |
| `opted-out`  | grey                            | user disabled telemetry; intentional             |
| `offline`    | **orange** in cloud mode        | misconfiguration — exact remediation in tooltip  |
| `offline`    | grey in local mode              | expected — local-only daemon                     |
| `error`      | red                             | credential present but tenant unreachable        |
| `unknown`    | grey                            | starting up                                      |

Daemon < 2.1 (no `dataplane` field) → "unsupported · daemon <2.1" with explanatory tooltip.

### What this PR does NOT change

- `/api/health` endpoint shape — these fields were already there.
- Daemon-side behaviour — purely UI plumbing.
- The sibling-not-child contract from Phase 3d — shell still never starts, stops, or signals the daemon. We just surface state it already computes.

## Verification

- `cargo test --lib daemon::tests` — 5/5 green (3 existing + 2 new for Phase 8)
- `tsc --noEmit` (apps/lore-shell) — clean
- Manual smoke deferred until #23 lands (this branch is stacked on it)

## Test plan

- [x] Daemon HealthBody parses with all Phase 8 fields
- [x] Daemon HealthBody tolerates missing fields (older daemon)
- [x] TS typecheck clean
- [ ] Manual smoke: with cloud-mode daemon, no API key → orange "offline (no key) · cloud mode" pill with launchd-plist remediation tooltip
- [ ] Manual smoke: with cloud-mode daemon, API key in keychain → green "bound · cloud mode" pill
- [ ] Manual smoke: with local-mode daemon → grey "offline · local mode" pill (expected, not a warning)
- [ ] Manual smoke: against a daemon <2.1 → "unsupported · daemon <2.1" pill

author: chainlensai-ux
body:
### Motivation

- Reduce load and improve resilience when calling CoinGecko/GeckoTerminal by adding a shared in-memory cache and surface stale-cache warnings. 
- Improve Base Radar UX with richer scoring, filtering, sorting, and actionable controls to better surface promising or risky launches. 
- Provide an integrated AI analysis workflow (Clark) to let users ask for concise verdicts or deep analysis from the UI.

### Description

- Adds a small cache utility `lib/coingeckoCache.ts` that performs shared fetch caching with TTL, hit/miss/stale semantics, and an optional `warning` when stale data is used. 
- Integrates the cache into API handlers by updating `/api/radar`, `/api/scan-token`, and `/api/trending` to use `getOrFetchCached` and to include optional `warning` fields in responses. 
- Extends `/api/scan-token` to return cache warnings and refactors `resolveNameToContract` and `fetchPools` to return structured results including warnings. 
- Reworks Base Radar UI `app/terminal/base-radar/page.tsx` with token enrichment (`enrichToken`), radar scoring and trust caps, momentum/status/flags, metrics components, filtering, sorting, tracking toggles, and actions to `Ask Clark` and `Scan` tokens; adjusts layout, styling and behavior for a denser dashboard. 
- Adds a new interactive `Clark AI` page at `app/terminal/clark-ai/page.tsx` that allows importing prompts from Radar, sending structured requests to `/api/clark`, and managing conversation state. 
- Updates `app/terminal/page.tsx` and `components/ClarkChat.tsx` to support initial prompts and a prefill-only mode so the Terminal and Clark components can pre-populate queries. 

### Testing

- Ran a production build with `next build` which completed successfully and reported no type errors. 
- Ran linting with `npm run lint` and unit tests with `npm test` (if present) which completed without failures. 
- Performed smoke API checks against `/api/radar`, `/api/scan-token?query=...`, and `/api/trending` returning `200` and including the expected `warning` fields when cached/stale responses were exercised.

author: sarthak1612
body:
PROBLEM
Installing with `pip install -e ".[all]"` fails on Windows with Python 3.14
because scipy attempts to build from source and requires C17, which is not
supported by MSVC.

This occurs when pre-built wheels for scipy are not available.

Solution

Added a note in the README installation section explaining the issue and
providing a workaround using:

    pip install scipy --only-binary=:all:
    pip install -e "."

This ensures users install pre-built binaries and avoid compilation errors.

Why this helps

Improves installation experience for Windows users on newer Python versions
and prevents confusing build failures.

author: danberry
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the build error from #348 (`Member` and `ModelContext` are non-Sendable, can't be captured in `addTask` closures)
- Delivers the actual ~5x throughput improvement via a `withTaskGroup` that uses only `Sendable` captures

## Root cause of #348's build error

Swift 6.2's `addTask` requires a `sending` closure. `Member` (SwiftData `@Model`) and `ModelContext` are both non-Sendable `@MainActor`-isolated types, so they can't be captured in child task closures regardless of how the task group is annotated.

## How this fix works

**`ContributionService`** — adds a `nonisolated` overload:
```swift
nonisolated func syncContributions(
    login: String,
    memberID: PersistentIdentifier,  // Sendable ✓
    organizationIDs: [String] = [],
    in container: ModelContainer      // Sendable ✓
) async
```
Each call creates its own isolated `ModelContext(container)`, fetches the member by `PersistentIdentifier`, and runs the full network + DB logic off MainActor. The existing `@MainActor` overload (`member: Member, in context: ModelContext`) is unchanged — `AddMemberView` and all tests keep working without modification.

**`BackgroundSyncManager.syncAllContributions`** — extracts only Sendable data before the task group:
```swift
let memberData: [(login: String, id: PersistentIdentifier)] = ...

await withTaskGroup(of: Void.self) { group in
    // all captures: service (Sendable), data.login (String), data.id (PersistentIdentifier),
    //               organizationIDs ([String]), container (ModelContainer) — all Sendable ✓
    group.addTask {
        await service.syncContributions(login: data.login, memberID: data.id, ...)
    }
}
```
Up to 5 tasks run concurrently (cooperative, not parallel — they interleave at `await graphQL.execute(...)` suspension points), keeping 5 API calls in-flight simultaneously.

## Test plan

- [x] `xcodebuild ... build` succeeds with no errors
- [x] All existing `ContributionServiceTests` pass unchanged (they still use the `@MainActor` overload)

body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `_PARSERS_BUILT` was a process-wide global that persisted across pytest test invocations when `PYTHONPATH=""` caused module re-imports. In batch mode, the first test set it to `True`, causing subsequent `cli_main()` calls within the same test worker to skip parser building entirely.
- **Fix**: Removed the unnecessary global `_PARSERS_BUILT` flag. Each `main()` call creates a fresh `ArgumentParser` with its own subparsers instance, so the flag was both unnecessary and harmful.
- **Result**: `test_cli_cite_import.py` (12/12) and `test_cli_import.py` (13/13) now pass in batch mode.

author: larfii
body:
## Summary

Rewrites `integrations/nanobot/README.md` to accurately cover both supported integration paths and to host the gateway-side reference material (adapters, embedding, subject derivation, mapping) that was previously only documented downstream in the nanobot fork.

## Two paths, one shared gateway

- **Path A — `nanobot[mgp]` extra (production)**: always-on `recall_memory` tool plus automatic Consolidator/Dream commit. This is what end users install. Tracks the integration that ships in HKUDS/nanobot PR #3408.
- **Path B — harness in this directory (validation)**: patches stock unmodified Nanobot at runtime with `off / shadow / primary` modes. For MGP CI and staged validation. Behavior unchanged from the previous README; only the surrounding narrative is restructured.

## What's added

- Adapter table for `postgres / oceanbase / lancedb / mem0 / zep` with install commands and required env vars.
- Authentication setup (`api_key` / `bearer`).
- LanceDB embedding configuration: three common recipes (OpenAI / sentence-transformers / OpenRouter) plus the OpenAI-compatible relay template (SiliconFlow, DeepInfra, Together, etc.).
- SaaS adapter notes for mem0 and zep, including the env-var fallback names.
- Adapter switching procedure.
- Common error/symptom table (`MGP_INVALID_OBJECT`, `PolicyDeniedError`, `401`, fail-open degraded calls, group-chat subject collapse).
- Canonical Dream-tag to MGP `(scope, memory_type)` mapping with the explicit note that `identity` is not a valid type — use `profile`.
- Subject (`user_id`) derivation chain (`sender_id → chat_id → default_user_id → getpass.getuser()`).

## Cross-references

- Adds a back-link from `docs/sidecar-integration.md` to this directory.
- Top of the README points readers at the runtime-side reference in `nanobot/agent/mgp/README.md` for skill, tool schema, AgentLoop hooks, and config keys.

## Companion PR

Lets the runtime-side README (HKUDS/nanobot PR #3408) shrink dramatically because gateway-side concerns now have a canonical home here.

## Verification

- 3 mermaid diagrams render (overview, Path B architecture, validation ladder).
- All internal links are repo-relative.
- No code changes; no wheel impact; no version bump.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: ivan-lb
body:
## Summary
- Introduces a six-specialist agentic system under `.claude/` with an orchestrator protocol that classifies, plans, dispatches, validates, and opens PRs.
- Rewrites `CLAUDE.md` as a session front door: branch model, build/test commands, load-bearing constraints, secrets list, specialist routing.
- Adds local quality tooling: curated `.swiftlint.yml`, pre-commit lint hook, commit-msg Conventional Commits hook, one-time install script.
- Wires first CI/CD pipeline: GitHub Actions workflow (lint → build → test → upload xcresult on failure), Dependabot weekly SPM bumps, PR + issue templates.

## Why
This codifies the workflow rules we agreed on (one PR at a time, options-over-decisions, no auto-merge, `dev` as integration branch, `main` as release-only) so they survive across Claude sessions instead of being re-derived each time. It also gets a CI gate on every PR before the codebase grows further.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI workflow runs on this PR (first run — Xcode version or simulator name in `ci.yml` may need a one-line tweak for `macos-15`'s actual installed Xcode; that is `build-ci-specialist`'s first follow-up).
- [ ] Locally: `./scripts/install-hooks.sh` activates hooks; `brew install swiftlint` enables the pre-commit lint check.
- [ ] Branch protection on `dev` and `main` set via GitHub UI (Settings → Branches → require PR + status check + linear history).

## Risks
- **CI workflow may fail on first run.** Expected — the Xcode version pin (`26.0`) and simulator name (`iPhone 16 Pro`) are guesses for what `macos-15` runners ship today. Easy fix once we see the failure.
- **`*.xcscheme` is gitignored globally.** Pre-existing rule, unchanged here. Will silently block any new shared scheme; flagged for follow-up in `gotchas` discussions.
- **`Savely/GoogleService-Info.plist` remains tracked in history.** Now in `.gitignore` (added on `main` with the redesign), so future changes won't be committed. Separate `chore/stop-tracking-firebase-config` PR will `git rm --cached` it. Repo is private and Firebase iOS API keys are not true secrets, so this is hygiene, not an emergency.

## Known follow-up tasks (queued for `build-ci-specialist`)
1. Align deployment target to iOS 26 (project default is 17.0, app is 26.0, tests are 17.5).
2. Investigate duplicate `ContentView.swift` (one in `Savely/`, one in `Savely/Views/`).
3. Decide on the `*.xcscheme` gitignore rule.
4. Make `SavelyTests` / `SavelyUITests` schemes shared if needed.

## Checklist
- [x] Branch named with approved prefix (`chore/`)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits (4 atomic commits, see history)
- [x] No hardcoded user-facing strings introduced
- [x] No secrets staged
- [x] Targets `dev`, not `main`

body:
This follow-up fixes the first post-merge deploy run.

Problem:
- `main` CI passed, but the Deploy workflow failed at staging frontend upload because no `STAGING_*` secrets/variables exist yet.

Change:
- Add a staging config guard that builds the frontend, then skips staging frontend deploy, backend deploy, or smoke checks with explicit GitHub notices if their required config is missing.
- Update CI/CD docs to document this behavior and the required staging secrets.

This keeps protected `main` green while still making the missing staging infrastructure explicit. Once staging secrets are added, the same workflow deploys automatically without code changes.

author: eurus7895
body:
Re-opens the GUI work against `dev` where it belongs as Day 4 work.

The original PR (#4) was merged directly into `main` by mistake. PR #6 reverts that merge from `main`. This PR re-targets the same GUI branch (`claude/add-crew-gui-obIw4`) at `dev`, with `dev` merged in to reconcile the two parallel Day 4-B implementations.

## What's in this PR

**Day 4-A (already on dev):** bounded session continuity for chatty modes (carried over from `dev`).

**Day 4-B (reconciled):** dev's canonical streamer + three new pipelines (`release-notes`, `ticket-refinement`, `code-review-routing`). The streamer is extended with an `on_delta` callback field and named-constructor subclasses (`TerminalStreamer`, `SummaryStreamer`, `CallbackStreamer`) so the GUI's SSE chat / pipeline-progress publishers work without a parallel implementation.

**Day 4-C (new — full GUI):**
- `crew/gui/` — FastAPI + Jinja + HTMX + vanilla CSS inside a PyWebView window
- Three swappable design languages (Warm, Terminal, Modernist), cookie-persisted
- `POST /chat` → `crew.direct.run_direct` with a `CallbackStreamer` publishing `chat_token` events on the SSE bus
- Clickable pinned rail (`POST /pinned/{kind}/{name}`): skills append, agents swap persona, pipelines kick off a run, memory pin opens `$EDITOR`
- Standup card with live `#standup-progress` strip — now wired through `CallbackStreamer` directly (no more `redirect_stdout` hack)
- PyInstaller packaging (`pip install -e '.[gui,package]' && python packaging/build.py`)

## Conflict resolution

`dev` and this branch each shipped Day 4-B independently. Resolved by:
- Pipelines (12 files): take dev's versions verbatim
- Streamer / `direct.py` / `pipeline_runner.py`: dev's design as the base; add `on_delta` field + named subclasses + a `streamer=` kwarg to `run_direct` / `run_pipeline` so the GUI can inject its `CallbackStreamer`
- Docs: combine both narratives (4-A + 4-B + 4-C)
- `tests/test_streamer.py`: dev's tests (match the canonical API)
- Drop the gui-branch schema rename `pipelines/code-review-routing/schemas/routing-verdict.json` in favour of dev's `review-routing.json`

## GUI ↔ backend wiring

After the merge, the GUI's three call paths all use the `streamer=` kwarg uniformly:

- `crew/gui/services/chat_service.py` — chat → `run_direct(streamer=CallbackStreamer(...))`
- `crew/gui/services/pinned_actions.py` — skills/agents/pipelines from the pinned rail → `run_direct` / `run_pipeline` with `CallbackStreamer`
- `crew/gui/services/standup_service.py` — refactored in this PR to use `CallbackStreamer` instead of `contextlib.redirect_stdout(_QueueSink(...))`

## Try it

```bash
git checkout claude/add-crew-gui-obIw4
pip install -e '.[gui]'
crew gui
```

## Related

- PR #4 — original (closed, merged into `main` by mistake)
- PR #6 — reverts the wrong main merge

author: guptesarvesh
body:
### Motivation

- Remove ambiguity and login failures caused by multiple identifier formats (`X123456`, `DK-XXXXX`, `DX-XXXXXXXX`) and make a single canonical user-facing identifier.  
- Ensure frontend validation, backend schemas, models, OTP/forgot-password, invite flows, and tests all treat the same visible identifier format.  
- Preserve backward compatibility for internal artifacts while hiding legacy formats from user-facing flows.

### Description

- Enforce `xID` as the single user-facing login identifier (format `X` + 6 digits) by updating the user model validation to accept only `^X\d{6}$` and making the legacy `xid` field an internal compatibility alias that is synchronized to `xID` on save (`src/models/User.model.js`).
- Stop generating/exposing DK-style canonical IDs and simplify canonicalization to sync the `xid` alias from the visible `xID` (removed DK-generation, updated `ensureCanonicalXid`) so tokens/claims remain compatible without exposing legacy formats (`src/controllers/auth.controller.js`).
- Align route validation and request schemas so login/OTP/forgot-password endpoints accept only the unified identifier formats, adding a shared `loginIdentifierString` (email or `X123456`) and updating schema checks (`src/schemas/auth.routes.schema.js`).
- Normalize identifier handling in OTP and forgot-password services/controllers to accept either an email or the `xID` and to resolve the canonical email for OTP delivery; lookups now search both `xID` and `xid` where appropriate (`src/services/otp.service.js`, `src/services/authOtp.service.js`, `src/services/authPassword.service.js`).
- Update frontend to submit a generic `identifier` for forgot-password and to validate `xID`/email consistently in the UI (`ui/src/services/authService.js`, `ui/src/pages/ForgotPasswordPage.jsx`).
- Add documentation and regression tests that assert frontend/backend validation parity and flow consistency, and add a short note in `docs/whats-new.md` plus `docs/product/login-identifier-model.md` describing the model (`tests/loginIdentifierModelConsistency.test.js`, `tests/authForgotPasswordFirmContext.test.js`).

### Testing

- Ran `node tests/loginIdentifierModelConsistency.test.js` which validates schema parity and frontend validator presence; the test passed.  
- Ran `node tests/authForgotPasswordFirmContext.test.js` which covers forgot-password firm-scoped behavior and the new xID identifier acceptance; the test passed.

author: aidanns
body:
Closes #294.

## Story

After #288 dropped the harness's ``-t 30`` override and the SIGTERM handlers from #154 took over, every per-test ``compose_stop`` still clustered tightly at ~5.7-6.7 s — the per-service ``stop_grace_period: 5s`` ceiling. The first commit instrumented the harness so we could find out which container was the bottleneck; the second fixes it.

## Diagnostic — first commit (``test(harness): split compose teardown into stop+ps+down``)

The integration plugin's ``save_logs_to`` runs *before* ``compose down``, so shutdown-time stderr (where #154's watchdog ``force-exiting`` line would appear) is never captured. Without per-container exit codes, "compose_stop took 6 s" tells us nothing about which service is the cause.

This commit splits the harness teardown into:

```
docker compose stop      # SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL
docker compose ps -a     # capture per-container exit codes (still in metadata)
docker compose logs <svc> # tail stderr for any non-clean exit
docker compose down -v   # cleanup; containers already stopped, this just removes
```

Each container's exit code lands on the ``integration.harness`` logger as ``compose_stop_diag service=<name> exit_code=<n>``, with a 20-line stderr tail when the exit code isn't clean. ``0`` = clean SIGTERM exit, ``1`` = #154's watchdog called ``os._exit(1)``, ``137`` = docker SIGKILL at the grace boundary.

CI ran this and the pattern was unambiguous — every test, every project:

```
compose_stop_diag service=agent-auth     exit_code=0
compose_stop_diag service=things-bridge  exit_code=0
compose_stop_diag service=notifier       exit_code=137  ← every single one
```

The diagnostic instrumentation is permanent — a future regression of this class (a service silently failing to handle SIGTERM) will leave the same artefact in CI logs without anyone needing to add tooling first.

## Fix — second commit (``fix(test-support): install SIGTERM handler in notifier``)

The notifier had no SIGTERM handler, on the assumption that Python's default ``SIG_DFL`` would terminate the process. That assumption is wrong when the process is **PID 1 inside a container**: the Linux kernel treats PID 1 specially — signals with no installed handler are silently *ignored*, not default-action. So the notifier sat through SIGTERM until docker SIGKILLed it at the 5 s grace boundary on every teardown. The agent-auth and things-bridge containers don't hit this because they install handlers explicitly via #154.

The fix mirrors the #154 pattern: install SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers in ``run_fixed_notifier`` that dispatch ``server.shutdown()`` onto a daemon thread (calling ``shutdown()`` from the signal frame would deadlock against ``serve_forever``). Handler installation is opt-in via ``install_signal_handlers=True`` so the in-process unit tests, which run the notifier from a daemon thread, can keep calling ``run_fixed_notifier`` directly without tripping ``signal.signal``'s "main thread of the main interpreter only" rule. The script entrypoint at ``__main__.py`` opts in.

A subprocess-level test mirrors the #163 pattern: spawn ``python -m tests_support.notifier`` as a real child, send SIGTERM, assert it exits 0 within 3 s. A regression of the PID-1-in-container shutdown path will tip that test into the wall-time guard rather than sliding past unnoticed.

With all three services now exiting cleanly, ``COMPOSE_STOP_BUDGET_SECONDS`` ratchets from 10 s to 3 s — the 10 s budget added by #288 absorbed the full 5 s grace ceiling that this commit removes. 3 s leaves margin for slow-CI noise without surrendering the regression-detection that lets the gate catch a future #288- or #294-class slowdown before it lands.

## Test plan

- [x] ``./scripts/test.sh --unit`` — all suites pass; per-package coverage floors satisfied.
- [x] ``./scripts/typecheck.sh`` / ``./scripts/lint.sh`` — clean (161 source files).
- [x] New unit test ``test_notifier_subprocess_exits_cleanly_on_sigterm`` confirms the notifier subprocess exits 0 within 3 s of SIGTERM.
- [x] Two new harness tests pin the diagnostic ``stop`` → ``ps`` → ``down`` ordering and the per-service exit-code log shape.
- [x] Existing ``test_compose_down_does_not_pass_explicit_timeout_flag`` widened to assert ``-t`` is absent on **both** ``stop`` and ``down``.
- [ ] CI integration jobs will run end-to-end. Expected: all four slices green; ``compose_stop`` p99 well under the new 3 s budget.

author: nickboy
body:
## Summary

Pressing a Row 0 session slot now activates Ghostty AND selects the tab where that Claude session is running — works from any app (Chrome, Slack, etc.). No more ⌘-Tab hunt for the right tab.

**Depends on #42** (shellPid capture). Branched off that PR; please merge #42 first or this PR's diff against \`main\` will look bigger than its actual delta.

## How it works

1. Plugin's \`SessionSlotAction.onKeyDown\` sends two WS commands:
   - \`session:focus\` (existing — plugin-internal focus state)
   - \`session:jump\` (new — pure macOS side-effect)

2. Daemon resolves \`session:jump\` → \`shellPid\` via \`ptyHolderForSession\` (added in #42).

3. Daemon fires \`osascript\` with this script:
   \`\`\`applescript
   tell application "Ghostty"
     activate
     repeat with w in windows
       repeat with t in tabs of w
         if pid of (focused terminal of t) is <shellPid> then
           set selected of t to true
           return
         end if
       end repeat
     end repeat
   end tell
   \`\`\`

**Live-verified**: ran the AS script against my Ghostty with a known shellPid (1093) — it returned \`MATCH:tab-cb19c0400\`, the correct tab id. Bare \`activate\` with a non-matching pid returned exit 0, confirming the syntax parses cleanly on Nick's Ghostty 1.3 nightly.

## Graceful fallbacks

- No matching pty-holder for that session's cwd → activate-only (Ghostty foregrounds, user picks tab manually).
- Older ptyRunner without shellPid → activate-only.
- Tab closed since registration → no match found, activate-only.
- osascript missing → silent no-op.

The osascript spawn is \`detached + stdio: "ignore" + .unref()\` so it can never block the WS message loop.

## Summary

- **Pure-Python PCAP parser** (`struct` only, no external deps) supporting IEEE 802.11 (link types 105/127) and BLE LE (link types 251/272), with a 1-second time-bucket index for fast candidate lookup
- **EnrichmentService** correlates each CSV scan row with the best-matching PCAP frame by a weighted time+identity score, writing a `*_ENRICHED.csv` artifact with per-row diagnostics (`match_found`, `match_method`, `match_score`, PCAP-derived fields)
- **REST endpoint** `POST /sessions/{id}/enrichment/run` — auto-detects the PCAP file by CSV basename when `selected_pcap_file` is omitted; returns `{ enrichment, session }` shape matching the frontend contract
- **Frontend** — `EnrichmentRunPayload` fields aligned (`output_enriched_file`, `diagnostics` with `unmatched_rows`); `ReIdEnrichmentPage.tsx` with parameter controls and quality stats panel

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| Backend model | `canonical_models.py`, `api_models.py` |
| Enrichment service | `app/modules/enrichment/service.py` |

- [x] WiFi 802.11 management frame parsing and MAC extraction
- [x] BLE ADV_IND frame parsing and address/name extraction

body:
The artist world bible lands at `designs/01-prototype/artist-world-bible.md` as a companion to the existing `artist-brief.md`. The brief is the deal; the bible is the world behind it. It focuses on form, mood, and theme, and deliberately abstracts the specific items the artist will be drawing so that visual decisions stay open while the texture stays consistent.

At a glance it covers the protagonist and the friend, the venues from court to garden to real-world memory beats, the trajectory the surface takes as the seam shows, the constants that recur across every shot, the phases of the prototype, the reference register the studio is drawing from, and the studio identity the work is being made under.

Closes SH-273

## Description

This PR adds WP ERP as a new action integration in Bit Integrations (Pro). Users can now connect WP ERP, choose a CRM/HRM/Accounting action, map trigger fields, and execute WP ERP actions through the existing flow engine.

## Motivation & Context

WP ERP users needed a direct way to automate CRM, HRM, and Accounting operations from WordPress triggers without custom code. This change enables that automation path with guided configuration, action-specific field mapping, and runtime logging.

### **Integrations**

- **Added** WP ERP action integration registration in action selector and integration screens (new, edit, info).
- **Added** WP ERP branding asset and integration discovery entry.

- **Added** full WP ERP setup flow with authorization, action selection, mapping UI, and final save flow.
- **Added** action catalog for CRM, HRM, and Accounting operations with required/optional field definitions.
- **Added** utility controls and dynamic data refresh for life stages, contact groups, departments, and designations.
- **Added** mapping validation for required fields and support for custom values/smart tags.

### **Backend**

- **Added** support for 18 WP ERP actions (contact, company, group, note, task, employee, department, designation, holiday, expense, payment).

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Summary

- Use a column-shaped innovation for the random matrix tracker extent correction.
- Replace elementwise `*` in the square-root extent update with matrix products / triangular solves.
- Add a regression test that checks the full extent matrix against the matrix-form update.

## Root Cause

`RandomMatrixTracker.update` mixed a `(d, 1)` measurement mean with a `(d,)` predicted measurement in the extent correction, causing broadcasting to `(d, d)`. The same block also used elementwise multiplication where the random matrix update needs matrix multiplication.

## Validation

- Not run locally; this Codex workspace is read-only.
- Added `test_update_extent_matches_matrix_form_with_column_innovation` to cover the corrected extent update.

- `lifecycle_runtime_correctness`, `takeover_execution_outcomes`, `participant_truth_reconciliation`, `evaluator_artifact_emission`, `continuity_recovery_safety`, `compatibility_legacy_suppression`

- `STRONG_PARTICIPANT_RUNTIME` — primary gate input; V2 may consume directly

- `DEPRECATED_COMPAT` — must NOT count toward gate satisfaction

author: dewinator
body:
## Summary

- Promote the inline `"contradiction_detected"` and `"contradiction_resolved"`
  literals — previously scattered across `agents/conscience-agent.ts` (one
  emission), `services/relations.ts` (one lookup + one emission) — to exported
  `CONTRADICTION_DETECTED_EVENT_TYPE` / `CONTRADICTION_RESOLVED_EVENT_TYPE`
  constants in `services/supabase.ts`, alongside the existing
  `MARK_USEFUL_EVENT_TYPE` / `RECALLED_EVENT_TYPE` pair.
- Add `affect-contradiction-event-types.test.ts` (10 tests) pinning both
  values, runtime types, non-emptiness, snake_case shape, pairwise
  distinctness from each other, and pairwise distinctness from the other
  two `compute_affect()` event-type literals.

## Why this matters

`compute_affect()` (docs/affect-observables.md §frustration) reads
`memory_events` filtered by *both* literals to compute `open_conflicts`:

```
open_conflicts = count(memory_events WHERE event_type='contradiction_detected'
                       AND created_at > now()-'48h'
                       AND NOT EXISTS (…resolution event with same trace_id…))
```

The "…resolution event…" sub-clause matches `event_type='contradiction_resolved'`.
The two literals are co-load-bearing — a silent rename of *either* zeroes
the `open_conflicts` term in different ways:

- rename `contradiction_detected` → frustration sees zero conflicts
  (the outer `count(*)` collapses to 0).
- rename `contradiction_resolved` → frustration over-counts indefinitely
  (no resolutions match, so every detection stays "open" forever).

The detection literal was also used inside `services/relations.ts` as the
`.eq("event_type", …)` filter that pairs detections with their resolution
— so producer + lookup must share one constant or the resolver silently
stops finding any detections to close.

A silent rename at any of those three sites would not break compilation,
would not break the JSONB-payload guards in `affect-event-payloads.test.ts`
(those test the context shape, not the event_type), would not surface in
the `FakeService` accumulator in `handlers.test.ts` (which records function
args, not the event_type), and would not be caught by `relations.test.ts`
(which exercises `findResolutionMatch` over a hand-constructed row set,
not the wire literal). Centralising + pinning the literals here makes a
rename a single deliberate edit that fails the new test until the spec doc
+ SQL are updated together.

Same defensive pattern as `MARK_USEFUL_EVENT_TYPE` (PR #36) and
`RECALLED_EVENT_TYPE` (PR #38).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 150 / 150 pass (140 prior + 10 new in
      `affect-contradiction-event-types.test.ts`)
- [x] No behavioural change: the runtime literals emitted/queried are
      identical bytes; only the source of those bytes moved into a named
      constant.
- [x] No SQL migration, no dependency change, no CI/CD edit.

## Constitution affirmation

Touches **Pillar 3 (Swarm intelligence)** — affect is the substrate that
lets specialized agents recognise their own performance state, and the
frustration dimension specifically gates whether the swarm escalates an
unresolved contradiction. This change is purely additive constants + a
non-behavioural call-site refactor + a new test file; no pillar is
weakened.

body:
## Summary

- ProjectManager now **auto-discovers templates** from `{packageDir}/templates/` when `templatesConfig` is not explicitly provided
- This eliminates the need for manual template configuration in `disclaude.config.yaml`
- Templates are scanned from subdirectories containing `CLAUDE.md`, with metadata from `template.yaml` or CLAUDE.md frontmatter

Related: #2286

## Problem

Issue #2286 reported that ProjectManager's template system required manual configuration through `disclaude.config.yaml`'s `projectTemplates` field. The `template-discovery.ts` module already existed with all the discovery logic, but was never wired into the ProjectManager constructor.

## Changes

### Core Integration (`packages/core/src/project/`)
- **`types.ts`**: Made `templatesConfig` optional in `ProjectManagerOptions` with clear JSDoc explaining auto-discovery fallback
- **`project-manager.ts`**: Integrated `discoverTemplatesAsConfig()` as the default when `templatesConfig` is omitted; stored `packageDir` for discovery
- **`project-manager.test.ts`**: Added 5 new integration tests covering auto-discovery scenarios

### Example Template (`packages/core/templates/`)
- Created `research/` template as the first example template with `CLAUDE.md` and `template.yaml`

## Test Results

All 118 tests pass (113 existing + 5 new):

```
✓ should auto-discover templates from packageDir/templates/ when templatesConfig is not provided
✓ should work with zero templates when templates/ directory does not exist
✓ should prefer explicit templatesConfig over auto-discovery
✓ should discover multiple templates from filesystem
✓ should allow creating instances from auto-discovered templates and persist
```

## Design Decisions

1. **Backward compatible**: Explicit `templatesConfig` still takes precedence over auto-discovery
2. **Zero-config by default**: If no templates directory exists, behavior is unchanged (all chatIds use workspace root)
3. **No config schema changes**: Removed the comment about "Only templates listed in projectTemplates config are available" from types, but no config schema modifications needed

body:
Android readiness evidence (from PR-6Android) spoke in Android-internal dimension terms with no explicit mapping to V2's canonical distributed gate categories, forcing reviewers to manually cross-reference and blocking V2 governance tooling from programmatically querying which Android evidence feeds which gate decision.

## Changes

### `AndroidDistributedGateCategoryMapping.kt` (new)

Alignment layer mapping all 26 `AndroidReadinessEvidenceSurface` evidence entries to 5 V2 canonical gate categories. Supersedes any prior Android PR-7 attempt.

- **`V2GateCategory`** — 5-value enum mirroring V2 PR-7 skeleton: `LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_CORRECTNESS`, `TAKEOVER_EXECUTION_OUTCOMES`, `RECONCILIATION_ARTIFACT_EMISSION`, `CONTINUITY_RECOVERY_SAFETY`, `COMPATIBILITY_SUPPRESSION`
- **`GateStrength`** — gate-level projection of Android `ConfidenceLevel`: `PARTICIPANT_RUNTIME` (strong; 23 entries) / `ADVISORY` (2 entries) / `DEFERRED_LOCAL` (1 entry — `long_tail_compat_registry_legacy_signals`, must not count toward gating)
- **`GateMappingEntry` registry** — maps every evidence entry; Android `SIGNAL_REPLAY_DUPLICATE_SAFETY` dimension is explicitly absorbed into `CONTINUITY_RECOVERY_SAFETY` per V2 canonical model
- **Query helpers** for V2 governance tooling:

```kotlin
// Strong Android participant input to a specific gate category
AndroidDistributedGateCategoryMapping.participantRuntimeMappingsFor(
    V2GateCategory.CONTINUITY_RECOVERY_SAFETY
)

// Which V2 gate categories does an Android dimension feed?
AndroidDistributedGateCategoryMapping.gateCategoriesForDimension(
    ReadinessDimension.SIGNAL_REPLAY_DUPLICATE_SAFETY
)
// → {CONTINUITY_RECOVERY_SAFETY}
```

No gate authority is added to Android — V2 remains the canonical orchestration authority.

### `Pr7AndroidDistributedGateMappingTest.kt` (new)

85 tests covering: `V2GateCategory`/`GateStrength` wire value round-trips, all 6 Android dimensions mapped to at least one gate category, per-category `PARTICIPANT_RUNTIME` coverage, every mapped `evidenceId` resolves to a real evidence entry with non-blank `testEvidence`, gate strength ↔ confidence level alignment invariants, 26 specific mapping spot-checks, authority boundary assertions, and all query helpers.

### `docs/ANDROID_READINESS_EVIDENCE.md` (updated)

Adds PR-7 section: dimension → gate category mapping matrix, gate strength table, coverage summary per gate category, and V2 consumption code examples.

- [ ] Input routing (`InputRouter`)

- Trigger / preconditions: Compile + JUnit run of new and existing evidence surface tests
- Expected behavior: All 85 new + 97 existing tests pass; every mapped evidenceId resolves to a real entry with test coverage
- Actual behavior after fix: 85/85 and 97/97 pass

### Verification blockers

- None

## Risks

- User-visible risk: None — no runtime behavior changed; mapping layer is audit/query only
- Operational / cross-device risk: None
- Logging / metrics / protocol compatibility risk: None — no wire protocol touched

## Rollback plan

- Files or components to revert: `AndroidDistributedGateCategoryMapping.kt`, `Pr7AndroidDistributedGateMappingTest.kt`, PR-7 section in `ANDROID_READINESS_EVIDENCE.md`

author: kiranvk-2011
body:
## Problem

Session lifecycle commands (`/new`, `/reset`) were getting queued behind active agent runs in the Telegram sequential key system. When a user sent one of these commands while an agent was running, the command would be queued and never execute until the agent finished — defeating the purpose of these interrupt commands.

## Solution

Added `resolveSessionControlCommand()` function to `extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.ts` that detects session lifecycle commands and routes them to the `:control` lane, bypassing the per-topic sequential queue.

## Changes

- **extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.ts**: Extracted shared command resolution into `resolveControlCommand()` predicate-based helper, added `resolveSessionControlCommand()` for `/new` and `/reset`
- **extensions/telegram/src/sequential-key.test.ts**: Added test coverage for session control command routing

## Technical Details

The fix follows the same pattern as the existing `resolveStatusCommandControlLane()`:
1. Normalizes the command body using `normalizeCommandBody()`
2. Resolves text aliases using `maybeResolveTextAlias()`
3. Looks up the command in `listChatCommands()`
4. Returns `true` if the command key is `new` or `reset`

When detected, these commands route to `telegram:${chatId}:control` instead of the normal per-topic lane, bypassing the queue and executing immediately.

body:
## Summary

Replaces the `clone ats-fukuyama/bpsd + git apply 2 patches` CI flow with a single clone of `k-yoshimi/bpsd@develop` — a personal fork that carries the same two TASK-private patches as proper commits on top of upstream main.

- **species_kid OOB write** (#140) → fork commit `879bb7ac`
- **plasmaf INTENT(OUT) zero-init** (#148) → fork commit `dcccf84f`

Both patches were emailed to upstream (Fukuyama-sensei) on 2026-04-22 and are awaiting upstream merge. When upstream merges either fix, rebasing fork `develop` onto `main` drops the corresponding commit naturally — no CI changes needed.

### Why fork instead of in-repo patches

The in-repo `git apply` flow had to be re-run on every fresh environment (CI clone, new dev box, new working-directory mount). The fork bakes the patches into the cloned tree, eliminating the per-environment ceremony. `gsaf` does not need patches, so it stays out of scope.

author: copilot
body:
Three interconnected bugs caused tracks from compilation albums to show wrong cover art (e.g. Cold Chisel art on "Hit Machine 22"), be placed under the wrong artist folder, and have mismatched MusicBrainz album IDs across tracks in the same release.

## Root causes & fixes

### 1. Original library files mutated before copy (`download_queue_manager.py`)
`move_single_track_to_music_dir` was calling `update_file_metadata_with_albumart(file_path, ...)` on the **source** file unconditionally — before the copy. When the source was an existing `/music` file (e.g. "Turn Back Time" from Aqua/Aquarium matched as a copy candidate for Hit Machine 21), the original track's tags, cover art, and album name were overwritten with the target compilation's metadata, causing it to be re-organised under the wrong folder.

**Fix**: tag writes are now gated on `source_already_in_music`:
- `source == dest` (in-place): tag the file directly as before
- source in `/downloads`: tag before move (unchanged)
- source in `/music`: **skip** pre-copy tag write; apply tags to the **destination copy** after transfer

### 2. Cover art URL order (`post_download_processor.py`)
`fetch_musicbrainz_release_metadata` tried the release-**group** CAA URL first. Compilations routinely have art on the specific release but not on the release group, so the lookup silently failed. Also used `release_info.get('release_mbid')` before that key was populated.

**Fix**: try `release/{actual_mbid}/front-500` first (using `mb_data.get('id')` directly), fall back to `release-group/{rg_id}/front-500`.

### 3. Missing columns on queue inserts (`musicbrainz_release_manager.py`, `app.py`)
Both `add_release_tracks_to_queue` and `api_musicbrainz_download` omitted `release_mbid`, `import_group`, `release_source`, and `cover_art_url` from their `INSERT` statements. This broke `_resolve_canonical_release_mbid` (requires `mbid_` import_group prefix for fast extraction) and left the cover art fallback URL empty.

**Fix**: both insert paths now populate all four columns; `import_group = f"mbid_{release_id}"`.

author: jsaorin
body:
## Summary

- Adds a socket.io realtime gateway in `apps/api` backed by Redis pub/sub (`@socket.io/redis-adapter`), so backend handlers can push state-change notifications to the frontend without polling.
- Centralizes the wire contract (actions, rooms, payloads, EventsMaps) in `@sentinel/common/realtime` — a single source of truth shared by backend and frontend, type-safe end-to-end.
- Wires emissions from existing handlers: `IngestThreatSignalCommandHandler`, `ScoreProposalsCommandHandler`, `ScoreMultisigHealthCommandHandler`, plus the reactor's `onThreatSignalReceived` / `onProposalScored` / `onMultisigScored` for granular `AGENT_MESSAGE` progress events.
- Adds `docs/WS.md` — frontend integration guide explaining the design, connection details, action catalog, and ready-to-paste Next.js App Router snippets.

## Design notes

- **Thin payloads**. Each event carries only the id of the affected resource. The frontend refetches the relevant REST endpoint for fresh state — keeps the wire contract tiny and impossible to drift.
- **Rooms as filters**. Clients `socket.emit("subscribe", room)` with rooms like `multisig:<id>`, `proposal:<id>`, or `watcher:feed`. Only subscribers receive the event.
- **Hexagonal compliance**. `IRealtimeService` lives in `domain`, `SocketIoRealtimeService` in `infrastructure`, gateway in `apps/api`. Application handlers depend on the port only.
- **Scales horizontally**. The Redis adapter syncs rooms across N API instances with no extra code.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — green
- [x] `pnpm lint` — green
- [x] Local smoke: API + Reactor up, socket.io-client connects to `/ws`, subscribes to `watcher:feed` + `multisig:<id>`
- [x] Direct `redis-cli PUBLISH sentinel.realtime …` reaches the subscribed client
- [x] Room filtering verified: events for `multisig:<other>` are NOT delivered to a client subscribed to `multisig:<id>`
- [x] Broadcast (`type:"broadcast"`) reaches all connected clients regardless of room
- [ ] Real end-to-end (POST /multisigs → reactor scoring → realtime fan-out) — requires a valid `HELIUS_API_KEY`; the internal chain is type- and contract-validated, the WS path is verified by the smoke above

## Frontend follow-up

`docs/WS.md` contains the integration guide. The `apps/web` change set (install `socket.io-client` + `@sentinel/common`, add the typed socket factory and the `useRealtimeRoom` hook) is intentionally out of scope for this PR.

author: ioannisj
body: ## :bulb: Motivation and Context Closes #321 and possibly #571 This PR improves screenshot performance by replacing `UIGraphicsImageRenderer` with a custom and more lightweight CGContext-backed renderer. Physical-device benchmarking and profiling on an old iPhone XR showed the UIView.toImage() path was the dominant source of UI glitches: - Baseline screenshot snapshots cost ~135ms on the main thread. - Each snapshot correlated with a >33ms frame hitch. - At higher snapshot rates, replay could saturate the app and drop effective frame pacing below 60fps. ### Changes - Adds `PostHogGraphicsImageRenderer`, a direct CoreGraphics bitmap renderer. - Uses it for `UIView.toImage()` screenshot capture. - Uses it for `RRWireframe.maskImage()` masked screenshot redraw. - Does not change masking traversal logic, masking decisions, serialization, or replay event structure. ### Findings Physical device benchmark on an iPhone XR (`iPhone11,8`), running screenshots on a complex idle view with re-layout ticks (to trigger snapshots) Judging from the metrics collected, snapshot main-thread cost dropped by ~92%: | Throttle | Baseline snapshot avg | This PR snapshot avg | Delta | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0.50s | 134.22ms | 11.14ms | -91.7% | | 0.25s | 134.58ms | 10.69ms | -92.1% | | 0.10s | 138.92ms | 10.66ms | -92.3% | There was also a big improvement on frame pacing and app hangs. This was also prominent when running the app, frame rate stayed at 60fps at all throttle levels (not recommended if you are reading this): | Throttle | Baseline frames >33ms | This PR frames >33ms | |---:|---:|---:| | 0.50s | 29 | 0 | | 0.25s | 57 | 0 | | 0.10s | 93 | 0 | **Before** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/adc13e41-1a83-4f54-9295-c79bbfab4b65 **After** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c283d247-1b58-4eb9-9818-5326b411ae9c ### Post-release - [ ] Bump RN posthog-ios min version - [ ] Bump Flutter posthog-ios min version ### Note We previously experimented with using a custom renderer to improve performance. Back then, the timing results were not that convincing and I decided not to ship a fix, which was the wrong call. This could be because: - I had the wrong approach on profiling the improvement and baseline - I was not profiling/testing on the correct device This one is on me because we could have shipped this improvement much earlier! ## :green_heart: How did you test it? - Profiling with Xcode Instruments and custom benchmarking - Running on a lower-end physical device - Verified that session recordings are scaled and masked correctly in the PostHog UI - This 👇 ## :pencil: Checklist - [x] I reviewed the submitted code. - [ ] I added tests to verify the changes. - [ ] I updated the docs if needed. - [ ] No breaking change or entry added to the changelog. ## If releasing new changes - [x] Ran `pnpm changeset` to generate a changeset file - [x] Added the `release` label to the PR
