## Summary
- Phase 5 (CLI / eval-harness wiring) and Phase 6 (docs + inline comments) of the rigor rollout.
- **CLI** (`bin/pm-tools.js`) — adds `--rigor=machine|human` (default machine) with input validation (exit 2 on typo) and threads it onto `config.input.rigor` for the draft path. USAGE block updated under DRAFT FLAGS.
- **Eval harness** (`eval/harness.js`) — `runFixture` explicitly pins Machine by default, accepts opt-in `options.rigor` override. The explicit pin is the load-bearing change: it stops the committed `baseline.json` from drifting if `createRun`'s default ever changes.
- **Eval runner** (`eval/run.js`) — gains a `--rigor` flag with the same validation, plus a hard refusal of `--rigor=human` together with `--check-regression` / `--baseline` so a Human-mode run cannot quietly overwrite or appear to compare against the Machine-only baseline. Help text updated.
- **README.md** — new "Rigor modes: Machine vs Human" section between Stage 6 and the CLI block. Explains the toggle UX, what each mode actually changes (reviewer prompts, voting discipline, humanizer gate), what stays identical (`PROTOCOL_CONTEXT` + the full pipeline), and the harness pin. CLI flag blurb gains `--rigor`.
- **Inline comments** — `src/App.jsx` `handleDraft` now spells out the contract that the `rigor` field at `RUN_START` is what freezes onto `run.input.rigor` for every later snapshot read in `handleReview` / `handleUpdate` / `handleAccept`. Other rigor read sites already had Phase 2/3 comments.

## Summary Полная переделка верхнего блока для мобилки, чтобы пальцами не попадать в настройки во время прокрутки. **Что изменилось вверху:** - Статус: оставлена только одна карточка «Состояние». «Авторизация» и «Сессия истекает» убраны — пользы 0. - Выпадашка для быстрой загрузки пресета промта. - Большие Старт/Стоп. - Радио «Основная/Фронтальная» камера — теперь над иконками. - **Ряд из 4 компактных иконок** без подписей: 📷 / 🎤 / 🧠+✓ / 🧹. Зелёная рамка = вкл, серая = выкл. - Одна кнопка **«⚙️ Настройки и промт»** заменила два аккордеона. **Bottom-sheet «Настройки»:** - Открывается по кнопке ⚙️, выезжает снизу (на десктопе центрируется). - Внутри две свёрнутые `
`-секции: - **Промт модели** — textarea, сброс к стандартному, пресеты (загрузить/удалить/сохранить). - **Настройки модели** — выбор модели, температура, голос, язык, размышления, поиск в интернете, очистка памяти (запасная), API-ключ. - Закрывается крестиком, кликом по фону или Escape (через нативный backdrop-клик). **Sticky-плашка снизу (только мобилка):** - Четыре мини-иконки 📷/🎤/🧠/🧹 в полупрозрачной таблетке с blur. - По центру, чуть приподнята от края — не лезет под палец. - **Автоматически скрывается, когда открыт settings-шит** — чтобы не мешать редактировать промт/пресеты. - На десктопе скрыта совсем (`min-width: 861px`). ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Открыть на телефоне → убедиться что верх стал ощутимо проще: статус, пресет-селектор, Старт/Стоп, радио камеры, 4 иконки, одна большая кнопка «⚙️ Настройки и промт». Больше ничего сверху быть не должно. - [ ] Нажать ⚙️ → открывается шторка снизу с двумя свёрнутыми секциями. Раскрыть «Промт» и «Настройки модели» — все старые поля на месте (модель, температура, голос, язык, размышления, поиск, API-ключ). - [ ] Закрыть шторку: крестиком и кликом по затемнённому фону. - [ ] Sticky-плашка снизу — четыре кружочка 📷/🎤/🧠/🧹. Когда открыта шторка настроек — плашка должна исчезнуть. Когда закрыта — снова появиться. - [ ] Запустить сессию, потыкать камеру/микрофон через иконки сверху и через sticky-плашку снизу — рамка должна меняться (зелёная/серая), у мозга — галочка/крестик. - [ ] Загрузить какой-нибудь пресет через выпадашку под статусом — текст промта должен обновиться. - [ ] На десктопе sticky-плашки быть не должно вообще; шторка настроек должна центрироваться, а не вылезать снизу. ### Notes - API-ключ переехал в шторку настроек — теперь это не верхняя часть страницы. - Сама логика (стейт, обработчики, network) не трогалась — только разметка и CSS, плюс одно новое состояние `isSettingsOpen`. - Кнопка «Очистить память диалога» осталась дублем внутри шторки (на случай если человек хочет сделать это явно из настроек, а не через 🧹 на главном экране). - Все автотесты и `npm run check` зелёные локально. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cb4908e333cf435ab39c1d57d782217b Requested by: @AnataBak ---

body:
## Summary

Major release reframing the skill from one-shot novelty to recurring maintenance ritual. Resolves every finding from the synthesised v1.0.0 audit.

- **Reversibility:** every "delete" is now a `mv` to `~/.claude/.audit-quarantine/<timestamp>/` with a 7-day TTL and one-line restore. No `rm -rf` in any normal flow.
- **Decision memory across runs:** `scripts/audit-history.py` persists per-audit decisions; the next audit surfaces only deltas (new items, changed evidence, snoozed items now due).
- **Security-pass agent:** dedicated 5th agent on both halves scanning hooks for shell injection, MCPs for suspicious endpoints, settings for hardcoded tokens, skills for over-broad `allowed-tools`.
- **Slash commands:** `/audit-skills` and `/audit-rules` via `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `commands/`.
- **XSS escaping pass:** every interpolation in both HTML templates wrapped in `escapeHtml()`. Skills template had zero escaping; rules template was partial — both now uniform.
- **Description trimmed** from 1057 to 877 chars (was over the 1024 spec limit).
- **Project-scope coverage:** `discover-config.sh --project` includes `$PWD/.claude/`. Flags user↔project rule contradictions.
- **Public-repo sweep:** every reference to specific plugins, skills, businesses, and case-study numbers stripped from public-facing copy. Skill discovers neighbour skills at runtime by reading the user's installed manifest — never by hardcoded name.

## Highlights

| Area | v1.0.0 | v2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Description chars | 1057 (over spec) | 877 |
| HTML interpolations escaped | partial | all of them, both templates |
| Backups | manifest only | every touched file, in one quarantine session |
| `rm -rf` calls in normal flow | several | 0 |
| Cross-run memory | none | full delta-only re-audit |
| Slash commands | 0 | 2 |
| Hardcoded user-specific names | many | zero |
| Eval suite | none | 10 should-trigger + 10 should-not-trigger |

Full breakdown in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/verify-prerequisites.sh` exits 0 with detection summary
- [x] `bash scripts/discover-config.sh` runs cleanly on macOS (BSD `stat`)
- [x] `bash scripts/discover-config.sh --project` includes project-scope when present
- [x] `bash scripts/quarantine.sh init` creates a session and prints the path
- [x] `bash scripts/quarantine.sh list` enumerates sessions
- [x] `python3 scripts/audit-history.py save/latest/diff` round-trips a synthetic markdown export end-to-end
- [x] SKILL.md description length: 877 chars (under 1024 spec limit)
- [x] `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` parses as valid JSON
- [x] `evals/evals.json` parses as valid JSON
- [x] Both HTML templates: every `innerHTML` interpolation either passes through `escapeHtml()` or comes from a known-safe enum / integer
- [x] No hardcoded skill/plugin/business names in public-facing copy (verified via grep sweep)
- [ ] Linux `stat -c` fallback path (relies on review — tested on macOS only)
- [ ] First end-to-end audit using v2 quarantine flow (recommended on a non-prod `~/.claude/` first)

## Migration

- Re-install or pull the new commit. No data migration needed.
- Existing `installed_plugins.json.bak` from v1 still valid.
- First v2 audit will be a "first audit" by decision-memory standards (no history yet); subsequent audits get the delta-only experience.

body:
This pull request adds new activities to the application, introduces the ability for students to unregister from activities, improves the frontend to display and manage participants, and adds comprehensive backend tests for activity signup and unregistration. These changes enhance both the user experience and the reliability of the activity management system.

**Backend functionality and data model:**

* Added several new activities (`Basketball Team`, `Tennis Club`, `Art Studio`, `Music Band`, `Debate Team`, `Science Club`) to the `activities` data structure in `src/app.py`, each with their own schedule, maximum participants, and initial participants.
* Implemented a new endpoint (`DELETE /activities/{activity_name}/signup`) to allow students to unregister from an activity, including proper error handling for non-existent activities and non-participants.
* Updated the signup logic to prevent duplicate registrations by checking if a student is already signed up before adding them.

**Frontend improvements:**

* Enhanced the activities UI to display a styled list of participants for each activity, including an "Unregister" button next to each participant, and handled the unregister action with appropriate API calls and UI updates. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7146e1c8a61ac4e715182863a67d7a5a3178a73033e8344cd24f1c67787236e3R22-R61) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7146e1c8a61ac4e715182863a67d7a5a3178a73033e8344cd24f1c67787236e3R97)
* Added new CSS styles for the participants section, participant list items, and the unregister button to improve usability and visual clarity.

**Testing enhancements:**

* Added fixtures to `tests/conftest.py` to reset the activities state between tests and provide a reusable test client.
* Introduced new tests in `tests/test_activities_endpoints.py` to verify that all activities are returned correctly by the API.
* Added comprehensive tests in `tests/test_signup_endpoints.py` to cover successful signup, duplicate signup prevention, signup for non-existent activities, successful unregistration, and error handling for unregistration of non-participants.

body:
This pull request refactors the icon pack controls and core infrastructure to simplify the handling of icon styles and improve compatibility with trimming and AOT scenarios. The main changes include removing pseudo-class-based style handling from all icon pack controls, updating the icon data loading mechanism for better trimming/AOT support, and cleaning up the control templates and base classes.

**Refactoring and Simplification of Icon Style Handling:**

* Removed the use of pseudo-classes (such as `:icon-filled`, `:icon-outlined`, and `:icon-data-flipped-vertically`) from `PackIconControlBase` and all derived icon pack controls, as well as the related style selectors and methods. This simplifies the way icon styles are applied and maintained. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a5e9d4054096a88e92a8843df7126ab4a4e5b9349ea4ebf604707c13f4851ceeL18-L40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a5e9d4054096a88e92a8843df7126ab4a4e5b9349ea4ebf604707c13f4851ceeL303-L309) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-518287bc5d0da4b28054c1ca25a160888a8e79e47cae6069867576243872c2b6L34-L54) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-fa7deddb357ae84564403b1843e01e3f59bff849ccf92090cb2265cd0c231e0fL15-L19) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0714a7f1c993c95b294c0a70c298aa655a926e861b31f35d67d76e14c10af4feL15-L19) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-00804b8b410c59c2d386a145ccfb2d225120c878c37b4275f0890ea6495c7030L15-L19) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d884de7593b4c8d21c4533b381a10807798f773a20bfcc18a3766d29413bdfc9L15-L19) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-62a6b54153b2ebb24a580b8da85c579a1b1bb5882b4319bba6f83d7f1d7508a9L15-L19) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-6b39ada345fa34b8d077f9c9db07c787a607eee25263c5e85f60bdbc70c1e089L15-L19) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-6ae978b1e565c93af0ad5eb790f3f75fad604ddd9f403eb0172988bc6d3a6dc0L15-L19) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-2ead662f8856f9cb7cde3fcb4aebf258819bd57285fe2840a4f9fdd7462f0e99L15-L19) [[12]](diffhunk://#diff-78c40f98a38cbc20f58b0e5efcde24e3020eda4689011afc48212dfda52bc968L15-L19) [[13]](diffhunk://#diff-31b64deb4397e398665805290e5d448cacbd6ab3dc7498660da1efa498f7b0d4L15-L19) [[14]](diffhunk://#diff-dbfe605d13c2103b2088df6d688ae5d1ae70a2f60245eaa173c089af1e7756e5L15-L19) [[15]](diffhunk://#diff-bd03d5540374e6eaff9e945bb4a67c25019c309e677bbadc82329a94946b2cb0L15-L19) [[16]](diffhunk://#diff-d90c39c169c9bafa682919304ace96a1d488b678dc60f7854151b8868d90306dL15-L19) [[17]](diffhunk://#diff-43b0ba3f0e7b3ae954ab556eab07eb954b52604bdadbad4f2cb734a42630894eL15-L19) [[18]](diffhunk://#diff-a070f3a6e078d659083cb6ae038af68499919618e52bb9501e4b170e510c4b93L15-L19)

* Updated the icon control template to set the `Fill` property of the icon path directly from the control's `Foreground` property, removing the need for conditional styling via pseudo-classes.

**Improvements for Trimming and AOT Compatibility:**

* Added a new `IconJsonContext` using `System.Text.Json` source generation to support metadata-based JSON deserialization, enabling safe trimming and AOT compatibility for loading icon data.

* Refactored `PackIconDataFactory` to use the new source-generated JSON context for deserializing icon data, ensuring compatibility with trimming and AOT scenarios. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2fa007478f980c46a5bfdab3be9b7a621305b4f08a8f4b2ffb1a5f530edd560cL5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2fa007478f980c46a5bfdab3be9b7a621305b4f08a8f4b2ffb1a5f530edd560cL22-R34)

* Updated the core project file (`IconPacks.Avalonia.Core.csproj`) to enable trimming, mark the assembly as trimmable and AOT compatible, and enable compiled bindings by default.

These changes collectively make the icon pack system more maintainable, performant, and ready for deployment in modern .NET environments with trimming and AOT requirements.

Closes #38

author: marianacannabis
body:
## Summary

P17 Pilot: kleinster sicherster Schritt der JS-Split-Serie.
`toast()` (5 LOC, 304 callers) aus `index.html` nach `src/legacy/toast.ts`.
Backwards-Compat über `window.toast`-Binding in `main.ts`.

Validiert das Extraktions-Schema:
- ESM-Modul mit pure-function-Export
- TypeScript-Types (`ToastType` union)
- 3 vitest unit tests (DOM via jsdom + fake-timers)
- `broken-flow-detect` grün (window-binding hält die Resolution)
- E2E grün (manueller Smoke der 5 Toast-trigger-Pfade)

## Boot-Race-Auffälligkeit

Erster Smoke-Run schlug fehl: `ReferenceError: toast is not defined` aus dem `setTimeout(()=>toast(...), 600)` bei `index.html:21657` (der Welcome-Banner mit der App-Version). Das Callback racet zur Module-Resolution.

**Lösung**: `function toast(msg, type)` als Shim im inline-script-Scope, liest `window.toast` zur Aufrufzeit (NICHT zur Definitionszeit), Identitäts-Guard verhindert Recursion vor Module-Boot. Pattern wiederverwendbar für Folge-Module — wenn es sich hält, kleines `boot-shim`-Helper-Modul erwägen.

## Bundle-Size

| Stand | index.html roh | index.html gz |
|---|---|---|
| vor PR | 1,277,647 | 347,754 |
| nach PR | 1,277,685 | 348,113 |
| delta | **+38 B** | **+359 B** |

Shim ist marginal größer als die ursprüngliche Funktion, aber lebt am selben Ort. Echter Bundle-Win kommt mit den größeren Folge-Modulen (`clipboard`, `addMsg`, `setSbMsg` …) — diesmal war das Ziel das Schema, nicht der Win.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `vitest` 152 → **155/155** (3 neue Toast-Tests)
- [x] `audit:broken-flows` 722 resolved unverändert (1 pre-existing FP `try{...}` bei :2395)
- [x] `audit:functions` 850 HTML-fns
- [x] Lighthouse-CI: keine Threshold-Verletzung erwartet (Pilot greift nur 1 Funktion)
- [x] Playwright **41/41** (5-Flow Smoke isoliert lief 5/5: Boot, save, cloud, dxf, modal-no-toast)

## Erkenntnisse fürs nächste Modul

Siehe Status-Bericht im Chat — Boot-Shim-Pattern dokumentiert + Verifizierung dass legacy-`var/function`-Hoisting + `window.X` aus dem Module gut zusammenspielen.

## New: `experiments/regime_v8.py`

- **Features**: `net_sentiment`, `abs_sentiment`, `extreme_streak_70`, `trend_strength_48b`, `divergence`, `signal_v2_raw`
- **Model**: `LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=200, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8)`
- **Walk-forward**: expanding window, min 3 years; model re-trained from scratch each fold on all prior years
- **Signal**: `position = sign(model.predict(X_test))`, `pnl = position × ret_48b`
- **Fold output**: `["year", "n", "mean", "sharpe", "hit_rate", "ic"]` where IC is Spearman correlation between predictions and realized returns
- Fails clearly on missing required columns; drops NaN rows within walk-forward (not at load time)

```python
df = load_data("data/output/master_research_dataset.csv")

summary = compute_pooled_summary(fold_df)
```

Thin launcher matching `run_regime_v7.py` style. File logging on by default (`logs/regime_v8_*.log`), no stdout when log file active. Args: `--data` (required), `--log-level`, `--log-file`.

author: oblangatas
body:
> Sidecars that survive SIGKILL, drain SIGTERM in 5 s, and refuse silly env values.

**TL;DR** — WOR-308 hardens the [WOR-307](https://github.com/shacharm2/worthless/pull/94) prototype sidecar against three production failure modes — stale sockets after SIGKILL, hung handlers blocking SIGTERM, and operator typos in `WORTHLESS_LOG_LEVEL`. Adds a §11 design note explaining why the sidecar deliberately doesn't use the OS keyring.

# Summary

WOR-307 shipped a working sidecar (IPC framing, peer-uid auth, Fernet backend, basic signal-driven shutdown). A 4-expert research pass on WOR-308 showed ~85 % of the originally-scoped work was already live in WOR-307. This PR narrows WOR-308 to exactly the production-hardening delta and **moves the healthcheck CLI to WOR-310** (where the Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` directive that invokes it lives) so we ship complete features instead of half of one.

The sidecar can now: refuse to clobber a live socket on restart, recover from a SIGKILL'd predecessor, cap drain at a tunable deadline (default 5 s) and forcibly cancel stuck handlers past it, validate `WORTHLESS_LOG_LEVEL` with `rc=1` on unknown values, and document — in the engineering reference — the deliberate no-keyring decision so a future contributor doesn't paper over it with a "helpful" fallback.

# What

**Slice 1 — stale-socket recovery (`5214027`)**
- New `_check_socket_path_available()` probes the socket path before bind: missing → bind, stale inode (connect → ECONNREFUSED) → unlink + bind, live peer → `rc=2` with `already running` stderr, non-socket file → refuse.

**Slice 2 — bounded drain on shutdown (`2b8cde1`)**
- New `_drain_server()` waits up to `WORTHLESS_SIDECAR_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (default `5.0`s) for tracked handler tasks; cancels stragglers; falls back to `abort_clients()` on Python 3.13+.
- `start_sidecar()` now tracks per-connection handler tasks on `server._worthless_handler_tasks` (single dunder attr, called out in commit body as v1.2 cleanup).

**Slice 3 — log-level validation (`6242f5c`)**
- New `_resolve_log_level()` accepts canonical `DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR|CRITICAL` (case- and whitespace-tolerant); rejects `WARN`, `FATAL`, `TRACE`, numeric, anything else.
- `main()` validates **before** `basicConfig` / `asyncio.run` so a bad value short-circuits with `rc=1` + stderr hint naming the offending env var.

**Slice 4 — §11 no-keyring design note (`18113cc`)**
- Appended `## §11 — Why the sidecar does not use the OS keyring` to [docs/wor-307-handoff.md](docs/wor-307-handoff.md): decision, three reasons, no-fallback rule, honest reversibility, see-also links to `docs/security.md` + `docs/adversarial/attack-map.md` (does **not** duplicate the threat model).

**Slice 5 — /simplify cleanup (`b650968`)**
- Extract `_DelegatingBackend` base for slow / stalling test backends (~25 LoC dedup).
- Hoist `WORTHLESS_SIDECAR_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` parse above `start_sidecar` so a bad value fails fast without a pointless bind/unbind cycle.
- `frozenset` for `_VALID_LOG_LEVELS`; group module constants.
- Trim narration from `_drain_server` / `_load_shares` docstrings.
- Fix obscure ` "info ".replace("info", "infomercial") ` test typo.

# Why

* **Stale sockets**: `asyncio.start_unix_server` auto-unlinks *any* existing socket path before binding — including live ones — so two sidecars pointed at the same socket silently race for new connections. The probe closes that gap.
* **Drain deadline**: pre-3.12 `Server.wait_closed()` returns as soon as the listener closes — it does **not** wait for connection tasks. Without an explicit drain-and-cancel the container hangs on shutdown when any handler is stuck.
* **Log-level guard**: operators set `WORTHLESS_LOG_LEVEL=DEUBG` and lose all logs. Failing fast with a stderr hint is cheaper than debugging silent observability holes.
* **§11 design note**: a future contributor reading `_load_shares` will wonder "why not fall back to the keyring on disk read fail?" — the docstring now points at §11 with the answer (headless backends + collapses two-share split into one secret).

# How

TDD per slice (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR). Each slice committed atomically with the WOR-308 ID in the message.

**Test layers exercised:**
- Unit: parametrized `_resolve_log_level`, in-process `_drain_server` with `_SlowSealBackend` and `_StallingSealBackend`.
- Integration: subprocess spawns of `python -m worthless.sidecar` for stale-socket recovery, two-sidecar bind clash, log-level rc=1.
- Container smoke: `tests/docker/test_container_smoke.py` re-run against the rebuilt image after the /simplify pass — passed in 31 s.
- Lint / format: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` clean.
- Final aggregate: **66 sidecar+ipc tests passed**, 1 skipped (AF_UNIX path-too-long on macOS), 1 xfailed.

**Cross-platform**:
- macOS Apple Silicon: integration suite + Docker smoke (Docker Desktop 29.0.1).
- Linux: covered by Docker smoke (the container *is* Linux).
- Windows / WSL: not exercised here — the sidecar runs in a container by design (`docs/wor-307-handoff.md` §1).

**Out of scope (filed as v1.2 follow-ups in commit body of `b650968`):**
- Replace dunder `server._worthless_handler_tasks` with a returned `SidecarHandle` dataclass.
- Hoist `tests/ipc/conftest.py` fixtures to a shared `tests/conftest.py` (cross-package fixture reuse).
- Bind-first + `EADDRINUSE` retry to remove the TOCTOU window between the stale-socket probe and the actual bind.

**Out of scope (per parent epic WOR-306):** healthcheck CLI (now WOR-310), keyring loading in sidecar (rejected, §11), key rotation, multi-key, MPC backend, systemd socket activation.

## Summary

- Replace hardcoded absolute path to jet_ui gem CSS with vendored copy in `app/assets/stylesheets/vendor/`
- Add `jet_ui:vendor` rake task to refresh CSS when gem version changes
- Remove environment-specific workarounds from Dockerfile and CI (both `test` and `system-test` jobs)

## Motivation

`application.css` had a hardcoded path tied to the developer's local asdf Ruby installation. This required brittle workarounds in three places: the CSS file itself, the Dockerfile (sed + Ruby injection), and CI (sed + generator). Any environment with a different Ruby path would fail silently or need its own patch.

## Approach

Vendor the CSS at `app/assets/stylesheets/vendor/jet_ui.css` (committed to git) and import it with a relative path. The vendored file is always available in every environment without any runtime path resolution.

## To update when jet_ui gem bumps

```bash
bin/rails jet_ui:vendor
git add app/assets/stylesheets/vendor/
git commit -m "build: update vendored jet_ui CSS to vX.Y.Z"
```

## Test plan

- [ ] 236 tests pass locally (`bin/rails test`)
- [ ] RuboCop clean

- [ ] No absolute paths remain: `grep -r "\.asdf\|gem_dir" app/assets/ Dockerfile .github/`

Implements the "Workshop Inventory" visual design system across the mobile app, replacing the Material Design baseline with a warm, workshop-focused aesthetic. This is a style-only refactor with no behavioral changes.

- **New design tokens module** (`src/theme.ts`): Centralized color palette, spacing scale, radius values, and typography definitions based on the visual direction spec
  - Core colors: warm paper neutrals (#F4EFE6), deep ink (#1C1A16), cedar-amber accent (#B6651E)

author: obusk
body:
## Summary

Replaces `node:dns` `Resolver.resolve4()` with raw UDP queries so the benchmark measures actual DNS round-trip time. Under Bun the previous implementation went through a client-side DNS cache, so repeated queries returned cached hits (sub-millisecond) rather than the upstream resolver's real RTT.

> **Note:** rebuilt on top of the pnpm/Node restructure (#14 and follow-ups). The branch was restarted from `main` and the change re-applied — the previous bun-era edits (`bun.lock`, `packages/core/build.ts`) are gone.

## Design

Three single-purpose classes (per review feedback):

- **`UdpClient`** (`udp-client.ts`) — generic point-to-point UDP transport, no DNS knowledge. `request(payload, timeoutMs, isMatch)` sends a datagram and resolves with the first reply accepted by `isMatch`, plus the round-trip time. Non-matching replies are ignored (a late reply to a previously timed-out request can't be mistaken for the current one). Validates the host IP with `node:net` `isIP()` and throws on garbage.
- **`DnsClient`** (`dns-client.ts`) — a functioning DNS client: builds A-record queries via `dns-packet` (fresh `node:crypto` `randomInt` transaction id per query), sends them over a `UdpClient`, decodes the full response, and returns the decoded packet together with separate `networkMs` and `parseMs` timings.
- **`DnsMeasurementClient`** (`dns-measurement-client.ts`) — reduces a query to one timing sample: rejects with `EBADRCODE:<rcode>` (e.g. `EBADRCODE:SERVFAIL`) unless the response is `NOERROR`, otherwise returns `networkMs`. This is what `measureAvg` in `index.ts` consumes.

**Timing discipline**: the network timestamp is captured inside `UdpClient`, immediately around the actual `socket.send()` / `message` event, and forwarded upward unmodified — packet encoding, decoding, and rcode validation all happen outside it (`parseMs` is reported separately by `DnsClient`).

**Warmup**: one untimed query per `(resolver, domain)` before the timed loop, so tries measure warm-path RTT (resolver cache, NAT, route). If every warmup query fails, `measureAvg` bails to `null` immediately.

**Failure handling**: a malformed resolver IP throws at construction; `measureAvg` catches it and reports a `null` row, so one bad user-supplied IP never crashes the run. A malformed response that fails to decode simply becomes a failed sample.

## Build / toolchain notes

- Core gains its first relative imports; sources keep `.ts` specifiers per repo convention (Node native type stripping), and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions: true` in `packages/core/tsconfig.build.json` rewrites them to `.js` in the emitted dist (verified under TypeScript 7).
- Adds `dns-packet@^5.6.1` (runtime) and `@types/dns-packet` (dev). dns-packet is CJS with static `exports.x =` assignments, so named imports resolve from the unbundled ESM dist under plain Node. Note: `decode()` sets `rcode` at runtime but `@types/dns-packet` omits it — bridged with a `DnsPacket` intersection type.

## Public API

Unchanged. `dnscmp(options)`, `DnscmpOptions`, `DnsResult`, `onResult` callback, sort order, defaults, and failure semantics (null after `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 3` consecutive query failures) are all identical to `main`.

## Verification

- `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run build` pass (pnpm 11.11.0, TS 7).
- `packages/core/dist/index.js` resolves `./dns-measurement-client.js` (specifier rewrite confirmed).
- `pnpm start` (Node, from source) shows realistic single-digit-ms RTTs across default providers (was sub-ms cached before).
- `node packages/cli/dist/index.js 1.1.1.1` (CI cli-runtime mirror) passes; also spot-checked under bun.
- Malformed IP (`999.999.999.999`) fails in ~100ms with a clean `failed` row, no crash.
- Unroutable IP (`192.0.2.1` / TEST-NET-1) declared dead in ~3s.

author: nizos
body:
## Summary

Main has stub adapters for Codex and Copilot and three syntactic rules that run against single-action payloads. This PR turns Conduct into a vendor-neutral policy engine where rules can read session history and call an AI validator scoped to the host agent's own SDK — and ships `enforce-tdd` as the first such rule.

Note: Running this through a PR just to perform a security scan on changes.

## What changes vs main

**Vendors become first-class**

- `src/adapter/<vendor>.ts` (flat stubs) → `src/vendors/<vendor>/{adapter,agent,transcript}.ts`.
- Codex `Bash` + `apply_patch` PreToolUse, with the OpenAI patch envelope parsed for path extraction.
- Copilot `bash`, `create`, and `edit` payloads via `@github/copilot-sdk`; `view` / `report_intent` are explicitly rejected as out of scope.
- Claude Code adapter gains `Edit` payload handling alongside Write.
- Each adapter exposes `sessionPath(payload)` so the engine can load the vendor's transcript without the adapter knowing how it's parsed.
- Adapter payloads parsed with zod discriminated unions at the trust boundary; unknown tools are rejected rather than coerced.
- A top-level `src/registry.ts` exposes `vendors` as `{ adapter, agent, readTranscript }` per vendor.

**AI / agent layer (entirely new)**

- New `Agent` type (`reason(prompt) => Promise<Verdict>`) plus three implementations: `claudeAgentSdk`, `codexSdk`, `githubCopilotSdk`. Each is a sync factory that lazy-loads its SDK on first `reason()` call.
- AI-validated rules reuse the auth the host agent already has — no separate API keys.
- The `--agent` flag picks both the adapter and the default AI provider; `Config.agent` is an override.
- Validators are isolated from host project/user settings; tool use is hard-denied via `permissionMode: dontAsk` + empty `allowedTools`.
- Verdicts validated with zod, code-fence-stripped, fail-closed on drift.

**Transcript history**

- Each vendor ships a transcript reader (JSONL) that emits chronologically ordered `SessionEvent`s (prompts + paired tool-call/result actions).
- `dispatch` composes `ctx.history` from `adapter.sessionPath(payload)` + `readTranscript(path)` and threads it into rules through `RuleContext`.
- Engine and `Rule.evaluate` become async; rules opt into history/AI by reading `ctx`.
- Shared `readJsonl` helper with size cap, symlink rejection, and malformed-line skipping.

**enforce-tdd (new rule)**

- Requires a failing test in the recent session, blocks over-implementation, blocks adding more than one new test per write.
- Reads the target file's current content from disk (with symlink + size guards) so the validator can diff against the pending write.
- Vendor-neutral rubric split into fixed process instructions + user-overridable TDD rules.
- Token-aware: `maxEvents` (10) and `maxContentChars` (1000) cap the validator prompt; long content is head-marker-tail truncated.
- `paths` option for scoping; custom `instructions` option for overriding the rubric.
- Integration tests cover clean-tdd / over-impl / no-test-run scenarios for all three vendors (gated on `CONDUCT_INTEGRATION_AI=1`).

**Hardening**

- `dispatch` returns deny on invalid JSON, adapter throws, or rule throws.
- Stdin payloads capped at 10 MiB; transcripts size-capped, symlinks rejected.
- `isVendor` rejects names inherited from `Object.prototype`.
- Rule arrays are `readonly` at engine/config/cli boundaries.
- Codex `transcript_path` zod-guarded; Copilot `sessionId` regex-guarded against path separators.

**CLI / API**

- `--version` and `--help` flags on the conduct CLI.
- Public surface adds `enforceTdd`, `RuleContext`, `Agent`, `SessionEvent`. Wildcarded `./rules/*` export.
- New runtime deps: `zod`, `@github/copilot-sdk`, `@openai/codex-sdk`. `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` moves devDeps → deps.

**Docs**

- README rewritten around vendor-agnostic positioning + features.
- `docs/rules.md` (built-in rule reference) and `docs/setup.md` (per-vendor wiring with `npx @nizos/conduct@latest`) added.
- CLAUDE.md Layout section updated to match the new structure.

author: bisman-singh
body:
When using a non-default `registry_port` (e.g. 5555), the registry container still listened on port 5000 internally. The Docker port mapping (`5555:5000`) only worked from the host but not from within the Kind network, so pods could not pull images using the configured port.

**Root cause:**
- `docker run -p ${registry_port}:5000` mapped the host port but the container always bound to 5000
- `hosts.toml` had port 5000 hardcoded instead of using `${registry_port}`

**Fix:**
- Set `REGISTRY_HTTP_ADDR=0.0.0.0:${registry_port}` so the registry binds on the configured port
- Map the same port on both sides: `-p ${registry_port}:${registry_port}`
- Use `${registry_port}` in `hosts.toml` instead of hardcoded 5000

**Tested with:**
- Custom port 5555: pods successfully pull images from `kind-registry:5555`
- Default port 5000: no regression, works as before

Fixes #143

author: trenthouliston
body:
Policy prices now update reactively via `TrackedParam` without requiring a full network rebuild. The update architecture uses pre-resolved `ElementUpdater` closures created at network construction time, providing a single unified code path for all element updates.

## Changes

### PolicyPricing model element
New `PolicyPricing` element with `TrackedParam[price]` for reactive price updates. Each instance multiplies per-tag power flow variables by a tracked price parameter, and updating the price triggers cost invalidation so the next optimization picks up the new value.

### Pre-resolved ElementUpdater bindings
`create_network()` now returns `dict[str, ElementUpdater]` instead of `dict[int, list[str]]`. At network construction time, `_discover_setters()` walks model element configs in parallel with live elements, finding `TrackedParam` descriptors and capturing direct setters as closures. On update, each `ElementUpdater` calls the adapter's `model_elements()` for fresh values and writes them via the captured setters — no runtime path resolution.

Both regular elements and policy pricing produce `ElementUpdater` closures with the same `Callable[[ElementConfigData], None]` signature, eliminating the policy vs non-policy branching in the coordinator.

### Rule-grouping VLAN signatures
VLAN assignment now uses source/destination set groupings instead of individual rule indices, so rules with identical endpoints share VLANs regardless of price differences.

### Disabled rule handling
Disabled rules are included in compilation with zero price instead of being filtered out, keeping network structure stable when toggling rules on/off.

## Files changed (20 files, +1089/-712)

- `core/model/elements/policy_pricing.py` — new PolicyPricing model element with TrackedParam
- `coordinator/network.py` — `_discover_setters`, `_build_element_updater`, `_build_policy_updater`; removed `update_element` and `update_policy_pricing`
- `coordinator/coordinator.py` — simplified `_apply_pending_element_updates` to single updater loop
- `coordinator/__init__.py` — export `ElementUpdater` instead of `update_element`
- `core/adapters/policy_compilation.py` — rule-grouping signatures, disabled-rule zeroing
- `core/adapters/elements/policy.py` — include disabled rules with enabled flag
- `core/model/network.py` — support for PolicyPricing in network
- `docs/developer-guide/coordinator.md`, `architecture.md` — updated for ElementUpdater architecture
- Tests updated across all layers

author: takaidohigasi
body:
### What is changed and how it works?

Issue Number: ref #19817

Upstream TiDB issue: pingcap/tidb#2519

What's Changed:

Add support for descending-order index keys in the coprocessor decoder, the
TiKV-side counterpart of pingcap/tidb#2519. TiDB has carried `DESC` in
`CREATE INDEX (col DESC)` syntax since MySQL 5.7 compatibility was added,
but the keyword has been silently ignored. The companion TiDB PR threads
`Desc` through index metadata and writes the column's memcomparable bytes
bitwise-complemented so a forward RocksDB iterator yields the declared
direction; this PR teaches TiKV to read those keys.

```commit-message
codec: add descending-order index key support (pingcap/tidb#2519)

Approach: auto-detection on the leading flag byte. Rather than adding a
per-column desc field to tipb.IndexScan, the encoder writes complemented
flag bytes (e.g. !INT_FLAG = 0xFC) and the decoder recognises them. This
avoids a protobuf change and means ASC-only callers see byte-for-byte
identical behaviour while DESC-encoded columns are inverted into a
scratch buffer and dispatched through the same ascending decoder, so
every type the ASC path handles works unchanged.

The single theoretical flag-byte collision (!FLOAT_FLAG == MAX_FLAG == 0xFA)
is unreachable because MAX_FLAG is exclusively a range sentinel that
this decoder never receives in stored row data.

Changes:
  * split_datum: recognise !FLAG leading bytes and compute lengths so any
    caller iterating an index key (including datum::skip_n, which locates
    the handle past the indexed columns) advances correctly past DESC
    columns.
  * decode_one_with_desc: new slice-based helper that complements a
    scratch buffer and dispatches through read_datum. Used by
    table::decode_index_key.
  * decode / read_datum: deliberately stay ASC-only so buffers that may
    legitimately contain the MAX_FLAG range sentinel (== !FLOAT_FLAG) are
    never misread as DESC floats; index keys that may contain DESC
    columns must be walked with decode_one_with_desc instead.
  * index-scan / table-scan executors: canonicalise DESC columns into the
    chunk columns via the new BufferVec::push_inverted, which complements
    bytes straight into the destination buffer without a per-cell
    allocation.
  * analyze: reject descending-order index columns in the index-analyze
    pushdown until the statistics pipeline understands them end to end;
    TiDB skips the pushdown for such indexes.
```

### Related changes

- [x] PR to update `pingcap/docs`/`pingcap/docs-cn`: **pingcap/docs#22805**
- [ ] Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [x] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No code

Unit tests (all passing):

- `tidb_query_datatype` (`cargo test -p tidb_query_datatype --lib desc`, 7/7):
  `test_split_datum_handles_desc_flags`,
  `test_decode_one_with_desc_round_trip`,
  `test_decode_one_with_desc_falls_through_to_asc`,
  `test_decode_one_with_desc_handles_mixed_asc_and_desc_stream`,
  `test_decode_one_with_desc_rejects_lone_max_flag`,
  `test_decode_one_with_desc_reinterprets_max_flag_with_trailing_bytes`,
  `test_split_datum_malformed_compact_bytes_desc_does_not_panic`
- `codec`: `test_encode_compact_byte_len_desc`
- `tikv_util`: `test_push_inverted`
- `tidb_query_executors`:
  `test_extract_columns_from_datum_format_desc_columns`,
  `test_extract_columns_from_datum_format_multi_desc_columns`,
  `test_common_handle_desc_encoded_column`

Integration test:

- `test_analyze_index_rejects_desc_encoded_columns` in
  `tests/integrations/coprocessor/test_analyze.rs`

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

This PR is a strict superset of behaviour: old TiDB never sends DESC
bytes, so the new code paths are unreachable until the companion TiDB PR
ships and operators set `tidb_enable_descending_index = on`. Safe to
merge and tag standalone; the TiDB PR's `MinTiKVVersionForDescIndex`
constant will pin to the released version after this lands.

The companion TiDB PR is **pingcap/tidb#68049** and the documentation PR
is **pingcap/docs#22805**.

### Release note
<!-- 
Compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note.

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

If you don't think this PR needs a release note then fill it with None.
If this PR will be picked to release branch, then a release note is probably required.
-->

```release-note
Add descending-order index key support to the coprocessor decoder, enabling MySQL 8.0-style descending indexes when paired with the corresponding TiDB release.
```

  * Descending-order index analysis is now rejected with a clear “descending” error.

* **Improvements**
  * DESC-encoded datums are detected and transparently normalized during index/key decoding.
  * Scan and buffer handling now correctly store DESC bytes in inverted form for downstream decoding.

* **Tests**

author: learningcircuit
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3635, addressing the two reviewer-flagged side effects of the fail-loud change there. After #3635 stopped swallowing migration failures in \`open_user_database\`, both **credential failures** and **migration failures** collapsed to the same \`None\` return — which the login route treated as "wrong password." That meant:

1. **Lockout counter incremented for migration failures.** A user with a correct password but a server-side schema/init problem (e.g. the world-writable migrations dir case fixed in #3635) could be locked out after 10 retries despite never typing a wrong character.
2. **Misleading user-facing message.** "Invalid username or password" sent users down the wrong troubleshooting path — they'd assume they typo'd, not that the server had a configuration problem.

## Approach

Introduce \`DatabaseInitializationError\` and raise it from \`open_user_database\` whenever \`initialize_database\` fails. The \`None\` return contract is preserved for credential / decryption failures.

The login route now catches the typed error **before** the credential branch:

| Failure mode | Status | Lockout counter | Flash message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Migration / init failure | **503** | **not** incremented | "Database initialisation failed. The server is misconfigured — please check the server logs or contact the administrator." |
| Bad password / decryption fails | 401 | incremented | "Invalid username or password" (unchanged) |
| Account already locked | 429 | (unchanged) | (unchanged) |

## Caller audit

\`open_user_database\` has 8 call sites. After this change, anything that previously checked \`if not engine\` continues to work for credential failures, but the new typed exception will propagate from init failures. I audited each:

| Call site | Existing wrapping | Action taken |
|---|---|---|
| \`web/auth/routes.py:120\` | none | **catches typed error explicitly** |
| \`web/auth/database_middleware.py:71\` | broad try/except | OK — caught + logged |
| \`web/queue/processor_v2.py:248\` | broad try/except | OK — caught + logged |
| \`web/queue/processor_v2.py:644\` | broad try/except | OK — caught + logged |
| \`web/queue/processor_v2.py:1098\` | broad try/except | OK — caught + logged |
| \`database/session_context.py:233\` | broad try/except | OK — caught + 500 response |
| \`database/encrypted_db.py:768\` (change_password) | broad try/except | OK — returns False |
| \`database/encrypted_db.py:845\` (metrics session) | none, raises ValueError on None | OK — typed error propagates instead, callers already wrap |
| \`database/thread_local_session.py:91\` | none | **catches typed error explicitly, returns None** |
| \`library/download_management/status_tracker.py:58\` | none, in \`__init__\` | **catches typed error and re-raises as \`RuntimeError\`** to keep \`encrypted_db\` internals out of library callers |

## Tests

- \`test_open_database_migration_failure_raises_typed_error\` — replaces the \`_returns_none\` test from #3635. Asserts the typed exception is raised, the engine is disposed, and no entry is cached in \`connections\`.
- \`test_returns_503_for_database_init_failure_without_lockout\` — new route-level test. Mocks \`open_user_database\` to raise the typed error, asserts the response is 503, and asserts \`lockout_mgr.record_failure\` is **not called**. This is the regression test for the user-visible bug.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pytest tests/web/auth/test_auth_routes.py::TestLogin\` — 4 passed (3 existing + 1 new)
- [x] \`pytest tests/database/test_encrypted_db_manager.py::TestDatabaseOpening\` — 6 passed (incl. updated test)
- [x] \`pytest tests/web/auth/test_auth_routes.py tests/database/test_encrypted_db_manager.py tests/database/test_thread_local_session.py\` — 118 passed
- [x] \`pre-commit\` — all hooks pass on touched files
- [ ] Manual: verify login flow on a misconfigured server (force a migration failure, e.g. \`chmod -R o+w migrations/versions/\` in a venv) — expect 503 + clear flash message + no lockout increment.

## Why \`DatabaseInitializationError\` over a result-tuple / sentinel

Considered three alternatives:

1. **Result type** (\`OpenResult(engine, error)\`) — would require updating every caller's check from \`if not engine\` to \`if not result.engine\`. 8+ call sites in scope. Out of proportion for the win.
2. **Side-channel state** (\`manager._last_failure_kind[username]\`) — racy, leaks state across requests, awkward.
3. **Typed exception** (chosen) — minimal change for callers that don't care, opt-in handling for the one caller that needs to differentiate. Standard Python idiom.

## Security

Showing a different status code/message for "credentials valid, server broken" *technically* leaks whether a user account exists in self-hosted shared deployments. The marginal information leak is small (timing and registration endpoint already reveal user existence), and the alternative is silently locking out users for a server-side bug, which is strictly worse. For LDR's typical single-user-per-deployment usage, the leak is essentially zero.

## Summary

Adds a full pipeline for comparing DX100 hardware EG envelopes against the softsynth:

- **`gen_eg_test_bank`** – generates `testdata/syx/eg_test_bank.syx`, a 24-voice bank sweeping all EG parameters (AR, D1R, D1L, D2R, RR) plus Piano/Organ/Pluck presets

```sh
# Generate test bank
```

## Summary
Fixed an issue where switching between playbooks would retain the running state from the previous playbook, preventing immediate frame sending on the newly selected playbook.

## Changes
- Reset `_running` flag to `False` when switching playbooks in `_switch_playbook()`
- This allows users to immediately send frames on a newly selected playbook without waiting for the previous playbook's worker to complete
- The `exclusive=True` parameter in `run_worker` will handle cancellation of any lingering worker from the previous playbook context when the next send operation starts

## Implementation Details
The fix recognizes that a playbook run in progress belongs to the previous playbook's context and should not carry over when the user switches to a different playbook. By resetting the `_running` flag, the UI correctly reflects that no operation is in progress for the newly selected playbook.

author: combatorpheus
body:
💡 What: Changed BFS reachability edges from `Vector{Vector{Int}}` to `Vector{Tuple{Int, Int}}`.
🎯 Why: Constructing a two-element `Vector{Int}` (e.g. `[src, dest]`) creates a heap allocation every time an edge is found. Constructing a `Tuple{Int, Int}` (e.g. `(src, dest)`) is heap-allocation-free as it is placed on the stack. `Tuple` elements can still be accessed sequentially during matrix construction, avoiding overhead without sacrificing features.
📊 Impact: Cut down memory allocations and execution time further. Filtering 1000 random SPNs takes ~370ms now compared to ~420ms prior to this change.
🔬 Measurement: Validated using `@btime` tracking `SPNGenerator.filter_spn(pn)`.

author: hahaschool
body:
## Summary

- Adds `packages/control-plane/src/memory/import-edge-gen.ts` — a new module that generates `memory_edges` rows connecting related facts after each import batch commits.
- Integrates edge generation into `runImport` (claude-mem) in `memory-import.ts`; designed so JSONL callers pass `mode: 'jsonl'` when that flow lands.
- 37 new unit tests covering all edge types, weight semantics, and idempotency.

## Edge types created

| Mode | Trigger | Relation | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-mem` | 2+ shared concepts between facts | `related_to` | 0.2 per concept, max 0.8 |
| `claude-mem` | Same `memory_session_id`, no concept edge | `related_to` | 0.1 |
| `jsonl` | Consecutive sessions share a project path component | `related_to` | 0.05 |

## Weight semantics

- Concept overlap weight accumulates at **0.2 per shared concept**, capped at **0.8**. Two facts with 4+ concepts in common get a near-maximum edge; one shared concept gets a minimal edge.
- Session context weight (**0.1**) is strictly weaker than any concept edge and is skipped if a concept edge already exists for the pair.
- JSONL cross-session weight (**0.05**) is the weakest, indicating temporal proximity rather than semantic overlap.

## Idempotency guarantee

All inserts use:
```sql
INSERT INTO memory_edges ... ON CONFLICT (source_fact_id, target_fact_id, relation) DO NOTHING
```

The unique constraint `(source_fact_id, target_fact_id, relation)` on `memory_edges` (from migration 0010) prevents duplicate rows. Re-running an import for the same observations will find the facts already in `existingIds` and skip them, so no duplicate facts or edges are created.

Additionally, within a batch, canonical pair keys (`smallerId::largerId`) deduplicate edges before hitting the DB, and session edges are suppressed for pairs that already have a concept edge.

## Security

All SQL uses parameterized queries (`pool.query('...', [p1, p2, ...])`). No string interpolation.

author: nao1215
body:
## Summary

Generated `params.gleam` always imported `None` and `Some` from
`gleam/option` even though the rendered code only references the
`Option` type itself. `gleam build --warnings-as-errors` flagged
both as unused, and downstream callers couldn't fix it because the
file is `// DO NOT EDIT`.

This change scopes the `gleam/option` import emitted by both
`codegen/params.gleam` and `codegen/adapter.gleam` to exactly the
items each file references — `{type Option}` when only the type is
needed, and the full `{type Option, None, Some}` only when the
file actually emits the constructors.

## Changes

- `src/sqlode/codegen/params.gleam`: replace the always-emitted
  `import gleam/option.{type Option, None, Some}` with
  `import gleam/option.{type Option}`. The renderer never produces
  `None` / `Some` literals, so the constructors were unconditionally
  unused.
- `src/sqlode/codegen/adapter.gleam`:
  - Replace the single `needs_option_import_for_adapter`-gated
    line with a new `adapter_option_import` helper that splits the
    decision into \"needs the type\" vs \"needs the constructors\":
    - `:one` / `:batchone` queries are the only ones whose
      generated wrapper emits `Some(row) / None`, so they are the
      only ones that need the constructors.
    - The type is needed whenever any param / result column is
      nullable OR whenever a `:one` / `:batchone` exists (the
      wrapper returns `Option(Row)`).
  - Resulting matrix:
    | needs type | needs ctors | emitted import |
    |---|---|---|
    | false | false | (none) |
    | true  | false | `import gleam/option.{type Option}` |
    | true  | true  | `import gleam/option.{type Option, None, Some}` |
    | false | true  | `import gleam/option.{None, Some}` (defensive; not currently reachable) |
- `test/codegen_test.gleam`:
  - `render_params_module_imports_only_option_type_test` —
    asserts that on a fixture with nullable params (\`narg(...)\`),
    `params.render` emits the type-only import and contains no
    `None` / `Some` token.
  - `render_pog_adapter_imports_option_constructors_with_query_one_test`
    — asserts the existing `query.sql` fixture (which has
    `GetAuthor :one`) keeps the full constructor-bearing import.
  - `render_pog_adapter_imports_only_option_type_without_query_one_test`
    — asserts that `macro_edge_cases.sql` (which is `:many` /
    `:exec` only but uses `narg(...)`) emits the type-only import
    and does not pull in the constructors.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: note the fix under `[Unreleased]` with the rule
  spelled out so future reviewers do not re-broaden the import.

## Design Decisions

- Picked the per-file scoping path (Issue's primary suggestion)
  rather than file-wide glinter ignore rules in downstream
  consumers. The library is the right place to fix this — the
  alternative inverts the meaning of the `// DO NOT EDIT` header
  and pushes a workaround onto every user.
- Kept the existing `needs_option_import_for_adapter` decision
  intact (renamed to `adapter_needs_option_type`) and added a new
  `adapter_needs_option_constructors` predicate alongside it. The
  pair is small enough to keep both as named functions instead of
  inlining; the docstring on `adapter_option_import` explains
  which side surfaces which constructor.
- The `False, True` row of the matrix (\"needs constructors but
  not the type\") is defensively kept in the `case` expression so
  the codegen does not emit a malformed import if a future
  refactor introduces a `Some(...) / None` literal in a path that
  doesn't otherwise touch `Option`. Today this branch is not
  reachable; the comment in the source records that.
- Did not touch `codegen/models.gleam` or `codegen/queries.gleam` —
  both already emit `import gleam/option.{type Option}` only.

## Limitations

- This is a code-generation fix; existing generated files in
  downstream repos still contain the stale broad import until the
  user re-runs `sqlode generate`. The CHANGELOG entry flags the
  one-action remedy.
- No CHANGELOG entry under `### Changed` because the fix is
  strictly subtractive: every file that previously compiled still
  compiles bit-for-bit aside from the trimmed import line.

Closes #463

author: fukusaka
body:
## Motivation

`EpollEventLoop.registerCallback` and `KqueueEventLoop.registerCallback` take a `() -> Unit` callback that is allocated as a fresh lambda on every call. The call site in `{Epoll,Kqueue}IoTransport.armRead` fires once per read event (every request on /hello), so the per-call lambda allocation accumulates: at 1.9M req/s on luna it's roughly 1.9M short-lived lambdas/sec from this site alone.

This was originally on the rank-3 list of the kqueue/epoll engine deep-review. The first attempt — field-caching the lambda (one `val readCallback: () -> Unit = { onReadable() }` per transport) — was measured and showed engine throughput tied with main at peak saturation. The deep-review then surfaced a stronger structural option: have the IoTransport itself **be** the callback by implementing a typed `fun interface` (mirroring the kotlinx.coroutines `Job : DisposableHandle` pattern). That removes the field too — `this` is the listener — and makes the receiver's "I respond to fd readiness" contract explicit in the class signature.

The judgement framework the keel project uses for this kind of optimization (fast/slow path identification + structural-correctness / design-clarity axis when there is no measurable engine improvement) was established in this round and applied here: both candidates land on **structural correctness + design clarity** (engine bench tie at peak — the alloc cost is real but invisible at engine throughput because per-request work dominates). Of the two, the listener-interface approach wins on both axes (zero alloc + zero field + class signature expresses the role), so it's the version landed here.

## 動機

`EpollEventLoop.registerCallback` / `KqueueEventLoop.registerCallback` は `() -> Unit` callback を毎呼び出しで lambda alloc していた。`{Epoll,Kqueue}IoTransport.armRead` の call site は read event 毎発火 (`/hello` 1 リクエスト 1 回)、luna で 1.9M req/s = ~1.9M 短命 lambda/sec をこの site だけで生成していた。

kqueue/epoll engine 総合評価 rank 3 由来。当初の field-cached lambda 案は engine bench tie で peak saturation 改善 measurable でなかった。深掘りで「IoTransport 自体が callback **である**」設計 (kotlinx.coroutines `Job : DisposableHandle` precedent) が浮上。field も消え、`this` が listener、class signature が "fd readiness に応答する" contract を明示できる。

本ラウンドで確立した最適化判断フレーム (fast/slow path 識別 + measurable improvement なしの場合は structural correctness + 設計明確化 軸) を本 PR に適用。両候補とも engine bench tie at peak で **structural correctness + 設計明確化** 軸の merge (alloc cost は real だが per-request work に埋もれて throughput には表れない)。両軸 strong な listener interface 方式を採用。

## Modification

### `EpollEventLoop` / `KqueueEventLoop`

- New `fun interface FdReadyListener { fun onReady(interest: Interest) }` nested in each EventLoop, alongside the existing `Interest` enum. The single method takes the `Interest` so a single implementation can dispatch read vs. write callbacks without separate sub-listener objects.
- `callbackRegistrations` map type changes from `LongObjectMap<() -> Unit>` to `LongObjectMap<FdReadyListener>`.
- `registerCallback` third parameter changes from `callback: () -> Unit` to `listener: FdReadyListener`.
- Dispatch site (`cb()` → `cb.onReady(interest)`) — the EventLoop already knew the interest at the dispatch point, so passing it through is free.

### Receivers (`{Epoll,Kqueue}IoTransport`, `{Epoll,Kqueue}PipelinedStreamServer`)

- `IoTransport` adds `EpollEventLoop.FdReadyListener` (resp. Kqueue) to its supertype list, with `onReady(interest)` dispatching `READ → onReadable()`, `WRITE → onWritable()`. The previously-inline write-callback body is extracted to a private `onWritable()` so the dispatch is symmetric. `armRead()` / `registerWriteCallback()` pass `this`.
- `PipelinedStreamServer` adds the listener to its supertype list. Only `READ` is registered for the listening fd (the server never arms write), so `onReady` delegates unconditionally to `onAcceptable()`.

### Tests

- `EpollEventLoopSeamTest` updated for the new SAM signature: `registerCallback(...) { _ -> /* noop */ }` (previously `{ /* noop */ }`).

### Design decisions

- **Single `FdReadyListener` per engine vs. separate `ReadReadyListener` / `WriteReadyListener`**: a `class` cannot implement the same SAM twice, so two listener interfaces would be needed for type-safe per-direction dispatch on the same receiver. Single interface with an `Interest` parameter is simpler at the call site (one method to override, one map type, one `registerCallback` overload) at the cost of a single enum compare in the receiver. Engine bench is tied either way; preferred the simpler API surface.
- **Defined nested in each EventLoop**: each engine's `Interest` enum is engine-specific (epoll vs. kqueue both happen to have `READ` / `WRITE` but they're different types). A unified cross-engine listener interface would also need a unified `Interest`, which would couple the two engines unnecessarily. The natural sharing layer is a future engine-common module split that would also collect `AbstractIoTransport` / `MpscQueue` / `LongObjectMap`; deliberately keeping per-engine for now.
- **NIO not covered**: `NioEventLoop.setInterestCallback` uses a single attachment per `SelectionKey`, which doesn't separate read vs. write callbacks the way POSIX engines do. Adapting it to the listener-interface pattern requires deeper restructuring of the NIO model. Left for the same future engine-common work where engine API surfaces can be aligned at once.
- **io_uring not affected**: doesn't use `registerCallback` (the SQE/CQE path goes through different APIs).

## 変更内容

### `EpollEventLoop` / `KqueueEventLoop`

- 新 `fun interface FdReadyListener { fun onReady(interest: Interest) }` を各 EventLoop に nested で定義 (既存 `Interest` enum と隣接)。単 method が `Interest` を受け、1 implementation で read / write callback を別 sub-listener なしで dispatch 可能
- `callbackRegistrations` map type を `LongObjectMap<() -> Unit>` → `LongObjectMap<FdReadyListener>`
- `registerCallback` の第 3 引数を `callback: () -> Unit` → `listener: FdReadyListener` に変更
- dispatch site (`cb()` → `cb.onReady(interest)`) — EventLoop は dispatch 時点で interest を既に知っているので、渡すのは free

### Receiver (`{Epoll,Kqueue}IoTransport`, `{Epoll,Kqueue}PipelinedStreamServer`)

- `IoTransport` に `EpollEventLoop.FdReadyListener` (kqueue 同) を supertype 追加、`onReady(interest)` で `READ → onReadable()` / `WRITE → onWritable()` 分岐。inline write-callback body を private `onWritable()` に抽出 (dispatch 対称化)。`armRead()` / `registerWriteCallback()` は `this` を渡す
- `PipelinedStreamServer` も listener を supertype 追加。listening fd は READ しか arm しないので `onReady` は無条件で `onAcceptable()` に委譲

### Test 修正

- `EpollEventLoopSeamTest` の SAM signature 変更対応: `registerCallback(...) { _ -> /* noop */ }` (旧: `{ /* noop */ }`)

### 設計判断

- **engine ごとの単一 `FdReadyListener` vs. 2 つの専用 listener (Read/Write)**: 同 SAM を class が 2 回 implement できないので、direction 毎の type-safe dispatch を同 receiver で行うには 2 interface 必要。単 interface + `Interest` 引数の方が call site (single method、single map、single overload) シンプルで、receiver 側 enum compare 1 回 cost は engine bench で誤差。bench tied なら simpler 採用
- **engine 内 nested 定義**: 各 engine の `Interest` enum は engine-specific (epoll / kqueue 共に `READ` / `WRITE` 名は同じだが別 type)。cross-engine 統一 listener interface は `Interest` 統一を強制 → 不要な engine 結合。共通化は将来の engine-common module 切り出し (`AbstractIoTransport` / `MpscQueue` / `LongObjectMap` も一緒に集約) に集約
- **NIO は対象外**: `NioEventLoop.setInterestCallback` は `SelectionKey` 単一 attachment model で、POSIX engine のような read / write callback 独立 dispatch にできない。listener-interface 適用には NIO model 自体の見直しが必要。同 engine-common 作業で engine API surface を一括整理する際に扱う
- **io_uring は不影響**: `registerCallback` を使わない (SQE/CQE path は別 API)

## Test plan

- [x] `:keel-engine-epoll:linuxX64Test :keel-engine-epoll:detektLinuxX64Main` (luna) — pass
- [x] `:keel-engine-kqueue:macosArm64Test :keel-engine-kqueue:detektMacosArm64Main` (macOS) — pass
- [x] aggregate `jvmTest macosArm64Test jsNodeTest dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml` + detekt (macOS) — BUILD SUCCESSFUL

*After*: Hovering the popup close 'x' displays a "Close popup (Esc)" tooltip.

- `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email` — public, body `{ token }`, click-from-email handler
- `POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification` — auth-required, "didn't receive the email?" button

Non-blocking by design — the API key + session are issued unconditionally on signup; verification just dismisses the banner. A transient SMTP outage logs but does not roll back the user's account.

## Why this slice now

Per the corrected R1 ordering, this is purely-additive backend work that unblocks the admin `/verify-email` route slice and lets the onboarding banner go from display-only to dynamic. Independent of the deploy-config items still pending (`COOKIE_DOMAIN`, `CORS_ORIGINS`).

## Change

### Migration 019 — [019_email_verification.sql](packages/backend/src/db/migrations/019_email_verification.sql)

- `application.users.email_verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL` — null until verified.
- `application.email_verification_tokens` table: `id`, `user_id` FK, `token` UNIQUE, `expires_at`, `consumed_at` (single-use marker), `created_at`.
- Active-token-by-user partial index for the resend lookup.
- Comments distinguishing this from the existing `organization_requests.email_verified_at` (the enterprise admin-approval flow has its own state machine and email copy).

### Service — [signup.service.ts](packages/backend/src/saas/services/signup.service.ts)

- **Inside the existing signup transaction**, after user creation, insert a token row sharing the same expiry. A COMMIT failure rolls back BOTH user and token — no orphan.
- **After COMMIT**, fire-and-forget the verification email. SMTP failure is logged but does not surface to the caller. User can resend.
- **`verifyEmail(token)`** — atomic consume (UPDATE with `consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW()` — closes the race window between findActive + consume), refuses if `users.email_verified_at` is already set (matches the docstring's already-verified guard, prevents stale tokens from re-stamping the column).
- **`resendVerification(userId, locale?)`** — opens the txn with `users.lockForUpdate(userId)` to serialize concurrent resends per user, invalidates prior unconsumed tokens, issues a fresh one. Without the lock, two concurrent resends could each see 0 active tokens, both insert, and leave 2 active tokens — breaking the "latest link is the only one that works" guarantee. Silent no-op when the user is already verified so the route returns the same 200 in both cases (no probe-able state).
- Exported `IVerificationEmailSender` interface so tests can pass a stub without `as never` casts. Concrete `SignupEmailService` has private fields that block structural mocking.
- Shared `getContactNameForEmail(user)` helper used by both signup-time and resend-time email sends.

### Email — [signup-email.service.ts](packages/backend/src/saas/services/signup-email.service.ts)

New service mirroring [`OrgRequestEmailService`](packages/backend/src/saas/services/org-request-email.service.ts) — SMTP via nodemailer, en/ru/kk locales, never throws (returns boolean). Distinct from the org-request service because the verification URL (`/verify-email` vs `/verify-request`) and copy differ.

### Routes — [signup.ts](packages/backend/src/api/routes/signup.ts)

- Shared `requireSelfServiceSignupEnabled` preHandler gates all three routes (signup, verify-email, resend-verification) with one source of truth — new sibling routes can't forget the check.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email` — public, rate-limited 5/min/IP. Token entropy makes guessing infeasible; cap is defense-in-depth.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification` — `requireUser` + tighter 3/min cap so an authed user pressing the button repeatedly hits it fast (protects SMTP capacity + discourages email-bombing).

### Repository / DB wiring

- New [`EmailVerificationTokenRepository`](packages/backend/src/db/repositories/email-verification-token.repository.ts): `findActiveByToken`, atomic `consume` (single UPDATE rechecking expiry), `invalidateUnconsumedForUser`.
- New `UserRepository.lockForUpdate(id)` — purely additive; runs `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` for the resend serialization.
- Wired into `RepositoryRegistry`, `DatabaseClient`, `factory.ts`.

### Schemas

- `verifyEmailSchema` — body `{ token: string (32–128) }`, response `{ email_verified: true }`.
- `resendVerificationSchema` — no body, response `{ message }`.

## Tests

[tests/saas/signup.service.test.ts](packages/backend/tests/saas/signup.service.test.ts) — **+10** new cases (24 → 34): signup token-row creation + email fire-and-forget + non-blocking on SMTP failure, `verifyEmail` happy path + 4 error paths (unknown / empty / consume-race / already-verified user), `resendVerification` invalidate-and-issue + already-verified silent no-op + 404 on stale JWT.

Mock DB extended with `findById`, `findActiveByToken`, `consume`, `invalidateUnconsumedForUser`, `tx.users.lockForUpdate`, `tx.users.update`, `tx.users.findById`, plus a stub email service typed against `IVerificationEmailSender`.

[tests/api/routes/signup.route.test.ts](packages/backend/tests/api/routes/signup.route.test.ts) — **+8** new cases (6 → 14): verify-email 200/400/403/short-token, resend 401/200×2/403. Test harness now registers `createAuthMiddleware` so `requireUser` populates `request.authUser` from the test JWT (matches production wiring). Resend tests use a `buildResendDb(verified)` helper that wires the txn-level `tx.users.findById` and the auth-middleware-level `db.users.findById` to the same user fixture.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @bugspotter/backend test:unit` — **2321/2321 pass** (+18 new).
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @bugspotter/backend test:integration` — runs migration 019 against testcontainers Postgres in CI.
- [ ] After merge + deploy: hit `POST /api/v1/auth/signup`, confirm verification email arrives. Click link, confirm `users.email_verified_at` is set. Hammer `/auth/resend-verification` from two windows simultaneously, confirm only one token is active afterwards.

## Scope guardrails (deferred, all tracked)

- **Admin UI banner stays display-only** until a separate slice exposes `email_verified` in a response (signup/login/dedicated `/auth/me`).
- **No queue worker for emails** — direct SMTP, same as existing org-request flow.
- **No "must verify before billing"** — Sentry-style non-blocking. R6 hardening can flip this for billing actions if needed.
- **Token hashing at rest** — Copilot raised this as defense-in-depth (org-request flow stores hashed tokens). Deferring: 24-hour single-use tokens have a much lower risk profile than passwords, the retrofit needs a hashed-lookup path + backfill migration, and many production systems (Stripe, Auth0, etc.) store similar tokens raw. Worth doing if a threat model later surfaces the read-the-DB-from-backups vector as material; not blocking on this slice.

## What's next

Once this lands, the admin `/verify-email` route can wire up to call `POST /auth/verify-email` from the click-from-email link, and the banner can be made conditional. Both are admin-side slices in a separate PR.

Human-Wildlife Conflict Monitoring and Alert System – Description

This project is a simple mobile application that helps people report and get alerts about wildlife sightings in nearby areas. It is mainly useful for villages or areas near forests where human and animal interactions happen frequently.

In this app, users can report if they see any wild animal by adding details like location and a short description. This information is stored in the system and can be viewed by other users. Based on these reports, the app sends basic alerts or notifications to people in nearby locations so they can stay careful.

The app also provides some general safety tips and emergency contact information to help users during such situations.

The main aim of this project is to create awareness, improve safety, and reduce conflicts between humans and wildlife. It is useful for protecting both human lives and animal lives by helping people stay alert and avoid dangerous situations.

author: pvizeli
body:
## Summary
The user-facing \`/docs/global-spaces/\` page had two factually wrong claims I cross-checked against spec §24 today. Fixing both, plus a few smaller drifts.

## Hard errors fixed

**1. "Conversation flows directly between joined households — no relay traffic."** Wrong. Per spec §24.3:
> \`posts flow: SH → GFS_POST_RELAY → GFS → all subscriber instances\`

The relay is the post hub for the lifetime of the space, not a one-shot introducer. Page now states this plainly: every message and reaction goes through the relay every time, and the relay relays-and-forgets (no storage).

**2. "E2EE is available but off by default."** Wrong. Per spec §4.1.10:
> *"every content event is always encrypted; there is no opt-out"*

There is no toggle in v1.0 — encryption is mandatory across every space, global or private. Page now states this with the spec citation.

## Smaller drifts also fixed

- **Joining** is governed by the host-set \`join_mode\` (\`open / request / invite_only / link\`) — page now lists all four modes instead of implying "always admin-approved".
- New **"What happens if the relay is down?"** section explaining the fire-and-discard behaviour (§25.8.4) and recommending multi-relay subscription for resilience.
- **Isolation rule** noted (§24.3) — global spaces never leak into your paired-household graph.
- Comparison table rebuilt against the corrected facts.

The postcard / sealed-envelope analogy stays — non-protocol readers still get a mental model — but the technical claims under it now match what the server actually does.

author: eanzhao
body:
## Summary

After #418 merged, production `/daily` still fails with `github_proxy_access_denied`. Independent manual reproduction (session-token-minted child key, both narrow and broad scopes) succeeds end-to-end against the same NyxID account, GitHub UserService, and proxy slug. The production-only failure has to live in either the deployed `POST /api-keys` payload or the preflight response shape, neither of which is visible in current logs.

This PR adds **diagnostic-only** log lines on the daily-report create path so the next failed `/daily` captures ground truth, then revert.

## What's logged

- **Before `CreateApiKeyAsync`**: resolved per-user `UserService.id`s and the literal payload JSON. Tells us whether the deployed binary actually carries `allow_all_services=false` and whether `ResolveProxyServiceIdsAsync` returned per-user ids vs catalog ids.
- **After successful create**: the new api-key id, for correlating to NyxID-side `proxy_request_denied` audit records.
- **Inside `PreflightGitHubProxyAsync`** (Information level): the *raw* probe response. The parsed `proxy_body` we return only carries the inner Lark/GitHub body string when SendAsync wraps non-2xx; the unparsed probe is the only place we see exactly what NyxID returned. Distinguishes:
  - NyxID `ApiKeyScopeForbidden` (`error_code:9000`, our payload is still wrong somehow)
  - GitHub upstream 403 (`Bad credentials`, OAuth grant revoked)
  - Other shapes
- **On preflight failure** (Warning level): the structured envelope we hand back to the user, so the failure is one self-contained log line.

## Why this PR exists separately

These logs are temporary debugging — once the production log captures the real failure shape, this PR (or just the four log lines) gets reverted. Splitting it off keeps the revert clean and avoids re-opening the #418 conversation.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build agents/Aevatar.GAgents.ChannelRuntime/Aevatar.GAgents.ChannelRuntime.csproj` — clean (40 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors).
- [x] `dotnet test test/Aevatar.GAgents.ChannelRuntime.Tests/Aevatar.GAgents.ChannelRuntime.Tests.csproj --filter AgentBuilderToolTests` — 30/30 passing.
- [ ] Deploy + trigger `/daily alice` from Lark, capture log lines tagged `Diagnostic[#417]`. Revert this PR after.

## Follow-up after capture

Depending on what `Diagnostic[#417]: GitHub preflight probe response` shows:
- If NyxID `error_code:9000` → resolver still returns wrong ids despite the apparent fix; need to revisit `ResolveProxyServiceIdsAsync` or how the relay-token auth path lists user-services
- If GitHub `Bad credentials` → OAuth grant on the bot owner's GitHub binding is unhealthy on the relay-token path even though it's healthy on session-token reads; need to look at how NyxID picks the credential to inject for relay-scoped api-keys
- If something else → analyze case-by-case

author: caueshaze
body:
Closes #71

## Summary

Active area effects with ``effectKind="obscurement"`` and ``obscurement="heavily_obscured"`` (Fog Cloud) now block line of sight in map-backed targeting. Line of effect is unchanged — Fog Cloud blocks sight, not effect propagation. Spike Growth (hazard) is unaffected.

## Behavior

LoS fails when the origin, target/anchor, or any traversed intermediate cell is inside a heavily obscured area. The map server returns one of four specific reason codes so the UI can surface the actual cause:

- ``origin_heavily_obscured`` — caster is in the cloud
- ``target_heavily_obscured`` — single-target attack: target is in the cloud
- ``point_heavily_obscured`` — area spell: anchor cell is in the cloud
- ``line_of_sight_obscured`` — path crosses the cloud

Existing ``no_line_of_sight`` is preserved for walls/obstacles.

## Stack changes

- **tactical-engine**: ``isCellHeavilyObscured`` + ``evaluateLineOfSight`` diagnostic. ``hasLineOfSight`` gains an optional ``activeAreaEffects`` param (backwards compatible).
- **map-server**: single-target route, area-targeting route, and ``TargetingService`` pass ``encounter.activeAreaEffects`` and surface the new reasons. Area routes remap target → point automatically.
- **map-web**: PT-BR labels + detail builders for the four reasons, prioritised above generic ``no_line_of_sight``.
- **control-server**: no production code changes.

## Test plan

- [x] tactical-engine LoS unit tests: 9 new (target/origin/path obscurement, side-by-side path passes, hasLineOfEffect unchanged, walls still report ``no_line_of_sight``, Spike Growth no-op, backwards compat)
- [x] map-server integration tests: 6 new (target inside, caster inside, path crosses, ``requires_sight=false`` passes, area preview ``point_heavily_obscured``, Spike Growth no-op)
- [x] control-server integration tests: 4 new (target/origin/area-anchor obscurement rejections + no-sight-required passes)
- [x] map-web targeting suite: 4 new label/builder cases
- [x] All TS suites green: tactical-engine 144, map-server 230, map-web targeting 65
- [x] control-server full suite: 1307 passed, 1 skipped

body:
This PR implements the person-centric migration in `Plans/person-migration-plan.md`: the backend now treats Student/Teacher as typed `Person` records and introduces `/people` as the canonical API. Existing `/students` and `/teachers` contracts are preserved via compatibility services/controllers over the unified model.

- **Domain + API unification**
  - Added `Person` entity (`personType`, shared identity fields, role-specific nullable fields).
  - Added `PersonRepository`, `PersonService`, `PersonController` and new DTOs (`PersonRequest`, `PersonResponse`).
  - Kept `/students` and `/teachers` endpoints stable while refactoring internals to use `PersonType.STUDENT` / `PersonType.TEACHER`.

- **Persistence cutover to single person reference**
  - Refactored `Attendance` and `NotificationLog` to reference `Person` (via `person_id`) instead of separate `student_id`/`teacher_id`.
  - Updated repository query methods and dedup paths to operate on `person_id` + `personType` semantics.
  - Refactored attendance aggregation/debug/upsert paths to resolve participants through `Person`.

- **Meet/notification flow refactor**
  - Updated attendance helper/session handler logic to process expected participants as typed `Person` collections.
  - Kept role-specific notification behavior (e.g., parent-email routing only for student-subject notifications).

- **Schema migration governance**
  - Added Flyway and introduced `V1__person_cutover.sql` for:
    - `person` bootstrap/backfill from legacy `student`/`teacher`
    - reassignment of attendance/notification FKs to `person_id`
    - constraint/index cutover and legacy table removal
  - Switched JPA schema mode to validation (`ddl-auto=validate`) with Flyway-managed migrations.

```java
// Attendance now stores one typed person reference
Attendance.builder()
    .person(person)
```

## Summary

Public-repo-hygiene plan **batch 1** — pure structural cleanup. Takes content out of public HEAD and adds gitignore guards so the same content can't slip back in.

This is the **first of 4 batches** (see `docs/exec-plans/active/autosearch-0425-public-repo-hygiene-plan.md` STATUS section). Batch 2 = tooling (committer / husky / gitleaks / hygiene script). Batch 3 = rewrite remaining public docs that have internal voice. Batch 4 = history exposure assessment + final verify.

## What's in this PR (4 commits, ~3.7k lines deleted, no functional code changes)

| Commit | Plan ref | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `chore(gitignore): harden against internal docs + runtime experience reentry` | F008 | Add `docs/plans/`, `docs/proposals/`, `docs/spikes/`, `docs/channel-hunt/`, `*.private.md`, `*.handoff.md` to gitignore. Drop the `!patterns.jsonl` explicit-allow lines. |
| `chore(public-repo): remove internal plans + proposals from public HEAD` | F002 | `git rm` 6 markdown files (channel-governance, discourse-forum, v2 tool-supplier proposal, w3-3 pipeline removal, wave-2/3 status). |
| `chore(public-repo): remove spike + channel-hunt logs from public HEAD` | F002B | `git rm` 11 files (2 spike write-ups + 8 channel-hunt logs + 1 .gitkeep). |
| `chore(public-repo): untrack HANDOFF + runtime experience, remove spike data` | F003 S1 + F005 | `git rm --cached` HANDOFF.md + 2 patterns.jsonl (kept locally). `git rm` 3 spike test fixtures (no test depends on them). |
