Public GitHub page currently exposes:

- Internal exec plans / architectural drafts / pre-implementation proposals
- One-shot spike harness write-ups with failure rates and "bypass via cookie/UA" suggestions
- Channel reconnaissance logs with rate-limit heuristics, anti-bot detection notes, supplier auth state
- Session handoff state (HANDOFF.md was tracked despite being in .gitignore — gitignore doesn't apply to already-tracked files)
- Live runtime experience JSONL with real query patterns

None of this is user-facing reference material. It exposes implementation strategy and process without giving the public any usable knowledge.

## What's intentionally NOT in this PR (deferred)

- **F003 S2/S3** — rewrite `CLAUDE.md` as public contributor guide + add `docs/internal-docs.md`. These are content rewrites, not structural cleanup, and need careful public/private boundary judgment. → batch 2.

- **F012 / F013** — history exposure assessment + final verify. → batch 4.

author: aquie00t
body:
Hi team! 👋

While reviewing `lib/config-validator.js`, I noticed a small opportunity to optimize the memory allocation in the `defaultSchemaErrorFormatter` function.

**Current Behavior:**
The current implementation uses `slice(0, -separator.length)` at the end of the loop. This creates a new string object in memory, which triggers unnecessary Garbage Collection, especially if the server is hit with a high volume of bad requests that fail schema validation.

**Proposed Change:**
I applied a simple loop unrolling technique:
- Extract the first error formatting outside the loop.
- Start the loop from index `1`.
- Prepend the `separator` instead of appending it.

**Benefits:**
1. Avoids the `slice()` completely, saving memory allocation.
2. Keeps the loop "branchless" (no `if` statements inside the loop), maintaining fast V8 execution.
3. Fully adheres to the existing StandardJS formatting.

Let me know if this makes sense for the repository!

author: cjot
body:
## Problem

The `observable-frontend-1` container was showing a warning icon in Docker tooling because the Docker healthcheck was reporting `unhealthy` (463+ consecutive failures) despite nginx serving real traffic correctly.

**Root cause:** The nginx config only had `listen 80;`, which binds to IPv4 only. Inside Alpine-based containers, `localhost` resolves to `::1` (IPv6). The healthcheck command `wget --spider -q http://localhost/` connects to `[::1]:80`, gets a connection refused, and fails — while external traffic routed through the Docker port mapping hits `0.0.0.0:80` just fine.

## Fix

Add `listen [::]:80;` to `apps/frontend/nginx.conf` so nginx binds on both IPv4 and IPv6 stacks. This makes the healthcheck work correctly regardless of how the container resolves `localhost`, and is the correct behaviour for any dual-stack or IPv6-only environment.

## Files Changed

- `apps/frontend/nginx.conf` — added `listen [::]:80;`

- Instruments `src/sessionManager.ts` with structured `key=value` log lines at every session-lifecycle decision point — tracking, close-detection tier outcomes (all three tiers), PID index writes/deletes, and reconcile poll ticks. **Zero logic changes** — instrumentation only
- 4 new tests: 3 in `test/debugLog.test.ts` (gate behaviour) + 1 wiring test in `test/sessionManager.debugLog.test.ts`

## Log prefix reference

| Prefix | Where emitted |
|---|---|
| `[track]` / `[track:pid]` | `_trackIfClaudeSession` — on track or skip, and when PID resolves |
| `[close]` | `_handleTerminalClose` — entry with `sessionsBefore` count |
| `[close:tier1]` / `[close:tier2]` / `[close:tier3]` | Per-tier hit or miss detail |
| `[close:tier3:no-pid]` | PID resolved to `undefined` or `processId` rejected |
| `[remove]` | `_removeByKey` — success with `sessionsAfter`, or double-fire miss |
| `[pid:delete]` | PID removed from index with `pidsAfter` count |
| `[reconcile]` | Reconcile entry with session and live-terminal counts |
| `[reconcile:evict]` | Each terminal evicted by reconcile |
| `[reconcile:clean]` | Reconcile tick with no evictions |

## Testing instructions for the user

To capture logs for #68 diagnosis:

1. Open VS Code Settings and set `claudeConductor.debugLogging` to `true`
2. Launch a Claude Conductor session normally (or let an existing one run)
3. Leave it running for several hours
4. When the bug occurs (session still shown in Active Sessions panel after closing the editor tab via X), immediately open **View → Output** and select **"Claude Conductor"** from the dropdown
5. Copy the full contents of the output channel and paste them into a comment on #68
6. In particular, look for `[close:` lines near the time the X was clicked — or their absence, which would indicate the `onDidCloseTerminal` event was never fired

Key diagnostic questions the logs answer:
- Did any `[close:` line fire at all? (If not: VS Code never fired `onDidCloseTerminal`)
- If `[close:tier1]` / `[close:tier2]` / `[close:tier3]` all show `miss`: reconcile should catch it on the next poll tick — look for `[reconcile:evict]`
- Compare `[track:pid]` name/pid pairs with `[close:tier3]` pid values to verify the PID index was populated correctly before the close fired

body:
## 🤖 New release * `oxideav-vp8`: 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 (✓ API compatible changes)
Changelog

## [0.1.2](https://github.com/OxideAV/oxideav-vp8/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2) - 2026-05-02 ### Other - per-frame scene-cut adaptation - per-MB segment maps with per-segment quantiser deltas - per-MB context-adaptive ref-frame probabilities - alt-ref / golden-ref planning + Lagrangian RDO mode decision - adopt slim VideoFrame shape - pin release-plz to patch-only bumps ### Added - Per-frame scene-cut adaptation in the encoder. New `Vp8EncoderConfig` knobs `enable_scene_cut` (default on), `scene_cut_threshold` (default 4.0), `scene_cut_quant_boost` (default 8) and `scene_cut_boost_frames` (default 4). The encoder watches each incoming source frame's per-pixel luma mean-absolute-difference (MAD) versus the previous source frame and flags a scene cut when the MAD exceeds `mean(MAD) + threshold · stddev(MAD)` over the running 16-frame window (also gated by an absolute floor of 12 luma units to avoid spurious cuts on quiet content). On a flagged cut the next frame is forced to a keyframe, the LAST / GOLDEN / ALTREF reference slots are dropped, and the post-cut N frames receive a linearly-tapered qindex boost so the rebuild GOP starts at higher quality. The legacy `make_encoder_with_qindex` constructor keeps the detector off so handcrafted small-frame test sequences stay bit-exact with pre-#166 behaviour. Six new integration tests in `tests/encoder_scene_cut.rs` cover the splice-point detection, the no-false-positive guarantee on steady-pan content, the post-cut PSNR regression, the legacy-cadence opt-out, and ffmpeg cross-decode validation. - Per-MB segment maps (RFC 6386 §10). The encoder classifies each MB by source-luma 16×16 variance into one of four segments, then emits the segmentation block (`segmentation_enabled = 1`, `update_map = 1`, `update_data = 1`, `abs_delta = 0`) with the per-segment quantiser deltas from `Vp8EncoderConfig`. Per-MB segment_id bits are written before the skip flag using entropy-matched `tree_probs`. Default deltas `[-8, -4, 0, +4]` put smooth content into the low-qi segments (extra bits where the eye notices banding) and high-variance content into the high-qi segments. On a synthetic mixed-content fixture the bit-saving variant `[0, +2, +6, +12]` shrinks the bitstream by ~14% with sub-1 dB PSNR cost. Disable with `enable_segments = false` to recover the legacy single-segment encoding bit-for-bit. - Decoder: per-MB dequant now consults `header.segmentation` + `info.segment_id` so segmented streams (from this encoder or libvpx) reconstruct correctly. Honours both `abs_delta` modes. - Five new integration tests in `tests/encoder_segments.rs` covering the frame-header signalling on/off, the byte-size shrink on the mixed clip, the encoder ↔ in-tree-decoder roundtrip with segments on, and ffmpeg cross-decode validation. - Alt-ref / golden-ref planning in the encoder. New `Vp8EncoderConfig` exposes `golden_interval` (default 8 P-frames), `alt_ref_interval` (default 13), `enable_multi_ref` and `enable_rdo` knobs; the encoder maintains LAST / GOLDEN / ALTREF reference slots on the schedule and emits the matching `refresh_golden_frame` / `refresh_alternate_frame` flags in the inter header. - Per-MB reference-frame selection across LAST / GOLDEN / ALTREF, with `find_near_mvs_enc` now ref-aware (neighbours whose ref_frame differs from ours contribute nothing, exactly mirroring the decoder's RFC 6386 §16.3 walk). - Lagrangian rate-distortion mode decision (`D + λ·R`) replacing the prior SAD-only picker. λ = `lambda_scale * QP^2 / 256` with a default scale of 218 (≈0.85·256). Rate is approximated from the per-MB mode-info bool-coded bits (skip / intra-vs-inter / ref / MV tree / MV deltas) using a 256-entry log2 LUT. - New `make_encoder_with_config(params, Vp8EncoderConfig)` constructor for callers that want fine-grained control over the new knobs. - Six new integration tests in `tests/encoder_altref_rdo.rs` covering the refresh-flag schedule, multi-ref vs single-ref BD-rate comparison, end-to-end decode at high PSNR, ffmpeg cross-decode validation, and the legacy single-ref opt-out path. ### Changed - Per-MB context-adaptive `prob_intra` / `prob_last` / `prob_gf` (RFC 6386 §9.10 field J): the encoder now runs the P-frame in two passes — pass 1 makes per-MB mode/ref decisions and accumulates the actual ref-frame distribution (intra / LAST / GOLDEN / ALT counts) without touching the bool encoder; pass 2 picks the entropy-matched prob triple from those counts (`round(256 · n_zero / total)`, clamped to 1..=255) and emits the frame with the optimised probs. Replaces the prior fixed `200 / 128 / 128` (multi-ref) and `200 / 1 / 128` (single-ref) literals. - Real-content byte-size deltas on the existing fixtures: SMPTE-bars 30-frame clip −13.4% (1336 → 1157 B); gray 30-frame clip −22.9% (782 → 603 B); Mandelbrot 30-frame clip −1.25% (14201 → 14023 B, small because residual dominates intra-heavy frames). ffmpeg cross-decodes every fixture cleanly. - New tests in `tests/encoder_ref_prob_context.rs` pin the per-frame prob triple against the actual MB ref-frame distribution and the total-bytes regression on the SMPTE fixture; new unit tests in `encoder.rs` cover `optimal_prob_8` rounding/clamping and the prob-triple emit on an all-SKIP P-frame.

body:
## Summary

- **Step 1**: Cache a structural `Int` hash on every `Type` node alongside the existing `TypeFlags`, computed at construction by combining children's cached hashes with a per-constructor salt. Adds `Hashable (Type a)` (O(1) via the cached field) and `Hashable (Constraint a)`.
- **Step 3**: Switch the `unificationCache` in `Unify.hs:121–123` from `Set (Type, Type)` to `HashSet (Type, Type)`. This drops `compareType` from the unification cache hot path entirely.
- Measured **-15.4% on full builds** of pr-admin (median of 4, 47515-49155 ms; tight). Neutral on the three incremental scenarios.
- `Ord Type` is deliberately unchanged — see the rust-interning Phase 2 trap in `LESSONS.md`.

`compareType` was the new top hotspot at 7.7% post-merges (after synonym-opt + skip-redundant-entailment-unify shipped). The unification cache is the largest single source.

## Final results (vs baseline `799e8208`)

| Scenario | Base (s) | Head (s) | Δ | Notes |
|----------|---------:|---------:|---|-------|
| full | 57.0 | 48.2 | **-15.4%** | tight, 47515-49155 ms |
| nochange | 0.6 | 0.6 | -1.9% | tight, 564-594 ms |
| prelude | 4.0 | 4.0 | -0.3% | within noise |
| leaf | 1.6 | 1.6 | -1.1% | very noisy (1550-8576 ms) |

## Two non-obvious implementation details

Both look like minor codegen hints but each is a 2× swing on full builds when missed. Documented in `experiments/LESSONS.md`:

1. **`{-# UNPACK #-}`** on the `!TypeFlags` field of every `Type` constructor. `TypeFlags` went from `newtype` (zero-cost wrapper) to a 2-field record; without UNPACK every Type allocation indirects through an extra boxed object — measured +107% on full. With UNPACK, the regression collapses to ~+1.8%.
2. **`{-# INLINE #-}`** on the `Hashable Type` instance methods. Without it GHC dispatches through the class dictionary at every hash call, allocates thunks, and the supposed HashSet win measures **worse** than Set (+102% on full). With INLINE the dictionary collapses through to a direct field read and the headline win drops out.

A `eqType` hash short-circuit (step 2) was tried and reverted — the hot callers (Entailment.hs:295 guard) compare equal types most of the time, so the hash check just adds work. See LESSONS.md.

## Test plan

- [x] `stack test --fast`: 1340 examples, 0 failures
- [x] All four scenarios on pr-admin: full / nochange / prelude / leaf

author: learningcircuit
body:
## Summary

The `journal-data-integration` release-gate workflow has been failing on transient mid-stream S3 disconnects:

```
ChunkedEncodingError(ProtocolError('Connection broken:
  IncompleteRead(835082 bytes read, 1262437 more expected)'))
```

## Root cause

`safe_get_with_retries` (introduced in ed7fc9e16) wraps the `safe_get` call only. The HTTP body isn't actually read until the caller touches `resp.content` — by which point `safe_get` has already returned, so the retry wrapper can't see the disconnect that fires during `tmp_part.write_bytes(resp.content)` inside `iter_partitions`. Result: a single partition's mid-stream hiccup aborts the whole 30-partition pull.

## Fix

Wrap the per-partition fetch + body-read in its own retry loop inside `iter_partitions` (3 attempts, 2/5/10s backoff) catching `ChunkedEncodingError` and `ConnectionError`. The outer `try/finally` still cleans up the tmp file on terminal failure; a partial download is unlinked between attempts so each retry starts from a clean slate.

This complements `safe_get_with_retries` rather than replacing it — that wrapper still handles header-stage failures (DNS, connect, 5xx), and the new loop handles body-stage failures.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/journal_quality/test_openalex_common.py` (10/10 pass — 7 existing + 3 new)
- [x] `pytest tests/journal_quality/` (139/139 pass)
- [x] `pre-commit run` clean on changed files
- [ ] CI green on `journal-data-integration` workflow (the actual end-to-end gate this PR aims to unblock)

## New unit tests
- `test_retries_on_chunked_encoding_error` — first attempt raises `ChunkedEncodingError`, second succeeds, output records intact
- `test_retries_on_connection_error` — same shape but with `ConnectionError`
- `test_gives_up_after_max_retries` — terminal failure raises through, tmp file cleaned up

author: omargawdat
body:
Followup to #201. Makes the DB pool fields required + documents them everywhere they're expected, so config drift fails loudly at startup instead of silently using a (possibly wrong) default.

## Changes

### `config/helpers/env.py` — remove defaults
```diff
-db_pool_min_size: int = 0
-db_pool_max_size: int = 5
+db_pool_min_size: int
+db_pool_max_size: int
```
Pydantic now raises `ValidationError` on app startup if either is missing — surfaces config drift immediately rather than silently falling back to defaults.

### `dummy.env` — add the vars (so local + CI work)
```diff
 # Database
 DATABASE_URL=postgis://postgres:postgres@postgres:5432/mydatabase
+# Connection pool per gunicorn worker (3 workers x max_size = total per instance)
+DB_POOL_MIN_SIZE=0
+DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE=5
```
Local dev (`cp dummy.env .env`) and CI (`docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml`) both pick these up automatically.

### `README.md` — list in AWS Secret Manager config block
```diff
 "DATABASE_URL": "postgis://user:password@host:5432/dbname",
+"DB_POOL_MIN_SIZE": "0",
+"DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE": "5",
```
Anyone deploying a fresh instance from this template now sees these keys in the required-secrets list.

## Why this approach

The defaults-in-code pattern (from #201) is convenient but hides intent — a fork can `cp dummy.env .env` and never know these env vars exist. Making them required + documenting in dummy.env/README means:

- Devs see the values when they look at dummy.env
- New prod deploys can't silently miss them — Pydantic blocks startup
- Tuning per-environment is the obvious workflow, not a hidden trick

## Migration impact

Existing forks that pull this template change must add `DB_POOL_MIN_SIZE` and `DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE` to their AWS Secret Manager configs. The 6 already-patched Eram-Group backends (foodmatic, Dars, sukoon, almansk, Alfaheam-oud, homeservices) hard-code the values in their own `base.py`, so they're not affected by this template change.

## Summary

每个 sisyphus 机械 checker（`spec_lint` / `dev_cross_check` / `staging_test` / `pr_ci_watch`）源码里都显式写了 `refusing to silent-pass` guard，设计上"零信号即 fail"。但只有源码层这一道防线 —— 一旦 guard 被改坏 / for 循环静默吃错误，checker 会报 `passed=true` 但其实啥也没跑，状态机就推下一 stage，最坏情况合掉一个根本没过测试的 PR。

**Q18 是事后 metrics 兜底**：从 `artifact_checks` 已落表样本反查"通过了但其实没干活"的记录。

三类信号（CASE 优先级从严到松）：
- `guard-leak` —— `stdout/stderr` 命中 `refusing to silent-pass` 但 `passed=true` → checker 内 guard 行打了但 exit code 仍是 0
- `no-gha-pass` —— `pr_ci_watch` stdout 留 `no-gha-checks-ran` 但 `passed=true` → `_classify` 分类逻辑被改坏
- `too-fast` —— `duration_sec < 0.2 × 同 stage 7d P50（passed=true 样本）` → 脚本短路（和 Q2 慢异常对称）

`guard-leak` / `no-gha-pass` 是绝对信号（不依赖基线），任意命中即告警；`too-fast` 同 Q2 一样 `HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20` 防小样本噪声。

## Summary

- Wire `GET /admin/api/v1/dynamo/tables` and `GET /admin/api/v1/dynamo/tables/{name}` per design doc Section 4.1, both gated by the existing protect chain (BodyLimit → SessionAuth → Audit → CSRF). Audit is a no-op for GET so dashboard polling does not flood the audit log.
- Adapter side: `AdminListTables` / `AdminDescribeTable` SigV4-bypass entrypoints (Section 3.2), exposing a stable `AdminTableSummary` DTO that keeps `dynamoTableSchema` private.
- Pagination matches Section 4.3: `limit` (default 100, hard max 1000) plus an opaque `next_token` (base64url-wrapped last name). A vanished cursor fast-forwards rather than stalling the SPA.
- `ServerDeps.Tables` is optional — leaving it nil keeps the dynamo paths off the wire (standard `unknown_endpoint` 404), so a build that ships only the cluster page works unchanged.
- `main_admin.go` bridges `*adapter.DynamoDBServer` via `dynamoTablesBridge`. The two summary structs are intentionally isomorphic so any future field drift breaks the build at the bridge.
- Internal errors are logged in full and surfaced to clients only as `dynamo_list_failed` / `dynamo_describe_failed` codes; raw `err.Error()` is never sent over the wire.

Stacked work this unblocks (separate PRs): `POST /dynamo/tables` (CreateTable), `DELETE /dynamo/tables/{name}`, AdminForward RPC for follower→leader forwarding (Section 3.3), and the matching S3 read-only endpoints.

Builds on PR #874 (slice 1: `rcan_version`, `signing_alg`, `agent_runtimes`, `rrn_format`) with three more RCAN 3.x structural checks. Each runs unconditionally in the `rcan_v3` category and skips on non-3.x manifests.

### `rcan_v3.estop_response_ms`

Art. 9 reactive-safety budget. When `safety.estop.software` is declared, `response_ms` must be declared AND ≤ 100ms (EU AI Act risk-management ceiling for collaborative manipulators). Catches:
- software estop with no `response_ms` → fail (silent reactive-safety hole)
- `response_ms` over budget → fail (declared latency too lax for collab use)

Skips when software estop isn't declared (budget check is N/A).

### `rcan_v3.capability_namespacing`

3.x mandates dotted `verb.noun` shape for `capabilities[]` (e.g., `manipulate.pick`, `perceive.rgb`). Pattern: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+)+$`. Multi-segment names like `manipulate.pick.precise` accepted. Catches legacy bare names (`pick`, `wave`) that survived 2.x→3.x migration. Empty capabilities list passes (no violations possible).

### `rcan_v3.record_url`

When `metadata.rrn` is declared, `metadata.record_url` must reference the canonical RRF v2 path (`https://robotregistryfoundation.org/v2/robots/<rrn>`). Catches:
- stale `rcan.dev` refs (legacy host pre-cascade) → fail
- `record_url` referencing a different RRN (copy-paste bug) → fail
- `rrn` declared but no `record_url` → warn (documentation gap, not blocker)

Skips when `rrn` isn't declared (nothing to canonicalize against).

## Verification

End-to-end on bob's ROBOT.md (`RRN-000000000002`, `rcan_version=3.2`):

```
✅ [rcan_v3.estop_response_ms] safety.estop.response_ms is 50ms — within Art. 9 budget
✅ [rcan_v3.capability_namespacing] all 5 capability name(s) use dotted verb.noun shape
✅ [rcan_v3.record_url] metadata.record_url references RRN-000000000002 on robotregistryfoundation.org
```

All 7 v3 checks ✅ for bob (4 slice 1 + 3 slice 2).

## Test plan

- [x] 18 new tests in `tests/test_conformance_v3_slice2.py`
- [x] estop_response_ms: 6 tests (declared/missing/over/at-ceiling/no-software/non-3x)
- [x] capability_namespacing: 5 tests (dotted/legacy/empty/multi-segment/non-3x)
- [x] record_url: 6 tests (canonical/missing/stale-rcan.dev/wrong-rrn/no-rrn/non-3x)
- [x] integration: slice-1+slice-2 = 7 v3 checks for 3.x manifests
- [x] 186/186 conformance + compliance tests green
- [x] ruff check + format clean

author: cortomaltese3
body:
## Summary

- **Export Diagnostics**: new Settings → Diagnostics section writes a local ZIP (no upload) bundling electron-log + Python backend logs from the last 7 days, system info (OS / CPU / RAM / disk free, app version, engine version), and the last 5 scenario metadata rows (`scenario_id`, `country`, `hazard`, `computed_at` only — no raw user data). Default save path is `Desktop/riskwise-diagnostics-<ISO-timestamp>.zip` with user override via `dialog.showSaveDialog`.
- **Opt-in Sentry**: `@sentry/electron` is initialized in the Electron **main process only**, gated on (1) a build-time `SENTRY_DSN` sidecar baked by `scripts/write-sentry-dsn.js` (the value never appears in source), (2) explicit user consent persisted in `electron-store`, and (3) offline mode being off. First-launch consent dialog is a MUI dialog that mirrors the auto-update consent pattern from #115.
- **Privacy doc**: `docs/privacy.md` enumerates what is logged, what Sentry sends, what is never sent, and how to opt out.
- **Three new IPC channels** (`diagnostics:export`, `diagnostics:get-sentry-status`, `diagnostics:set-sentry-consent`) added to the preload allowlist test so the bridge surface stays explicitly auditable.

## Notes for reviewers

- Issue lists `build/electron.js` and `vite.config.ts` as files to modify; the actual source-of-truth in this repo is `public/electron.js` (Vite copies `public/` → `build/` at build time, and `build/` is gitignored) and `vite.config.mjs`. I edited the right ones.
- DSN injection avoids touching Vite — the renderer never sees the DSN. Instead, the post-build `scripts/write-sentry-dsn.js` writes `build/sentry-dsn.json` from the env var, and `electron.js` reads from that sidecar (with a `process.env.SENTRY_DSN` fallback for local `npm run start:electron`).
- Scenario rows are fetched via `httpRequest("GET", "/api/v1/scenarios")` rather than opening DuckDB from Electron main — opening the DB file from a second process while the backend holds the connection would risk a lock conflict, and the backend already exposes the exact rows we need ordered by `created_at DESC`.
- The ZIP is hand-rolled on top of `zlib.deflateRawSync` (no new ZIP dep). Round-trip tested via a minimal central-directory parser in the test suite.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 28 files, 155 tests pass (added `diagnostics.test.js` for the ZIP/log-collection logic and `DiagnosticsSection.test.jsx` for the UI; updated `preload.test.js` allowlist)
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (24 unrelated pre-existing warnings)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `prettier --check` on all changed files — clean
- [ ] Manual smoke test in a packaged build (out of scope for this PR — the IPC + ZIP path is covered by unit tests, but a real run with `SENTRY_DSN` set would need a release-channel CI build to verify Sentry events land in the dashboard)

author: clubanderson
body:
## Problem

StackContext creates a new `value` object on every render, causing all consumers (StackStatusCard, LLMDStackCard) to re-render even when no stack data changed. Additionally, `getStackById` and the demo-mode `refetch` create new function references each render.

## Changes

- **`getStackById`** → wrapped in `useCallback` (depends only on `stacks`)
- **`selectedStack`** → replaced inline IIFE with `useMemo` (depends on `stacks`, `selectedStackId`)
- **Demo-mode `refetch`** → stable `useCallback(() => {}, [])` instead of inline arrow
- **Context `value`** → wrapped in `useMemo` with all dependencies listed

## Impact

Eliminates unnecessary re-renders for StackContext consumers on every provider render cycle. Follows the same proven pattern used in PR #10028 (AlertsContext memoization).

## Testing

- `npm run build` ✅
- `npm run lint` ✅ (no new errors)

author: drufball
body:
## Summary

- **Issues are now branch-aware**: every issue gets a `branch` field. With no parent and no `--branch` flag the branch is auto-slugified from `<id>-<title>`; child issues inherit their parent's branch; `--branch` overrides both. `ns2 issue edit --branch` and `ns2 issue list` (new branch column) also supported.
- **Sessions run inside git worktrees**: when a session starts, the harness resolves `<worktree-base>/<branch>`, creating the worktree from `origin/main` if it doesn't exist. The worktree path becomes the cwd for all tool calls (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`). Worktrees persist across sessions — never auto-deleted.
- **`ns2 worktree list|create|delete`**: three new CLI commands to inspect and clean up ns2-managed worktrees. `delete` checks whether the branch is merged to `main` and errors unless `--force` is passed.
- **`ns2.toml` config**: `[worktrees] path = "..."` configures the worktree base directory; defaults to `~/.ns2/<repo>/worktrees/`.
- **Branch-level concurrency lock removed**: multiple sessions on the same branch are now allowed; worktree isolation provides the necessary separation.
- **Product-flow specs 24–26** added for the new flows; all existing specs re-verified.
- **Mutation test coverage improved**: self-contained workspace git tests, testable `format_issue_row`, injectable `resolve_session_cwd_with_root`, whitespace/home-dir edge-case tests. Mutation score on changed lines: 31/34 caught (3 inherently untestable thin wrappers).

author: nao1215
body:
## Summary

`sqlode generate` rejected a SQLite `WHERE x BETWEEN ? AND ?` query
with:

```
Query "ListEntries": could not infer type for parameter $1.
Use a type cast (e.g. $1::int) to specify the type
```

Both halves of that message are wrong for SQLite:

- `\$1` is a Postgres-style placeholder reference. SQLite uses `?`
  (or `?N`); the configured engine never produced `\$N`.
- `\$1::int` is a Postgres-only cast extension. Pasting that into a
  SQLite query is a parse error.

The same failure mode affected MySQL, where the canonical cast
form is `CAST(? AS SIGNED)`. Following the hint produced a fresh
error in both engines.

This change makes `analysis_error_to_string` engine-aware. The
placeholder reference and the cast-syntax hint both now follow the
configured engine's dialect, so the suggested fix in the error
message is something the user can paste into their query verbatim.

## Changes

- `src/sqlode/query_analyzer/context.gleam`:
  - `analysis_error_to_string` now takes a second `engine:
    model.Engine` argument.
  - Two new private helpers, `placeholder_label(engine, idx)` and
    `cast_hint(engine, idx)`, encode the dialect for each engine
    in one place. The `ParameterTypeNotInferred`,
    `UnrecognizedCastType`, and `ParameterTypeConflict` arms all
    route through `placeholder_label` (and the first one through
    `cast_hint`) so a future engine only requires editing two
    helpers.
  - Engine matrix:

    | engine | placeholder | cast hint |
    |---|---|---|
    | PostgreSQL | `\$N` | `Use a type cast (e.g. \$N::int) to specify the type` |
    | SQLite | `?N` | `Use CAST(? AS INTEGER) to specify the type` |
    | MySQL | `?N` | `Use CAST(? AS SIGNED) to specify the type` |

- `src/sqlode/query_analyzer.gleam`: bump the public re-export
  signature to match.
- `src/sqlode/generate.gleam`: pass `block.engine` into
  `analysis_error_to_string`.
- `src/sqlode/verify.gleam`: same.
- `test/query_analyzer_test.gleam`:
  - Update the six existing call sites to pass `model.PostgreSQL`
    (the previous default the tests were written against).
  - Add five new tests pinning the per-engine wording: PostgreSQL
    keeps the dollar/cast hint; SQLite swaps to `?N` and `CAST(?
    AS INTEGER)` AND must NOT produce \`\$1\` / \`::int\`; MySQL
    swaps to `?N` and `CAST(? AS SIGNED)`; the placeholder-label
    swap also takes effect on \`UnrecognizedCastType\` and
    \`ParameterTypeConflict\`.
- `test/sqlode_test.gleam`: re-export the five new tests.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: note the user-visible behaviour change AND the
  signature change under `### Changed` with a `**BREAKING**`
  marker so library consumers calling
  `analysis_error_to_string` directly know to add the engine
  argument.

## Design Decisions

- Threaded the engine through the function signature rather than
  baking it into the `AnalysisError` variants. The error type is
  produced deep inside the analyser (per parameter, per query) and
  is reused across multiple consumers; carrying engine on every
  variant would duplicate the same value across hundreds of error
  values without buying anything. Passing it at the formatting
  boundary keeps the value where it is naturally available
  (`block.engine` is in scope at every caller).
- Used `?N` (1-based) for SQLite and MySQL placeholders. SQLite
  natively accepts the `?N` form; MySQL's wire-level placeholder
  is the bare `?` but the *reference* in an error message is
  informational, and `?N` reads as \"the Nth `?`\" without
  ambiguity. The alternative — falling back to prose like
  \"parameter at position N\" — would have meant longer messages
  with no syntactic precedent in the engine's own diagnostics.
- Marked the change as breaking (`!` in the commit type) because
  `analysis_error_to_string` is `pub` and library consumers can
  call it. The CHANGELOG entry spells out the migration (one
  added argument). No internal call site is left in the old
  shape.
- Did not add an engine-aware variant of `UnsupportedExpression`'s
  hint (`Use CAST to specify the type explicitly`), because that
  message does not embed any engine-specific syntax — it just
  tells the user to use `CAST`, which all three engines support
  in the ANSI form. Touching it would be churn without a user
  benefit.

## Limitations

- This PR fixes the *suggestion* shape but does not extend the
  type inferencer to handle every SQLite range query out of the
  box. The Issue notes that even with `CAST(? AS TEXT)`
  substituted in, sqlode still failed with the same \"could not
  infer type\" error for some shapes — that is a separate
  inferencer-coverage gap (a follow-up Issue would track it). The
  diagnostic the user now sees is at least pasteable.
- Library consumers calling `analysis_error_to_string` directly
  must add the engine argument. The CHANGELOG flags this; the
  internal callers are migrated.

Closes #473

author: kennethsinder
body:
Closes #565.

## Summary

Implements the `code_index/` module in `harn-hostlib` end-to-end, lighting up the five host builtins whose schemas were locked in by [#563](https://github.com/burin-labs/harn/issues/563):

- `hostlib_code_index_query` — trigram-accelerated literal substring search (`needle`, `case_sensitive`, `max_results`, `scope` filter).
- `hostlib_code_index_rebuild` — depth-first walk + (re)build of the in-memory index.
- `hostlib_code_index_stats` — file count / distinct trigrams / words / memory bytes / last rebuild ms.
- `hostlib_code_index_imports_for` — per-file imports as `(module, resolved_path, kind)` triples.
- `hostlib_code_index_importers_of` — reverse import lookup.

Ports the Swift `Sources/BurinCodeIndex/` actor from `burin-labs/burin-code` byte-for-byte where the encoding mattered (FNV-1a 64 hash, ASCII case-fold trigram pack, identifier-shaped word tokenizer). Import resolution is data-driven via `data/code_index_import_rules.json` (Python, TS/JS, Java/Kotlin, Scala, C#, PHP, Elixir, Haskell, Lua, Ruby, C/C++, Zig, R, Swift, Rust, Go) — adding a language is a JSON edit, not a Rust edit.

## Module layout

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/code_index/trigram.rs` | `TrigramIndex` posting list, sliding 3-byte window, ASCII case-fold |
| `src/code_index/words.rs` | `WordIndex` with `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` tokenizer |
| `src/code_index/graph.rs` | `DepGraph` forward + reverse + unresolved side table |
| `src/code_index/file_table.rs` | `IndexedFile`, `FileId`, FNV-1a 64 |
| `src/code_index/walker.rs` | Filtered walker + sensitive-file rejection (mirrors `FilteredWalker`/`SensitiveFilter`) |
| `src/code_index/imports.rs` | Keyword-prefix extraction + data-driven resolver |
| `src/code_index/state.rs` | `IndexState` orchestrator, `last_built_unix_ms`, git HEAD |
| `src/code_index/builtins.rs` | Five host handlers behind a single shared `Arc<Mutex<Option<IndexState>>>` |
| `data/code_index_import_rules.json` | Per-language resolver config (bundled via `include_str!`) |

## Performance

Live `BURIN_CODE_REPO=~/projects/burin-code` rebuild over the burin-code monorepo:

```
live burin-code rebuild: 5442 files in 3.57s
```

Well within CI time budget (env-var-gated; default scenario test uses a synthetic Swift fixture).

- 21 new unit tests across the seven sub-modules (trigram, words, graph, walker, imports, file_table, state).
- 9 builtin-level integration tests in `tests/code_index.rs` exercising every handler end-to-end via the registry.
- 2 scenario tests in `tests/code_index_scenario.rs`: synthetic fixture under `tests/fixtures/burin_code_subset/` (always run) + env-var-gated `BURIN_CODE_REPO` smoke (manual).

author: copilot
body:
Node.js was installed via the NodeSource apt repo (pinned to 24.x), which makes version switching awkward and requires rebuilding the image to upgrade. Non-root container users also couldn't run `npm install -g` since the global prefix was owned by root.

## Changes

- **nvm instead of NodeSource apt**
  - nvm v0.40.3 installed to `/usr/local/nvm` (shared, not `~/.nvm`) so every user in the container has access
  - Installs the latest LTS and sets it as default (`nvm alias default lts/*`)
  - Switching versions inside the container is now just `nvm install <version> && nvm use <version>`

- **Non-root write access**
  - `chmod -R a+rwX "$NVM_DIR"` applied after install — intentional dev-only trade-off to let any container user run `npm install -g` without sudo

- **Shell init**
  - `/etc/profile.d/nvm.sh` written for login shells
  - Same snippet appended to `/etc/bash.bashrc` for interactive non-login shells
  - `NVM_DIR` exported as a Docker `ENV` so it's available at both build and runtime

- **bats**
  - `npm install -g bats` run as part of the nvm setup layer — available globally to all users

author: laurigates
body:
## Summary

The `XTAL_FREQ_AUTO` and `BTDM_CTRL_*` Kconfig symbols are only defined
when `IDF_TARGET=esp32`. Keeping them in the shared `sdkconfig.defaults`
causes "unknown kconfig symbol" warnings on every other target supported
by the ESP-IDF example build (ESP32-S3, S2, C3, C6, H2):

```
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'XTAL_FREQ_AUTO' assigned to 'y' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'BTDM_CTRL_MODE_BTDM' assigned to 'y' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'BTDM_CTRL_BR_EDR_MAX_ACL_CONN' assigned to '5' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'BTDM_CTRL_BLE_MAX_CONN' assigned to '5' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'BTDM_CTRL_BR_EDR_MAX_SYNC_CONN' assigned to '0' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'BTDM_CTRL_AUTO_LATENCY' assigned to 'y' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'BTDM_CTRL_MODEM_SLEEP' assigned to 'n' in sdkconfig.defaults
warning: unknown kconfig symbol 'ESP32_XTAL_FREQ_AUTO' assigned to 'y' in sdkconfig.defaults
```

ESP-IDF automatically loads `sdkconfig.defaults.<target>` alongside
`sdkconfig.defaults` for each entry in `SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS`
([`tools/cmake/kconfig.cmake`][cmake]), so the move is transparent to
both plain `idf.py build` and the explicit-`SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS` form
used by the platform CI builds (`build_plat_unijoysticle`, etc.).

[cmake]: https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/v5.5.2/tools/cmake/kconfig.cmake#L78-L83

## Verification (ESP-IDF v5.5.2 in `espressif/idf:v5.5.2`)

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `examples/esp32` → ESP32 | clean | clean (BTDM_CTRL_*, XTAL_FREQ_AUTO still resolved) |
| `examples/esp32` → ESP32-S3 | 8 unknown-kconfig warnings | clean |
| `examples/esp32` → ESP32-C6 | 8 unknown-kconfig warnings | clean |
| `src` Unijoysticle (explicit `SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS`, target=esp32) | clean | clean (BTDM_CTRL_MODE_BTDM, XTAL_FREQ_AUTO, BLUEPAD32_PLATFORM_UNIJOYSTICLE all set) |

## Note on #204

This PR does not fix the `CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_LOG_LEVEL undeclared`
compile error in #204. That symbol is not referenced from Bluepad32
sources, and Bluepad32 itself builds cleanly on v5.5.2 across all five
example targets (verified above). The reporter's error originates in
their own project's `sdkconfig.defaults` — ESP-IDF v5.5 turned
`BOOTLOADER_LOG_LEVEL` into a Kconfig choice, so a literal
`CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_LOG_LEVEL=3` no longer takes effect; they should use
`CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_LOG_LEVEL_INFO=y` (or another `_*` member). I'll leave
that note on the issue itself.

Refs #204

## Test plan

- [x] `idf.py build` on `examples/esp32` for ESP32, ESP32-S3, ESP32-C6
      under `espressif/idf:v5.5.2` — all warning-free.
- [x] Generated `sdkconfig` on ESP32 still contains
      `CONFIG_BTDM_CTRL_MODE_BTDM=y`, `CONFIG_BTDM_CTRL_BLE_MAX_CONN=5`,
      `CONFIG_XTAL_FREQ_AUTO=y`.
- [x] `idf.py -B build_plat_unijoysticle -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.ci.plat_unijoysticle" set-target esp32 reconfigure` resolves
      `CONFIG_BLUEPAD32_PLATFORM_UNIJOYSTICLE=y` plus the BTDM_CTRL_* and
      XTAL_FREQ_AUTO symbols.
- [ ] CI: ESP-IDF v4.4 and v5.3 builds.

body:
## Summary

Three independent cleanups that surfaced during the [2026-04-25 platform state research](https://github.com/easingthemes/dx-aem-flow/blob/main/docs/research/2026-04-25-platform-state-update.md). All `chore:`/`docs:` — no release trigger.

## What's in this PR

- **`chore(cli):` Drop deprecated `.ai/project.yaml` emission from scaffold (-17 lines)** — TODO #8 (config.yaml + project.yaml consolidation, 2026-03-22) moved `type`, `toolchain.{build,test,lint}`, `modules.frontend` into `config.yaml`, but the standalone scaffolder kept emitting the deprecated flat file. dx-doctor section 1b was warning users about a file the scaffolder itself created — a self-inflicted bad first run. No skill/agent reads `.ai/project.yaml` (the deprecated path); they all read `config.yaml` or the active seed-data file `.ai/project/project.yaml` (different file, `/project/` subdir). Smoke-tested with `node cli/bin/dx-scaffold.js /tmp/scaffold-test --quiet`.
- **`docs(auto-init):` Document the Azure DevOps + AWS Lambda platform constraint** — dx-automation pipelines target ADO + Lambda exclusively, but the constraint was implicit (Azure CLI required, ADO service hooks, Lambda handlers). A user on GitHub Actions running `/auto-init` would generate ADO-flavored YAMLs and only discover the mismatch at deploy. New "Platform Compatibility" section sits before Phase 0 prerequisites. Backlog tracked as TODO #94 + new section in `todo-automation.md`.
- **`docs:` Cross-link `allowed-tools-compatibility.md` ↔ `2026-04-25-platform-state-update.md`** — the two docs cover overlapping ground from different angles (field-scoped vs platform-scoped). The allowed-tools doc's Copilot CLI version table stops at v1.0.12; the platform update has v1.0.14 → v1.0.36. Cross-links help readers follow the trail in either direction.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify scaffold no longer emits the deprecated file: `mkdir /tmp/sc && node cli/bin/dx-scaffold.js /tmp/sc --quiet && ls /tmp/sc/.ai/` should NOT include `project.yaml`.
- [ ] Verify dx-doctor still warns on legacy `.ai/project.yaml` files in existing projects (regression check — the warning is still useful for users upgrading from before TODO #8).
- [ ] Spot-check the auto-init Platform Compatibility section renders correctly when the skill is rendered (Copilot CLI side too — the section uses standard markdown).
- [ ] Click through the cross-links in `allowed-tools-compatibility.md` and `2026-04-25-platform-state-update.md` to confirm relative paths resolve in the GitHub UI.

## Notes

- 3 commits, all `chore:`/`docs:` types — semantic-release will skip this PR (intentional; no behavior changes for end users besides "no immediately-deprecated file" on fresh scaffold).
- An unrelated `.gitignore` edit (`.claude/settings-local.json` with hyphen) was deliberately NOT included — looks like a typo of the existing `settings.local.json` ignore, but kept out of this PR for the user to verify.

Two-phase mob: four ideators (random, obvious, contrarian, combiner) fan

GitHub Actions の deploy workflow を実本番 (launchd) と整合させ、PM2 経路の連続失敗を解消する。

- 本番は `~/clapbot-prod` の別 clone を `com.user.clapbot.plist` (launchd) で `npm run start -- -p 3100` として常駐

- `deploy.yml`: lint/test 通過後に `~/clapbot-prod/.deploy/deploy.sh` を呼び、health check は port 3100 を参照

- secrets/vars 検証ステップ削除 (`.deploy/deploy.sh` 配下では別管理)

author: xang1234
body: ## Summary - A fresh bootstrap on a non-trading day previously produced no IBD industry-group rankings: `calculate_daily_group_rankings` short-circuits at its trading-day guard, and HK/JP/TW/IN were skipped entirely because the chain wrapped ranking in `if market == \"US\":`. - This PR mirrors the breadth gap-fill pattern: new `calculate_daily_group_rankings_with_gapfill` task fills missing trading days first, then runs the daily helper only if today is a session — and is now wired into bootstrap and the beat schedule for **all** enabled markets (US/HK/JP/TW/IN). - Also fixes a latent bug shared with the breadth shim: `task.run()` does **not** bypass the `@serialized_market_workload` decorator. The inner call would silently `Retry` and the orchestrator's `except Exception` would swallow it, leaving `result['today']` permanently `None`. The shim now wraps the inner call in `disable_serialized_market_workload()` (a ContextVar bypass that already existed in the codebase) so the orchestrator's own lease is honored as the bypass. ## Context The user observed the bug live: triggering bootstrap on Sat 2026-04-25 produced `Skipping group rankings - 2026-04-25 is not a trading day for US` and no rankings populated. Asian markets were doubly affected — even on weekdays, bootstrap never computed their rankings, leaving the UI's market toggle (`GroupRankingsPage.jsx:562,581`, `queryKey: ['groupRankings', selectedMarket]`) showing empty data for HK/JP/TW. Service-layer support for non-US markets already existed: `IBDIndustryService.get_all_groups` delegates to `MarketTaxonomyService` for HK/JP/TW/IN (`ibd_industry_service.py:214-219`), and `IBDGroupRankService` auto-switches benchmarks SPY → HSI/N225/TAIEX/NIFTY (`ibd_group_rank_service.py:942`). Only the bootstrap and beat-schedule wiring needed to catch up. ## Files changed | File | Change | |---|---| | `backend/app/tasks/group_rank_tasks.py` | Add `calculate_daily_group_rankings_with_gapfill` orchestrator + `_calculate_daily_group_rankings_in_process` shim with proper lease bypass; promote `from ..config import settings` to module top | | `backend/app/tasks/runtime_bootstrap_tasks.py` | Swap US group-ranking call to orchestrator; new `else:` branch so HK/JP/TW/IN bootstraps include rankings | | `backend/app/celery_app.py` | Beat-schedule task name swap (per-market loop already covers HK/JP/TW/IN); add new task to `_MARKET_JOB_TASKS` routing allowlist | | `backend/app/config/settings.py` | `group_rank_gapfill_enabled` default flipped from `False` to `True` | | `backend/tests/unit/test_group_rank_tasks.py` | 5 new tests: gap-fill-then-today on trading day, gap-fill-only on non-trading day, disabled-market early return, missing-taxonomy defensive skip, non-US end-to-end, and a dedicated test that asserts the lease-bypass ContextVar is engaged during the inner call | | `backend/tests/unit/test_runtime_bootstrap_tasks.py` | Updated chain assertions for the new orchestrator name and the now-4-step non-US chain | ## Defensive behaviors - If a market is enabled in runtime preferences but has no taxonomy, the orchestrator returns `{'status': 'skipped', 'reason': 'no_taxonomy_for_market'}` rather than raising `MissingIBDIndustryMappingsError`. - If the gap-fill setting is off, the orchestrator still runs the daily step (matching breadth's behavior). - `disable_serialized_market_workload()` uses a `ContextVar` so the bypass auto-resets on context exit, even if the inner task raises. ## Test plan - [x] `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_group_rank_tasks.py` — 23 pass (18 existing + 5 new) - [x] `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_runtime_bootstrap_tasks.py` — 4 pass (existing tests updated) - [x] `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_breadth_tasks.py` — 10 pass (no regressions) - [x] `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_workload_coordination.py` — pass (lease bypass primitive unchanged) - [x] Manual wiring smoke test: confirmed beat entries for `daily-group-ranking-calculation-{us,hk,jp,tw}` all point at the orchestrator and HK bootstrap chain contains the orchestrator after `smart_refresh_cache`/`refresh_all_fundamentals`. - [ ] **Live verification on the user's machine**: wipe `ibd_group_ranks`, trigger `POST /api/v1/runtime/bootstrap` on a non-trading day, confirm the orchestrator logs `Found N missing dates → Gap-fill complete` for each market and `GET /api/v1/groups/rankings/current?market={US,HK,JP,TW}` returns ranks for each market's last completed trading day. - [ ] **Live verification on a trading day**: confirm orchestrator gap-fills nothing (already complete) and computes today's ranking via the daily helper, with `result['today']` populated (was previously broken by the lease re-entry bug). ## Out of scope - Same lease-bypass bug exists in `breadth_tasks.py:362-369`. Fix is identical (wrap the inner call in `disable_serialized_market_workload()`). Worth a follow-up PR. - Extending breadth to Asian markets — separate change with its own per-market design considerations (advance/decline thresholds, multi-day ratio behavior). - Refactoring the duplicated activity-tracking and exception-handler boilerplate across breadth/groups/daily tasks into a shared decorator — would need to touch unrelated code; appropriate as a focused follow-up once a third caller materializes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Group Rank gap-filling enabled by default and used during scheduled runs and bootstrap across all markets * **Improvements** * More reliable gap-detection and backfill of missing ranking dates * Robust taxonomy loading with clearer error reporting when data files or headers are invalid * **Tests** * Extensive unit tests covering gapfill orchestration, bootstrap behavior, and taxonomy error handling

author: zoedolan
body:
Fixes the crash from the most recent session:

```
File "/home/vybnz69/Vybn/spark/vybn_spark_agent.py", line 2395, in main
    user_input = input("\033[1;36mzoe>\033[0m ").strip()
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xc2 in position 26: invalid continuation byte
```

Root cause: a paste containing a non-breaking space (`\xc2\xa0`) arrived at `input()` split mid-codepoint (or with the continuation byte stripped by the terminal layer). `sys.stdin` was `utf-8 strict`, so a single bad byte killed the whole REPL instead of degrading one character.

Fix is two minimal edits, no new files:

1. At `main()` entry, reconfigure stdin/stdout/stderr with `errors='replace'` so a stray byte becomes `\ufffd` instead of fatal.
2. Around the `input()` call, catch `UnicodeDecodeError` as recoverable: log it and `continue`, keeping the loop alive.

Verified by replaying the exact failing byte sequence (`0xc2` at position 26): `errors='strict'` reproduces the original `UnicodeDecodeError` verbatim; `errors='replace'` returns the line with one `�` and the loop survives.

No protected-branch bypass used. Posted on a feature branch behind the antibody.

### Motivation
- Scheduled reports were being dispatched at the wrong local time (e.g., ~12:30 PM instead of 8:00 AM) because stored user timezone values were sometimes display-friendly strings or offsets instead of strict IANA identifiers.
- The change aims to normalize various timezone formats before the schedule check so the service uses the intended local time for dispatch.

### Description
- Reworked `resolveTimezone` in `app/Services/ScheduledReportService.php` to use a new `normalizeTimezone` helper and import `DateTimeZone` for validation.
- Added `normalizeTimezone`, `normalizeOffset`, and `isValidTimezone` helpers that accept IANA identifiers, offsets (e.g. `+05:30`, `UTC+05:30`), and display labels containing region IDs or `(GMT+05:30)` and return a validated timezone/offset or `null`.
- Kept safe fallback behavior by resolving to the application timezone via `config('app.timezone')` and finally `UTC` when parsing fails.

author: billduke13
body:
## Summary

- Helper \`extract_markdown_md_links\` finds \`[text](path.md)\` and \`[text](path.md#fragment)\` links, skips http/https/mailto URLs, and strips fragments.
- Helper \`collect_markdown_files\` recursively walks a directory for \`.md\` files (no \`walkdir\` dep).
- Integration test \`every_markdown_doc_cross_reference_resolves_to_an_existing_file\` walks every \`.md\` under \`docs/\` plus the repo-root \`README.md\`, resolves each link relative to the containing file's parent directory (markdown convention), and asserts the target exists. Failure messages batch every broken reference with source + resolved paths so a contributor can fix the whole tree in one pass.

## Why

Markdown links between docs are easy to break: rename a guide without updating inbound links, type a typo, copy-paste a stale path. The rendered view (GitHub, mdBook) shows a 404 the contributor doesn't notice until a reader reports it. \`cargo test\` is the only place a single check sees both ends of every link at once.

## Summary
- Express server (port 3001) with session-based authentication
- `/api/auth` routes: register, login, logout, and session check — passwords hashed with bcrypt
- `/api/vault` routes: GET, POST, DELETE vault entries — each password encrypted with AES-256-CBC before being stored in the database

- `db.js` connects to the local MySQL `password_manager` database via mysql2

author: purisev
body:
## Summary

Aligns the chart's `values.yaml` with the [Helm best practice](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/values#consider-how-users-will-use-your-values) of preferring maps (or lists of strings) over lists of objects whose only meaningful field is a name. Closes the remaining list→map migrations within the 2.0.0 breaking-change window.

### List of strings (key was previously the only field)

- `imagePullSecrets`
- `envSecrets`
- `envConfigMaps` — chart-owned vs external is now resolved by looking up the name in `.Values.configMaps`; the `{configMapRef: key}` shorthand is gone

### Map keyed by name (resulting k8s API field documented inline in `values.yaml`)

| Path | Map key → |
|---|---|
| `volumes`, `volumeMounts` (all levels) | `spec.volumes[].name` / `containers[].volumeMounts[].name` |
| `ingress.hosts`, `ingresses[*].hosts` | `spec.rules[].host` |
| `ingress.tls`, `ingresses[*].tls` | `spec.tls[].secretName` |
| `deployments[*].service.ports`, `statefulSets[*].service.ports` | `spec.ports[].name` |
| `deployments[*].ports`, `statefulSets[*].ports`, `sidecars[*].ports` | `containers[].ports[].name` |
| `integrations.argocd.imageUpdater.images` | `applicationRefs[].images[].alias` |
| `integrations.eso.externalSecrets[*].data` | `spec.data[].secretKey` |

Existing map-shaped fields (`configMaps`, `deployments`, `statefulSets`, `jobGroups`, `ingresses`, `httpRoutes`, `grpcRoutes`, `tlsRoutes`, `referenceGrants`, `secretStores`, `externalSecrets`) gained the same `Map key → <field>` header comments for consistency.

### Kept as lists by design

`tolerations`, `topologySpreadConstraints.constraints`, `securityContext.capabilities.drop`, `rbac.rules`, Gateway API `rules`/`parentRefs`/`hostnames`, `referenceGrant.from`/`.to`, `imageUpdater.applicationRefs` (raw CRD), `hostAliases`, `ingress.hosts[*].paths` (path-match order can matter for legacy ingress controllers), ESO `dataFrom` (no natural unique key).

### Implementation notes

- Templates iterate maps with `keys ... | sortAlpha` for deterministic rendering.
- `jobGroups` merge for `volumes`/`volumeMounts` switched from list-concat to map-merge with job winning over group on key collisions; `envSecrets`/`envConfigMaps` stay concat-merged (now of strings).
- `values.schema.json` updated to enforce the new shapes.

## Test plan

- [x] `helm lint .` clean
- [x] `helm unittest .` — 482/482 tests pass (existing suites migrated, new sort-order assertions added for every new map)
- [ ] Render this chart against a real downstream values file in a consumer repo and eyeball the diff
- [ ] Verify `helm install --dry-run` rejects the old list shapes for the affected fields

## Breaking changes

All migrated fields above. Consumers must update their values files to the new shape — examples for every block are inline in `values.yaml`.

author: grvpanchal
body:
## Summary

The site code samples were being silently mangled because Jekyll runs Liquid **before** kramdown, so `{{ ... }}` and `{% ... %}` *inside fenced code blocks* were being interpreted as Liquid expressions instead of left literal. The build still succeeded (Liquid renders unknown variables to empty string), so CI was green — but the rendered HTML showed broken Vue interpolation, broken JSX `style={{ ... }}` props, and broken Angular template bindings.

### Examples that were silently broken

| File | Line | Mangled by Liquid |
|---|---|---|
| `ui/molecule.md` | 121 | `{{ buttonInfo.label }}` (Angular template) |
| `ui/molecule.md` | 137 | `{{ label }}` (Vue interpolation) |
| `ui/story.md` | 122 | `{{ args.label }}` (Vue Storybook template) |
| `ui/story.md` | 204+ | `style={{ maxWidth: '400px' }}` (JSX) |
| `ui/attributes.md` | 95 | `{{ name || 'Some Label' }}` (Angular) |

…and similar across `ui/{atomic-design, component, organism, props, skeleton, theme}.md`, `server/{app-shell, authentication, localization, mfe}.md`.

### Fix

Walk every doc, find every fenced code block, wrap any block containing `{{` or `{%` (and not already inside a `{% raw %}` region) with `{% raw %}` ... `{% endraw %}`. The `{% include quiz.html %}` calls live outside fenced blocks and are deliberately left as live Liquid.

**13 files, 40 lines added — only the wrap markers, no prose or structural changes.**

### Note: 503 on the custom domain

The site at `elegantfrontend.training` was returning **HTTP 503** when this was filed (the `grvpanchal.github.io/elegant` URL also redirects there and returns 503). The recent build + deploy CI runs both succeeded, so the 503 looks like a DNS / Pages-config / TLS-cert issue rather than a Jekyll problem. Worth checking:
- The DNS `A` records for `elegantfrontend.training` apex point at GitHub's current Pages IPs (185.199.108.153, 185.199.109.153, 185.199.110.153, 185.199.111.153)
- The "Enforce HTTPS" toggle in *Settings → Pages* — it sometimes needs to be re-enabled after a domain change
- The `CNAME` file in `docs/` matches the custom domain entered in Pages settings (it does — `elegantfrontend.training`)

This PR fixes the Jekyll-side issues. The 503 is separate and likely needs a touch in Pages settings / DNS.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI build + deploy both succeed
- [ ] After deploy, spot-check the rendered Vue tab in `ui/molecule.md`: `{{ label }}` should appear *as-is* in the code block, not as empty space
- [ ] Confirm `elegantfrontend.training` resolves and returns 200

author: ordinaryjoys
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes a few latent issues in the `target/linux/qualcommax/base-files` startup chain that affect AX6 / IPQ807x / IPQ60xx boards on first boot and on sysupgrade.

## Issues fixed

1. **11 `lib/upgrade/api-*.sh` files + `lib/functions/bootconfig.sh` lack `#!/bin/sh`**
   `shellcheck` flags them with SC2148. They are sourced by sysupgrade so it usually works, but bare execution / static analysis breaks. Adds the shebang.

2. **`uci-defaults/999_auto-restart.sh` restarts `network` / `odhcpd` / `rpcd` during uci-defaults boot phase**
   This is a known anti-pattern: procd hasn't fully come up yet, restarting these services here is racy and serves no purpose because procd will start them in the proper order anyway. The script is deleted.

3. **`uci-defaults/992_set-nss-load.sh`**
   - The `sed` regex `popen('top.*')` is greedy and risks damaging multi-line `popen` calls in `/usr/share/rpcd/ucode/luci`. Made non-greedy and bounded.
   - `sysctl -w dev.nss.clock.auto_scale='0'` runs in uci-defaults phase — but `qca-nss-drv` may not be loaded yet at that point, so the sysctl fails silently. Moved to `/etc/sysctl.d/97-nss-lock-clock.conf` so `procd-sysctl` applies it at the correct moment.

4. **`uci-defaults/993_set-ecm-conntrack.sh` silently fails when target file missing**
   Adds `[ -f "$FILE" ] || exit 0` guard so non-NSS builds don't generate noisy `sed` errors.

5. **`uci-defaults/991_set-network.sh` always sets `packet_steering=0`**
   This assumes NSS is loaded. If `qca_nss_drv` failed to load (kernel mismatch, hardware variant, etc.), packet_steering=0 plus no NSS = traffic single-cores and throughput collapses. Adds a fallback to `=1` when the module isn't loaded.

## Testing

- `shellcheck -S error` clean on the touched files
- `bash -n` on each rewritten script passes
- Manual review: matches OpenWrt sysupgrade conventions

## Compatibility

No DT / image / package list changes. Only modifies init scripts under `target/linux/qualcommax/base-files/`. Safe to backport to any branch that has this layout.

## Problem

The application crashes at startup with `ImportError: libgthread-2.0.so.0: cannot open shared object file`. This shared object is provided by `libglib2.0-0`, which was missing from the Dockerfile's apt-get install command despite the other OpenCV system dependencies (`libgl1`, `libsm6`, `libxext6`, `libxrender-dev`) already being present.

Added `libglib2.0-0` to the `apt-get install` block in the Dockerfile. This package ships `libgthread-2.0.so.0` and is a required runtime dependency for OpenCV in `python:3.10-slim`, which does not bundle GLib by default.

body:
## Summary

Adds an ERP-native marketing module under the existing **Sales → Marketing** sidebar slot (no sidebar changes — locked spec preserved). Sales/admin/exec users can plan campaigns, schedule posts across LinkedIn/X/Meta/IG/TikTok via the Ayrshare aggregator, track engagement, link engaged authors to CRM contacts, and attribute campaign spend to orders for ROI. Builds on top with creator-relationship tracking: outreach pipeline, deals, deliverables, performance.

## What ships

**Schema (9 new tables)** — canonical SQL in `drizzle/0037_marketing_social.sql` and `drizzle/0038_influencer_crm.sql`, mirrored idempotently in `ensureTables()` in `server/_core/index.ts` so prod boots cleanly regardless of migration drift:

- `social_accounts`, `marketing_campaigns`, `marketing_posts`, `marketing_engagements`, `marketing_metrics`
- `influencers`, `influencer_campaign_participations`, `influencer_deliverables`, `influencer_outreach`

**Server**
- `server/socialProviderService.ts` — Ayrshare adapter, env-gated (`AYRSHARE_API_KEY`), no-ops cleanly when unset so dev/CI never depend on the network.
- `server/db/marketingDb.ts` — CRUD + overview rollup + ROI join (engaged contacts → customers → orders since `campaign.startDate`); influencer pipeline counts, performance rollup (deliverables/spend/CPM), per-campaign rollup.
- `server/routers/marketing.ts` — tRPC routes under `marketing.*` (campaigns, posts, engagement, metrics) + `marketing.influencers.*`, `marketing.participations.*`, `marketing.deliverables.*`. All gated to admin/sales/exec.

**UI** — `client/src/pages/marketing/MarketingHub.tsx`
- Tabs: Overview · Calendar · Posts · Engagement · Campaigns · Influencers
- Influencers tab: 8-status pipeline strip, search/filter, roster table, detail dialog with stats + outreach log + campaign deals
- Campaigns ROI panel cross-links influencer participants + committed/paid spend
- "Generate with AI" links to existing `ContentHub` at `/marketing/content`

## Migration approach

Initially explored regenerating `_journal.json` and adding a backfill SQL migration, but reverted that approach after diagnosing that:
1. Several historical migrations have multi-statement chunks that mysql2 silently drops without `multipleStatements: true`
2. The project already routes around this via `ensureTables()` (which uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`)
3. Enabling `multipleStatements` would change deploy behavior in ways that risk breaking working installs

So this PR follows the project's existing pattern: SQL migration files for canonical schema + `ensureTables()` entries for runtime resilience.

## Verified

- **Typecheck:** zero errors
- **Tests:** 789/789 pass (the previously-flaky `employeePortal` test was fixed on main)
- **Sidebar lock:** `DashboardLayout.test.ts` (35 tests) green — no nav changes
- **DDL validity:** all 9 `ensureTables()` CREATE statements applied cleanly against MariaDB 10.11; idempotent on re-run
- **Realistic data flow:** seeded full chain (CRM contact → campaign → post → engagement → metrics → influencer → participation → deliverable → outreach), confirmed all FK references resolve and the app's actual aggregate queries return correct results

## Test plan

body: ## Description Adds CriticResult visualization support to the GUI frontend, enabling the web UI to display critic evaluation results that are already flowing through SDK events. This mirrors the critic visualization functionality from the [OpenHands CLI](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/tree/main/openhands_cli/tui/utils/critic), adapted for the React web frontend. w/o iterative refinement w/ iterative refinement ## Changes ### Types (`frontend/src/types/v1/core/base/critic.ts`) - **`CriticResult`** — `score` (0-1), `message`, `metadata` - **`CriticFeature`** — `name`, `display_name`, `probability` - **`CriticCategorizedFeatures`** — `agent_behavioral_issues`, `user_followup_patterns`, `infrastructure_issues`, `other` - **`CriticMetadata`** — wraps categorized features and event IDs - Added optional `critic_result` field to **`ActionEvent`** and **`MessageEvent`** ### Component (`critic-result-display.tsx`) - Star rating (0-5 ★) with color coding: green ≥60%, yellow ≥40%, red <40% - Percentage display - Expandable categorized feature breakdown with per-feature probabilities - Full i18n support (15 languages) ### Integration - **`FinishEventMessage`** — renders `CriticResultDisplay` below the finish message when `critic_result` is present - **`UserAssistantEventMessage`** — renders `CriticResultDisplay` for agent messages when `critic_result` is present ### Tests - 12 unit tests covering score rendering, star ratings, color coding, label rendering, expand/collapse, and multiple feature categories ## Default behavior and deployment note Critic is enabled by default for new OpenHands app users so critic feedback appears in the GUI without extra setup. Deployments that want to avoid critic usage or associated LLM costs can opt out by disabling `verification.critic_enabled` in user or organization verification settings. When `CRITIC_API_KEY` is configured, critic requests use that deployment-level service key for centralized cost management instead of per-user budget-limited keys. ## How it works The SDK already attaches `CriticResult` to `ActionEvent` and `MessageEvent` when the critic is enabled (via verification settings). The server sends these events over WebSocket. Previously the frontend ignored the `critic_result` field — now it renders an inline evaluation widget. Example rendering: ``` Critic: agent success likelihood ★★★★☆ (72.0%) ▼ Potential Issues: Insufficient Testing (75%) · Incomplete Changes (60%) Infrastructure: Build Failure (40%) ``` --- _This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the user._ --- To run this PR locally, use the following command: GUI with Docker: ``` docker run -it --rm -p 3000:3000 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway --name openhands-app-77bf479 docker.openhands.dev/openhands/openhands:77bf479 ```

## Summary

- Detailed design for propagating W3C `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` headers through `KvCommand` into openraft's internal task boundaries
- Fixes the broken trace connection between inbound user RPC and follower apply work
- Enables end-to-end observability of the consensus path in OpenTelemetry

## Design Highlights

- Add three optional string fields to `KvCommand::Put`, `Delete`, and `Cas` variants
- Implement `trace_context.rs` module in `ggap-consensus` with helpers to inject/extract trace context
- Re-anchor outbound `rpc.client.append_entries` spans and all `apply.entry` spans to the captured user trace
- Preserve `ggap-types` zero-dependency constraint (new fields are plain `Option<String>`)

## Testing

- Build, lint, and full test suite pass per CLAUDE.md pre-push checklist
- Tighten existing `trace_propagation.rs::outbound_raft_rpc_carries_injected_trace_context` test
- Add new multi-node test verifying trace + baggage flow across 3-node cluster
- Plan includes manual end-to-end smoke test via Kind + OTel Collector

## Risk

`KvCommand` is bincode-serialized into the Raft log. Adding fields to existing variants is **not backwards-compatible** with existing logs/snapshots. Per CLAUDE.md, Phase 6 uses tempdirs and no documented log-compat policy exists; wipe-on-upgrade is acceptable for this phase.

body:
## Summary

- When the LLM-picked element's top stable selector is ambiguous on the page, we previously cached it anyway "so future runs skip the LLM" — Playwright then resolved that selector DOM-first on the next run, deterministically targeting the wrong element.
- New behavior: walk the candidate's pre-generated `selectorCandidates` and cache the first selector that resolves to exactly one element. If none do, skip the cache write entirely.
- Execution semantics are unchanged: the run that detects ambiguity still uses `[data-kaizen-id='…']` for that execution. Only the cache write changes.

## Repro fixed

Two textboxes share `role=textbox[name="Email Address"]` (login + signup). Step "type … in signup-email":

| Run | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | L0 archetype → login email (wrong); user marks fail | same |
| 2 | LLM picks signup email (correct); caches the **ambiguous** selector | LLM picks signup email; caches a unique alternative or nothing |
| 3 | L2 hits cached ambiguous selector → login email (wrong) | L2 hits unique alt (correct) or LLM re-runs (correct) |

## Spec

`docs/specs/smart-brain/spec-element-resolver-ambiguous-cache-write.md`

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `llm.element-resolver.test.ts` covering: ambiguous-with-unique-alt, ambiguous-no-alt, unambiguous-passthrough
- [x] Typecheck clean
- [x] Lint clean (only pre-existing `any` warnings consistent with project style)

author: eirenjacobson
body:
## Why

A fresh run of v3 produced pathological geometry — E-BFMI = 0.01 (threshold 0.30), every iteration hitting max-treedepth, mean stepsize ~1.5e-6, and Rhat > 2 across essentially all parameters. The chains were stuck in different narrow modes of a multimodal posterior that NUTS could not navigate.

## What

Five changes to the existing v3 files (no fork; file paths unchanged; version label in each script header bumped to **v3.1**).

### 1. Smooth out the phi hinge

```diff
- real log_phi_s = beta0_phi[s] + log_lam_sum
-                  + fmax(gamma0_phi[s] - gamma1_phi[s] * log_lam_s, 0.0);
- real phi_s     = exp(fmin(log_phi_s, 10.0));
+ real log_phi_s = beta0_phi[s] + log_lam_sum
+                  + log1p_exp(gamma0_phi[s] - gamma1_phi[s] * log_lam_s);
+ real phi_s     = exp(log_phi_s);
```

`fmax(..., 0)` is non-differentiable at the kink — softplus has the same shape with a smooth gradient. Also removed the redundant `fmin(log_phi_s, 10.0)` cap (softplus is already bounded by `max(x, 0) + log(2)`).

### 2. Fix `kappa` as data

`kappa` becomes a fixed input alongside `alpha_ct` and `beta_ct`. The qPCR detection-rate calibration is treated as known. Drops one tight, multimodal-attractor parameter from the sampler; pulls `kappa` out of `init_fn` and the recovery table accordingly.

### 3. Pin `gamma0_phi` / `gamma1_phi` with very tight priors

Same parameter shape, but the data-supplied prior sigmas drop hard:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `prior_gamma0_phi_sig` | 1.00 | **0.05** |
| `prior_gamma1_phi_sig` | 0.30 | **0.02** |

The whales' MB data is too sparse to identify all three dispersion knobs jointly (`beta0_phi`, `gamma0_phi`, `gamma1_phi`); tightening the gammas pins them so `beta0_phi` does the heavy lifting.

### 4. Drop `HSGP_M` from `c(10, 8, 8)` to `c(5, 5, 5)`

`M_total: 640 → 125`. That removes ~1500 `z_beta` coefficients per species. With the gp_l priors now concentrated near 50/150/300, 5 basis functions per dimension are plenty for the domain.

### 5. Tighten `gp_l` priors

| | mu | sig before | sig after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prior_gp_lx_*` | 50 | 40 | **10** |
| `prior_gp_ly_*` | 150 | 80 | **20** |
| `prior_gp_lz_*` | 300 | 150 | **40** |

Keeps `gp_l` in the regime where the SE spectral weights are well-conditioned (the original sigmas allowed length-scales of a few km / m, which gave the spectral weights a near-singular shape).

## Files changed

- `stan/whale_edna_hsgp_v3.stan` — softplus replacement, `kappa` to data, prior_kappa_* removed, header rewritten with v3.1 changelog.
- `scripts/03_format_stan_data_v3.r` — `HSGP_M = c(5,5,5)`, `kappa` passed in, tightened gp_l + gamma prior sigmas, `prior_kappa_*` dropped.
- `scripts/04_run_whale_edna_model_v3.r` — `kappa` removed from `init_fn`; `gamma0_phi`/`gamma1_phi` init now at the new prior means.
- `scripts/05_check_whale_edna_model_v3.r` — `"kappa"` removed from `scalar_pars` and from the recovery table.
- `00_pipeline_v3.r`, `scripts/01_simulate_whale_edna_v3.r`, `scripts/02_plot_simulated_data_v3.r` — header labels bumped to v3.1 (no logical changes; the v3.1 reparameterisation only touches the model fit chain).

## Test plan

- [x] `Rscript scripts/01_simulate_whale_edna_v3.r` — unchanged.
- [x] `Rscript scripts/03_format_stan_data_v3.r` — `M = 125`; `kappa = 0.850` in stan_data; tightened sigmas present.
- [x] Stan model compiles; `setdiff` of model data vars vs `stan_data` is empty in both directions.
- [ ] Full Stan fit not re-run in this PR (long sample); the rationale is laid out in commit body and the geometry-fixing changes are independent.

v4 has the same pathology and is left as-is per the request — happy to apply the same set of changes to v4 in a follow-up.

## Summary

Adds an install-to-use smoke gate matching axonflow-openclaw-plugin#56 (QF-17), adapted for the Claude Code bash-script plugin shape.

Stages the plugin to a clean tmp dir on every PR, validates the file list and `hooks.json` command paths, spawns a stub MCP server on a random port, and exercises `pre-tool-check.sh` against it for both deny (SQLi) and allow (benign) paths. Asserts the Plugin Batch 1 wire-shape fields (`decision_id`, `risk_level`, `override_available`) surface in the deny decision text.

## What it catches

The class of regressions `tests/test-hooks.sh` misses because it runs against the source tree, not what consumers install:
- `hooks.json` command paths broken after install (wrong relative path or missing `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/` prefix)
- Required files missing from the install payload
- Scripts referencing files relative to source tree that don't exist post-install

## Companion gates

This is the install-payload-path gate. It runs alongside:
- the existing `tests/test-hooks.sh` (mock-MCP regression tests, in `.github/workflows/test.yml`) — covers hook behaviour
- the wire-shape contract gate (parallel PR) — covers script-jq-vs-spec drift

Together the three cover the gate classes the SDK rigor work identified per ADR-047.

- [x] Local 15/15 pass against the bundled stub server
- [ ] CI green

## Summary

Discovered-state correction for the original Phase-2 emission-rollouts handoff after shipping bundles #1 (state-patch) and #2 (NPC) in the server repo (slabgorb/sidequest-server#49, #50).

The original handoff assumed all ~26 SPAN_* families had live OTEL spans being opened in Python production code. Audit found that the Python port (ADR-082) replaced most Rust \`info_span!\`/\`start_as_current_span\` emissions with \`logger.info(...)\` strings or direct \`_watcher_publish\` calls. The \`SPAN_*\` constants in \`spans.py\` are mostly byte-identical-to-Rust name-string prefixes, not actual span openings.

This follow-up:
- Documents which families are genuinely live in Python.
- Marks ~7 bundles from the original handoff as port-dead (require engine porting before routing).
- Splits the real Phase-2 work into two workstreams: migrate live \`_watcher_publish\` sites (what #49/#50 did) vs. port the missing engines (out of scope for telemetry restoration).
- Suggests the next bundle picks from the live-emission census.
- Records the \`severity\` span-attribute escape hatch added in #50.
- Captures an open question about bridging port gaps via log-string parsing (recommendation: no, ADR-031 Illusionism violation).

author: dtterastar
body:
## Summary
- Liftoff retired the `v2-12-2` host with `"The server is deprecated."`, breaking every authenticated subcommand once the cached access token expires. Bumps the compiled-in default to `v2-12-3` (probed: v2-12-3 is the only live host right now — v2-13-0..2 also return deprecated; v2-14+ don't resolve).
- Adds a `LIFTOFF_API_BASE` env-var override so the next deprecation can be worked around without waiting on a release. Logged once to stderr when the override is in effect.
- Surfaces an actionable error when the backend returns the deprecation marker, from `auth refresh`, `auth login`, or any authenticated tRPC query — points users at the env-var workaround and notes that the Liftoff iOS/Android app shows its version under Settings → About.

## Why this design
- Env-var override + clear error beats automatic version probing/fallback in the CLI; probing would silently mask real breakage.
- `tokenURL`/path stays unchanged — only the host varies between Liftoff versions.
- Tokens are user-bound, not host-bound: existing `~/.config/liftoff-export/auth.json` survives the version bump (verified locally — `workouts list --since 7d` succeeded with the previous token against the new default).

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `LIFTOFF_API_BASE=https://v2-12-2.api.getgymbros.com liftoff-export auth refresh` → emits override banner, then actionable deprecation error (not bare upstream text)
- [x] `liftoff-export auth refresh` (no override, default v2-12-3) → succeeds
- [x] `liftoff-export workouts list --since 7d` → returns real workouts via tRPC
- [ ] After release: re-run morning Liftoff digest end-to-end to confirm it feeds the coach again

## Followup (release)
After merge, cut `v1.0.6` so the goreleaser workflow rebuilds the five platform binaries + checksums. Hold for explicit go-ahead before tagging.

> **Overview**
> **Adds unified runtime logging.** Introduces `src/runtime/UnifiedLogger.lua` (also exported as `addon.Log`) with an in-memory ring buffer, optional persistence into `MogTrackerDB.runtimeLogs`, and export helpers for filtered/limited log dumps.

> 
> **Docs and packaging updates.** `MogTracker.toc` now loads `UnifiedLogger`; the root `README.md` is heavily trimmed and documentation is re-homed under `docs/` with a new `docs/README.md` and a large loot-panel refactor runbook, while older `docs/DESIGN.md` and `docs/DebugPanel.md` are removed. body:
## Summary
Updated the image file filtering logic in `find_similar.py` to exclude any images located within directories named "_duplicates" from the similarity search.

## Key Changes
- Modified the image path filtering condition to check that "_duplicates" is not present in the path components
- This prevents the tool from re-analyzing duplicate images that have already been organized into the "_duplicates" directory

## Implementation Details
- The filter now uses `and "_duplicates" not in p.parts` to check all directory components in the path
- This approach ensures that any nested "_duplicates" directory at any level will be excluded
- The change is applied during the initial image discovery phase, improving efficiency by avoiding unnecessary processing of already-identified duplicates
