body:
## Summary

- Remove active spell area effects when their caster loses concentration, drops concentration, or casts a new concentration spell.
- Create per-participant concentration tracking effects on the caster when persistent concentration area spells (Fog Cloud, Spike Growth) are cast, so the existing concentration check pipeline (damage → CON save → break) works for these spells.
- Sync updated area effect state to LimiarMap after any concentration cleanup, ensuring overlays and tactical effects (movement cost, hazard damage, visibility blocking) are removed.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `concentration.py` | New `_remove_area_effects_for_concentration_group()` and `_sync_area_effects_if_changed()`. `_remove_effect_group` / `_clear_concentration_for_source` now also remove matching area effects. `_resolve_concentration_check_after_damage` syncs map + includes area effect names in labels. `_clear_concentration_for_participant_status` syncs map on status change. |
| `cast_area.py` | On persistent concentration spell cast: clear existing concentration, generate `concentration_group`, create per-participant concentration effect on caster, pass group to area effect builder. |
| `persistent_area_effects.py` | `build_persistent_spell_area_effect` accepts optional `concentration_group` param, stored as internal-only field. |
| `spell_automation.py` | `_cast_hunters_mark_automation` handles new return type + syncs area effects. |
| `effects_actions.py` | Manual GM effect removal triggers area effect cleanup + map sync. |

## Test coverage (13 new tests)

- Fog Cloud / Spike Growth create per-participant concentration effect on caster
- Area effect has internal `concentration_group` matching per-participant effect
- Damage → failed CON save removes area effects + syncs map (Fog Cloud, Spike Growth)
- Casting new concentration spell replaces prior area effects (Fog Cloud → Spike Growth)
- Fog Cloud → Hunter's Mark cross-path: area effect removed, HM per-participant effects active
- Hunter's Mark → Spike Growth cross-path: HM effects removed, Spike Growth area effect created
- Non-concentration area effect survives unrelated concentration cleanup
- Concentration break on status change (death/downed) removes area effects + syncs map
- Manual effect removal cleans up area effects + syncs map
- Removed Spike Growth not in `active_area_effects_for_map` payload (mechanical effects gone)

## Validation

- 1309 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failures (full control-server suite)
- `npm run lint` clean
- `git diff --check` clean
- No schema/migration changes required

### Motivation
- Replace the old seated human rig with an option to load a lightweight GLTF model for Pool Royale players and provide a procedural fallback while the GLTF loads.
- Normalize and expose reference measurements so pose, cue, and hand placement calculations become data-driven and easier to tune across models.
- Improve bone lookup and driving logic to adapt generic GLTF rigs to existing procedural animation code.

### Description
- Introduces `POOL_ROYALE_HUMAN_GLTF_URLS` and increases `POOL_ROYALE_HUMAN_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` to adjust GLTF model sizing for portrait view.
- Adds many `REFERENCE_HUMAN_*` constants to centralize human/cue dimensional references used by pose and cue calculations.
- Replaces single-source GLTF load with `loadFirstAvailableGltf(POOL_ROYALE_HUMAN_GLTF_URLS)` in `ensureSeatedHumanTemplate` and improves error handling.
- Implements bone utilities: `cleanBoneName`, `findBoneByAliases`, and `buildPlayerAvatarBones` to robustly locate common bones across varied GLTF naming schemes.
- Adds `driveGltfPlayerPose` to apply aim/strike pose blends to discovered GLTF bones using a preserved rest pose.
- Updates `createPlayerCharacterRig` to create both a procedural character (`proceduralRoot`) and a GLTF root (`gltfRoot`), store GLTF state in `userData.anim`, and attach the loaded GLTF into the rig while hiding the procedural fallback when ready.
- Adjusts runtime animation logic to toggle between procedural and GLTF representations, and refactors bridge, cue, and pull math to use the new reference constants (e.g. `REFERENCE_HUMAN_PULL_RANGE`, `REFERENCE_HUMAN_IDLE_GAP`, `REFERENCE_HUMAN_CUE_LENGTH`).

### Testing
- Ran the frontend build with `yarn build` and the command completed successfully.
- Executed the existing frontend unit test suite with `yarn test` and all tests passed.
- No new automated tests were added in this change.

author: jdx
body:
## Summary

When `github::list_releases` fails transiently (rate limit, 5xx, network blip), `get_tags_with_created_at` previously bubbled the error. The caller in `_list_remote_versions` swallowed any error into an empty `Vec`, surfacing as `[]` from `mise ls-remote --json` — which downstream pipelines treat as "no versions exist".

This patches `get_tags_with_created_at` to fall back to `list_tags` on `list_releases` error, matching the shape of the existing `releases.is_empty()` fallback.

## Why

[mise-versions](https://github.com/jdx/mise-versions) snapshots `mise ls-remote --json` output every 15 minutes. When the JSON came back empty due to a transient API hiccup, the script fell back to plain-text version input (no metadata) and wrote new versions without `release_url` or a real `created_at`. Concretely, in [jdx/mise-versions@e1ff2c2f](https://github.com/jdx/mise-versions/commit/e1ff2c2fa31dec4871d88c21bdaff26f71b82d98) the entry for \`code\` 0.6.95 landed as:

\`\`\`
"0.6.95" = { created_at = 2026-04-25T13:31:32.512Z }
\`\`\`

(milliseconds in the timestamp give it away as the script's \`Date.now()\` fallback, not a real GitHub timestamp). The next run picked up the correct values, but the bad row was already committed.

## Behavior changes

- **list_releases errors** → now falls back to tags (no timestamps), returning all tag names instead of `Err`.
- **list_releases succeeds (empty)** → unchanged (already falls back to tags).
- **list_releases succeeds (non-empty)** → unchanged.
- **`pkg.version_source = "github_tag"`** → unchanged.

No new versions are surfaced — only the *error* path is widened.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` clean
- [x] `cargo test backend::aqua` — 16/16 pass
- [x] Live smoke: `mise ls-remote --json code` returns 0.6.95 with both `created_at` and `release_url`
- [x] Pre-commit hooks (cargo-check, cargo-fmt, clippy, shellcheck, prettier, pkl) all pass

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk change limited to the Aqua remote version listing path; it only alters behavior on GitHub `list_releases` failures by returning tags instead of propagating an error that was later coerced into an empty result.
> 
> **Overview**
> Improves resiliency of Aqua version discovery by **falling back to `github::list_tags` when `github::list_releases` errors**, instead of bubbling the error up.
> 
> This prevents transient GitHub API failures (rate limits/5xx/network issues) from causing callers to see an empty version list; normal behavior when releases succeed or when `version_source` is `github_tag` remains unchanged.
>

author: wqiluc
body:
API REST — NestJS + Swagger

--- ## 📌 O que é este projeto? API REST construída com **NestJS** e **TypeScript**, seguindo a arquitetura **SCM** (Service, Controller, Module). Possui autenticação via **JWT**, hash de senhas com **bcrypt**, banco de dados **PostgreSQL** gerenciado pelo **Prisma ORM**, containerização via **Docker** e documentação interativa pelo **Swagger UI**. --- ## 🏛️ Arquitetura SCM O projeto separa responsabilidades em três camadas bem definidas: | Camada | Arquivo | Responsabilidade | |--------|---------|-----------------| | ![Controller](https://img.shields.io/badge/Controller-F7DF1E?style=flat-square&logo=typescript&logoColor=black) | `*.controller.ts` | Recebe requisições HTTP, define rotas e delega ao Service | | ![Service](https://img.shields.io/badge/Service-3178C6?style=flat-square&logo=typescript&logoColor=white) | `*.service.ts` | Contém toda a lógica de negócio, validações e comunicação com o banco | | ![Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/Module-E0234E?style=flat-square&logo=nestjs&logoColor=white) | `*.module.ts` | Agrupa e registra Controller + Service de cada domínio | --- ## 🔐 Autenticação JWT + bcrypt O fluxo de autenticação funciona assim: 1. No **cadastro**, a senha é convertida em hash irreversível antes de salvar no banco: ```ts const hash = await bcrypt.hash(senha, 10); // 10 salt rounds ``` 2. No **login**, a senha digitada é comparada ao hash armazenado: ```ts const valido = await bcrypt.compare(senha, user.password); ``` 3. Se válido, um **token JWT** é gerado e retornado ao cliente. 4. Nas rotas protegidas, o token é validado via `JwtStrategy` antes de processar a requisição. > O prefixo `$2b$10$` no banco confirma que o bcrypt foi aplicado com 10 salt rounds. --- ## 📄 Swagger UI Com o servidor rodando, acesse a documentação interativa em: ``` http://localhost:3000/api ``` | Método | Rota | Auth | Descrição | |--------|------|------|-----------| | `POST` | `/auth/login` | ❌ | Retorna o token JWT | | `GET` | `/users` | ✅ | Lista todos os usuários | | `GET` | `/users/:id` | ✅ | Busca usuário por ID | | `POST` | `/users` | ❌ | Cria novo usuário | | `PUT` | `/users/:id` | ✅ | Atualiza um usuário | | `DELETE` | `/users/:id` | ✅ | Remove um usuário | Para testar rotas protegidas: faça login → copie o `access_token` → clique em **Authorize 🔒** → cole o token. --- ## 🐘 Prisma + PostgreSQL O Prisma atua como ORM entre a aplicação e o banco PostgreSQL rodando em container Docker. O `schema.prisma` define os modelos, e as migrations controlam o versionamento do banco. ```bash docker-compose exec api npx prisma migrate dev --name init # cria e aplica migration docker-compose exec api npx prisma studio # interface visual do banco ``` No Prisma Studio (`localhost:5555`), a coluna `password` da tabela `User` exibe o hash gerado pelo bcrypt — nunca a senha em texto puro. --- ## Autor ✍🏻

Lucas Paguetti Pereira 🦇
🏫 Instituição: Cesar School 🎓🧡
📍 Recife, Pernambuco — Brazil 🇧🇷

author: deanmarano
body:
## Summary

- Add `fixed?: boolean` to `SchemeOptions` (defaults to `true` for deterministic attributes, matching Rails). When `fixed`, `EncryptedAttributeType.serialize` uses the **oldest** previous scheme so deterministic ciphertexts remain stable across key rotations. When `fixed: false`, the current (newest) scheme is used.
- Unskip 5 tests in `EncryptionSchemesTest`:
  - deterministic encryption is fixed by default: it will always use the oldest scheme to encrypt data
  - don't use global previous schemes with a different deterministic nature
  - deterministic encryption will use the newest encryption scheme to encrypt data when setting it to `{ fixed: false }`
  - use global previous schemes when performing queries
  - don't use global previous schemes with a different deterministic nature when performing queries

The compatibility filtering (`isCompatibleWith`) and global-scheme wiring (`globalPreviousSchemesFor`) were already implemented; the new tests assert both code paths explicitly.

## Test plan

- [ ] `encryption-schemes.test.ts` — all 15 tests pass (was 10; 5 unskipped)

body:
## Summary

Replaces the "Next Task" action (browse current/next toggle) with a new **"Up Next"** action modelled on Android's Up Next notification — a single auto-advancing display with a live countdown.

### Display logic

| State | Value | Sub-label |
|---|---|---|
| Task in progress (`currentTask`) | Task title | `"12m left"` / `"1h 5m left"` |
| Task upcoming (`nextTask`) | Task title | `"in 45m"` / `"in 2h"` |
| Nothing scheduled | `"All clear"` | `"nothing up next"` (dimmed) |

The countdown refreshes every 60 seconds via `setInterval` between server state pushes. Auto-advance to the next task happens naturally when the server sends a new state (currentTask changes as tasks become in-progress or complete).

### Interactions

- **Press / dial push / long-press strip**: complete the current in-progress task (no-op when showing an upcoming task)
- **No dial cycling** — the display is intentionally automatic

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Addresses the Devin Review finding on [PR #4](https://github.com/linfordlee14/founder-brief-api/pull/4#discussion_r3142371789). `get_remote_address` returns `request.client.host` only and ignores `X-Forwarded-For`. On Render, the service sits behind a reverse proxy, and Uvicorn's default `forwarded_allow_ips='127.0.0.1'` means the `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` doesn't trust Render's proxy — so `request.client.host` is the proxy IP for everyone, and all users collapse into a single 5/minute bucket. Switching to `slowapi.util.get_ipaddr`, which inspects `X-Forwarded-For`, so the rate limit is per end-client IP. Change: - `main.py`: `from slowapi.util import get_remote_address` → `from slowapi.util import get_ipaddr` - `main.py`: `Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)` → `Limiter(key_func=get_ipaddr)` ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Fast-forward merge to keep a single commit on `main`. - [ ] After redeploy, hit `/api/brief` from two different client IPs in the same minute and confirm each gets its own 5-request budget (i.e., they don't throttle each other). - [ ] Confirm Render logs show distinct client IPs on the request metadata. ### Notes - No dependency or config changes; `slowapi==0.1.9` already exports `get_ipaddr` in `slowapi.util`. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f080d8088baa4b96a877c526221768f6 Requested by: @linfordlee14 ---

author: happy5318
body:
# Fix: GLM models via API gateways incorrectly treated as Ollama backends

## Summary

This PR fixes a false positive in `_is_ollama_glm_backend()` that caused GLM models accessed through API gateways on private IPs to be incorrectly treated as Ollama-hosted models.

## Problem

The original implementation used `is_local_endpoint()` as a fallback detection mechanism. This function returns `True` for all RFC-1918 private IP addresses (`192.168.x.x`, `10.x.x.x`, `172.16-31.x.x`), which includes:

- Local Ollama instances ✅ (intended)
- API gateways like New API on private IPs ❌ (false positive)

When a GLM model is accessed via an API gateway on a private IP, the workaround for Ollama/GLM stop misreports was incorrectly triggered, causing:
- Normal `finish_reason="stop"` responses being treated as truncated
- Unnecessary continuation messages injected into conversations
- Internal system messages visible to users

## Solution

Modified `_is_ollama_glm_backend()` to only return `True` for:

1. **Ollama endpoints**: URLs containing `"ollama"` or using port `:11434`
2. **z.ai provider**: Always treat as affected (existing behavior)

Removed the `is_local_endpoint()` fallback because:
- API gateways (New API, One API, etc.) properly report `finish_reason`
- The Ollama/GLM stop misreport workaround is specifically for local Ollama instances
- Private IPs don't necessarily mean "Ollama instance"

## Changes

- Modified `_is_ollama_glm_backend()` in `run_agent.py`
- Added detailed docstring explaining the rationale
- Added inline comments for clarity

## Testing

Tested with:
- GLM-5 model via New API gateway on private IP → No longer triggers false positive
- Local Ollama with GLM model → Still correctly detected (port 11434)
- z.ai provider → Still correctly detected

## Related

Fixes #15751

body:
## What

Extract a small `_label_matches()` predicate in `src/frontend_visualqa/grounding.py` and use it in the three places that were inlining the same multi-condition label-matching check.

## Why

The same 4-condition predicate (exact, prefix, fuzzy-exact, fuzzy-prefix) was repeated in:

- `_matching_button_states` (4 conditions)
- `_check_button_match` — `visibleButtons` fallback loop (4 conditions)
- `_matching_progress_bars` (the same 4, plus 2 substring-containment conditions for the more permissive progress-bar matching)

Three near-identical decisions in one file are the kind of duplication where future tweaks to the matching logic will silently drift between call sites. Pulling them into a single helper with an explicit `allow_substring` flag makes the progress-bar variant self-documenting and keeps the rule in one place.

## Why it's safe

- Pure structural refactor in a single file. No behavior change.
- The helper is a direct rewrite of the existing conditional — same conditions, same short-circuit order, same handling of empty `fuzzy_label` (the `(fuzzy_label and …)` guards are preserved verbatim).
- `allow_substring=True` reproduces the two extra conditions previously only present in `_matching_progress_bars`.
- Existing unit tests in `tests/test_claim_verifier.py` exercise `ground_claim_verdict` and the underlying matchers; if they pass, behavior is preserved.

author: anish749
body:
## Problem

`commands.LatestTs` bucketed `paths.CommentsFile` with messaging / email / thread and scanned the file for the `"ts"` field. But Drive comments JSONL lines carry `createdTime` and `modifiedTime` (the Google Drive Comments API shape) — never `"ts"`. Effect: any Drive doc whose only recent activity in the `--since` window was a comment thread reported a zero `LatestTs`, surfacing as a stale age (or `active` with no timestamp) in `pigeon list --since`.

Sample real on-disk line:

```
{"id":"...","author":{...},"content":"What is your data size?",
 "createdTime":"2019-12-01T16:32:03.831Z",
 "modifiedTime":"2019-12-01T21:50:55.493Z",...}
```

## Solution

Move `CommentsFile` into the Drive content case alongside `TabFile`, `SheetFile`, `FormulaFile` so it dispatches through `latestDriveMetaDate(filepath.Dir(...))`. Justified by the storage protocol: `internal/gws/poller/drive.go` writes `comments.jsonl` and rewrites `drive-meta-YYYY-MM-DD.json` in the same change handler (lines 148+164 / 227+243), so the meta sidecar is the canonical "when did this doc change" anchor for every part of a Drive doc's state, including its comments. This is the same anchor tabs and sheets already use.

Regression test asserts a Drive doc with only a `comments.jsonl` write plus a meta sidecar reports the sidecar date — verified failing before the fix (returns zero) and passing after.

author: copilot
body:
The mgmt generator's emitted `AddTag`/`SetTags`/`RemoveTag` methods threw `NullReferenceException` at runtime on every `TrackedResource` whenever `CanUseTagResource(...)` returned `false`. The fallback branch instantiated the patch via the **internal parameterless deserialization ctor** instead of the public `[InitializationConstructor]`, leaving `Tags = null`.

```csharp
// Before — NRE on patch.Tags.Add(...) because the parameterless ctor leaves Tags = null
FooData patch = new FooData();

// After — public [InitializationConstructor] initializes Tags to an empty ChangeTrackingDictionary
FooData patch = new FooData(current.Location);
```

## Description

- **`BaseTagMethodProvider.BuildPatchCtorCall`**: when `_isPatch` is true, generically resolve the patch type's `ModelProvider` via a direct `(ModelProvider)CSharpTypeMap[patchType]` cast, look up its public initialization constructor (the public ctor with required-property parameters; the public mocking ctor is filtered out by the parameter-count check), and forward each required argument from `current` by mapping `ParameterProvider.Property?.Name` (Pascal-cased fallback to the parameter name) onto the `current` resource-data variable. This naturally covers:
  - `TrackedResourceData`-derived patches → forwards `current.Location`.
  - `ResourceData`-derived (untracked) patches → init ctor has no required parameters, falls back to `new TPatch()`.
  - Any future base type with additional required init params → no further code changes needed.

  Defensive guards for framework types and unresolved `CSharpTypeMap` entries were dropped: patch models in tag methods always come from generated TypeSpec service models via `PopulateUpdateMethod()`, so they always resolve to a `ModelProvider`. The only remaining fallback to `new TPatch()` covers the case where the only public ctor is the parameterless mocking ctor.
- **Regenerated `Mgmt-TypeSpec` local test project**: `BarResource`, `BazResource`, `ClusterResource`, `WorkloadNetworkSegmentResource`, `WorkloadNetworkVmGroupResource` now emit `new TPatch(current.Location)` in their patch-fallback branches (6 method variants × 5 resources). Existing `TagMethodProviderTests` snapshots are unchanged because their input model is not tracked.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Second slice of **Phase B (P0 security)** — make every uploaded firmware traceable to whoever holds the signing key. HTTPS (B.1) protects the upload channel; this PR protects the firmware *artifact* itself. * `sdkconfig.defaults` enables `CONFIG_SECURE_SIGNED_APPS_NO_SECURE_BOOT=y` + `CONFIG_SECURE_SIGNED_APPS_ECDSA_V2_SCHEME=y` and points `CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_SIGNING_KEY` at `../keys/secure_boot_signing_key.pem`. **No eFuse changes** — the chip stays unlocked, full Secure Boot v2 is deferred to Phase E. * `idf.py build` will now append a signature block to every app image. The OTA path (`esp_ota_end()`) rejects any binary whose hash/signature doesn't verify with the embedded public key, returning `ESP_ERR_OTA_VALIDATE_FAILED`. * `components/gw_ota/gw_ota.c` distinguishes that specific error from generic `ota_end` failures and surfaces a clear "image signature invalid (rebuild with correct key)" message in `ota_status.error_msg` / HTTP 500 body. * `keys/` folder added with `.gitignore` (`*.pem`, except `secure_boot_pubkey.pem`) and a README explaining how to generate the key with `espsecure.py`, where to keep it, and the loss-of-key blast radius. Adds **`docs/phase_B2_signed_ota.md`** — teaching chapter covering: insider / lost-laptop / OTA-server-hack threat models, hash + public-key signature primer (with ASCII flow), RSA-3072 vs ECDSA-P256 on ESP32, anti-rollback mechanism, app image binary layout (header → app_desc → sections → checksum → SHA-256 → signature block), eFuse / Secure Boot v2 / Flash Encryption layered model, signing-key generation recipe, expected pass/fail test cases, production warnings, 5 self-study exercises. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Read `docs/phase_B2_signed_ota.md` — flag any unclear section. - [ ] Run `espsecure.py generate_signing_key --version 2 --scheme ecdsa256 keys/secure_boot_signing_key.pem` (this file is gitignored). - [ ] `idf.py fullclean && idf.py build` — confirm log line "Signing image with key keys/secure_boot_signing_key.pem". - [ ] Flash, then upload `build/modbus_gateway.bin` via the web OTA — should succeed; device reboots into `ota_1`. - [ ] Tamper one byte (`printf '\xFF' | dd of=build/modbus_gateway.bin bs=1 count=1 seek=10000 conv=notrunc`) and re-upload — `/api/ota/status` should report state=`OTA_FAILED`, `error_msg = "image signature invalid (rebuild with correct key)"`. - [ ] Confirm `keys/secure_boot_signing_key.pem` is **not** tracked by git (`git status` should show clean). ### Notes This phase only enables **signed app images**, not full Secure Boot v2 (which would also lock the bootloader and burn an eFuse). That's a deliberate choice — eFuse changes are irreversible per chip, so we wait until Phase E when fleet operations and key-management are settled. Anti-rollback (`secure_version`) is wired (CONFIG flag stays on from earlier) but not yet bumped per release; that workflow is part of Phase E. Stacks on top of `devin/phase-b1-https`. Merge order: A → B.1 → B.2. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b67370e32b42416297199b5dc7931cc8 Requested by: @chucndhoaloi-bot ---

author: rzi3d
body:
## Checklist
- [x] Tested on Linux (NixOS) with flutter_gemma 0.13.6
- [x] Does not break existing behavior on standard distros
- [x] Single file change, no new dependencies
- [x] Follows existing code style

## Problem

On non-standard Linux distributions (NixOS mostly.), the LiteRT-LM 
server subprocess fails to initialize the native engine with a silent 
gRPC UNKNOWN error (code 2).

The root cause is that `Process.start()` is called with a manually 
constructed environment that only contains `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` set to 
the natives path — completely replacing the parent process environment. 
This means any system libraries not in standard paths (such as 
`libvulkan.so.1` on NixOS) are invisible to the subprocess, causing 
`liblitertlm_jni.so` to fail loading at runtime with no useful error message.

## Fix

Spread `Platform.environment` into the subprocess environment first, 
then append the natives path to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`/`DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` 
rather than replacing it. This ensures the subprocess inherits all 
parent environment variables while still prioritizing the bundled natives.

## Testing

Verified on NixOS with `flutter_gemma` 0.13.6 — model initializes 
successfully after this change. Previously failed silently at 
`Creating EngineConfig` with `gRPC Error (code: 2, codeName: UNKNOWN, 
message: null)`.

## Notes

This is a one-line fix that shouldn't affect any existing behavior on 
standard distros — if `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is already set correctly, 
spreading `Platform.environment` and appending to it is equivalent 
to the previous behavior.

Extract platform-agnostic types into a new SwiftMuxCore library
(SessionInfo, SessionManager, SessionService, CommandRunner) so the
existing macOS app and a new SwiftMuxServer executable can share the
same data layer and `tp ls --json` enrichment logic without drift.
SwiftMuxCore is deliberately UI-free; the SessionStatus → SwiftUI.Color
mapping moves to the SwiftMux app target as an extension.

Add SwiftMuxServer (Hummingbird + HummingbirdWebSocket) with:
  - GET  /healthz
  - GET  /api/sessions
  - GET  /api/sessions/:name/peek?lines=N
  - POST /api/sessions/:name/kill
  - WS   /ws/sessions/:name (PTY attached to `tmux attach -t <name>`)

PTY support is provided by a small CSwiftMuxPTY C target that wraps
forkpty(3) and ioctl(TIOCSWINSZ) so PTYProcess.swift stays clean.
Optional bearer-token middleware (SWIFTMUX_TOKEN); host/port via env.

The web client (xterm.js PWA) is the next slice and not part of this
commit.

NOTE: this commit was authored without a Swift toolchain available, so
it has not been compiled. Expect minor adjustments around Hummingbird 2
API surface (parameter access, middleware registration) on first build.

author: thieung
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of v3.11.x sync — auto-generated REST API endpoint catalog covering all 260 live endpoints from goclaw source. Trilingual (EN/VI/ZH).

Audit (`plans/reports/api-audit-260425-2237-endpoint-drift.md`) flagged 196 endpoints undocumented in hand-written `reference/rest-api.md`. Hand-writing 200 endpoint stubs × 3 locales is unmaintainable, so this PR introduces an auto-gen catalog kept fresh by a build script.

## Approach

- **New page** `reference/api-endpoints-catalog.md` (+ vi/ + zh/) — flat catalog grouped by handler domain (37 groups). One row per endpoint with method + path.
- **Existing `rest-api.md` untouched** — stays as hand-curated narrative ref. Cross-link callout added to top of all 3 locales.
- **Build script** `scripts/build-api-catalog.js` — Node.js, no external deps, scans `goclaw/internal/http/*.go` + `gateway/server.go` for `mux.Handle`/`HandleFunc` patterns. Run via `npm run build:api-catalog` or `GOCLAW_SOURCE_PATH=... node scripts/build-api-catalog.js`.

## Files

| File | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/build-api-catalog.js` | new | 296-line generator |
| `reference/api-endpoints-catalog.md` | new | 465 lines, 260 endpoints / 37 groups |
| `vi/reference/api-endpoints-catalog.md` | new | mirror, localized intro |
| `zh/reference/api-endpoints-catalog.md` | new | mirror, localized intro |
| `package.json` | mod | `build:api-catalog` npm script |
| `js/docs-app.js` | mod | DOC_MAP entry (triple-sync) |
| `index.html` | mod | sidebar link under Reference |
| `README.md` | mod | DOC MAP link + reference page count 16→17 |
| `reference/rest-api.md` (× 3 locales) | mod | cross-link callout after Overview |

Total: 11 files / +1703/-2.

## Generated from

- GoClaw SHA: `29457bb3`
- Date: `2026-04-25`
- Endpoint count: **260**
- Domain groups: **37** (by handler file basename)

## How regeneration works

```bash
npm run build:api-catalog
# or with custom source:
GOCLAW_SOURCE_PATH=/path/to/goclaw node scripts/build-api-catalog.js
```

The script:
1. Greps `mux.Handle("METHOD /path", ...)` patterns from `internal/http/*.go` + `internal/gateway/server.go`
2. Groups by handler file basename (e.g., `vault.go` → "Vault")
3. Renders markdown table per group, alphabetically sorted
4. Writes to all 3 locales with localized intro headings

On future goclaw syncs, just run the script — catalog stays fresh without hand-editing.

## DOC_MAP triple-sync (per project convention)

All 3 required locations updated together: `README.md` + `js/docs-app.js` + `index.html`.

## Reports

- Implementation: `plans/reports/fullstack-260426-0113-GH-1-api-catalog-impl.md`
- Original API drift audit: `plans/reports/api-audit-260425-2237-endpoint-drift.md`

## Test plan

- [ ] Render `reference/api-endpoints-catalog.md` locally, verify table formatting + group headers
- [ ] Click cross-link from `rest-api.md` → catalog page (all 3 locales)
- [ ] Verify sidebar entry appears under Reference group
- [ ] Spot-check key endpoints: `POST /v1/vault/upload`, `GET /v1/agents/{agentID}/kg/graph`, `POST /v1/api-keys`, `GET /v1/voices`
- [ ] `npm run build:api-catalog` runs cleanly without modifying anything else

## Out of scope

- Per-endpoint request/response schemas — narrative ref `rest-api.md` covers OpenAI-compat surface; remaining endpoints intentionally catalog-only (path discoverability is the goal here)
- Fumadocs migration integration — this catalog format will carry over fine; if migration restructures `reference/`, just re-run script

body:
The settings view's GitHub token shows "Set" right after entering the
token (the backend pushes status after a successful set), but reverts to
"Not set" after reopening. The frontend's INIT_COMMANDS list — sent on
first load — did not include GET_GITHUB_TOKEN_STATUS, so a freshly-created
panel never asked the host for the actual status and stayed at the
default 'none'. Same problem for GET_PR_SUBSCRIPTIONS.

Add both commands to INIT_COMMANDS so they populate on every open.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: this is a wiring change to initial settings-view hydration and message schema registration, with minimal behavioral impact beyond ensuring data is fetched on open.
> 
> **Overview**
> Settings view no longer fires a hardcoded frontend `INIT_COMMANDS` list on mount; instead, it relies on a lifecycle `WEBVIEW_READY` message handled in `SettingsViewMessageHandler` to call `sendAllData` as the single source of truth for initial tab hydration.
> 
> The settings inbound message schema now includes `WebviewReadyMessageSchema`, enabling the new lifecycle command to validate/dispatch correctly and ensuring GitHub token status and PR subscription data are refreshed whenever the settings webview opens.

author: vellum-apollo-bot[bot]
body: ## Problem The wake hint (merged in #28017) was injected as a plain `role: "assistant"` text message. When the platform proxy routes the request to Anthropic, it rejects conversations ending with an assistant message: ``` "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." ``` This broke the agent loop for all wake-triggered flows (scheduled tasks, GitHub poll, etc.). ## Fix Replace the single assistant text hint with a **tool_use / tool_result pair**: 1. **Assistant message** with a synthetic `_wake_hint` tool_use block 2. **User message** with the matching `tool_result` containing the hint text This fixes the immediate issue (conversation now ends on a user-role message) while preserving prompt-injection resistance — LLMs treat tool results as data, not instructions, so crafted hints can't hijack behavior. ## Changes - `agent-wake.ts`: Replace assistant text hint with tool_use/tool_result pair, update `inspectWakeOutput` offset from +1 to +2 - `agent-wake.test.ts`: Update assertions for new hint shape - `anthropic-provider.test.ts`: Remove stale wake-specific comment from merge test - `anthropic/client.ts`: Remove stale comment about wake hints in merge logic ## Testing - Updated unit tests verify the new message shape - CI will validate end-to-end ---

## Summary
- Adds a guaranteed-visible section-level circuit-city checkpoint behind every `.sec`, independent of WebGL — solves the regression where every section after hero read as empty dark space on desktop.
- Per-section structure silhouette per `data-bg`: HQ spire, foundry racks, antenna array, ops tower with radar, reactor core, broadcast studio screen wall, integration hub bridge with port LEDs, landing pad with twin pylons.
- Shared base across all variants: perspective PCB grid, cyan/red highway, dashed center spine (animated), glowing vias, distant skyline silhouette.
- Bumps asset version to `v=20260425-circuit-city-6`.

## Root cause of prior blank sections
The previous fix relied on the Three.js camera path traversing checkpoints. When the camera frame on desktop did not align with any geometry between hero and the next checkpoint (or fog/clipping cut it), there was nothing else behind the section panel. Adding a CSS/SVG companion layer per section removes that single point of failure: even if WebGL renders nothing, the section still reads as a circuit-city checkpoint.

## Files changed
- `index.html` — `.sec-bg` div added to all 8 non-hero sections; cache bust + new sync `section-bg.js` script tag.
- `section-bg.js` (new) — synchronously paints per-section SVG into `.sec-bg`. Pure DOM, no WebGL.
- `style.css` — `.sec-bg` layer + animations (`sb-spine`, `sb-pulse`, `sb-beacon`); mobile tone-down.

## Test plan
- [ ] Desktop: hero shows circuit-city; scrolling through Spire, Foundry, Voice, Ops, Revenue, Content, Integration, Contact each show visible circuit traces, glowing rails, vias, and a unique structure silhouette.
- [ ] Mobile: layout still legible, .sec-bg slightly dimmed for performance, no horizontal overflow.
- [ ] `SCROLL TO EXPLORE` fades after first scroll (existing behavior preserved).
- [ ] HUD shows 270+ agents; no stale 47.
- [ ] No em/en dashes in user-visible copy; no banned wording.

author: waholulu
body:
### Motivation
- Move toward a data-first, automation-first pipeline by encoding canonical source capabilities and research templates to allow deterministic candidate enumeration and prechecks without LLMs.
- Provide a machine-friendly path from composed candidates to runnable engineering artifacts via `ImplementationSpec` and a development pack for engineers/LLM-assisted writers.
- Harden cloud runtime defaults and dependency packaging by upgrading to Python `3.11` and introducing optional `geospatial` extras to keep default deployments lightweight.

### Description
- Introduces a lightweight `SourceRegistry` and `config/source_capabilities.yaml` plus `research_template_loader` and a `built_environment_health` template to represent canonical sources, roles, tiers, and variable families.
- Adds `agents.candidate_composer`, `models.candidate_composer_schema`, `agents.implementation_spec_builder`, and `models.implementation_schema` to programmatically enumerate candidates and produce `ImplementationSpec` objects for each candidate.
- Adds `agents.development_pack_writer` to write a per-candidate development pack (README, `implementation_spec.json`, `claude_task_prompt.md`, data/analysis plan, acceptance tests) into run-scoped output directories and exposes generation/listing/download endpoints in `api.server`.
- Updates deterministic checks: `agents.data_accessibility` now supports role-based source fields and stricter reasons/verdicts, and `agents.rule_engine` gains a role-based `check_G3_role_based_data_availability` helper to evaluate catalogs; also adds an emergency deterministic ideation fallback in `agents.ideation_agent` when both V2 and legacy V0 fail.
- Adds API and model surface changes: new template endpoints (`/templates*`), candidate and development-pack endpoints (`/runs/{run_id}/candidates*`, `/runs/{run_id}/development-packs*`), and new Pydantic models to surface candidate/development-pack metadata.
- Bumps runtime and packaging: `Dockerfile` now uses `python:3.11-slim` and installs `pip install --no-cache-dir ".[geospatial]"`; `pyproject.toml` updated to require `>=3.11` and declare optional extras (`geospatial`, `vision`, `deepvision`).

### Testing
- Added and ran unit tests covering source registry and template loading via `tests/test_source_capabilities.py` and `tests/test_template_loader.py`, which passed.
- Added and ran candidate composition, role-based G3 checks, data-access evaluation, implementation-spec building, and development-pack generation tests (`tests/test_candidate_composer.py`, `tests/test_rule_engine_role_based_g3.py`, `tests/test_role_based_data_access.py`, `tests/test_implementation_spec_builder.py`, `tests/test_development_pack_writer.py`) which passed.
- Exercised API-level candidate and pack flows with `tests/test_api_candidates_and_packs.py` and ran the ideation emergency fallback test `tests/test_ideation_emergency_fallback.py`, both of which passed under the local test harness (all new tests executed via `pytest -q tests/` succeeded).

## Summary

Adds **`docs/02_planning/21_Phase3_SprintDevelopmentPlan.md`** — sprint decomposition for Phase 3 (2027). Until PR #36 + this PR, only Phase 1 had a sprint plan; Phases 2 + 3 were one-liners in the Release Plan. With both now in place, "how many sprints across all phases" has a defensible answer.

## Shape

**6 sprints, ~22 weeks.**

| Sprint | Weeks | Theme |
|---|---|---|
| **P3-S0** | 1–3 | Foundation + 6 gating ADRs (marketplace economics, KYC, Stripe Connect, webhook semantics, predictive arch, recommendation algorithm) |
| **P3-S1** | 4–7 | Live tutor marketplace — supply side (onboarding, KYC, calendar) |
| **P3-S2** | 8–11 | Live tutor marketplace — demand side + payouts (discovery, booking, ratings, Stripe Connect) |
| **P3-S3** | 12–15 | Content marketplace (creator authoring v2, royalty engine, refunds) |
| **P3-S4** | 16–18 | B2B API writes + webhooks (idempotency, signed delivery, partner SDK) |
| **P3-S5** | 19–21 | Predictive analytics + recommendations maturity (drop-out forecasting, intervention engine, A/B-tested recs) |
| **P3-S6** | 22 | Stabilization + launch (Drills 7+8, soft → full launch) |

## Cross-phase sprint count (now defensible)

| Phase | Sprints |
|---|---|
| Phase 0 | 1 |
| Phase 1 | 4 |
| Phase 2 | 5 (PR #36) |

**Pending today: ~12.5** (Phase 1 carry-over ~1.5 + all of Phase 2 + all of Phase 3)

author: luke-bradford
body:
## What

PR C of the visibility-driven live-prices plan (spec at [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-visibility-driven-live-prices-spec.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-visibility-driven-live-prices-spec.md)).

- FX cron cadence cut from 5 min via the orchestrator high-frequency path to 24 h (ECB publishes once per working day; tighter was wasting Frankfurter calls).
- Phase 2 (eToro batch quotes) deleted — WS live-tick pipeline (#274) covers `quotes` for every visible instrument.
- Lifespan bootstrap calls `fx_rates_refresh()` directly when `live_fx_rates` is empty at boot, BEFORE `start_runtime()` so the boot path doesn't race APScheduler catch-up.
- `FxRateUnavailable` exception in `budget.py` — fail-closed on missing GBP→USD AND non-zero `tax_gbp`. Caught in execution_guard (block BUY/ADD), api/budget (503), reporting (null degrade with `fx_unavailable: True` flag).

## Why

Operator's settled-decision direction: scheduled jobs that run when nothing on screen needs them are wasteful. Daily matches the ECB publish cadence with the same operator outcome.

Closes the execution-safety hole where missing FX silently degraded `estimated_tax_usd = 0` — order would have been allowed through with no tax provision.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run ruff check .`
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`
- [x] `uv run pyright`
- [x] Narrow tests pass: `test_budget.py` 31/31, `test_sync_orchestrator_freshness.py` (added boundary tests)
- [ ] Full backend pytest — running in CI (local Windows had flaky background-task output capture; trusting CI as source of truth)
- [ ] Live smoke (operator, after merge):
  - Boot fresh DB → log shows `fx bootstrap: live_fx_rates is empty, running fx_rates_refresh inline` followed by `fx_rates_refresh complete: fx_pairs=N`
  - Boot with non-empty table → log shows `fx bootstrap: N existing rows, skipping inline fetch`
  - `/system/status` shows `fx_rates_refresh` running daily, not every 5 min
  - With Frankfurter unreachable + empty table at boot, BUY/ADD on a UK operator blocks at the guard with `budget_available: FX rate (GBP→USD) unavailable`

## Codex review

Round 1 raised 3 findings, all fixed:
1. Bootstrap → catch-up double Frankfurter hit — fixed by calling `fx_rates_refresh()` directly so watermark + audit row advance.
2. Reporting paths bare-called `compute_budget_state`, would hard-fail on missing FX — fixed with try/except + null snapshot in `_budget_snapshot` + `_tax_provision_snapshot`.
3. Freshness test still pinned 5-min window — fixed param + added explicit fresh-at-12h / stale-at-25h boundary tests.

**Stash merge notes:** `stash@{3}` (stream client) and `stash@{1}` (extension/chat/daemon lifecycle) were applied with manual conflict resolution. `stash@{0}` contributed tests and the fixture only; its workflow edits were **not** applied because they would remove the current tag-driven release job (lint, tests, versioned VSIX, publish gates). `stash@{2}` was skipped as a duplicate of `stash@{3}`. `stash@{5}`, `stash@{6}`, and `stash@{7}` matched `main` or would regress behavior (Rust CLI `consume_stream`, daemon `service.rs`, doc tables) and were not applied.

author: jdealtia-sys
body:
## Summary

Two iPhone-side issues Joe reported:

### 1) "Kanban not loading" diagnostic on every other open
The crm.js renderer fired the diagnostic banner any time the in-memory lead cache was empty. The dashboard's \`loadLeads\` catch block sets \`window._leads = []\` on transient failures too — common on iPhone Safari when the app wakes from background and the Firestore SDK has to re-handshake. Joe was "fixing" it by spam open/close (gave the SDK time to recover).

- Gate the diagnostic on \`window._leadsLoaded === true\` so it only fires for a genuinely empty account.
- Add cold-start auto-retry in \`loadLeads\` catch: on the first cold-start failure (and only for transient error codes — \`unavailable\`, \`deadline-exceeded\`, \`cancelled\`, \`internal\`, network/timeout messages), retry up to 3 times with 600ms / 1.2s / 1.8s backoff. Permission-denied and other permanent errors fall through unchanged.

### 2) Kanban cards overcrowded on mobile
Cards ate two-per-viewport with lots of vertical whitespace. New \`@media (max-width:900px)\` block trims paddings, font sizes, and gaps without touching desktop. The 480px tier hides the email row entirely (phone is the primary field contact) and tightens column min-width to 220px so side-scroll reveals more of the next column. Per-card height drops ~30%.

## Test plan
- [ ] Cold-start the PWA on iPhone with airplane mode toggled — diagnostic does NOT appear, retry kicks in, leads populate
- [ ] Genuine empty account (zero leads, successful read) — diagnostic still appears as before
- [ ] Permanent error (bad rules) — diagnostic appears immediately, no auto-retry
- [ ] Kanban on iPhone — visibly more cards visible per scroll, side-scroll reveals more of next column
- [ ] Desktop kanban — unchanged

author: volkovio

## What’s included in this PR

- reorganize `booking` and `inventory` into a clearer hexagonal structure
- introduce explicit `application.port.in` and `application.port.out`
- separate use case interfaces from service implementations
- expose published inventory use cases for cross-module integration
- route `booking -> inventory` integration through published contracts instead of internal dependencies
- prepare module boundaries for future multi-module split and service extraction

## Why

This PR strengthens the boundary between `booking` and `inventory` before the next architectural steps:

- Gradle multi-module split
- separate runnable applications
- persistence migration

The goal is to make integration depend on published contracts rather than internal repositories and implementation details.

## Result

After this PR:

- both `booking` and `inventory` have a more explicit hexagonal structure
- inbound and outbound ports are clearer
- `booking` no longer relies directly on internal inventory details
- integration is routed through published inventory use cases
- the codebase is better prepared for ACL-based integration and future service separation

author: meqhisto
body:
**💡 What:** 
- Replaced `new PrismaClient()` with `import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'` in `app/api/analytics/kpis/route.ts`, `app/api/analytics/monthly-trend/route.ts`, and `app/api/analytics/pipeline/route.ts`.
- Replaced unoptimized `findMany()` + `.filter()/.reduce()` Javascript memory processing with Prisma DB level methods like `.count()`, `.aggregate()`, and `.groupBy()`.
- Parallelized the concurrent independent DB queries using `Promise.all`.
- Created a `.jules/bolt.md` journal entry to track this codebase anti-pattern for future reference.

**🎯 Why:** 
Directly calling `new PrismaClient()` in API routes causes severe database connection leakage and exhaustion in serverless environments. Fetching thousands of properties into Node.js memory over the network simply to compute `.length` and counts is a major performance bottleneck that eats up Node.js V8 heap space, spikes DB transfer times, and scales extremely poorly as data grows.

**📊 Impact:** 
- Eliminates risk of maxing out database connections.
- Reduces DB response size payload from O(N) full records down to O(1) integer counts (e.g. going from MBs of JSON fetched down to tiny SQL `COUNT` return statements).
- Vastly reduced Node.js memory usage and overall faster execution times via `Promise.all` parallel DB querying.

**🔬 Measurement:** 
- Measure the DB connection pool size.
- Ensure the `analytics` API endpoint payloads and TTFB (Time to First Byte) remain extremely low even with 10k+ rows in the local database.
- `pnpm build` completes normally without errors indicating zero loss of functionality.

author: oscardlfr
body:
## Summary

While adding broad test coverage for the PR #10 benchmark platform-filter work, **two pre-existing bugs** in `detect_benchmark_modules` (sh) were caught by the new test cases. Both are masked-on-Linux issues the existing CI-only-on-Linux setup never surfaced.

### Bugs caught + fixed

**1. Default `--module-filter "*"` silently filtered every module out.** The check was `[[ "$mod" != *"$filter"* ]]` — with `filter="*"` it did a literal substring match on `*` inside module names, so `"benchmark"` (no asterisk) was always rejected. Result: any default `kmp-test benchmark` invocation returned zero modules + `[WARN] No benchmark modules found` (silent broken-default).

Fix: treat `*` and `""` as "match all"; apply substring filter only for non-empty, non-asterisk patterns.

**2. `grep -oP` (PCRE) include() extraction failed under MinGW / Git Bash** with `-P supports only unibyte and UTF-8 locales` when `LC_ALL=C`, returning zero modules.

Fix: replace with POSIX `grep -E` + `sed -E`.

### New coverage

**bats** (`tests/bats/test-benchmark.bats`) — 18 total now (3 pre-existing + 15 new):
- `detect_module_benchmark_platforms`: android-only / jvm-only / both / none / nested-colon path / missing & empty build files / hyphenated form
- `module_supports_platform`: positive / negative / permissive-when-unknown
- `get_benchmark_gradle_task`: jvm/{smoke,stress,main} + android (all configs)
- `detect_benchmark_modules`: default `"*"` filter (regression for bug 1), empty filter, substring filter, `LC_ALL=C` locale-portable extraction (regression for bug 2)
- End-to-end integration: `--platform jvm` against `androidx.benchmark`-only module → exit 3 with hint, `gradlew` NEVER invoked

**Pester** (`tests/pester/Benchmark-Detect.Tests.ps1`) — new file, 13 tests covering `Get-ModuleBenchmarkPlatforms`, `Test-ModuleSupportsPlatform`, `Get-BenchmarkGradleTask` with the same edge-case matrix.

CHANGELOG `[0.3.4] ### Fixed` extended with 2 entries documenting the latent bugs.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: 6 checks must be green (Pester suite runs in `gradle-plugin-test`/Windows job)

body:
Follow-up to #8.

## Summary
- **`functions/ross.js`** — wire four documented-but-dropped workflow fields in `rossCreateWorkflow` and `rossActivateWorkflow`:
  - `description` (workflow level; activate falls back to `template.description`)
  - `customInterval` (validated positive integer; passthrough only — recurrence engine still uses the discrete `recurrence` string)
  - `locationAssignedTo` (per-location; map keyed by `locationId`)
  - `activatedAt` (per-location; was only stamped on activate before — now stamped on create too)
- **`public/kb/features/ROSS.md`** — fix data-model drift between docs and code:
  - Workflows: schema block rewritten to show tasks living **per-location** (`locations/{id}/tasks/{id}`) — was incorrectly documented as a flat `tasks: Task[]` at workflow root.
  - Runs: correct the RTDB path from `ross/runs/{locationId}/{workflowId}/...` with `current/history/` nesting to the actual flat path `ross/runs/{uid}/{workflowId}/{locationId}/{runId}`.
  - New **Runs lifecycle** subsection: idempotent `rossCreateRun`, auto-flagging on out-of-range `number`/`temperature`, `requiredNote` HTTP 422 rejection, auto-completion when all required tasks have responses.
  - `notifyPhone` / `notifyEmail` / `customInterval` annotated as **Phase 2** (stored but not yet delivered/used).

## Why
Followed from the gap analysis on master. Code and docs had diverged in three places (workflow tasks shape, runs path, notification delivery). This PR makes the code persist what the docs already promised, and updates the docs where the code intentionally differs.

## Risk / Compatibility
- Reads of existing workflows still work — new fields default to `null` when absent.
- No RTDB rules / composite-index changes.
- No frontend changes needed (consumers already tolerate the absence of these fields and will pick them up where present).

## Test plan

author: craigbehnke
body:
## Summary
This change adds kernel-level ICMP hardening to the runner startup script to mitigate security risks while preserving Path MTU Discovery functionality.

## Key Changes
- Added `icmp_hardening_subscript` local variable that configures sysctl parameters to harden the kernel against security-sensitive ICMP behaviors
- Integrated the hardening script into the startup sequence, executing before optional setup and install steps
- Configured the following security mitigations:
  - Disabled ICMP redirects (both regular and secure variants) for IPv4 and IPv6
  - Disabled source routing for both IPv4 and IPv6
  - Enabled broadcast echo ignore and bogus error response filtering for IPv4

## Implementation Details
The hardening script creates a sysctl configuration file at `/etc/sysctl.d/99-runner-icmp-hardening.conf` and applies it via `sysctl --system`. This approach allows the VPC firewall to continue permitting all ICMP ingress (necessary for Path MTU Discovery fragmentation needed responses) while the kernel drops dangerous ICMP behaviors at the system level. The script runs early in the startup sequence to ensure security hardening is applied before any other initialization steps.

body:
## Summary

Three changes packaged together:

1. **Android keyboard overlap fix.** Capacitor `Keyboard` plugin now uses `resize: 'body'` + `style: 'dark'`, and `keyboardWillShow` / `keyboardWillHide` events feed a new `--keyboard-height` CSS var (CSS px, divided by `devicePixelRatio` to match the visual viewport). A `.keyboard-aware` utility consumes it as `padding-bottom`. Applied to the onboarding container (BYOK key input) and the new license input in Settings. The legacy `--kb-height` (visualViewport-based, used by `.fixed.inset-0` modals) is kept as a safety net.

2. **Post-checkout subscription verification.** After `Browser.open` for Lemon Squeezy resolves (or `browserFinished` fires on native), the subscription card swaps to a "Vérification de ton abonnement…" spinner for at least 3 seconds while it calls `GET /api/subscription/status` with the Google token. On `plan === 'subscription' && status === 'active'` it shows "Abonnement activé !"; otherwise "Paiement en cours de traitement". Both paths mark `onboardingDone` so the user is never stuck.

3. **Pro license activation in Settings.** New `proLicense` service manages a stable device_id (UUID v4) in localStorage and calls `POST /api/license/activate { license_key, email, device_id }` with the Google token forwarded as `x-google-token`. SettingsModal grows a "Licence Pro" section with email + key inputs, error / success messages and an "activated for <email>" view. TopBar shows a `Pro` badge when activated, refreshed via the new `pro-license-changed` event.

## Files

- `capacitor.config.ts` — Keyboard plugin config
- `src/main.tsx` — `@capacitor/keyboard` listeners + `setAccessoryBarVisible(false)`
- `src/index.css` — `--keyboard-height` + `.keyboard-aware`
- `src/components/onboarding/OnboardingChoice.tsx` — verifying / active / pending phases
- `src/components/settings/SettingsModal.tsx` — Pro license section
- `src/components/layout/TopBar.tsx` — Pro badge
- `src/services/proLicense.ts` — new

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (verified locally)
- [ ] `npm test -- --run` — 131/131 pass (verified locally)
- [ ] Manual: open BYOK form on Android APK, focus the API key input → input is visible above the keyboard.
- [ ] Manual: open Settings → Licence Pro → focus the license key input → input is visible above the keyboard.
- [ ] Manual: tap "Démarrer l'abonnement" → close the in-app browser → spinner appears for 3 s → either "Abonnement activé !" or "Paiement en cours de traitement".
- [ ] Manual: enter a valid license key in Settings → check that the "Pro" badge appears in the TopBar without reload.

## Audit sécu

No new server endpoints were added in this PR — `GET /api/subscription/status` and `POST /api/license/activate` are referenced by the client and assumed to exist (or to be added in a follow-up). When those endpoints land, RÈGLE 6 must be re-checked:

- **Authentification** — both endpoints MUST call `checkAllowedUser()` (or equivalent) using the `x-google-token` already forwarded by the client.
- **Autorisation** — `email` from the body MUST be cross-checked against the verified Google `sub` / email; never trust the `email` field alone (otherwise a user can activate a license against another account).
- **Abus infra** — `/api/license/activate` is a write endpoint; rate-limit per `device_id` + IP to prevent brute force of license keys.
- **Leak d'info** — error messages must NOT distinguish "license key not found" from "license already used by another device" (uniform 404 / generic message).
- **Origin / CSRF** — POST endpoints must be in the existing `_middleware.ts` Origin whitelist; do not bypass.

body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the `filter`, `reduce`, and `sort` operations in `storeService.getStats()` with a single `for` loop that uses string comparisons for ISO 8601 dates.
🎯 **Why:** The original code parsed ISO strings into `Date` objects repeatedly inside a loop and executed a full `O(N log N)` sort over the entire history of crises merely to find the most recent date for `daysFree`, heavily dragging down calculation time on large datasets.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** In a benchmark processing 5000 records, the calculation time dropped from an average of ~47.6ms down to ~0.15ms. This represents over a 300x speedup by completely eliminating redundant object allocations and reducing iteration counts.

author: hyang0129
body:
Closes #59

## What changed

The bug in `callers_of`, `callees_of`, `module_callers`, and `module_callees` was not the cap size — it was ranking. `_bfs` returned `sorted(seen)` (alphabetical order), which meant depth-1 callers/callees could be silently dropped when 50+ depth-2 nodes sorted alphabetically earlier. This PR fixes the ranking bug, adds `dropped: int` to all four tool responses, and updates the TypedDicts and server descriptions to match.

## Implementation walkthrough

### `_bfs(g, start, depth)` in `src/pyscope_mcp/graph.py`

Changed return type from `list[str]` to `dict[str, int]` (fqn → min_hop_depth). The BFS loop now records the hop index (1-based) for each newly discovered node as it expands layer by layer. The set of reachable nodes is identical to before; only the return type and depth metadata are new. All three call sites (`callers_of`, `callees_of`, `_prefix_module_bfs`) are updated simultaneously.

### `_rank_bfs_results(bfs_result, graph)` in `src/pyscope_mcp/graph.py`

New helper on `CallGraphIndex`. Takes the `dict[str, int]` from `_bfs` and sorts nodes by `(hop_depth ASC, -total_degree DESC, fqn ASC)` — the same convention used by `neighborhood`. Total degree (in + out) is computed from the underlying forward `_DiGraph` (`graph._g` for `_DiGraphReverseView` inputs). A degree cache is precomputed over result nodes before sorting to avoid O(N×degree) redundant traversals.

### `_rank_module_bfs_results(bfs_result, module_graph)` in `src/pyscope_mcp/graph.py`

Symmetric helper for module-level tools. Uses `module_graph` for degree computation (module in-degree + out-degree), consistent with module-level semantics.

### `_prefix_module_bfs(...)` in `src/pyscope_mcp/graph.py`

Updated to union BFS results using `min(existing_depth, new_depth)` when a result node appears under multiple seeds (closest path wins). Returns a raw `dict[str, int]` under the `results` key (previously a `list[str]`). Also returns `dropped: int` computed before the slice, so callers can pass it through without recomputing. The actual cap+slice is now applied by the callers (`module_callers`, `module_callees`) after ranking.

### `callers_of`, `callees_of` in `src/pyscope_mcp/graph.py`

Both now call `_bfs` → `_rank_bfs_results` → slice. `dropped = max(0, len(ranked) - cap)` is computed on the ranked list before slicing, and both `truncated` and `dropped` are included in the returned `CallersResult`/`CalleesResult`.

### `module_callers`, `module_callees` in `src/pyscope_mcp/graph.py`

Both call `_prefix_module_bfs` → `_rank_module_bfs_results` → slice. The `dropped` value is forwarded from `_prefix_module_bfs` (already computed over the full union) and included in the returned `ModuleResult`.

### `CallersResult`, `CalleesResult`, `ModuleResult` in `src/pyscope_mcp/types.py`

All three TypedDicts gain a required `dropped: int` field. It is always present — not `NotRequired` — because consumers should always be able to read it without a key-existence check.

### Server tool descriptions in `src/pyscope_mcp/server.py`

All four tool descriptions updated to document the new `dropped: int` field, the ranking order, and the consumer-facing guidance ("use `dropped` to detect partial views and narrow your query or escalate accordingly").

## Default execution path

**Before**: `_bfs` → `sorted(seen)` → `[:50]` → respond. Alphabetical truncation could silently drop all depth-1 callers if 50 depth-2 nodes sorted earlier.

**After**: `_bfs` → `dict[fqn, hop]` → rank by `(hop ASC, -degree DESC, fqn ASC)` → `dropped = len - 50` → `[:50]` → respond with `dropped`. Depth-1 results always appear first regardless of FQN alphabetical order; consumers see `dropped > 0` and know the view is partial.

## Edge cases and error handling

- `dropped=0` is explicitly returned when results fit within the cap — consumers can always read the field without checking `truncated` first.
- When `_bfs` returns an empty dict (unknown start node or depth ≤ 0), `dropped=0` and `truncated=False`.
- `_prefix_module_bfs` with no matching seeds returns `{"results": {}, "truncated": False, "dropped": 0}` — all four module methods handle this correctly.

## What was intentionally not changed

- The cap value stays at 50 for all four tools — no configurable parameter per spec.
- `neighborhood` is untouched — it has its own ranking and budget logic.
- `_bfs` traversal logic (which nodes are visited) is identical — only the return type changed.
- `truncated: bool` semantics unchanged.

## Tier / approach

Tier 1 — Planner → Coder (single commit, all changes in graph.py / types.py / server.py / tests/test_graph.py)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `callers_of(depth=2)` on a high-fanout symbol returns ≤50 results
- [x] `callees_of(depth=2)` same
- [x] Results ranked `(hop_depth ASC, -total_degree DESC, fqn ASC)` — depth-1 before depth-2
- [x] Response includes `dropped: int` always present, equals number of results beyond cap
- [x] `dropped=0` when not truncated
- [x] Existing depth=1 tests unaffected (577 → 588 tests, all pass)
- [x] New tests: ranking + dropped correct for all four tools (`callers_of`, `callees_of`, `module_callers`, `module_callees`)

## Summary

PR #121 made refund/exchange cash visibility *derived* via cashbox+time-window matching. PR-R1 makes that linkage **explicit at write time** via a source selector (open shift / direct cashbox), and **closes a long-standing data gap** where exchanges with a cash difference never wrote any cashbox transaction in either direction.

## Migration 099 — additive + idempotent + safe

- ALTER `returns` + `exchanges`: nullable `shift_id` (FK→shifts) + `cashbox_id` (FK→cashboxes), partial indexes
- Targeted backfill of `returns` from existing `cashbox_transactions` (only when the shift is unambiguous → exactly one open shift on the CT's cashbox in its window)
- No `journal_entries` / `journal_lines` / `cashbox_transactions` writes; no `cashboxes.current_balance` edits
- RET-2026-000001 should backfill to SHF-2026-00006

## Permissions added

- **`returns.refund.direct_cashbox`** — gates the direct-cashbox branch (refund OUT only). Required because the user has explicitly asked for a refund flow that does not appear in any shift closing. Wildcard (`*` / `returns.*`) also satisfies it.

## Backend changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| [database/migrations/099_returns_exchanges_shift_linkage.sql](database/migrations/099_returns_exchanges_shift_linkage.sql) | NEW |
| [backend/src/returns/dto/return.dto.ts](backend/src/returns/dto/return.dto.ts) | RefundReturnDto + CreateExchangeDto get optional `shift_id` + `cashbox_id` (UUID) |
| [backend/src/returns/returns.service.ts](backend/src/returns/returns.service.ts) | refund(): replaced silent auto-resolve with explicit pick; persists linkage; perm-gates direct branch. createExchange(): same source flow + **writes CT for both cash directions** via canonical `engine.recordCashOnlyMovement` |
| [backend/src/returns/returns.controller.ts](backend/src/returns/returns.controller.ts) | passes `user.permissions` into refund + createExchange |
| [backend/src/shifts/shifts.service.ts](backend/src/shifts/shifts.service.ts) | computeSummary refundCtRows query rewritten: prefers explicit `shift_id`, filters out direct-cashbox + cross-shift rows, falls back to derived for legacy. Emits `link_method` + `shift_no` |
| [backend/src/settings/settings.service.ts](backend/src/settings/settings.service.ts) | registers `returns.refund.direct_cashbox` |

## Frontend changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| [frontend/src/api/returns.api.ts](frontend/src/api/returns.api.ts) | refund payload + CreateExchangePayload accept `shift_id?` / `cashbox_id?` |
| [frontend/src/api/shifts.api.ts](frontend/src/api/shifts.api.ts) | `RefundCashMovement.shift_no?` |
| [frontend/src/pages/Returns.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Returns.tsx) | RefundModal renders `<CashSourceSelector>` when cash; submit blocked until picked. Exchange modal renders selector when there's a non-zero cash diff (label flips OUT/IN) |
| [frontend/src/pages/Shifts.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Shifts.tsx) | refund detail table adds الوردية column |

Reuses the existing [CashSourceSelector](frontend/src/components/CashSourceSelector.tsx) (PR-15/PR-A) — no UI duplication.

## Accounting impact (zero new GL/CT during build)

- Refund / exchange cash writes route through `FinancialEngineService.recordCashOnlyMovement` → `fn_record_cashbox_txn`
- No journal_lines edited; no manual cashbox.current_balance edits
- Refunds/exchanges land in `category='refund' + reference_type IN ('return','exchange')` — operating-expense bucket reads from the `expenses` table only, no overlap
- Equal exchanges (price_difference = 0) write zero CT rows
- Direct-cashbox rows (`shift_id IS NULL, cashbox_id IS NOT NULL`) are now explicitly **excluded** from every shift closing summary

## Shift closing proof (target schema)

After deploy, SHF-2026-00006's refund detail row for RET-2026-000001 should render with `link_method='explicit'` (post-backfill) and `shift_no='SHF-2026-00006'`. Direct-cashbox refunds and refunds belonging to a different explicit shift will not appear.

## Test plan

- [ ] Migration applies; `returns.shift_id`/`cashbox_id` and `exchanges.shift_id`/`cashbox_id` exist; partial indexes exist
- [ ] RET-2026-000001 backfilled (`returns.shift_id = SHF-2026-00006.id`, `cashbox_id = الخزينة الرئيسية.id`)
- [ ] **Refund — open shift**: row `link_method='explicit'`; appears in that shift's closing; expected drawer cash decreases
- [ ] **Refund — direct cashbox**: requires `returns.refund.direct_cashbox`; `returns.shift_id=NULL`; CT exists but does NOT appear in any shift closing
- [ ] **Refund — non-cash**: no CT; no drawer impact
- [ ] **Exchange — customer receives 100 cash from shift**: CT `out:refund:exchange:100`; appears as خارج 100; expected drawer −100
- [ ] **Exchange — customer pays 100 cash into shift**: CT `in:refund:exchange:100`; appears as داخل 100; expected drawer +100
- [ ] **Exchange — equal**: zero CT; zero drawer impact
- [ ] No new operating-expense rows; no double-counting in `total_cash_out`
- [ ] Trial balance / cashbox drift / refund_inconsistent / engine_bypass_unresolved 7d **all 0** (the new bypass alert from migration 099's helper-less UPDATE will need a follow-up resolve PR if it triggers — migration does no `fn_record_cashbox_txn` calls, so it should not)

body:
Implements the "aggressive trim" recommendation from [#7](https://github.com/TUNC-AI/tunc-clm/pull/7)'s `RESULTS.md`. The v3.0 bench measured -21.4% savings at 50 sessions and noted that pushing `[ROLL.CALL]` / `[DREAM.LOG]` / `[STATE].decisions.live` overflow to the sibling archive should recover most of the optimistic prediction. v3.1 implements that, and the bench confirms.

## Result (validates the recommendation)

50-session synthetic, local tiktoken `o200k_base` probe:

| variant | live-context tokens | vs raw |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prose summary (lossy on lineage) | 438 | -92.3% |
| **CLM/3.1 trim sibling-archive** | **2,603** | **-54.5%** |
| CLM/3.0 sibling (no trim) | 4,498 | -21.4% |
| Raw append (CLM/2.1) | 5,726 | (baseline) |

**Incremental v3.1 vs v3.0:** -42.1% live-context tokens.

The trim recommendation predicted 35–50% savings. The bench shows 54.5% — the prediction was right and slightly conservative.

## What changed

### `SPEC-v3.1-trim-modes.md`

Spec addendum to v3.0. Documents the trim policy formally:

| section | live keeps | overflow goes to (sibling) |
|---|---:|---|
| `[ROLL.CALL]` | last 10 entries | `[ROLL.CALL.ARCHIVE]` |
| `[DREAM.LOG]` | last 3 entries | `[DREAM.LOG.ARCHIVE]` |
| `[STATE].decisions.live` | last 8 decisions | `[DECISIONS.ARCHIVE]` |

Each is independently configurable. Header declares the trim mode (`trim.mode: aggressive`) so a reading AI knows what's offloaded. Self-bootstrap preserved: a fresh AI sees a compact `[STATE]` and recent activity, fetches the sibling for full audit history.

Trade-offs documented honestly:
- Audit-thread visibility narrows in the live doc.
- First-time-reader experience requires an explicit archive read for full lineage.
- Total storage (live + archive) up ~8% because offload sections duplicate session-level info.
- Worth it for any thread read more often than archived.

### `gen_50_session.py`

Adds `trim_mode` parameter (`"none"` or `"aggressive"`) plus configurable `roll_call_keep` / `dream_log_keep` / `decisions_live_keep`. Generates `dreamed-sibling-50-trim.clm` + `.archive.clm` deterministically.

### `tokens.py`

Reports both v3.0 and v3.1 alongside raw + prose. Includes a scaling table showing the 10→50 session growth ratios for raw and v3.0, plus the absolute v3.1 number at 50 sessions.

### `RESULTS.md`

Updated verdict: now four variants tracked (raw / v3.0 / v3.1 / prose). The "honest reflection on prediction-vs-reality" framing carries through — v3.0 oversold; v3.1 trim recovers what v3.0 promised.

## Trade-offs trim mode makes deliberately

1. **Audit-thread visibility narrows** in the live doc. Last 10 ROLL.CALL signers visible; older history requires loading the sibling. Header declares it.
2. **First-time-reader requires two reads for full lineage.** Self-bootstrap still works (live doc teaches the format); lineage queries pay an extra fetch.
3. **Total storage up ~8%.** Offload sections duplicate session-level info that was already implicit in deltas. Live-context savings are ~6.5× the storage overhead — favorable for any read-mostly thread.

## When NOT to use trim mode

- Threads under ~20 sessions (savings marginal; complexity not worth it).
- Audit/compliance contexts where every read must show full lineage inline.
- Documents intended for human reading.

For these, v3.0 (no trim) or even raw v2.1 append is the right choice.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 gen_50_session.py` generates 6 files deterministically.
- [x] `python3 tokens.py` reports the trim mode's win (-54.5% live vs raw).
- [x] Trim mode preserves all the lineage that's queryable from sibling — same archived deltas + new offload sections.
- [ ] Reviewer (gene): confirm trim defaults (10/3/8) are sane vs aggressive vs conservative.
- [ ] Open: trim threshold sweep on a 100+ session thread. Defer.

## Suggested follow-ups

1. **Trim-aware clm-rs.** Parser doesn't validate the new archive section types yet. Low-effort PR.
2. **Lineage Q&A run** (`frontier.py`) to validate that trim mode preserves fidelity. ~$0.10 API spend; settles the architecture's claims for both depths.
3. **200-session bench** to test the savings curve further. If trim continues to scale (~60–70% at 200 sessions), the architecture's pitch is locked in.
4. **Promote v3.0 + v3.1 to main `SPEC.md`** once we're confident in the trim defaults. Leave `experiments/v3/` for the validation artifacts.

🤖 Authored by CLd.Ops4.7 (1M context) at gene's direction.

*"my v3.0 'constant-size live doc' pitch was wrong; my v3.1 'aggressive trim recovers it' recommendation was right. the bench falsifies one and validates the other. honest is on-thesis."*

author: cgmossa
body:
## Summary

- **Bug fix**: sidecar `Type_get_field` / `Type_set_field` wrappers from `#[derive(ExternalPtr)]` were calling `.Call(C_..., x)` without `.call = match.call()`. The C wrappers take `__miniextendr_call: SEXP` as their first parameter, so omitting it shifted the user's `x` argument into the call slot and broke error attribution under panic. Twelve sites covered (getter+setter × Env/R6/S3/S4/S7/Vctrs).
- **DotCallBuilder unification**: routed every remaining hand-rolled `format!(".Call(..., .call = match.call(), ...)")` through `DotCallBuilder` — `MethodContext::{static_call, instance_call}`, `match_arg_prelude`, S4 instance methods, S7 validator/convert_from/convert_to, R6 finalizer/deep_clone/active-binding setter, and the standalone `match_arg` choices helper. Output is byte-identical for all routed sites; the only behavioural diff in `rpkg/R/miniextendr-wrappers.R` is exactly the 46 sidecar lines (verified).
- **Regression test**: `externalptr_derive::tests::sidecar_accessors_pass_match_call` exercises every `ClassSystem` variant of `generate_r_wrapper_for_slot` and asserts both getter and setter contain `.call = match.call()`.
- **Documentation**: new `docs/CALL_ATTRIBUTION.md` with a runnable fixture (`rpkg/src/rust/call_attribution_demo.rs`) showing two functions that raise the same error — one through the standard wrapper, one as `extern "C-unwind"` with no wrapper. Transcript captured from `Rscript` against the freshly installed package; auto-regenerated to `site/content/manual/call-attribution.md` via `just site-docs`.

## Why the sidecar gap mattered

`error_in_r_check_lines` reads `.val\$call %||% sys.call()`. The `.val\$call` field is populated by the C wrapper, which receives `__miniextendr_call` as the **first** SEXP and threads it through `with_r_unwind_protect_error_in_r`. When the R wrapper wrote `.Call(C_..._get_field, x)` instead of `.Call(C_..._get_field, .call = match.call(), x)`, the first positional SEXP arriving in C was `x` (the externalptr) — so the call slot held a pointer-y SEXP and the field accessor's first formal received nothing. Either way error attribution was wrong; under panic the diagnostic could be misleading or worse.

## Demo from the new fixture

```r
> outer_with    <- function(x) call_attr_with(x, x + 1L)
> outer_without <- function(x) miniextendr:::unsafe_C_call_attr_without(x, x + 1L)

> outer_with(5L)
Error in call_attr_with(left = x, right = x + 1L) :
  left + right is too risky

> outer_without(5L)
Error in miniextendr:::unsafe_C_call_attr_without(x, x + 1L) :
  left + right is too risky

> class(tryCatch(outer_with(5L), error = identity))
[1] "rust_error"  "simpleError" "error"       "condition"

> class(tryCatch(outer_without(5L), error = identity))
[1] "simpleError" "error"       "condition"
```

Three concrete benefits the wrapped path delivers: formal arg name matching, public symbol attribution (no `:::` leak of internal names), and structured `rust_error` class.

## Follow-ups (deferred to issues)

- #317 — Rust macros `condition!` / `error!` / `message!` / `warning!` for the full `simpleCondition` / `simpleError` / `simpleMessage` / `simpleWarning` set, layered with `rust_*` subclasses.
- #318 — The new demo fixture (`call_attr_with`, `unsafe_C_call_attr_without`) is exported into the public namespace; should be marked internal or moved into a test.
- #319 — `match.call()` in R6 finalizer / `deep_clone` / S7 property getter/setter/validator captures the internal R6/S7 dispatch frame, not the user's call. Decide between dropping `.call`, synthesizing a meaningful call expression, or walking back via `sys.call(-N)`.

- [x] `just clippy` (workspace + cross-package + rpkg) — clean
- [x] `just configure && just rcmdinstall && just devtools-document` — green; wrapper diff is exactly 46 sidecar lines + the new demo wrappers, no unintended drift
- [x] Demo fixture run via `Rscript` against the installed package — error-attribution differences confirmed visually and via `tryCatch` class inspection

author: bluestreak01
body:
## Summary

The `Build and upload snapshot (Linux)` Azure pipeline has been failing on every push to master since the JDK 25 bump (b700076). The job declares:

```yaml
JAVA_HOME_25_X64: "/opt/graalvm"
JAVA_HOME: "/opt/graalvm"
```

but on the `hetzner-incus` agent pool `/opt/graalvm` still points at a GraalVM 17 install. The Maven task therefore runs under Java 17.0.9, and the `enforce-versions` rule (which now requires Java 25) aborts the build before any code is compiled:

```
Java version: 17.0.9, vendor: GraalVM Community, runtime: /opt/graalvm
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-enforcer-plugin:3.0.0-M3:enforce (enforce-versions)
```

This PR points both env vars at `/opt/graalvm-25`, which is the path the rest of the self-hosted pipelines (`ci/templates/self-hosted-jobs.yml`, `ci/templates/steps.yml`) already use.

It also renames the stale `linux-jdk17` matrix key in `ci/templates/aux-job.yml` to `linux-jdk25`. The `jdk: "1.25"` value was already correct, so the underlying job was building under JDK 25; only the matrix label was wrong and was showing a misleading `RunOn linux-jdk17` row in the Azure UI.

## Scope and limits

- This restores the snapshot job. It does not address the unrelated `paths`-filter skips on `GLIBC Smoke Test` and `rebuild_native_libs` for the JDK 25 commit.
- `.github/workflows/parquet_compat.yml` still installs JDK 17 for the PySpark step. PySpark 3.5.x does not run on JDK 25, and `requirements_parquet_pyspark.txt` is pinned at `pyspark>=3.5.0`. Removing the JDK 17 install would require also pinning to `pyspark>=4.0.0`; left as a separate change.

## Test plan

- After merge, confirm `Build and upload snapshot (Linux)` succeeds on the next master push.
- Confirm the `JavaAndRustLint` stage's `RunOn` job now appears as `linux-jdk25` in the Azure DevOps UI.

author: avrabe
body:
This PR is from the Mythos research-agent sweep post-#205. It restores full Rocq proof verification in CI, which had been narrowed to a schema-only build by commit `e4e9ba8` while the underlying issues were investigated.

## Change 1: Validation.v cross-library import

`Require Import Schema.` -> `From proofs.rocq Require Import Schema.`

`rules_rocq_rust` derives the logical prefix from the Bazel package path, so for `//proofs/rocq:rivet_schema` the prefix is `proofs.rocq`. The bare `Require Import Schema.` was unresolvable across library boundaries. The qualified-import pattern is the same one used in the upstream `examples/rust_to_rocq/point_proofs.v` precedent.

## Change 2: Schema.v -- replace two Admitted lemmas with concrete proofs

`no_source_no_violations` and `zero_violations_implies_satisfied` were both Admitted with documented closure-over-`s` gaps. Replaced with:

- A `filter_length_zero_forall` helper that extracts pointwise predicate falsity from a zero-length filter result.
- An auxiliary lemma `no_source_no_violations_aux` that decouples the lookup list from the iterated list -- the missing piece in the original closure-over-`s` proof.
- The two top-level statements then discharge cleanly via the helper + aux.

The two `(* CHECK *)` items flagged in the plan -- the constructor-pair `destruct ... ; destruct ...` block (mirrors `Validation.v:158-170 check_artifact_rule_clean`) and the `andb_false_iff` / `negb_false_iff` lemma-name resolution under Rocq 9.0 -- were applied as written without iteration; if Rocq CI rejects either, the fallback is `apply Bool.andb_false_iff` / `apply Bool.negb_false_iff`.

The closing summary near the bottom of `Schema.v` no longer claims "One theorem is partially verified".

## Change 3: ci.yml -- re-enable full Rocq verification

The Rocq step reverts to:

```yaml
      - name: Verify Rocq proofs
        run: bazel test //proofs/rocq:rivet_metamodel_test
```

The temporary "build only schema" comment block is dropped now that the underlying issues (cross-library import + Admitteds) are addressed. The `continue-on-error: true` and the existing pacing comment ("Not yet a hard gate") remain intact -- this restores verification, not the hard-gate flip.

Verifies: REQ-004
