author: le-who
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: API parameter injection via f-strings and string concatenation in `requests.get()` within `update.py`. User-controlled `tag` input was interpolated directly into the query string, which could break the URL structure or inject unintended parameters if it contained characters like `&` or `#`.
🎯 Impact: Potentially allows manipulating the Gelbooru API request to fetch unintended data, bypass rate limits, or perform SSRF if the base URL is ever made dynamic. Also fixes potential bugs with tags containing special characters.
🔧 Fix: Replaced manual f-string URL construction with the `requests.get(params=...)` dictionary, which automatically and safely handles URL encoding of parameters.
✅ Verification: Created a local virtual environment, installed requests, and verified that `get_data()` still successfully fetches data for a valid tag without throwing errors or returning None.

author: yukikurisu1990-gh
body:
## Summary

Phase 9.17 closure memo + 20-pair 4-cell ensemble eval log.

**Verdict: NO ADOPT** for all ensemble cells. Production default unchanged: 20-pair v9 symmetric spread bundle (Sharpe 0.160, PnL 8,157, DD%PnL 2.5%).

## Results (39-fold walk-forward, 20-pair v9 universe)

| Cell | Sharpe | PnL (pip) | DD%PnL | WinFold% | SigRate | Trades | Max ρ |
|------|--------|-----------|--------|----------|---------|--------|-------|
| lgbm_only (baseline) | **0.160** | 8,157 | 2.5% | 90% | 4.5% | 12,461 | — |
| lgbm+mr | 0.053 | 12,360 (1.52×) | 1.4% | 95% | 69.8% | 192,832 | 0.317 |
| lgbm+bo | 0.035 | 7,843 (0.96×) | 2.5% | 95% | 65.9% | 181,927 | 0.206 |
| lgbm+mr+bo | 0.036 | 9,023 (1.11×) | 2.7% | 97% | 80.0% | 220,839 | 0.582 |

**lgbm_only exactly reproduces Phase 9.16 v9 baseline** — validates the v13 script.

## Different failure mode than predicted

The design memo §9.3 honesty disclosure warned strategies might correlate ρ ≈ 0.7+ with LightGBM. The 2-pair smoke seemed to confirm this (ρ 0.726 / 0.548 / 0.870). **The 20-pair full eval revealed a different failure mode:**

1. **Strategies ARE orthogonal at scale** — all cross-correlations |ρ| ≤ 0.582
2. **Trade rate explodes 15×** (12,461 → 192,832) because MR/BO have no LightGBM-style confidence-threshold filter
3. **SELECTOR dominated by MR/BO** (~95% share); LightGBM falls to < 5%
4. **Per-trade EV dilutes** → Sharpe collapses despite low correlation

The orthogonality thesis is supported. The SELECTOR-budget thesis is not.

## Why each cell fails the gate

| Cell | Gate failure |
|------|--------------|
| lgbm+mr | Sharpe 0.053 < baseline 0.160 (PARTIAL GO requires Sharpe ≥ baseline) |
| lgbm+bo | Sharpe 0.035 < baseline; PnL 0.96× < 1.10× GO threshold |
| lgbm+mr+bo | Sharpe 0.036 < baseline; ρ 0.582 in 0.4–0.6 PARTIAL GO band |

No cell reaches Sharpe ≥ 0.18 either, so STRETCH GO also fails.

## Inter-strategy correlation (notable)

```
                lgbm        mr        bo
lgbm           +1.000    +0.317   -0.206
mr             +0.317    +1.000   -0.582
bo             -0.206    -0.582   +1.000
```

MR and BO are **strongly anti-correlated** (ρ = -0.582) — band-touch fade vs band-break follow are structurally opposite. Useful future signal if trade-rate is contained.

## What's next

Two options before pivoting to model-class change:

- **Option A (9.17b)**: add confidence threshold (e.g. ≥ 0.5) to MR/BO. Cuts trade rate but may starve trade volume. Fast experiment (~1 day).
- **Option B**: pivot to alternative model class (LSTM, alt labels, alt features). Structural fix; larger scope.

Phase 9.11 (3+ yr robustness) remains **BLOCKED** on Sharpe ≥ 0.20. G-5 (production runtime wiring) **not triggered**.

## Test plan

- [x] Memo references all 4 cell results
- [x] Verdict gates correctly mapped to design memo §5
- [x] Per-cell strategy share documented
- [x] Eval log artefact attached for traceability

author: nmengual
body:
## Summary

Wires the cost view to the daily pricing dataset published by [#16](https://github.com/folio-pro/kdashboard/pull/16). The Rust resolver fetches the dataset directly from the `pricing-data` GitHub release, **uses ETag for conditional fetches** (so daily revalidations are ~0 bytes when nothing changed), caches everything on disk, and runs a **background refresh once every 24h**. No more dependency on `www.kdashboard.app/api/pricing/resolve`.

## What changes

- **`src-tauri/src/k8s/cost/pricing.rs`** — full rewrite. Public signature `resolve_pricing(&[NodeInfo]) -> Option<HashMap<String, f64>>` is preserved (key `provider/region/instance_type`), so `calculations.rs` and `node_metrics.rs` need zero changes.
- **`src-tauri/src/k8s/cost/types.rs`** — removed obsolete request/response structs (`PricingResolveRequest`, `PricingResolveResponse`, `PricingResolveItem`, `ResolvedPricing`).
- **`src-tauri/src/k8s/cost/mod.rs`** — exports new `spawn_periodic_refresh`.
- **`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`** — calls `spawn_periodic_refresh()` from the Tauri `setup` callback so the daily revalidation runs even if the cost view is never opened after launch.

## How it works

```
resolve_pricing(nodes)
  └─ for each unique provider:
       memory cache fresh? (24h)
         └─ no → meta.fetched_at fresh? (24h)
              └─ yes → load body from disk, install in memory
              └─ no  → conditional GET with If-None-Match
                   ├─ 304 → touch meta (new fetched_at), reload disk body
                   ├─ 200 → write new body + new etag, install in memory
                   └─ network err → fall back to stale disk body
```

`spawn_periodic_refresh()` ticks every 24h and revalidates every provider already in the memory cache. Each tick is a conditional GET — typically 304 with no body — so daily refresh of an unchanged dataset is essentially free on the wire.

## Disk layout

```
~/.kdashboard/pricing/
├── aws.json         (~2 MB — raw dataset body)
├── aws.meta.json    ({ etag, fetched_at })
├── azure.json
├── azure.meta.json
├── gcp.json
└── gcp.meta.json
```

Freshness is driven by `meta.fetched_at` rather than file mtime, so a 304 just rewrites the meta and leaves the body untouched.

## Knobs

- `KDASHBOARD_PRICING_URL` env var overrides the base URL (testing, self-hosted mirror).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` clean.
- [x] `cargo test --lib cost::pricing` — 9 tests pass, 1 `--ignored`.
- [x] **Live test against the real release**:
  ```
  cargo test --lib cost::pricing -- --ignored --nocapture
  ```
  - First call hits the network (200) and persists `aws.json` + `aws.meta.json`.
  - Second call sends `If-None-Match: <etag>` and gets back 304, asserted via `revalidate_provider("aws") == Ok(false)`.
- [ ] Manual: `bun run tauri dev`, open cost view, confirm `source: cloud-pricing` on the overview. Inspect `~/.kdashboard/pricing/` for body + meta sidecars.
- [ ] Manual: leave the app open >24h and confirm a `pricing dataset unchanged on revalidation` log line appears (`RUST_LOG=kdashboard_lib=debug`).

## Out of scope

- UI surfacing of "last refreshed at" or "stale data" hints in the cost view.
- GCP zone-vs-region nuances (`us-central1` vs `us-central1-a`) — node label parsing in `nodes.rs` was already handling this and is untouched here.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Daily background refresh of cloud pricing datasets for up-to-date rates.
  * Pricing resolves from local provider datasets for faster, offline-capable lookups.
  * Metrics availability tracking to avoid repeated failing probes and reduce noise.

* **Bug Fixes / Reliability**
  * Multi-layer caching with conditional validation and atomic disk writes to reduce downloads and tolerate network failures.
  * Metrics endpoint gating and reset on context/settings changes to force fresh probing and improve stability.
* **Other**

author: gianniskotsas
body:
## Summary

PR #91's IBAN backfill broke in production with \`TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str'\` (surfaced via PR #92's traceback logging). Root cause:

> EB's \`GET /sessions/{uid}\` returns rich account objects **only at OAuth time**. On subsequent calls (post-mapping, post-sync) the \`accounts\` field collapses to a list of UID strings.

The existing \`EnableBankingAdapter.fetch_accounts\` was dead code on the EB sync path until PR #91 wired it up — the bug was latent. With UID strings, \`acc[\"uid\"]\` blows up.

## Fix

1. **New method \`fetch_account_iban(uid)\`** in the EB adapter — calls \`GET /accounts/{uid}/details\` (the symmetric per-account endpoint to \`fetch_balances\` / \`fetch_transactions\`). Always returns the canonical IBAN, normalized via \`_extract_iban\`.

2. **Replaced bulk fetch in \`sync_bank_connection\`** with a per-account loop. Skips accounts that already have \`iban_hash\` (immutable). Per-account \`try/except\` so one bad account doesn't block the others.

## Test plan

- [x] All 31 adapter + transfer-service + sync-encryption tests pass locally
- [ ] Deploy → trigger sync → \`accounts.iban_hash\` populated for all 9 synced accounts
- [ ] Subsequent sync's \`InternalTransferService.detect_for_transactions\` matches transfers between synced accounts

## Risk

Low. Per-account fetch is opt-in (only runs if \`iban_hash\` is NULL), idempotent, and wrapped in try/except so failures don't break the rest of the sync.

author: pschmitz-valckenberg
body:
Sets up everything needed to run and record a reproducible 4-strategy benchmark campaign, without changing the evaluation data model.

- scripts/run_benchmark.sh — automates the full campaign:
    1. creates a benchmark with NONE + INPUT_FILTER + INPUT_OUTPUT + PROMPT_HARDENING for a configurable model (default gemini-2.0-flash, --model flag to switch to Anthropic)
    2. executes it synchronously (up to 10min timeout)
    3. fetches the report and saves all three JSON responses to a timestamped results/<timestamp>_<model>/ subdirectory
    4. prints a human-readable summary table to stdout
- results/README.md — explains the directory layout and how to reproduce
- .gitignore — excludes results/*/ from version control so raw API responses (which may contain prompt text) stay local; the summary numbers go into README.md manually
- README.md — adds a "Benchmark Results" section with the table structure ready to fill in after the first live run; includes the one-liner to reproduce

The campaign is intentionally run once per model / case-suite version. caseSuiteFingerprint on each EvaluationRun guarantees that a stored benchmark report is only compared against runs with the same fingerprint, so results remain methodologically sound even if the case suite grows later.

body:
## Summary Follow-up to #80. Extracts mermaid rendering into a new `@slayzone/markdown` shared package and eliminates ~150 LOC of pasted plumbing between `file-editor/MermaidBlock.tsx` (added by #80) and `worktrees/GhMarkdown.tsx` (existing). `task/AssetsPanel.tsx` gains mermaid support for free. ## Structural fixes vs. the duplicated copy - **Pure-React controls** — pan/zoom/copy buttons are JSX (`IconButton` + `lucide-react`) instead of imperative `document.createElement` + `innerHTML`. Removes the strict-mode double-attach bug that affected both prior copies. - **Theme reactive** — `useTheme()` drives a theme-keyed cache; toggling dark/light invalidates and re-renders mounted blocks. Old code only cleared the cache on next call, so visible diagrams stayed stale-themed. - **Lazy-init dedup** — single in-flight promise. N concurrent first-mount blocks share one `mermaid.initialize` call. - **Object-URL leak fix** — `copyDiagramAsImage` revokes URL in `finally`, including the `img.onerror` path. - **Copy errors surface** — `console.warn` instead of `.catch(() => {})`. - **`securityLevel: 'strict'`** (`GhMarkdown` was `'loose'`). - **`code` component override** (standard react-markdown hook) instead of `pre`-child sniff. body:
## Summary

Lands 2023 into the canonical training/baseline DB so downstream model work
(position-weight sweep, referee revisit, Glicko-2) has a third season of
walk-forward signal to consume.

- \`python -m fantasy_coach backfill --season 2023\` ran clean: **213 matches
  across 31 rounds, 0 failures**.
- \`tests/fixtures/baseline-nrl.db\` rebuilt as 2023+2024+2025+2026 (843 rows;
  692 non-draw predictions when walked).
- \`SEASONS\` in \`test_baseline_metrics.py\` extended to \`(2023, 2024, 2025, 2026)\`.
- \`EXPECTED\` dict refreshed for all 7 predictors; per-model rationale in the
  test's comment block.

## Walk-forward metric shifts (480 → 692 pool)

| model | accuracy Δ | log_loss Δ | brier Δ | direction |
|-------|-----------:|-----------:|--------:|-----------|
| home    | +0.0004 | −0.0001 | 0.0000 | flat (sanity) |
| elo     | +0.0352 | −0.0079 | −0.0038 | warmer ratings into 2024+ |
| elo_mov | +0.0147 | −0.0102 | −0.0051 | same effect, smaller |
| logistic| −0.0092 | −0.0423 | −0.0152 | accuracy dip on cold-2023, big calibration win |
| xgboost | −0.0392 | −0.0032 | +0.0001 | cold-start 2023 drag (see below) |
| skellam | +0.0251 | −0.0415 | −0.0154 | strong-L2 prior + more data |
| stacked | +0.0100 | −0.0098 | −0.0039 | net positive |

**XGBoost regression — not a leakage flag.** The harness has no warmup mode,
so 2023's first ~10 rounds train on near-empty rolling features and predict
near 0.5. That portion of the pooled n=692 average drags accuracy down. The
held-out 2026 slice (the production-relevant one) is essentially unchanged.

The issue's prediction (\"Plain Elo / EloMOV should be roughly unchanged
… anything bigger would be a red flag for leakage\") was about per-season
metrics, not the pooled-with-cold-2023 metric — Elo's +3.5pp here is the
*warmer ratings into the existing 2024+ predictions*, plus the larger
denominator diluting cold rounds. No leakage indicators.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] \`backfill --season 2023\` runs clean (213/213 fetched, retry log empty).
- [x] 2023 in \`data/nrl.db\`; \`baseline-nrl.db\` rebuilt as the single source of truth.
- [ ] Production Firestore backfilled via \`copy-matches-to-firestore --season 2023\`
      — held back for explicit operator approval; this PR is the data + test refresh
      only. Dry-run confirmed: 213 matches across 1 season ready to copy.
- [x] \`test_baseline_metrics.py\` EXPECTED refreshed; 7/7 predictors green locally
      (\`uv run pytest tests/test_baseline_metrics.py\` → \`7 passed in 370.96s\`).
- [ ] \`docs/model.md\` ablation tables — qualitative conclusions still hold against
      the larger pool; re-running each numeric ablation against the new DB is a
      follow-up (the key-absence and position-weight sweeps are the most likely to
      meaningfully shift).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (lint + full pytest including the 6-minute baseline metrics run).
- [ ] After merge: confirm prod deploys clean and Firestore backfill is run separately.

body: ## Summary Phase 2 из плана прокачки дашборда. Две большие фичи + графdegrade при отсутствии миграции. ### 1. Справочник контрагентов Новая таблица `contacts` со своим RLS. Каждый юзер видит только свой справочник. - **Вкладка «Контрагенты»**: список с поиском по ФИО/ИНН/телефону/email, фильтр физ./юр. лица, сортировка по имени/типу/количеству договоров. - **Модалка создания/редактирования**: ФИО, тип, ИНН, паспорт/ОГРН, телефон, email, адрес, заметки. - **Автоподстановка в форме договора**: новый дропдаун над полем ФИО — выбираешь контрагента, ФИО подставляется, под полем хинт `Подставлено из справочника: ИНН ... · +7 ... · email`. - **Кнопка «+ Сохранить как контрагента»** прямо в форме договора: впечатываешь ФИО руками — одним кликом отправляешь в справочник, в следующих договорах будет в дропдауне. - **Привязка**: `contracts.contact_id` (FK на `contacts`) — необязательная. Сохранится в БД, и в карточке контрагента будет счётчик «Договоров: N». ### 2. Чеклисты по этапам производства Новая вкладка «Чеклисты». Источник пунктов — `CHECKLISTS.md` из репо. - **4 этапа**: До съёмок (10 пунктов), В ходе съёмок (3), После съёмок/МТП (5), Перед сдачей/дистрибуцией (6). - **Интерактивные галочки**: ручная отметка сохраняется в `projects.checklist_state` (JSONB). - **Авто-сверка с договорами проекта**: если в проекте есть подписанный договор режиссёра — пункт «Договор с режиссёром-постановщиком» автоматически отмечен с бейджем `АВТО` и недоступен для ручной правки. Аналогично для оператора, актёров, сценариста, НДА, согласий, лицензии на музыку. - **Прогресс-бары** по каждому этапу: `2 / 10 · 20%`. - **Красные флаги** из `CHECKLISTS.md` показаны блоком внизу. ### 3. SQL-миграция (1 раз) `migrations/2026-04-26_contacts_checklists.sql` — все изменения **additive**, существующие данные не трогаются: - `create table contacts` + RLS-политики - `alter table contracts add column contact_id uuid references contacts(id) on delete set null` - `alter table projects add column checklist_state jsonb default '{}'` **Как накатить**: открой Supabase Studio → SQL Editor → New query → вставь содержимое миграции → Run. ### 4. Graceful degrade Если миграцию не накатать — приложение **не падает**, а: - показывает жёлтый баннер сверху с инструкцией; - скрывает поле `contact_id` из payload договора (старая логика работает 1-в-1); - блокирует попытку открыть модалку контрагента / тоггл чеклиста с понятным toast'ом. После применения миграции и refresh — баннер исчезнет, фичи активируются. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Запустить SQL-миграцию** в Supabase Studio (`migrations/2026-04-26_contacts_checklists.sql`). Без неё новые фичи не работают. - [ ] На превью Cloudflare Pages открой PR-deploy → залогинься. - [ ] Вкладка «Контрагенты»: создай 2-3 контрагента (физ. + юр. лицо), проверь редактирование и удаление. - [ ] Создай новый договор → в селекте «Контрагент» выбери одного из справочника → ФИО подставилось, появился хинт. ## Summary

For a 10,000-message mailbox, incremental sync goes from scanning all flags to only the handful that changed.

Dovecot, Fastmail, Outlook/O365, Cyrus: supported. Gmail IMAP: not supported (uses REST API). Fallback: unchanged UID-based sync.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

`map_storage_err` rendered every storage failure as `AppError::Storage` → HTTP 500. Filesystem `ENAMETOOLONG` (path or name segment exceeds the underlying FS limit, typically 255 bytes on ext4/xfs) is caused by malformed client input, not a server failure. Clients should see 400 Bad Request and a precise message so they can correct the path, not an opaque 500.

Surfaced by release-gate run [24941173682](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper-test/actions/runs/24941173682) on the "Upload with extremely long path segments returns error" assertion in `tests/formats/test-conan-errors.sh`, which sends a 300-character package name and asserts the server does NOT return 500.

## Change

`backend/src/api/handlers/error_helpers.rs`: detect the canonical message fragments that `std::io` and storage backends emit (`File name too long`, raw `ENAMETOOLONG`, wrapped `name too long`) and short-circuit to 400 with a precise message before the generic Storage error path. Match is case-insensitive and uses substring detection so wrapped messages from upper layers are still classified correctly.

Affects every format handler that uses `map_storage_err` (maven, npm, pypi, cargo, conan, generic, others). 4 new unit tests cover Linux canonical, wrapped, raw-token, and negative cases.

## Test Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --lib` passes (8446 passed, 0 failed; 5 new tests in this module)
- [x] Negative test included (unrelated storage messages still 500)

## API Changes

None directly. Behavior change: requests with paths exceeding FS name limits now return 400 instead of 500. No other endpoints affected.

Last fix needed for v1.2.0-rc.1 gate green.

## What
Adds [TIES](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.01708) (Yadav et al. 2023) as a second merge mode on the just-shipped POST `/v1/adapters/merge` endpoint, alongside the existing `weighted_average` mode.

## Why
The `adapter_merge` module header explicitly deferred TIES; this is the natural follow-up after #575 (download) and #577 (upload). TIES handles task interference better than naive linear interpolation when merging adapters that adapt the same model in conflicting directions, which is the common case for shared-experience LoRA hubs.

## How
Per tensor:
1. **Trim** — keep only the top `density` fraction of values by absolute magnitude per adapter; the rest are zeroed.
2. **Elect sign** — per parameter position, the sign of `Σⱼ wⱼ · trimmed_j[i]` is the elected sign.
3. **Disjoint merge** — per parameter position, weight-average only the trimmed values whose sign matches the elected sign:
   `out[i] = (Σ_{j ∈ S} wⱼ · trimmed_j[i]) / (Σ_{j ∈ S} wⱼ)` where `S = { j : sign(trimmed_j[i]) == elected }`.

API: `mode: \"ties\"` plus optional `density: f32` (default 0.2, range `(0.0, 1.0]` — paper recommendation). `density` is rejected with 400 when `mode != \"ties\"` so callers can't silently typo it. Pure CPU/f32, no CUDA dependency.

Validation matches `merge_linear`: at least one adapter, identical rank / target_modules / base model / tensor key sets / shapes.

## Tests

`cargo test -p kiln-model adapter_merge` — 18/18 passed locally, including 7 new TIES tests:

- `test_merge_ties_density_one_equals_linear_when_signs_agree` — density=1.0 with weights summing to 1 collapses to merge_linear's weighted sum
- `test_merge_ties_trims_low_magnitude_values` — top-k cut on a single adapter zeros below-threshold magnitudes
- `test_merge_ties_sign_election_resolves_conflicts` — opposing-sign adapters; higher-weighted side drives both elected sign and final value
- `test_merge_ties_validates_density_range` — 0.0, >1.0, negative, NaN all rejected
- `test_merge_ties_empty_errors`
- `test_merge_ties_rank_mismatch_errors`
- `test_merge_ties_save_and_load_roundtrip` — TIES output is on-disk PEFT-compatible

`crates/kiln-server/tests/adapter_merge_ties.rs` exercises the HTTP surface (200 + correct merged values; 400 on bad density; 400 when density passed without `mode==\"ties\"`).

## Sandbox build note
`cargo check -p kiln-server` cannot run in the Cloud Eric Alpine sandbox because `reqwest`'s transitive `openssl-sys` dep needs system OpenSSL headers that aren't installed (per the existing `kiln-sandbox-rust-tooling` agent note). `cargo check -p kiln-model` and `cargo test -p kiln-model` run cleanly. The kiln-server changes are CPU-only Rust around the merge_ties dispatch and an integration test, with no new dependencies — they should build wherever the existing crate already builds.

author: aletc1
body:
Project-level Scripts widget that runs configured commands in real terminals from the Details sidebar.

- Schema: extend .1code/worktree.json with scripts: [{ name, command }].
- Widget: deterministic paneId per script so Run is idempotent and Stop can find/kill the right terminal. 2s getSession poll detects external exits (Ctrl+C, crash) and flips the button back to Run.
- Editor: new Scripts section in the Projects settings tab with auto-save and dedupe-by-name validation.
- Fill with AI: /scripts-fill prompt and button generate the array based on detected project type (npm/bun/pnpm/yarn, dotnet, cargo, go, python).
- TerminalInstance.initialCommands so each tab carries its own startup command (was sidebar-level, would re-fire on every tab).

Terminal manager fixes shaken out by the widget:

- killProcessTree walks the pty's descendants via pidtree and signals every one before the shell. pty.kill() alone leaks bun run dev -> vite -> node chains.
- Stop now uses SIGKILL: SIGTERM gave dev servers a graceful-shutdown window measured in seconds.
- intentionalKill flag suppresses the "shell crashed quickly -> recover with fallback shell" path. SIGKILL exits look like crashes (non-zero, sub-second) and were resurrecting the session, swallowing the next Run.
- Sessions evicted from the manager Map synchronously after kill so a fast Run-after-Stop creates a brand-new session instead of attaching to the dying one.
- before-quit now awaits terminalManager.cleanup() (bounded 2s) so app shutdown also kills every terminal's process tree.

author: mavrikant
body:
## Summary

Adds an `Average: %1` line to the win dialog showing the player's mean
winning time on the current difficulty once they have won that
difficulty at least 3 times. Best time tracks the *peak* run; this is
the *typical* run — the lever a player wants to move with practice.

## Design

- **Persistence:** new `total_seconds_won` field on `Stats::Record`
  accumulating every counted winning duration. Same `seconds > 0` gate
  as `bestSeconds` so a sub-tick test win never poisons the divisor.
- **Surfacing:** two new fields on `Stats::WinOutcome` —
  `winsAfter` (post-increment wins count) and `averageSecondsAfter`
  (= `totalSecondsWon / won`). Caller doesn't re-load the record.
- **Threshold:** `MainWindow::onGameWon` passes `0.0` (the
  "do-not-show" sentinel) when `winsAfter < 3`. n=1 reduces to
  best-time; n=2 is a single data point of variation; n>=3 is the
  canonical speedrun "ao3" minimum.
- **Replay / custom exclusion:** existing
  `!m_isReplay && !m_isCustom` gate around `recordWin` already
  excludes those — memorising a board to game the average is a
  non-issue.
- **Backwards compatibility:** a pre-1.36 plist with no
  `total_seconds_won` key loads as 0.0. The first 1.36+ win on each
  difficulty seeds the accumulator. The first three displayed
  averages drift slightly until the accumulator catches up.
  Considered seeding from `bestSeconds * won` and rejected — best is
  the *minimum* run, so seeded averages would be optimistically
  wrong.
- **Reset semantics:** `Stats::reset(name)` removes the key
  alongside `played` / `won`. `resetAll()` already wipes the whole
  `stats/` group.
- **Format:** reuses `formatElapsedTime` so the mean reads with the
  same M:SS.S / H:MM:SS.S grammar as every other time string —
  zero new format helpers, zero new translatable formats.

## Diff shape

- Production: ~26 LOC of `stats.{h,cpp}`, ~15 LOC of
  `mainwindow.{h,cpp}`, 1 LOC version bump.
- Tests: 12 new `tst_stats` cases (~140 LOC) covering accumulator
  semantics, `WinOutcome` field plumbing, per-difficulty isolation,
  sub-tick rejection, reset semantics, and the legacy-plist load
  path.
- Translations: 1 new hand-translated key x 9 non-English locales.
  All 10 locales report `107 finished, 0 unfinished`.

Total real diff well under the 400-LOC cycle cap.

## Local verification

- `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -G Ninja`: clean.
- `update_translations`: "1 new and 106 already existing" across all
  10 locales.
- `apply_translations.py`: 104 translations applied per non-English
  locale.
- `cmake --build build`: clean. All 8 test binaries link.
- `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ctest --output-on-failure`: 8/8 pass
  (`tst_stats` 104 passed, was 92 pre-cycle).
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror`: clean.

## Adversarial self-review

- **Overflow?** `double` accumulator can hold ~1.8e308; unreachable.
- **Floating-point drift?** Same `double` the `bestSeconds` field
  has used since v1.0.
- **Backwards-compatible API?** Yes — `WinOutcome` gains two
  appended fields; `bool` conversion contract unchanged.
- **Error paths?** No new I/O. QSettings load returns 0.0 on missing
  key.
- **Secrets / PII?** None. No new telemetry tag — existing per-game
  `duration_seconds` supports distribution analysis.
- **Performance?** O(1): one extra double load + one extra
  `setValue` per game.
- **Concurrency?** Single-threaded UI; no shared state added.

## Assumptions

- >=3 wins threshold; mirrors standard speedrun trackers' "ao3".
- Line shows on every win past the threshold, including new-best
  runs. The average is always >= best (best is the minimum), so
  seeing the gap between current run and lifetime average is
  itself informative.

## Test plan

- [x] `tst_stats` covers all twelve new test cases
- [x] All 10 locales have hand-translated `Average: %1` strings
- [x] No translation regressions (107 finished, 0 unfinished)
- [x] clang-format clean
- [x] CI-equivalent build/test passes locally

author: builtwithrobots
body:
Closes the gap where SOP-import-flagged terms land in the glossary with English definitions Sonnet wrote but no Spanish definition, because the terms gate only requires the EN/ES *term* pair (the definitions are optional). Managers were left with empty Spanish definition fields and no easy way to backfill them at scale.

New affordance: a small "Translate from English" link sits next to each Spanish field's label inside both the create and edit dialogs. Click → call Google Translate via the existing translateMarkdown path → replace the Spanish field's value with the result. The manager edits before clicking Save, so this is a *suggestion* not a write. When the field already has Spanish content, the link swaps to "Re-translate" so the manager can iterate based on feedback without hunting for the same affordance.

Server action `suggestTranslation`:
  - manager-only via getCompanyContext
  - feeds the call the company's active glossary minus the in-flight term itself (excludeTermLower), so re-translating Forklift's English definition doesn't substitute "Forklift" → "Montacargas" inside its own definition before Google ever sees it
  - reuses translateMarkdown — same cost logging path, so the spend lands on the platform AI usage tab as Google characters automatically
  - sopId left undefined since these calls aren't tied to an SOP

Pending state shows "Translating…" and pulses the icon; one suggest call at a time across both fields. Errors render in a single inline alert above the form so the manager can retry. Disabled when the English source is empty (nothing to translate).

The pattern stays inside TermFormFields so both AddTermButtonClient and the GlossaryListClient edit dialog get it without duplication. GlossaryListClient passes the original term_en (lowercased) as the exclude key; AddTermButtonClient passes nothing since there's no in-flight term yet.

author: mekxh
body:
**💡 What:** 
Added an auto-scrolling mechanism to the `ChatTimeline` component so that it automatically scrolls to the latest message. Also added explicit ARIA accessibility attributes (`role="log"`, `aria-live="polite"`, and `aria-busy`).

**🎯 Why:**
When a chat timeline receives new messages (or when a long message makes the container scrollable), users shouldn't have to manually scroll down to read the new text. Without the ARIA `log` role, screen readers fail to automatically read out dynamically added chat content. This makes the interface more robust for both visual and non-visual interactions.

**📸 Before/After:**
- Before: Sending long messages or multiple messages required manual scrolling.
- After: The panel automatically jumps to the bottom (via `scrollTop = scrollHeight`) whenever new messages are appended, avoiding layout jank by utilizing Vue's post-flush watcher.

**♿ Accessibility:**
- Added `role="log"` and `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers actively announce new messages added to the chat interface.
- Added `:aria-busy="isSending"` so assistive technologies know when the system is processing a response.

Description:
This PR introduces a standardized, automated pipeline for deploying and verifying smart contracts on the Stellar Testnet. This replaces manual deployment workflows, reducing the risk of human error and providing a verified source-of-truth for our on-chain infrastructure.

Changes:

Automation: Developed scripts/deploy-testnet.sh and supporting logic to handle the contract installation and initialization lifecycle.

Verification: Implemented a verification step that ensures the deployed bytecode matches the local source hash.

author: billduke13
body:
## Summary
Closes the MSRV triangle. Three files declare the same Rust toolchain floor:
- `Cargo.toml` — `[workspace.package] rust-version = \"1.88\"`
- `rust-toolchain.toml` — `[toolchain] channel = \"1.88\"`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` step's `toolchain: \"1.88\"` input

A bump to one without the others fails silently: local `cargo` honours the toolchain-file pin while CI keeps verifying against the older `rust-version` floor, so any feature that needs the newer toolchain (e.g. iced 0.14 / ashpd 0.13 → >= 1.88) appears to work locally and breaks downstream.

`rust-toolchain.toml`'s comment already names this triangle in prose but does not enforce it. This PR adds the enforcement test.

## Test plan

## Summary

Research deliverable for OP-168 — review of [zellij](https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij) as a candidate replacement for the tmux + iTerm-orchestrator stack that hosts op-obsidian agents today.

**Verdict: HOLD.** Revisit when zellij closes the multi-client mirror gap ([#4253](https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/4253)) **or** the team consciously accepts losing the per-pane viewer pattern + iTerm-CC native tabs.

Key findings (full evidence in `docs/research/OP-168-zellij-as-target.md`):

- **Probe-verified.** Headless orchestration works today against zellij 0.44.1: `zellij attach -b` for detached create, `action new-tab -l <kdl>` for layout injection, `--pane-id` for `dump-screen`/`focus-pane-id` (focus-independent, no client required), `--tab-id` for cross-tab spawn, `list-sessions -s` as a clean has-session analogue.
- **Two structural gaps.** (1) Zellij is mirror-only when multiple clients attach to one session — the `view-${issueId}` grouped-tmux trick at `orchestrator.ts:263–290` doesn't translate. (2) No tmux -CC analogue → iTerm native-tabs-from-tmux integration (the non-orchestrator launch path) goes away.
- **Timing yellow flag.** The 0.44 CLI surface we'd depend on is ~3 weeks old. Zellij is still pre-1.0.
- **Migration size.** Role (c) — both replacements — sheds ~2.7k LoC of hand-written source + ~19k LoC of generated protobuf types. Significant, but not favorable enough today given the gaps and timing.
- **OP-154 is unaffected.** It should proceed independently and continues to improve the current stack.

## Test plan

- [ ] No code changes; doc-only PR. CI is green / N/A.
- [ ] Reviewer reads `docs/research/OP-168-zellij-as-target.md` end-to-end and sanity-checks the verdict against §3 probe transcripts and the dimension-by-dimension table.

## Summary

Bumps `VERSION` from `0.1.9.1` to `0.2.0` so the file matches what we're about to tag.

After this PR merges, pushing the `v0.2.0` tag triggers `build-image.yml`, which publishes:

- `ghcr.io/mnexa-ai/e2a:0.2.0` / `:0.2` / `:0` / **`:latest`**
- `ghcr.io/mnexa-ai/e2a-web:0.2.0` / `:0.2` / `:0` / **`:latest`**

The `:latest` tag is gated on semver-tag pushes (per `build-image.yml`'s metadata-action config) so this is the first time it'll exist. Today `docker pull ghcr.io/mnexa-ai/e2a:latest` returns 404; after the tag push it works. Same for `e2a-web`.

GitHub release sidebar will populate once `gh release create v0.2.0` runs after the tag.

## Why 0.2.0 (not 1.0.0)

0.2.0 is the natural next step from `0.1.9.1`. A `1.0.0` cut commits to long-term API stability — that's a separate decision worth thinking about deliberately, not folded into a release-tag mechanic.

author: mvnkoo
body:
…al bugs

Tier 3 cleanup of the typecheck backlog. Started at 107 errors after the xyflow v12 migration (mix of pre-existing CRA-era debt and v12's stricter generics on Node/Edge surfacing it), ended at 0. The build script is now `tsc -b && vite build`, so future type errors will break the build instead of slipping through silently.

Type system consolidation:
- Centralize IliNode in IliBaseTypes (was duplicated, with subtly different `data` shapes, in IliSchemaExplorer, useIliSchema and IliLayoutService).
- Add IliFlowNodeData, SearchOption and NavigationState as the single source of truth; remove the local copies.
- expTypes.NodeData / SchemaNode rewritten as `Node<NodeData, ...>` with an index signature so v12's `Record<string, unknown>` data constraint is satisfied.
- useNodesState/useEdgesState now take generics; without them v12 inferred `never[]` and made downstream calls fail.
- useIliSchema's setter parameter types switched from `(value) => void` to `Dispatch<SetStateAction<...>>` so callers can pass updater functions (which they already did at runtime).

Real bugs surfaced and fixed (not type-only):
- useIliSchema:739 pushed `string[]` into setNavigationHistory which expects `NavigationState[]`. Now constructs proper objects.
- IliSchemaExplorer:195 pushed HistoryEntry-shaped objects (id, label, type, isAbstract, timestamp) into the same history, while useIliSchema:550 read `previousState.nodeId`. The two halves never matched at runtime. Consolidated into one NavigationState shape with the breadcrumb fields as optional, and rewrote the push to use `nodeId` so the back-navigation actually works.
- IliParserService:585 stored enum values as `string[]` into a field typed `IliEnumValue[]`. Mapped them into `{value}` objects.
- IliClassNode was missing the `associations` field that the parser sets; added it.
- IliAttribute was missing `isReference?: boolean` that nodes read.

Two visual bugs (post xyflow v12):
- IliAssociationNode bottom-left/right corners were not rounded at certain zoom levels. The collapsed state used `borderBottomLeftRadius: 'inherit'` which renders inconsistently on subpixel boundaries — replaced with concrete value `2`.
- EXP Explorer rendered no edges to enum nodes after the v12 bump. expEnumNode's <Handle> elements lacked `id="left"`/`id="right"`, while createTypeReferenceEdge sets `sourceHandle: 'right'` / `targetHandle: 'left'`. v11 fell back to the first matching handle, v12 matches strictly. Added the IDs.

Dead-code removal:
- src/features/exp-explorer/index.tsx (imported a non-existent `IfcSchemaFlow` export, never imported by anyone).
- src/features/ili-explorer/components/sidebar/index.ts (re-exported a non-existent `IliSidebar` file, never imported).

Misc:
- ThemeContext.tsx: typed an implicit-any `mode` parameter.
- IliToolbar.tsx: typed Autocomplete renderOption `props` with `& { key: string }` (known MUI 5 quirk).

## Summary

Closes #481 — config validation found 5 must-fix issues in `.env.example` and `docker-compose.prod.yml`. This PR fixes all five:

- **Removes stale Auth0 config** from `docker-compose.prod.yml` and `docker/frontend/Dockerfile.prod`. Auth0 was removed 2026-01-01 (replaced by email auth) but the env vars / build args lingered. The build-arg fallbacks were also leaking a **real Auth0 domain + client ID** into a public repo — fixed.
- **Drops `AUDIT_URL`** from `.env.example` — references a removed `audit-logger` service, not used anywhere in the backend.
- **Adds `FRONTEND_URL`** to `.env.example` — read by `services/slack_service.py` (OAuth redirects), `services/ssh_service.py` (SSH host auto-detect), and `routers/public_links.py`. Operators following the template were silently breaking OAuth + SSH.
- **Documents SMTP fields** (`SMTP_HOST` / `SMTP_PORT` / `SMTP_USER` / `SMTP_PASSWORD`) and **`SENDGRID_API_KEY`** so the advertised `EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp` and `EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid` modes are actually configurable from the template.

- `docker-compose.prod.yml` — removed `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `AUTH0_ALLOWED_DOMAIN`, `VITE_AUTH0_*` build args (5 lines)
- `docker/frontend/Dockerfile.prod` — removed `VITE_AUTH0_*` ARG/ENV declarations (6 lines)
- `.env.example` — removed `AUDIT_URL`, added `FRONTEND_URL`, `SMTP_*`, `SENDGRID_API_KEY` (net +5 lines)

Net: 16 insertions, 12 deletions across 3 files. No code logic touched.

The validation report flagged additional informational items (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` alias, `VOICE_*`, `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, `OTEL_SAMPLE_RATE`, `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS`, etc.) that are not in the must-fix list. Those should be a follow-up issue.

## Summary

Fixes `{"code":"validation_error","detail":"responses array is required","attribute":"responses"}`.

`pollUntilCompletion()` returns a wrapper: `{ success: true, result: { responses: [...], action: "...", ... } }`. We were sending the entire wrapper object to the backend, so the World ID API never saw the `responses` array (it was nested inside `result`).

**Fix**: Send `completion.result` (the actual IDKit proof data) instead of the whole `completion` wrapper. Also added proper error handling for when `completion.success` is `false`.

author: mepoo23123123
body: ## Summary Addresses all 10 items from the code review: 1. **`getRedirectResult()` handler** — `auth.js` now exposes `redirectReady`, an IIFE that drains the redirect-flow credential before `onAuthStateChanged` fires. First-time Google sign-ins that fall back to `signInWithRedirect` now correctly run `initUserData()`. Without this, new users landed on the app with no `studioTree` / `projects/default` / `chats/default` and the UI broke. 2. **Drop dead RTDB rules** — `database.rules.json` no longer declares `studioTree/$uid` and `sync/$uid` at the top level (the code only writes under `users/$uid/...`). Closes the gap that let any authenticated user write to those unused top-level paths. 3. **SRI on Monaco loader** — added `integrity="sha384-…"` + `crossorigin="anonymous"` to the jsDelivr Monaco loader script. (Firebase compat scripts on `gstatic.com` don't ship SRI hashes, so they're left as-is.) 4. **CI lint+format check** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `npm run lint` + `npm run format:check` on every PR and push to `main`. ⚠ See "Notes" below — this file could not be pushed by the bot due to OAuth scope, you'll need to add it yourself. 5. **UI hint for OpenRouter key sync** — added `.form__hint` warning under the sync checkbox explaining the key is stored unencrypted in RTDB and that XSS could leak it. Default (off) keeps the key only in `localStorage`. 6. **Bind chat scroll listener once** — `bindChat()` now runs at `DOMContentLoaded` instead of inside `loadApp()` (every login). Re-binding per login was stacking duplicate scroll listeners. 7. **Folder expand state in `localStorage`** — `tree.js` now persists folder expand/collapse to a `localStorage` map keyed by folder id, mirroring how instance nodes already worked. Toggling a folder no longer rewrites the entire `studioTree` to RTDB and no longer triggers a re-render via the listener echo. 8. **Parallelize `apply*` writes** — all five batchers (`applyScripts`/`applyInstances`/`applySetProperties`/`applyDeletes`/`applyMoves`) now collect refs and `await Promise.all(writes)` instead of sequential `await` per item. A 30-op AI batch no longer serializes ~3-5s of round-trips. The studioTree write inside `applyScripts` is now a single write per batch instead of per-script. 9. **`HTTP-Referer` from origin** — OpenRouter request now sends `window.location.origin` so forks attribute correctly. 10. **Collapse legacy auth error codes** — `mapAuthError` returns the same generic "Неверный email или пароль" for `auth/invalid-credential` / `auth/user-not-found` / `auth/wrong-password` (modern Firebase Auth collapses them by design). `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` both pass clean. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Add the CI workflow manually.** The `.github/workflows/ci.yml` file is below — copy it into the repo and commit on this branch (or main). This was blocked by OAuth `workflow` scope on my push. - [ ] **Smoke-test Google sign-in in an incognito window with popups blocked.** Should redirect, come back, and seed `users//studioTree` etc. for new users. - [ ] **Smoke-test the explorer.** Toggle a folder a few times, reload the page — folder should remember its state. Then sign in on a different browser — folder state shouldn't follow you (this is now intentional, the state is `localStorage`-only). - [ ] **Run a chat that emits multiple SCRIPT/INSTANCE markers** and confirm everything still applies correctly (parallelized writes are atomic per-op but the order is now non-deterministic across sibling ops — should be safe because each op has a unique key). - [ ] **Test plan:** 1. Open the deployed site. 2. Sign in via email/password — confirm `loadApp()` works. 3. Sign out, sign in again with Google — confirm new user data initialization works on first time, idempotent on subsequent. 4. Open Settings → enable "Синхронизировать ключ" — confirm the new warning hint is visible and styled. 5. In Explorer, toggle ServerScriptService a few times, F5, confirm state restores. 6. Send a chat that creates 3+ scripts; confirm they apply and Studio plugin gets them. ### Notes **The CI workflow file (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) couldn't be pushed by the bot** because the OAuth integration only has `repo` scope, not `workflow`. To add it, run locally on this branch: ```bash mkdir -p .github/workflows cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml << 'YAML' # Lint and Prettier check on every push and PR. name: CI on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: permissions: contents: read jobs: lint: name: Lint & format runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: '20' cache: 'npm' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run format:check YAML git add .github/workflows/ci.yml git commit -m "Add lint+format CI workflow" git push ``` The original 10-fix commit (`446d975`) was reset to drop the workflow file; the head commit (`8f10b1b` or similar) on this branch still references the workflow only in this PR description, not in the diff. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/360f01a76c1d4c3686e95dc0c9bb1d35 Requested by: @Mepoo23123123 ---

Mixture density networks typically uses the negative log-likelihood (nll) objective, which can suffer from slow convergence and mode collapse. The natural gradient expectation maximization (ngem) objective can achieve up to 10x faster convergence while adding almost zero computational overhead, and scales well to high-dimensional data where nll fails.

body:
## Summary
- **Lens null `verify_attestation` (production)** — Dockerfile was missing `libtss2-tctildr0t64`. Added the package + a `ctypes.CDLL` smoke check in the same RUN so a missing TPM2 lib fails the build.
- **Lens null `verify_attestation` (QA)** — `AuthenticationService.start()` skipped attestation under `CIRIS_IMPORT_MODE`/`CIRIS_MOCK_LLM` and ran startup attestation as fire-and-forget. Removed the skip, captured the task on `self._attestation_task`, added `await_attestation_ready()` for consumers. `prefetch_batch_context()` blocks on it before reading the cache and no longer has a silent fallback — missing/failed attestation is now fatal.
- **Google Play 16 KB page-size rejection (full)** — every `.so` in the AAB now 16 KB-aligned: bumped `onnxruntime-android` 1.17.0 → 1.25.0 (1.21 only fixed `libonnxruntime.so`; its `libonnxruntime4j_jni.so` was still 4 KB), and rebuilt `libllama_server.so` from llama.cpp HEAD with NDK 27 + `-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384` (37 MB → 8.8 MB stripped).
- **Apple native auth on iOS/macOS without oauth.json** (#a8313d68b — iOS team) — falls back to bundle-ID audiences (`ai.ciris.mobile{,.debug}`) on Apple platforms; non-Apple platforms still 503. New tests pin all four branches.
- **SonarCloud blockers** — removed undefined `geo_wisdom`/`weather_wisdom`/`sensor_wisdom` from `ciris_adapters/__init__.py:__all__`.

## Test infrastructure
- `MockRuntime` bakes in the ciris_verify adapter, adapter_manager, service_registry, bus_manager.
- `MockServiceRegistry` carries an attestation-aware `get_authentication()`.
- All three `mock_runtime` fixtures (root conftest, `system_snapshot_fixtures`, `ciris_engine/logic/context` conftest) delegate to the same class.
- ~75 tests across 9 files updated to use the centralized fixtures instead of inline `Mock()` runtimes.
- New auth-fallback coverage: 6 tests in `TestNativeAppleTokenExchange`.

body: ## Summary Dual-writes `upsertContact()` mutations to the gateway DB via IPC, as part of the contacts → gateway source of truth migration ([ATL-288](https://linear.app/vellum/issue/ATL-288)). ## What changed ### Gateway side - **`ContactStore.upsertContactWithChannels()`** — new write method that upserts a contact + all its channels in a single transaction. Uses `onConflictDoUpdate` for idempotency. - **`upsert_contact_with_channels` IPC handler** — exposes the write method over IPC with zod validation for the full payload (contact + channels array). ### Assistant side - **`gateway-dual-write.ts`** — new module with `syncContactToGateway()` that maps a `ContactWithChannels` to the gateway's ingress-relevant subset (drops `notes`, `userFile`, `contactType`) and fires a one-shot IPC call. - **`contact-store.ts`** — all three return paths in `upsertContact()` now call `syncContactToGateway()` after the local write succeeds. ### Design - **Fire-and-forget**: The IPC call is async with `.catch()` — gateway write failures are logged but never propagate to the caller. Assistant DB remains the primary path. - **Ingress-relevant subset only**: Gateway receives `id`, `displayName`, `role`, `principalId`, timestamps. Context-only fields (`notes`, `userFile`, `contactType`) stay assistant-only. - **Channels included**: All channel fields are synced since they're all ingress-relevant (status, policy, externalUserId, etc.). ## Linear [ATL-290](https://linear.app/vellum/issue/ATL-290) — part of [ATL-288: Contacts → Gateway Source of Truth Migration](https://linear.app/vellum/issue/ATL-288) ---

author: troglodyne
body:
## What
Two independent idempotency gaps not covered by any of PRs #5–#16.

## Why
**sendmail target** (`makefile.tt`): had no `touch $@`, so Make never considered the target "done" — `systemctl restart sendmail` fired on **every** `make` invocation (every redeploy, test run, or manual make call). On a shared system this causes needless service churn. Also, the restart was inline rather than deferred.

**mariadb secure installation** (`mariadb.tt`): `secure_installation.sql` (which contains the root password in plaintext) was rendered, copied to `/opt/mysql`, executed, and deleted on **every** deploy. While the SQL itself is idempotent, writing credentials to disk and re-running the secure-install block on every redeploy is unnecessary and slightly risky.

## How
- `makefile.tt`: defer `systemctl restart sendmail` via `queue_postrun_task` (consistent with every other service restart in the codebase); add `touch $@` so the target is stamped done after first successful run.
- `mariadb.tt`: guard the secure-install block with `[ -f /opt/mysql/.secured ] ||`; touch the marker on success; use `rm -f` to clean up from both the staging dir and `/opt/mysql` regardless of which path was taken.

## Testing
No automated test suite. Verified diff against all open PRs — no overlap on these specific changes. Patterns follow established guards from the codebase (queue_postrun_task, state file guards).

Note: this PR modifies `makefile.tt` (also touched by PR #7) and `mariadb.tt` (also touched by PR #6) — different lines, minor conflict to resolve at merge time.

author: jamie8johnson
body:
# refactor: collapse Commands enum into single registration table

Closes #1097.

## Problem

Adding a new top-level `Commands` variant required coordinated edits in 5 exhaustive matches across two files. Forgetting one was a compile error in the lucky case (the `batch_support()` and `command_variant_name()` matches were exhaustive) but a silent default in the unlucky case (the `_ => {}` and `_ => unreachable!()` catch-alls in `dispatch.rs` swallowed misses, with the latter only surfacing as a runtime panic).

## Solution

Single registration table in `src/cli/registry.rs`. Each command is one row carrying both its bind-pattern and wildcard-pattern (so emitters can choose, avoiding `unused_variables` warnings on dispatch-irrelevant matches), the tracing label, the daemon-forwarding policy, and the dispatch body.

Four `macro_rules!` emitters consume the table:

| Emitter | Generates | File |
|---|---|---|
| `gen_batch_support_impl` | `Commands::batch_support()` exhaustive match | `definitions.rs` |
| `gen_variant_name_impl`  | `Commands::variant_name()` exhaustive match | `definitions.rs` |
| `gen_dispatch_group_a`   | `run_with`'s pre-context match (Group A return + Group B no-op) | `dispatch.rs` |
| `gen_dispatch_group_b`   | `run_with`'s post-context match (Group A unreachable + Group B dispatch) | `dispatch.rs` |

The registry splits rows into `group_a:` (no-store, lifecycle, mutation) and `group_b:` (store-using) lists so the dispatch emitters can emit different RHS per group without nested macros (which Rust doesn't allow in match-arm position).

`cli` / `ctx` / `project_cqs_dir` are passed as `:ident` parameters so captured row bodies retain their call-site syntactic context (macro_rules' mixed-site hygiene means literal identifiers in a captured `$body:block` don't see caller locals; `:ident` substitution does).

## Acceptance criteria (from #1097)

- [x] **One new file + one registration line per new command** — adding a variant now requires (a) the `clap`-derive declaration in `definitions.rs::Commands` (clap requires a real enum), and (b) one row in `registry.rs`. The handler module is the same as before.
- [x] **Reflection: `is_pipeable` / `batch_support` / `name` from single registration** — `batch_support()` and `variant_name()` are both `for_each_command!` calls. (`is_pipeable` lives on `BatchCmd`, a separate enum, and is out of scope here.)
- [x] **All 56 commands migrated; no `_ =>` catch-all in dispatch** — the `_ => {}` fall-through and `_ => unreachable!()` are gone. Both matches are exhaustive over `Commands`. Group A variants in the Group B match emit `unreachable!("Group A variant `{name}` handled before context open", $name)` — explicit per-variant arms, not catch-alls.
- [x] **Compile-time wiring check** — every emitter expands to an exhaustive match. A new `Commands` variant without a registry row fails to compile in four places.
- [x] **Clap derive still owns per-command arg parsing** — the `Commands` enum and all `args::*Args` structs are untouched; the macro lives strictly above clap.

## Verification

* `cargo build --features gpu-index` — clean (0 warnings, 0 errors).
* `cargo clippy --features gpu-index --lib` — clean.
* `cargo test --lib --features gpu-index` — 1736 passed, 16 ignored.
* `cargo test --bin cqs --features gpu-index` — 574 passed, 3 ignored. Includes existing `batch_support_*` pinning tests + a new `variant_name_pins_critical_command_labels` test for the macro-generated label map.
* Smoke: `cqs --version`, `cqs ping`, `cqs stats`, `cqs scout` all behave identically to main.

One pre-existing integration test fails on `main` and on this branch independently of this change (`test_cache_stats_empty_cache_emits_zero_envelope` — fixture issue with project-scoped `embeddings_cache.db` shadowing the test's tempdir). Tracking separately.

## File deltas

| File | Before | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/cli/registry.rs` | 0 | 747 | new |
| `src/cli/dispatch.rs` | 878 | 445 | −433 |
| `src/cli/definitions.rs` | 1139 | 1166 | +27 |

Net +341 lines. The growth is the dual-pattern-per-row tax (one bind, one wildcard so the emitters can pick the right one without `#[allow(unused_variables)]` per match arm). The win is structural: the 5 silently-coupled match sites collapse to one registration row.

body: ## The bug Latest blog post hero image (and every other dynamic OG image on the site) was failing to load — both on the blog index card and on the article page. ## Root cause Production logs showed every \`/api/og/*\` call returning 500 with \`Error: Missing required environment variable\`. Tracing it back: 1. \`instrumentation.ts\` calls \`validateEnv()\` on every function startup. 2. \`validateEnv()\` throws when \`OPENWEATHER_API_KEY\` is missing. 3. \`instrumentation.register()\` re-throws in production. 4. Edge function startup aborts → 500 to the client, no image rendered. But \`/api/og/blog\` doesn't use \`OPENWEATHER_API_KEY\` at all. The validation was killing edge functions for a key they don't need. The key is no longer actually required since the Open-Meteo migration. \`.env.example\` already says so: > NOTE: Primary weather data comes from Open-Meteo (free, no key needed)... This key is only still referenced by legacy/fallback endpoints: pollen, UV (onecall v3), precipitation history, extremes. ## Fix Move \`OPENWEATHER_API_KEY\` from \`required\` → \`optional\` in \`lib/env-validation.ts\`. Routes that still need it check at request time and handle missing keys themselves (verified — every legacy caller does \`process.env.OPENWEATHER_API_KEY\` at request scope). ## Diagnosis trace - Probed live site with Playwright: confirmed \`/api/og/blog?title=...&type=space\` returns 500, hero \`\` has \`naturalWidth: 0\`. - Tested \`/api/og\`, \`/api/og/weather-card\`, \`/api/og/blog\` with curl — all 500. - Vercel runtime logs (production, level=error, last 2h): every \`/api/og/*\` shows \`Missing required environment variable\`. Same message also flooding non-OG routes (\`/blog\`, \`/weather/[city]\`) but those return 200 because the throw doesn't kill node-runtime serverless functions the same way it kills edge functions. ## Test plan - [ ] Vercel preview deploys; hit \`/api/og/blog?title=test&type=space\` on the preview URL — expect 200 + a PNG. - [ ] Visit \`/blog\` on preview, confirm featured-card hero image renders. - [ ] Click into latest post, confirm article hero image renders. - [ ] After merge, re-probe production: \`curl -I https://www.16bitweather.co/api/og/blog?title=test&type=space\` should return 200. ## Side benefit The cascade of \`Missing required environment variable\` log spam on \`/blog\`, \`/weather/[city]\`, etc. (visible in the runtime logs but ignored because pages still rendered) will also stop. Cleaner production logs. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * OpenWeather API key is now optional in environment configuration, streamlining setup requirements and reducing mandatory configuration parameters.
